Add 3/4 cup milk powder and mix well, continuing to roast for another 3-4 minutes. The mixture should be smooth and have a creamy appearance. Coarsely grind 4 green cardamom pods and add to the mixture. Add 1 cup sugar and mix thoroughly until all sugar crystals dissolve into the warm mixture. Transfer the mixture immediately to a greased rectangular tray or plate and press gently with a spatula to even the surface. Sprinkle 1 tbsp almond flakes and 1 tbsp pistachio flakes on top. Allow to cool completely at room temperature for 1-2 hours. Once firm, cut into square pieces using a sharp knife. Store in an airtight container.

name: jeera aloo
instructions: Boil 5 potatoes, peel and cut into pieces. Heat 2-3 tbsp oil on low flame, add cumin, asafoetida, turmeric, green chili and ginger, fry lightly. Add potatoes and salt, fry on medium-high heat. Add dry fenugreek and fry 3-4 minutes. Add coriander powder, red chili, black pepper, dry mango powder and garam masala, roast well. Garnish with green coriander and serve hot with parathas or roti.

name: paneer kali mirch makhani
instructions: Prepare paneer marinade: mix paneer with curd, cream, cornflour, fenugreek, coriander stem, black pepper, cardamom and salt. Make gravy: soak cashews and muskmelon seeds, grind with green chili and ginger into paste. Heat oil and butter, add spices and gravy paste, fry until oil separates. Add cream, salt, sugar and remaining curd. Simmer and add marinated paneer pieces. Cook until paneer is tender. Serve hot.

name: kolhapuri kat vada
ingredients: oil 5 tbsp plus 1-1.5 tbsp plus frying oil
instructions: Make kat: Roast cumin, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, pepper, black cardamom, coriander and poppy seeds. Add grated coconut and ginger, roast. Add chopped tomatoes and salt, cook covered 4-5 minutes. Blend when cool. Make vada filling: Heat oil, add mustard seeds, asafoetida, ginger, green chili, curry leaves. Add boiled mashed potato, salt, amchoor, garam masala. Add coriander and roast 5 minutes. Make vada batter: Mix gram flour, rice flour, turmeric, red chili, salt, asafoetida, baking soda with water to pouring consistency. Shape filling into potato balls, coat with batter. Fry in hot oil until golden. Prepare kat: heat oil with spices, add blended masala, fry until oil separates. Add water, salt and coriander, simmer 7 minutes. Pour hot kat into plate, add fried vadas, garnish with coriander and sev.

name: dahi bengan
instructions: Roast cloves, black pepper, coriander powder, turmeric and cumin seeds over low heat. Add ginger and roast. Add chopped tomato and salt, cook covered 4-5 minutes. Stir and cook another 2 minutes. Heat oil separately, add mustard seeds to crackle. Add asafoetida, ginger, green chili and curry leaves. Layer in dish: spread half the curd, add eggplant pieces, top with masala mixture and remaining curd. Season with cumin seeds and red chili oil on top. Cook covered on low heat or steam until eggplant is tender.

name: gajar ki kanji
ingredients: black mustard seeds 2 tbsp coarsely ground
instructions: Cut black carrots into pieces or chips. Place in a clean glass jar. Add coarsely ground mustard seeds, salt, black salt, black pepper and asafoetida. Cover with water completely. Cover the jar loosely with cloth or lid. Leave to ferment for 3-5 days at room temperature. The kanji will become dark and develop tangy fermented flavor. Drink as a traditional digestive beverage.

name: steamed modak
instructions: Prepare filling: Mix jaggery, grated coconut, almond flakes, cashew powder and ground cardamom. Keep aside. Make dough: Mix rice flour with salt. Add ghee and water gradually to make soft dough. Knead well. Let dough rest few minutes. Prepare modak: Oil hands lightly, take portion of dough, make shallow cup shape, fill with spoon of jaggery-coconut mixture. Close edges and shape into traditional modak form. Steam modaks in steamer for 10-15 minutes until cooked through. Serve warm.

name: veg mughlai paratha
ingredients: oil 2 tsp plus 1 tsp plus 3 tbsp for frying
instructions: Prepare dough: Mix flour, salt and baking powder. Add oil and water gradually, knead into soft dough. Rest dough. Prepare filling: Heat oil, add ginger and green chili. Add grated carrot, chopped capsicum and cauliflower. Add turmeric, red chili, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, amchoor and salt. Cook until vegetables are tender. Add crumbled paneer and coriander leaves, mix well. Cool filling. Roll dough into thin circle, place filling in center, gather edges and seal. Flatten gently. Heat oil in pan, fry paratha until golden brown on both sides. Serve hot with chutney or achar.

name: eggless chocolate cupcake
instructions: Mix flour, cornflour, cocoa powder, sugar powder, baking soda and baking powder in bowl. In another bowl, mix oil, milk, vinegar and vanilla essence. Combine wet and dry ingredients, mix until smooth batter forms. Pour into cupcake molds or small cups. For no-bake version: refrigerate for 2-3 hours until set. For baked version: bake at 180C for 15-18 minutes. Garnish with almond flakes. Serve chilled.

name: masala fulwadi
instructions: Mix gram flour, semolina, turmeric, cumin powder, coriander seeds, fennel seeds, black pepper, red chilli, sesame seeds, dry mango powder, and salt. Add curd, sugar powder, 6 tbsp oil, and baking soda. Mix well to form a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes. Heat oil for frying. Using a sev maker or squeeze bottle, extrude long strips of dough directly into hot oil. Fry until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels. Store in an airtight container.

name: matar ki muthiya
instructions: Grind green peas coarsely. Mix with wheat flour, gram flour, fenugreek leaves, salt, turmeric, coriander powder, green chilli, red chilli, ginger, cumin seeds, and carom seeds. Add baking soda mixed with curd and knead to soft dough with water. Boil water and grease a sieve with oil. Divide dough into 2 equal parts and roll into logs. Steam on sieve for 2 minutes on high heat, then 20 minutes on medium heat. Cut into 1/2 inch pieces. Heat oil in pan, add sesame seeds, cumin seeds, salt, and red chilli powder. Add muthiya pieces and crisp both sides. Make chutney from coriander leaves, green chilli, ginger, black salt, salt, cumin, and amchur. Serve muthiya with chutney.

name: khasta mathri
instructions: Mix wheat flour, refined flour, semolina, carom seeds, cumin seeds, black pepper, kalonji, kasuri methi, and salt. Add 1/4 cup oil and ghee, and rub into flour until breadcrumb texture. Add water gradually and knead to stiff dough. Let rest for 30 minutes. Divide dough into portions. Roll each thin, brush with ghee and 2 tbsp refined flour, roll up, coil, and flatten. Roll again to thin disc. Heat oil for frying. Fry mathri until light golden and crisp on both sides. Drain on paper towels. Cool and store in airtight container.

name: thai basil chicken
instructions: Mix dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, castor sugar, and chicken stock in a bowl. Heat oil in a kadai. Add chopped garlic and saute till golden brown. Add chopped red chillies and mix. Add chicken pieces and saute on high heat for 2-3 minutes. Add spring onion bulbs and saute for 2 minutes. Pour in sauce mixture, add salt, and cook for 6-8 minutes. Add Thai basil leaves and white sesame seeds, mix well. Transfer to serving bowl and garnish with fresh red chillies. Serve hot with sticky rice.

name: saffron cookies
instructions: Soak saffron in warm milk and let infuse. Beat butter lightly in a bowl. Add icing sugar and beat till light and fluffy. Add refined flour, green cardamom powder, and salt and beat well. Transfer mixture into a piping bag fitted with a star nozzle. Line a baking tray with greased parchment paper and pipe small cookie portions. Sprinkle pistachios on top. Freeze for 10-15 minutes. Preheat oven to 180°C. Bake in preheated oven for 10-12 minutes till light golden. Allow to cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

name: pasta in saffron sauce
ingredients: yellow capsicum 0.5 small seeded cut into triangles
red capsicum 0.5 small seeded cut into triangles
green capsicum 0.5 small seeded cut into triangles
instructions: Heat olive oil and butter in a pan. Add refined flour and saffron, saute till fragrant. Add chopped garlic and saute till golden brown. Add red chilli flakes and mix well. Pour in milk gradually, stirring constantly, and cook till sauce thickens. Add blanched broccoli florets, yellow capsicum triangles, red capsicum triangles, green capsicum triangles, and cooked mushroom slices. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Add boiled penne pasta and salt, mix gently and cook for 2-3 minutes more. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with fresh basil sprig, and serve hot with garlic bread.

name: Mushroom and Turmeric Soup
instructions: Heat butter in a pan and sauté garlic until golden brown. Add onion and cook until translucent. Add turmeric, shitake mushrooms, button mushrooms, salt, black pepper and herbs. Cook for 4-5 minutes. Add water and bring to boil, then simmer covered for 6-8 minutes. Cool and grind to a fine mixture. In a fresh pan, heat the ground mixture with water, discard scum, add fresh cream. In another pan, sauté shimeji mushrooms in butter on high heat for 2-3 minutes. Pour soup into serving bowls, top with sautéed shimeji mushrooms, sprinkle pepper, and serve hot with lavash.

name: Moong Osaman
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds. When they crackle, add finely chopped garlic and ginger, sauté for a minute. Add chopped onion and cook until golden. Add turmeric powder and salt. Add soaked whole moong and roast for 2-3 minutes. Add water and bring to boil. Simmer until moong is cooked through but retains its shape, about 20-25 minutes. Add green chillies towards the end. Serve hot.

name: Peanut Sauce
instructions: Crush garlic cloves and shallots in a mortar with red chilli powder. Grind roasted peanuts to fine powder in a grinder. Heat a pan and add coconut milk, turmeric, coriander, crushed garlic-shallot mixture and Thai red curry paste. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Add peanut powder and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Add tamarind paste, lemon juice, salt and brown sugar. Cook until sugar melts. Cool completely. Garnish with bird eye chillies and serve as a dip or dressing.

name: Green Moong Mathri
instructions: Grind soaked green gram coarsely in a grinder. In a bowl, mix whole wheat flour, semolina, asafoetida, onion seeds, carom seeds, baking soda, fennel seeds, cumin seeds, black pepper, turmeric, salt, fenugreek leaves and melted ghee. Add ground green gram and mix well. Add water and knead to a soft dough. Add oil and knead well. On an oiled surface, roll dough into semi-thick discs, dock all over with a fork and cut into small roundels using a cookie cutter. Heat sufficient oil and deep fry until golden brown and crisp. Drain on absorbent paper and cool completely before storing.

name: Rice Parantha
instructions: In a bowl, mix whole wheat flour, salt, 2 tsp ghee and yogurt. Add water and knead to soft dough with 2 tsp oil. Cover with moist cloth for 15-20 minutes. In another bowl, mix cooked rice, red chilli powder, cumin powder, chopped green chillies, coriander, salt and chopped onion. On a floured surface, roll dough into thin roundels and press between palms. Flatten into thick disc, drizzle 1 tsp ghee on it and stuff with rice mixture. Seal edges and roll out into parantha. Heat a tawa, place parantha on it and cook. Drizzle 2 tsp ghee on both sides and shallow fry until golden brown. Cut into quarters and serve hot with pickle.

name: Peas Cashew Samosa
ingredients: date and tamarind chutney for serving
instructions: For dough: Mix refined flour, carom seeds, salt, ghee and water. Knead to stiff dough and cover for 10-15 minutes. For stuffing: Dry roast coriander, fennel and cumin seeds until fragrant and crush coarsely. Heat oil, add ginger, green chillies, roasted spices and asafoetida. Sauté for 30 seconds. Add cashew nuts, dried mango powder, red chilli powder and salt. Mix well. Add green peas and boiled mashed potatoes. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Cool. Divide dough into 5 portions and roll into thick ovals. Cut into half, apply water on edges and shape into cones. Stuff with potato mixture and seal. Preheat air fryer to 180C for 2-3 minutes. Spray oil on basket, arrange samosas and spray oil on them. Air fry for 40-45 minutes until golden. Serve with green chutney and date-tamarind chutney.

name: Mushroom Satay
ingredients: spring onion greens chopped for garnish
instructions: 1. Grind shallots, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, and red chilli powder coarsely with 1 tbsp water. 2. Add coconut milk, Thai red curry paste and brown sugar and grind to fine paste. 3. Mix mushrooms in bowl with ground paste, turmeric and coriander powder and salt. 4. Thread mushroom pieces on wooden skewers. 5. Heat oil in nonstick grill pan and arrange skewers. 6. Cook on medium heat 3-4 minutes per side. 7. Transfer to serving plate, sprinkle spring onion greens and serve hot with peanut sauce.

name: Saffron Madeleines
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 180°C. 2. Soak saffron in warm milk and set aside. 3. Beat eggs with castor sugar gradually until light and fluffy. 4. Sift refined flour, baking powder, salt and green cardamom powder together. 5. Fold dry ingredients into egg mixture. 6. Add saffron milk and beat well. 7. Transfer to piping bag and pipe into madeleine mould. 8. Bake in preheated oven for 10-12 minutes. 9. Allow to cool and serve.

name: Green Moong and Avocado Hummus
instructions: 1. Soak and cook green moong dal until soft. 2. Take cooked moong and avocado in a blender. 3. Add garlic cloves, lemon juice, olive oil and salt. 4. Blend until creamy. 5. Add cumin powder and adjust seasonings. 6. Serve as a dip with vegetables or crackers.

name: Meetho Lolo
instructions: 1. Heat 1 cup water in nonstick pan, add sugar and stir until dissolved. 2. Add 1/4 tsp green cardamom powder and cook until syrup forms. 3. Mix flour with remaining 1/4 tsp cardamom powder. 4. Add sugar syrup to flour and knead into stiff dough. 5. Divide dough into lemon-sized portions and roll into balls. 6. Flatten balls and roll into thick rotis. 7. Roast on nonstick tawa on low heat, turn over and drizzle oil. 8. Cook until both sides are golden. 9. Serve hot or at room temperature.

name: Sui Mai
ingredients: refined flour 1.5 cups plus for dusting
soaked dried shitake mushrooms chopped 2-3 tbsps
instructions: 1. Mix turmeric powder with 3/4 cup water. 2. Knead refined flour with salt, egg yolk and turmeric water into stiff dough, rest 30 minutes. 3. Mix chicken mince with ground prawns, spring onion greens, mushrooms, spring onion bulbs, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, stock powder and salt. 4. Divide dough into small portions, roll into thin disks. 5. Place disk between thumb and finger and stuff filling. 6. Press lightly and pinch sides. 7. Sprinkle chopped carrot on top and arrange in dim sum basket. 8. Steam for 8-10 minutes. 9. Serve hot with chilli oil dip.

name: Quick Chicken Tikka
ingredients: 400 gms boneless chicken breasts, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
2 medium green capsicums, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
instructions: 1. Marinate chicken pieces with red chilli paste, salt, ginger-garlic paste, yogurt, garam masala powder and lemon juice. 2. Add 2 tbsps oil and marinate for a few hours in refrigerator. 3. Heat non-stick pan and pour orange juice into it. 4. String chicken and capsicum pieces alternately onto skewers. 5. Heat non-stick tawa, drizzle oil and place skewers on it. 6. Pack rice into mould and demould on serving plate, drizzle 1 tbsp oil over it. 7. Add salt, pepper powder and sugar to orange juice and cook. 8. Turn skewers so chicken cooks evenly all around. 9. When sauce thickens, remove from heat, add butter and mix well. 10. Place skewers over rice, drizzle sauce and serve immediately.

name: Chicken Popcorn
ingredients: 300 grams boneless chicken breast, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
instructions: 1. Take chicken pieces in bowl. Add salt, red chilli powder, black pepper powder, ginger-garlic paste and vinegar, mix well. 2. Sift refined flour, salt and baking powder in a bowl. 3. Roll chicken pieces in refined flour mixture and dip in ice cold water for 30 seconds. 4. Roll in refined flour mixture again. 5. Preheat air fryer at 190°C for 2-3 minutes. 6. Spray oil on air fryer basket and arrange chicken pieces in single layer. 7. Air fry for 6 minutes. Flip chicken pieces, spray more oil and air fry for 6 more minutes. 8. Serve hot.

name: Mooli Gajar Achar
instructions: Cut radish and carrot into thin sticks. Mix with chopped green chilli and garlic. Dry roast mustard, coriander, cumin, fennel, and fenugreek seeds lightly. Heat mustard oil in a pan, add the roasted spices. Add the radish-carrot mixture along with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, amchur powder, hing, and salt. Mix well until all vegetables are coated. Store in an airtight container without sun-drying for instant pickle.

name: Gobhi Matar Kofta Curry
instructions: For kofta: Boil and finely chop cauliflower and peas. Mix with coriander leaves, minced garlic, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and gram flour. Season with salt. Form into balls. Heat oil and fry koftas until golden on all sides. For curry: Heat oil in a large pan, add cumin seeds. Sauté finely chopped onions until golden. Add minced ginger and garlic, cook for a minute. Add chopped tomatoes, coconut, and dry spices (turmeric, red chilli, coriander, cumin powders, garam masala). Cook until tomatoes soften. Add the fried koftas and simmer until gravy is well blended. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: Chana Dal Poori
instructions: For stuffing: Soak and cook chana dal with water, ginger, garlic, and green chilli until soft. Add turmeric, salt, and roasted cumin powder. Mash lightly and cool. For dough: Mix wheat flour with salt and knead with water to soft but firm consistency. For curry: Heat oil, add bay leaves and cumin seeds. Sauté onion until golden. Add tomato, cook until soft. Add spices (turmeric, red chilli, coriander, cumin, garam masala). Pour in the cooked dal water or stock. Simmer to get curry consistency. Assembly: Take a portion of dough, flatten, add dal stuffing in center, seal edges well. Deep fry in hot oil until puffed and golden on both sides. Serve hot with the prepared curry.

name: Gobhi ke Parathe
instructions: For stuffing: Finely chop cauliflower. Mince garlic, green chilli, and ginger. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan, add cumin seeds. Add the finely chopped cauliflower along with minced garlic, ginger, and green chilli. Add turmeric, red chilli powder, garam masala, asafoetida, salt, and chopped coriander leaves. Cook on medium heat until cauliflower is tender and most moisture evaporates. Cool the filling. For dough: Mix wheat flour with salt and knead with water to make a smooth, soft dough. Let it rest for 15 minutes. Divide dough into equal balls. Roll out each portion, spread cauliflower filling in the center, bring edges together and seal. Flatten gently and roll to paratha thickness. Cook on a hot griddle with oil/ghee until golden brown spots appear on both sides and it's cooked through.

name: Matar Aloo Nimona
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add bay leaves. Add cumin and coriander seeds and let them crackle. Add finely chopped green chilli, ginger, and garlic. Sauté for a minute until fragrant. Cut potatoes into small cubes and add to the pan. Cook potatoes for 4-5 minutes until they start to soften. Add fresh green peas and mix well. Sprinkle turmeric powder, salt, and asafoetida. Add black pepper. Cook on medium heat for 5-7 minutes until potatoes are tender and peas are cooked through. Add chopped coriander leaves and mix. Adjust seasoning and serve hot. This dish serves as both a main vegetable and a dal substitute.

name: Mixed Dal Dosa
instructions: Soak all dals (masoor, chana, moong, chilke wali moong, toor) for 1-2 hours (or skip for instant version). Grind the soaked dals with ginger, garlic cloves, curry leaves, and coriander leaves to a smooth consistency. The batter should be thick but pourable. If not using instant, let the batter ferment for 4-6 hours to get the authentic dosa taste, or use immediately for instant dosa. Heat a cast iron griddle or dosa pan. Apply ghee lightly. Pour a ladleful of batter and spread in a circular motion using the ladle to create a thin crepe. Drizzle ghee around the edges and cook until the bottom is golden and crispy. Flip and cook the other side briefly. For chutney: Grind amla, fresh coconut, green chilli, ginger, garlic, and coriander leaves with a little water to make a smooth chutney. Add salt to taste. Serve dosa with chutney.

name: Rabdi Malpua
instructions: For rabdi: Boil 1.5 liters of milk in a heavy-bottomed pan on medium-high heat. Keep stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. Let the milk reduce to about 3/4 of its original volume, becoming thick and creamy. Add 2 tbsp sugar and simmer for another 5-10 minutes. Cool completely. For syrup: Mix 1 cup sugar with 1 cup water in a pan. Bring to boil, add a pinch of saffron, and let the syrup cool completely. For malpua: Make a smooth batter using maida flour and 1/2 cup milk (consistency should be like crepe batter). Heat ghee in a shallow pan. Drop spoonfuls of batter and fry until puffed and golden on both sides. Quickly dip the hot malpua into the sugar syrup for a second, then place on a serving plate. Pour the prepared rabdi over the malpua and garnish with chopped pistachio and cashews. Serve cold or at room temperature.

name: Paneer Tikka Thali
instructions: Marinate paneer cubes in curd and spices for 30 minutes. Prepare onion-tomato paste with ginger, garlic, and cashews. Heat ghee and temper with cinnamon, cardamom, and bay leaves. Add the paste and cook until fragrant. Add marinated paneer, cream, and yogurt. Simmer for 15 minutes. Prepare laccha paratha dough, make green chutney, coat paneer pieces in chutney and fry. Serve with paratha, raita, and fried paneer tikka.

name: Kaju Peanut Barfi
instructions: Roast cashews and peanuts until fragrant and lightly golden. Grind them together to a fine powder using a food processor. Make sugar syrup by boiling sugar with water until it reaches one-thread consistency. Mix the ground nut powder with sugar syrup while hot, stirring continuously. Spread the mixture on a parchment-lined pan and let set for a few hours. Cut into pieces with a sharp knife.

name: Palak Aloo
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling water, drain, and grind to smooth paste. Cube potatoes. Heat oil and add cumin seeds, then onions and garlic. Cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for a minute. Add turmeric and chilli powder, then cubed potatoes. Cook until soft. Stir in spinach paste and yogurt. Simmer for 10 minutes until flavors combine. Temper with ghee, chopped garlic, and dry red chilli. Finish with garam masala.

name: Double Layer Veg Sandwich
instructions: Prepare green chutney by blending coriander, green chilli, ginger, garlic. Layer bread with mashed potatoes mixed with spices and greens, then add fresh onion, cucumber, tomato slices, and apply chutney. Toast on griddle until golden and crispy.

name: Bengali Dum Aloo
instructions: Toast spices (cumin, coriander, black pepper, poppy seeds). Grind with cashews to make paste. Peel and fry potatoes until light golden. Blend tomatoes, add to potatoes with spice paste, ginger, green chilli, and mustard oil. Simmer covered until potatoes are tender.

name: Sooji Ka Halwa
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan, roast sooji until fragrant. Add milk gradually and stir continuously to avoid lumps. Once mixture thickens, add sugar and continue cooking. Serve hot topped with cardamom powder and dry fruits.

name: Paneer Afghani
instructions: Marinate paneer cubes in 2 tbsp curd mixed with ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder (0.5 tsp), turmeric, garam masala (0.5 tsp), black pepper, and salt for 20 minutes. Prepare onion paste by blending onion, green chilli, garlic cloves, coriander leaves, and cashews. Prepare curd masala paste by mixing 1 cup curd with kasuri methi, turmeric, red chilli powder (2 tsp), coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala (1 tsp), and black pepper. Heat oil, fry paneer until golden, remove. Heat oil again, add bay leaf, black cardamom, mace. Add onion paste, cook until aromatic. Add curd masala paste, mix well. Add fried paneer, simmer. Finish with butter and kasuri methi. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Chandrakala
instructions: Prepare filling: mix mawa with powdered sugar, almonds, cashews, and 1 tsp ghee. Prepare dough: mix all purpose flour with 2 tbsp ghee and baking soda, knead with water to soft dough. Prepare sugar syrup: boil sugar and water until one-string consistency, add food colour if desired. Roll dough thin, spread filling on half of each piece, fold to create crescent shape. Deep fry in oil until golden brown. Dip in warm sugar syrup. Garnish with pista. Dry on a rack.

name: Bombay Mix
ingredients: cooking oil 2 tbsp plus for frying
instructions: Prepare sev: mix besan with turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, aamchur powder (0.5 tsp), salt, and 2 tbsp cooking oil. Gradually add water to make stiff dough. Press through sev maker into hot oil, fry until crispy, drain. Separately fry soaked chana dal and moong dal until crispy and golden. Toast raw peanuts in oil until crunchy. Combine all fried items in a large bowl. Season with chaat masala, remaining aamchur powder (0.5 tsp), black salt, and regular salt to taste. Mix well and store in an airtight container for up to one month.

name: Healthy Poha Chivda
instructions: Dry roast thin poha on low heat until completely crispy (8-10 minutes), transfer to a bowl. In the same pan, separately roast raw peanuts until golden (5-7 minutes), set aside. Roast cashews until golden (3-4 minutes), set aside. Roast bengal gram and dry coconut together until fragrant (5 minutes), set aside. Prepare tadka: heat 1 tsp oil, add cumin seeds, fennel seeds, and hing. When fragrant, add curry leaves and finely chopped green chilli, cook for 30 seconds. Pour tadka over roasted poha. Add peanuts, cashews, bengal gram, and coconut. Toss well. Season with rock salt, powdered sugar, aamchur powder, and turmeric powder. Mix thoroughly. Store in airtight container.

name: Mooli Leaves and Eggplant Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, and methi seeds. When they splutter, add chopped garlic. Add finely chopped mooli leaves and diced eggplant. Sprinkle turmeric powder and green chilli. Mix well and cook covered on medium heat for about 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender. Season with salt to taste.

name: Papad Curry
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add finely chopped onion and cook until golden. Add minced garlic and ginger, cook for a minute. Break urad dal papads into pieces and add to the pan. Stir well. Add curd and mix thoroughly. Add bay leaf, cinnamon, and all dry spice powders (turmeric, red chilli, coriander, cumin, garam masala). Add water as needed to create a curry consistency. Simmer for 10 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve.

name: Namakpara
instructions: Mix all purpose flour with carom seeds and salt in a bowl. Add cooking oil and mix well. Add water gradually and knead into a stiff dough. Let the dough rest for 15 minutes. Roll out the dough thin on a surface and cut into diamond or rectangular shapes. Heat oil for frying in a pan. Fry the crackers in batches until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Store in an airtight container.

name: Paneer Tawa Fry
instructions: Cut paneer into cubes or slices. Make a marinade with curd, besan, mustard oil, kasuri methi, red chilli powder, garam masala, chaat masala, black pepper, and salt. Coat paneer pieces in the marinade and let sit for 5 minutes. For green chutney, blend coriander leaves, mint leaves, garlic, ginger, salt, and lemon juice into a paste; mix in sev bhujiya and curd. Heat butter and oil on a tawa or griddle. Cook marinated paneer pieces until golden on all sides. Serve hot with green chutney on the side.

name: Achari Aloo and Ajwain Poori
instructions: For achari aloo: Dice potatoes. Toast cumin seeds, coriander seeds, black pepper, fennel seeds, mustard seeds, and dry red chilli in oil until fragrant. Add diced potatoes and mix. Add turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt. Cook covered on medium heat for 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender. For ajwain poori: Mix wheat flour with carom seeds, salt, and ghee. Add water gradually to form a stiff dough. Rest for 10 minutes. Take small balls, roll into thin discs, and deep fry in hot oil until puffed and golden. Serve hot pouris with achari aloo.

name: adadiya pak
instructions: Dry roast split black gram in ghee until golden brown. Add edible gum and roast till it puffs and turns light brown, about 2-3 minutes. Add roasted and crushed almonds, pistachios, and cashews. Mix in grated coconut. Heat milk with milk powder and add to the mixture. Dissolve jaggery and add, stirring constantly. Add dry ginger powder and mix well. Spread on greased tray, cool slightly, and cut into pieces.

name: zero oil chicken masala
instructions: Blend garlic, ginger, green chilli, coriander leaves, and mint leaves into a fine paste. Mix chicken with curd and half of the paste along with turmeric powder and let marinate for 10 minutes. Heat a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker on high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook in its own juices without any oil. Add the remaining spice paste and all the dry spice powders. Cook on high heat for 15-20 minutes till chicken is fully cooked and the gravy reduces. The moisture from the chicken itself will create the cooking medium. Garnish with coriander leaves before serving.

name: egg cheese masala
instructions: Heat butter and cooking oil together in a pan over medium heat. Add ginger-garlic paste and minced green chilli, cook for about 1 minute until aromatic. Add diced onions and cook until they turn golden brown. Add diced tomatoes and cook until they soften and begin to break down, about 2-3 minutes. Add diced capsicum and green peas, cook for 2 minutes. Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala, and coriander powder. Mix well and cook for 1 minute to blend the spices. Cut boiled eggs into halves or pieces and gently add to the mixture. Shred the cheese and add to the pan, cook for about 2 minutes until the cheese melts and coats everything. Add chilli flakes and mixed herbs. Mix gently to avoid breaking the eggs. Taste and adjust salt. Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot.

name: Palak Paneer Kofta Curry
instructions: Blend spinach into a paste. Mix paneer with besan and spinach to form kofta dough. Shape into balls. Prepare a tomato gravy with onions, ginger, garlic and spices. Simmer the koftas in the gravy until cooked through and flavors are absorbed.

name: Suran Sabzi
instructions: Peel and cube the suran. Heat mustard oil and temper with cumin seeds, bay leaves and black cardamom. Add onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic-chilli paste and tomatoes. Add the suran and cook until tender. Add mango pickle and spices. Finish with ghee and coriander leaves.

name: Basanti Pulao
instructions: Heat ghee and oil together. Sauté green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick and bay leaf. Add ginger paste and sauté. Add rice and stir to coat. Pour water and bring to boil. Add sugar, cashews, raisins and saffron. Cook until rice is tender and water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.

name: Rice Flour Dosa
instructions: Mix rice flour, ginger, coriander leaves, chilli flakes and salt with water to make thin batter. Heat dosa pan and pour batter, spread thin. Cook until golden on both sides. For chutney, grind onion, tomato, red chilli, curry leaves, dals, garlic, tamarind paste and salt into a smooth paste. Serve dosa with chutney.

name: Chinese Sizzler
instructions: Prepare fried rice by heating oil, adding garlic-ginger, vegetables including corn, then rice. Add soy sauce and black pepper. For noodles, heat oil, add garlic, vegetables including cabbage, then noodles. Season with soy sauce, vinegar, red chilli sauce and ketchup. For manchurian, mix grated vegetables with corn flour, flour and schezwan chutney, form balls and fry. For gravy, heat oil, add garlic-ginger-green chilli, sautéed peppers and onions, add sauces, vinegar and cornflour slurry. Plate sizzler with fried rice, noodles and manchurian balls in gravy.

name: Bakarwadi
instructions: 1. Mix maida, salt, and warm oil. Add water gradually and knead semi-stiff dough. Rest 10 minutes, knead well for 4-5 minutes, cover with moist cloth and rest 30 minutes. 2. Dry roast jeera, dhaniya, and sesame on low flame until aromatic. Divide into two batches - make one fine powder and keep one coarse. 3. Mix both spice batches with hing and chilli powder. 4. Dry roast fresh coconut to remove moisture. 5. Cook tamarind pulp with jaggery and water for 3-4 minutes until thick. 6. Mix mora sev, roasted coconut, fresh coriander, green chilli paste, spice mix, and tamarind-jaggery syrup. 7. Roll dough thin, spread filling, roll into spiral, flatten slightly. 8. Deep fry in hot oil until crispy and golden brown. 9. Drain on paper towel and serve.

name: Sarson ka Saag with Makke ki Roti
instructions: Boil mustard leaves, spinach, radish, onion, tomato, garlic and green chilli with water and salt until soft. Drain and chop finely. Heat oil and ghee, add cumin seeds and dry red chilli. Add ginger, then onion and cook until golden. Add tomato and dry spices (turmeric, red chilli powder). Add the boiled greens and mix well. Sprinkle maize flour to thicken the curry and simmer. For Makke ki Roti: Mix maize flour, wheat flour and salt. Add water and knead into soft dough. Divide into portions, roll into thin circles and cook on hot griddle until done.

name: Dum Aloo with Basanti Pulao
instructions: For Dum Aloo: Soak and grind cashew, melon seeds, cumin, coriander, black pepper, dry red chilli and poppy seeds into a smooth paste with ginger and green chilli. Peel and halve potatoes. Heat mustard oil and fry potatoes. Remove and set aside. In same oil, add the ground paste and fry. Add tomatoes and spices (turmeric, red chilli powder, sugar, salt, bay leaf, black cardamom). Add potatoes back, cover and cook on high heat (dum) for 15-20 minutes. For Basanti Pulao: Wash and soak rice. Heat ghee and oil, add cardamom, clove, bay leaf, cinnamon. Toast rice and add fried cashews and raisins. Add water and cook covered until rice is tender.

name: Louki Muthiya
instructions: Grate louki (bottle gourd) and squeeze out excess water using a cloth. Mix all flours (gram, jowar, bajra, wheat) together. Mince ginger, garlic, green chilli and coriander leaves. Add minced ingredients to flour mixture. Add all spices (carom seeds, sesame seeds, hing, turmeric, red chilli, coriander, cumin, garam masala). Mix dahi and oil into the mixture to form a dough-like consistency. Shape into cylindrical muthiya by rolling between palms. Steam in a steamer until cooked through (15-20 minutes). Serve hot with any curry or chutney.

name: Arbi ke Patte ki Sabzi
instructions: Mix besan with ginger-garlic paste, sesame seeds, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, lemon juice, rice flour and salt. Spread this mixture evenly on arbi leaves. Roll tightly into cylinders and steam or boil for 20 minutes. Cool and cut into pieces. Fry until crispy and golden. For curry: Heat oil, add mustard and cumin seeds. Add minced garlic and ginger, then onion. Add tomato and cook. Add remaining spices (turmeric, red chilli, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala). Add the fried pakode and simmer for 5 minutes. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Beetroot Paneer Paratha
instructions: Boil beetroot until tender, peel and grate finely. Mix grated beetroot with wheat flour and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and let rest for 15-20 minutes. Crumble paneer and mix with chopped onion, green chilli, coriander leaves, mixed herbs and chilli flakes. Divide dough into 4 equal portions. Roll each into a flat circle, place paneer filling in center, fold edges to seal and flatten gently. Cook on a hot griddle with ghee or oil until golden brown spots appear on both sides.

name: Panchmewa Paag
instructions: Dry roast all nuts and dry fruits separately until fragrant. In a pan, heat ghee and lightly toast the roasted ingredients. Add sugar and water, cook on medium heat stirring continuously until the mixture reaches a thick, crumbly consistency. Cool slightly and serve as a dry fruit paag pudding.

name: Barbatti Aloo
instructions: Heat oil and add cumin seeds. Once they crackle, add sliced onions and cook until translucent. Add ginger-green chilli paste and cook for 30 seconds. Add diced potatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Add chopped long beans and cook for 5 minutes. Add tomatoes, all spice powders, and salt. Cook covered on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until vegetables are tender. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

name: Stuffed Capsicum
instructions: Mash boiled potatoes and mix with chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, green chilli, roasted peanuts, and all spices. Cut capsicums into halves lengthwise and remove seeds. Fill the potato mixture into capsicum halves. Heat oil in a pan and place stuffed capsicums with filling side down. Cover and cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes until capsicums are tender. Serve hot.

name: churma laddoo
instructions: Mix karkara atta and ghee in a bowl and rub well until flour sticks. Gradually add luke warm water and knead into a stiff dough. Divide dough into portions and knead well for 2-3 minutes each. Cover with damp cloth and rest for 15 minutes. Divide into small portions and press into stick shapes. Heat ghee in a wok to 140°C and shallow fry the sticks on low heat until crisp and golden brown, turning carefully. Cool completely and crush with hands. Transfer to mixer grinder and grind in pulse mode until coarse texture. Pass through sieve to get fine powder. Mix grated nutmeg with the powdered churma. Heat ghee from frying, melt jaggery completely, sprinkle water and mix. Add melted jaggery and ghee to churma powder and mix well. Shape into laddoos without pressing hard and coat lightly with poppy seeds. Store in airtight container.

name: garlic pickle
instructions: Peel and clean garlic cloves. In a pan, heat mustard oil until smoking. Add mustard seeds, black mustard, carom, fennel, coriander, cumin, and fenugreek seeds. Add garlic cloves and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Add turmeric, red chilli, and amchur powder. Mix well. Add nigella seeds and salt. Transfer to a glass jar and let cure for 3-4 days before serving.

name: black chickpea stir-fry
instructions: Pressure cook soaked bengali gram with water until tender (about 20 minutes). In a pan, heat ghee and sauté chopped garlic and green chilli. Add diced onion, capsicum, french beans, carrot, and broccoli. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes. Add cooked gram, turmeric, salt and coriander leaves. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes.

name: kadhi pakora
instructions: Soak urad dal and chana dal separately. Grind urad dal with ginger, cloves, black pepper, black cardamom and salt. Deep fry spoonfuls to make vadas. Grind chana dal with green chilli and garlic, fry as vadas. Make boondi by dropping besan batter through a sieve into hot oil. For kadhi: whisk curd with besan, turmeric and salt. In a pan, heat mustard oil, add methi seeds, cumin and dry red chillies. Add curd-besan mixture. Add water to desired consistency. Bring to boil. Add cooked vadas and boondi. Simmer for 10-15 minutes.

name: chilli baby corn
instructions: Cut baby corn into medium pieces. Make a batter with maida, 2 tbsp corn flour, red chilli powder, black pepper, salt and water. Coat baby corn pieces and deep fry until crispy. For sauce: mix 4 tbsp corn flour with water. Heat oil, sauté minced garlic, ginger and green chilli. Add diced peppers and onion, stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add soy sauce, chilli sauce, tomato sauce and green chilli sauce. Pour the corn flour-water mixture to thicken. Add cooked baby corn, mix well. Top with spring onion and serve.

name: vrat thali
instructions: For rajgira poori: Mix rajgira flour with sendha namak, mashed boiled potato and water to make a soft dough. Knead well. Roll into small rounds and deep fry in ghee until puffed and golden. For green chutney: Grind coriander leaves, roasted peanuts, green chilli, ginger and lemon juice. Mix with curd and salt. For aloo sabzi: Cut boiled potatoes into cubes. Heat ghee, add cumin seeds and curry leaves. Add potato cubes, roasted peanut powder and salt. Stir well and cook for 3-4 minutes. Serve hot rajgira puri with aloo sabzi and green chutney.

name: Chilli Gobi
instructions: Cut cauliflower into florets. Make a batter with corn flour, maida, and spices. Coat florets and deep fry until golden. In a separate pan, heat oil and mix in the fried florets with soy sauce, chilli sauces, ketchup, onions and peppers. Toss well and serve hot with spring onion garnish.

name: Aata Namakpara
instructions: Knead wheat flour with ghee, fenugreek leaves, carom seeds, black pepper and salt to make a stiff dough. Roll out thin and cut into ribbons or small squares. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towel and cool completely before storing.

name: Methi Kofta Curry
instructions: Finely chop methi leaves and mix with gram flour, onion, ginger-garlic paste, and spices. Shape into small koftas and lightly fry. Make a tomato-onion gravy by cooking onions, tomatoes with green chilli, garlic, and ginger. Add the fried koftas to the gravy and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve.

name: Rava Laddoo
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and roast the rava until light golden and fragrant, stirring continuously. Add milk slowly while roasting. Once the rava absorbs the milk and becomes crumbly, remove from heat. Add powdered sugar, cardamom powder, and lightly roasted cashews and almonds. Mix well and let cool slightly. Shape into balls using wet hands or a mold. Serve once completely cooled.

name: Louki Panaka
instructions: Grate louki, carrot and spinach. Finely chop onion, ginger, green chilli and garlic. Squeeze excess moisture from grated louki. Mix grated vegetables and onion with jowar flour, gram flour, salt, garlic, ginger and green chilli. Heat ghee in a pan and drop spoonful of batter to make thin pancakes. Cook on both sides until golden brown and crispy. Serve hot with chutney.

name: Bengali Chana Dal Curry
instructions: Rinse chana dal and pressure cook with water, ginger, green chilli, black cardamom, cinnamon stick, cumin seeds, bay leaf and dry red chilli for 2-3 whistles. Heat mustard oil in a pan and add the cooked dal. Season with turmeric powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, roasted cumin powder and kasuri methi. Add fresh grated coconut and simmer for 5 minutes. Adjust salt and serve hot.

name: Hyderabadi Mutton Biryani
instructions: Marinate mutton with salt, spices, garlic-ginger paste, curd, and mint leaves. Boil rice in salted water with cardamom and green chilli. Layer marinated meat in pot with boiled rice, saffron-soaked ghee, and mint. Seal with dough and cook on high heat then low heat until meat is tender and rice is cooked.

name: Onion Tomato Chutney
instructions: Heat oil and temper with asafoetida, urad dal, red chilli, mustard seeds, cumin, garlic, ginger, and curry leaves. Add onion and green chilli, cook until soft. Add tomato chunks and cook until they break down. Add tamarind pulp and salt. Cook until thick and serve as chutney.

name: Tomato Basil Focaccia Bread
instructions: Mix flour, water, salt, and yeast to make dough. Let rise for 1 hour. Knead and spread on baking tray. Top with tomato slices, basil leaves, olive oil, and sea salt. Let rise for 30 minutes. Bake at 220°C for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

name: Paneer Makhni
instructions: Heat water and add diced tomatoes, onion, garlic, ginger, and whole spices. Simmer for 15 minutes. Blend into smooth sauce. Cook cashew nuts and add to sauce. Heat butter on pan, add ginger, green chilli, and paneer cubes. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato sauce, salt, chilli powder, fenugreek leaves, and sugar. Simmer for 5 minutes. Finish with cream and serve.

name: Crispy Masala Dosa
instructions: Soak rice, urad dal, channa dal, and methi seeds overnight. Grind to make fermented batter. For masala: Heat oil, temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves, channa dal. Add onions and green chilli, cook until soft. Add turmeric powder, boiled mashed potatoes, and salt. Mix well and cool. To cook dosa: Spread batter on greased tawa in circular motion. Drizzle oil around edges. Cook until crispy. Spread masala filling in center, fold and serve. Top uttapam with onion, tomato, and coriander.

name: Cheese Burst Paratha
instructions: Make soft dough with aatta and maida. Roll out dough circles. Mix mozzarella, cheddar, cheese slices, Italian seasoning and basil. Stuff mixture into dough. Fold and seal edges. Roast on tawa with oil until golden and cheese bursts out.

name: Sabudana Dosa
instructions: Soak sabudana and samak chawal per recipe. Mix sabudana, samak chawal, curd, salt and sugar. Heat oil, temper with cumin. Add ginger, green chilli, curry leaves. Mix in potato filling. Spread batter on heated tawa, fry until crispy. Grind coconut, herbs, spices, anardana and salt with water for chutney. Serve dosa with chutney.

name: Masala Corn Makhan Malai
instructions: Roast corn on tawa or open flame, turning frequently until kernels are soft and charred. Rub roasted corn with butter. Mix chaat masala, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Sprinkle masala mixture generously over buttered corn. Serve hot.

name: Apple Cinnamon Pancake
instructions: Blend rolled oats with milk until smooth. Add eggs, salt, vanilla extract, sugar and baking powder. Mix until smooth batter. Peel and chop apple finely. Mix apple with cinnamon powder and nutmeg. Fold apple mixture into batter. Heat butter on a griddle or tawa. Pour batter portions and cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden. Serve hot with maple syrup.

name: Crispy Fried Chicken
instructions: Cut chicken into pieces. Marinate chicken with salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder and onion powder for at least 30 minutes. Mix flour and cornstarch. Beat egg with milk. Dip marinated chicken in egg-milk mixture. Coat thoroughly in flour-cornstarch mixture. Deep fry in hot oil at 170°C until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towels. Serve hot.

name: Ginger Turmeric Sherbet
instructions: Boil water with fresh ginger slices for 5 minutes. Add turmeric powder and let it steep for 2 minutes. Strain into a glass. Add honey and lemon juice. Stir well. Serve warm and sip gently.

name: Pyaz ki Kachori
instructions: Make a stiff dough with maida, salt, ghee, oil and water. Rest for 15 minutes. For filling: heat oil, add cumin, fennel, asafoetida, then ginger and chilli. Add chopped onions and cook until golden. Season with salt, pepper, turmeric and chilli powder. Cool completely. Roll dough thin, fill with onion mixture and seal. Deep fry in hot oil on low-medium heat until golden and crispy. Serve hot with pudina chutney.

name: Watermelon Halwa
instructions: Peel and grate the white portion of watermelon rind finely. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and add the grated rind. Stir continuously on medium heat. Add sugar and milk gradually. Keep stirring to prevent lumps and sticking. Cook until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan (about 30-40 minutes). Add condensed milk, cardamom powder and dry fruits. Mix well. Serve warm or cold.

name: Kaju Namak Pare
instructions: Mix maida, salt, baking powder, baking soda and ajwain. Add ghee and mix until breadcrumb texture. Add water gradually to make a stiff dough. Knead well. Roll out thin on a greased surface. Cut into diamond or half-moon shapes using a knife or cookie cutter. Heat oil and fry on low heat initially until shapes start to puff, then increase heat to medium to get golden crispy texture. Drain on paper towels. While still warm, toss in a mixture of black salt, pepper powder, chilli powder and amchur. Store in an airtight container.

name: Langar Wali Dal
ingredients: mixed dal (masoor, moong, chana), 1 cup soaked
instructions: Soak mixed dals for 1-2 hours. Boil dals with water and turmeric until completely soft and mushy (about 30-40 minutes). Add salt to taste. In a separate pan, heat ghee and add cumin seeds. When they crackle, add dry red chilli and asafoetida. Add chopped onion and cook until translucent. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli. Cook for a minute. Pour this tempering into the cooked dal. Stir well and simmer on low heat for another 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot.

name: No-Bake Chocolate Cake
instructions: Crush biscuits into fine crumbs. Melt chocolate chunks and butter together. Mix crushed biscuits, cocoa powder, melted chocolate-butter mixture and chopped nuts. Press this mixture firmly in a lined 8-inch round pan. Refrigerate for 2 hours. Whip heavy cream with sugar until stiff peaks form. Spread whipped cream over the set base. Prepare chocolate ganache with remaining melted chocolate and whipping cream. Pipe chocolate ganache on top using a piping bag. Garnish with mint leaves, cherries and chocolate shavings. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.

name: Chole Matar Kulcha
instructions: For the curry: Heat oil, add onions and cook until golden. Add tomatoes and green chilli. Add cooked chickpeas/peas and all spices (chilli powder, pepper, cumin, chaat masala, coriander powder). Add salt and black salt. Cook on low heat for 15 minutes. Finish with amchoor powder and lemon juice. For the kulcha: Mix maida, salt, baking powder and baking soda. Add curd and melted butter. Add water to make a soft dough. Cover and let it rest for 2-3 hours for fermentation. Divide into balls, flatten, brush with butter, sprinkle onion seeds. Cook on a hot tawa until puffed and golden on both sides. Serve hot kulcha with the spiced chickpea curry.

name: Hot Garlic Sauce
instructions: Boil kashmiri chillies in hot water to create a paste. Heat oil, add garlic and sauté. Add tomato ketchup, soya sauce, salt, sugar, and vinegar. Pour in 3 cups water and bring to simmer. Mix corn starch with 4 tbsp water to create slurry and add to sauce to thicken. Stir in spring onions. Serve as a dip or condiment.

name: Peanut Chutney
instructions: Heat oil and add asafoetida, cumin, and curry leaves. Grind roasted peanuts with garlic, ginger, fresh coconut, green chilli, and tamarind. Mix ground paste with the tempering oil and add water to achieve chutney consistency. Season with salt. In a separate pan, heat 2 tbsp oil and add dry red chillies, mustard seeds, and curry leaves for tempering. Pour tempering into chutney. Serve with idli, dosa, or vada.

name: Bel Sherbet
instructions: Cut open the bael fruit and scoop out the pulp along with seeds and fibers. Mix bael pulp with 1 liter of water. Strain through a fine sieve to separate seeds and fiber from the juice. Add sugar and stir well until dissolved. Add a tiny pinch of salt if desired. Chill the drink. Serve in glasses over ice cubes with fresh mint leaves garnish.

name: Peanut Ladoo
instructions: Dry roast peanuts in a heavy-bottomed pan until fragrant. Crush or coarsely grind the roasted peanuts. In the same pan, heat ghee and dry roast singhara atta until golden brown and fragrant. Add crushed peanuts to the roasted flour. Mix in desiccated coconut, sugar, and cardamom powder. Add chopped dry fruits and melon seeds. Mix everything together thoroughly with the ghee. Cool slightly until you can handle the mixture. Roll into equal-sized balls with your palms, pressing gently. Store in an airtight container.

name: sandesh
instructions: Curdle 2 liters of cow milk with vinegar and water to make paneer. Drain and press the cottage cheese. Mix pressed paneer with sugar and cornstarch. Heat the mixture until combined, season with cardamom powder. Garnish with dissolved saffron. Serve as a sweet treat.

name: bhutte ka shorba
instructions: Heat butter, sauté cumin and bay leaf. Add chopped onions, ginger, garlic, green chilly, and curry leaves. Cook until onions soften. Stir in turmeric and curry powder. Add boiled sweet corn kernels and flour, cook for 2 minutes. Pour in water and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend the soup until smooth. Return to heat, season with salt and pepper. Serve hot garnished with spring onions and popcorn.

name: methi malai mater
ingredients: dried methi leaves 3 tablespoons blanched 1 cup
instructions: Sauté onions, ginger, garlic, and green chillies in oil and butter with shahi jeera. Grind to a smooth paste. Cook the paste with black cardamom, cardamom, peppercorn, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander, and cumin. Add cashew paste and curd, cook for 5 minutes. Add water and bring to boil. Add blanched methi leaves and green peas, simmer for 15 minutes. Finish with cream and salt. Serve with parantha.

name: chicken rice momos
instructions: Mix minced chicken with finely chopped onion, garlic, green chilli, and soy sauce in a bowl. Divide into portions and coat each portion with cooked rice to form shape. Steam in a steamer for 8-10 minutes until chicken is cooked through. Serve hot with chilli oil or vinegar.

name: onion tomato sandwich
instructions: Mix chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, coriander, green chilli, chaat masala, salt, and lemon juice in a bowl. Butter the bread slices. Roast papad until crispy and crush into small pieces. Layer cheese slices on bread, add vegetable filling, top with crushed papad. Cook on tawa or griddle over medium heat until golden. Serve hot.

name: watermelon sorbet
instructions: Roughly chop fresh watermelon into chunks. Blend watermelon chunks with fresh mint leaves and lemon juice until smooth. Add sugar if needed. Pour into ice cream maker and churn for 15 minutes, or freeze in a container for 3-4 hours, stirring occasionally. Alternatively, blend and serve immediately as a slush. Garnish with mint leaves.

name: Falsa Sharbat
instructions: Wash phalsa berries thoroughly. Blend berries with a little water to crush and extract juice. Strain through a fine sieve to remove seeds and pulp. In a large pot, combine strained juice with remaining chilled water. Add sugar and stir until dissolved. Add salt, black salt, and pepper powder. Mix well. Chill in refrigerator. Serve in tall glasses with ice cubes and a mint leaf garnish.

name: Tandoori Chicken Tikka
instructions: Make a marination paste with yogurt, chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, salt, and garam masala. Coat chicken pieces thoroughly in the marinade. Brush with mustard oil and lemon juice. Marinate for at least 30 minutes or preferably 2-4 hours in refrigerator. Grill on a tandoor, barbecue grill, hot oven at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, or on a hot skillet at high heat, turning occasionally until cooked through and edges are charred. Serve hot with lemon wedges and onion slices.

name: Kalakand
instructions: Pour full cream milk into a heavy-bottomed pan and heat to boiling. Add vinegar slowly while stirring, which will cause milk to separate into solids and whey. Remove from heat and strain through a muslin cloth. Squeeze out excess liquid and collect the milk solids (chenna). Grease a flat pan with ghee. Crumble the milk solids and cook in a pan with sugar over medium heat, stirring continuously until the mixture develops a grainy, moist texture (about 15-20 minutes). Add cardamom powder and mix well. Transfer to the greased pan while still warm and press down. Allow to cool completely, then cut into pieces. Garnish with chopped pistachios.

name: green juice
instructions: Blend the kale and spinach with ginger and lemon juice. Add diced cucumber and mint. Combine with passion fruit juice and coconut water. Chill and serve.

name: berry yogurt tart
instructions: Crush marie cookies and mix with melted butter. Press into a tart shell and set. Whisk hung curd with condensed milk, vanilla extract, and allspice powder until smooth. Pour filling into crust. Top with fresh strawberries and blueberries. Garnish with mint. Refrigerate and serve chilled.

name: dal tadka heeng jeera
instructions: Rinse and combine masoor, moong, and toor dals. Boil with water, salt, green chilly, ginger, and turmeric until dals are soft and cooked through. In a separate pan, heat desi ghee over medium heat. Add heeng and let it bloom, then add cumin seeds and dry red chilly. Pour this tadka over the cooked dal. Stir in fresh coriander and add a squeeze of lemon juice if desired. Serve hot.

name: crispy moong dal namkeen
ingredients: moong dal (without skin and split) 1 cup
instructions: Soak moong dal for 30 minutes to 1 hour. Drain and spread on a clean cloth to dry completely. Heat oil in a deep pan. Once oil is hot, add dried moong dal in batches and deep fry until golden and crispy, stirring occasionally to ensure even cooking. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Sprinkle salt to taste while still warm. Store in an airtight container.

name: tawa pizza
instructions: For dough: Mix all purpose flour, semolina, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar in a bowl. Add curd and oil. Add water gradually while kneading until soft dough forms. Keep aside. For sauce: Heat olive oil in a pan. Add chopped garlic and chilli flakes. Add chopped tomatoes, onions, salt, oregano, and pepper. Cook until tomatoes break down into a paste. To cook: Heat a tawa or flat pan over medium-high heat. Apply oil lightly. Take a portion of dough, flatten it into a pizza base, and place on the tawa. Cook the base until crispy on the bottom, then flip. Apply sauce and toppings on one side, cover, and cook until base is cooked through and edges are crispy.

name: Bhatti Ka Paneer Tikka Masala
instructions: Marinate paneer cubes in yogurt mixed with kala masala, ginger, and garlic for at least 30 minutes. Thread marinated paneer onto skewers and grill on charcoal or cook in oven, on grill, barbecue, or tawa until golden and charred on edges. Serve hot.

name: Cactus Subzi
instructions: Clean cactus by carefully removing thorns and cut into strips. Heat ghee and temper with asafoetida and dry red chillies. Add cumin and fennel seeds. Add garlic and cook briefly. Add onion chunks and sauté. Add cactus strips and mix well. Add salt, chilli powder, turmeric, and coriander powder. Mix in dry mango powder. Cook covered on medium heat until cactus is tender, stirring occasionally.

name: Veg Masala Pulao
instructions: Heat oil and add black cardamom, bay leaf, peppercorn, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Add sliced onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and chilli powder. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until oil separates. Add all vegetables (beans, carrot, potato, peas) and mix well. Add soaked basmati rice and stir to coat with spices. Add water and bring to boil. Cover and cook on high heat until rice is cooked. Sprinkle kasoori methi and garnish with fresh coriander.

name: Ginger Ale Squash
instructions: Mix ginger paste, turmeric, and water in a pot. Bring to boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Add sugar and stir until dissolved. Remove from heat and let cool completely. Add honey and lemon juice. Strain and store in refrigerator for up to a month. To serve: pour 2-3 tablespoons of squash in a glass, add ice cubes, top with cold water or soda water, and garnish with mint leaves.

name: Jeera Water
instructions: Boil water in a pot. Add cumin seeds and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the cumin infuses the water and it becomes slightly concentrated. Let it cool completely. Strain and store in a refrigerator. When serving, add sugar, salt, black salt and fresh lemon juice to taste. Can be consumed warm or cold throughout the day.

name: Bichu Buti ka Saag
instructions: Pluck stinging nettle leaves using tongs or gloves to avoid the needles. Boil the nettle leaves in water with salt for 5-7 minutes to remove the sting. Drain and squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop the boiled nettle or singe it over flame if preferred. Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds. Add chopped ginger and green chilli. Add the processed nettle leaves. Season with turmeric and chilli powder. Mix well and cook for 3-5 minutes. Serve hot with madua roti or steamed rice.

name: Salli Boti Zardaloo Phulka Tacos
instructions: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder, and coriander powder for 30 minutes. Heat oil in an oven-safe pan, sauté onions until golden. Add marinated chicken and cook on medium heat. Add dried apricots. Cover and cook in oven at 170°C for 15-17 minutes until chicken is cooked through. Meanwhile, julienne potatoes and deep fry until crispy golden (salli). Warm phulkas on tawa. Fill phulkas with salli boti zardaloo mixture, garnish with coriander and serve.

name: Roti Pizza
instructions: Heat tawa on medium heat. Lightly spread butter on a roti. Place roti butter-side down on tawa. Spread tomato sauce on top, followed by grated mozzarella cheese. Add your choice of toppings (onions, capsicum, corn, mushrooms, olives). Top with more cheese and sprinkle herbs. Cook on tawa for 3-4 minutes until cheese melts and the base becomes crispy. Carefully flip if needed to ensure cheese is fully melted. Serve hot.

name: instant aam panna
instructions: Blend raw and ripe mangoes with water and sugar. Add roasted cumin, pepper powder, black salt, and salt. Strain the mixture. Add mint leaves and ice cubes. Serve immediately.

name: chana sattu drink
instructions: Mix chana sattu with water and sugar until smooth. Add black salt, salt, and pepper powder. Squeeze lemon juice. Add coriander leaves. Stir well and add ice cubes. Serve immediately.

name: baked samosa
instructions: Make dough with refined flour, salt, baking powder, oil, and water. Rest for 30 minutes. For filling, heat oil and add ginger and green chilli. Mix in mashed potato and peas. Add spices (cumin, coriander, red chilli, dry mango, garam masala) and fresh coriander. Roll dough thin, cut into triangles, fill with potato mixture, and seal edges. Bake at 180°C until golden, or cook in pressure cooker on high heat.

name: kuttu atta tart
instructions: Mix buckwheat flour with ghee to form crumbly texture. Press onto a tawa base to form tart shell. Cook on medium heat until base is firm. Prepare filling by mashing bananas with roasted peanuts and peanut butter. Add caramel sauce. Fill the tart shell. Cover and cook until done. Serve warm.

name: Red Chutney
instructions: Soak byadgi chillies. Grind soaked chillies with grated coconut and salt to a smooth paste, adding water gradually. The chutney should be a smooth red paste. Serve as accompaniment to dosa, idli or vada.

name: Bhang Ki Chutney
instructions: Dry roast cumin and red chillies briefly. Grind hemp seeds, roasted cumin, red chillies, garlic, mint leaves and coriander leaves to a coarse paste. Add lemon juice and salt. Add a dash of water if needed to achieve desired consistency. Serve as a condiment with main meals or rolled in roti.

name: Chana Dal Namkeen
instructions: Soak chana dal for 2-3 hours. Add baking soda to water and bring to boil. Add soaked chana dal and cook until they start to split and become tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain and dry completely on a kitchen cloth. Heat oil in a pan and deep fry the dal until golden and crispy. Mix heeng, salt, black salt, amachur, mint leaves and chilli powder together. Toss the fried dal with the masala mix while still warm. Store in an airtight container.

name: Vrat Upma
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves and peanuts. Stir for a minute. Add the soaked and drained samak chawal and roast for 2-3 minutes. Pour in water and bring to boil. Add rock salt and cook until grains are tender and water is absorbed, about 15 minutes. Add boiled potato pieces, milk/water and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander and pepper powder. Serve hot.

name: Eggless Chocolate Mug Cake
instructions: In a large mug, mix flour, cocoa powder, coffee powder, sugar, baking powder, salt and vanilla extract. Add melted butter and milk. Mix well until all ingredients are properly combined. Fold in chocolate chips. Place the mug in a microwave and cook on high heat for 2.5-3 minutes. Remove carefully and serve warm, hot or cold. Can be topped with ice cream or whipped cream.

name: Fresh Mango Juice
instructions: Combine water with chopped raw mango and diced ripe mango in a pot. Bring to boil and simmer until mangoes are very tender, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Puree the cooked mango mixture until smooth. Strain if desired to remove any fiber. Add sugar and stir until dissolved. Cool completely. Pour into glasses, add ice cubes and top up with chilled water. Garnish with fresh mint leaves. Serve immediately.

name: Agra Parantha
instructions: Prepare soft dough with flour, salt and water. Knead well and let rest. Roll dough and stuff with generously filled mixture. Cook on a thick iron tawa (griddle) over medium-low heat. The thickness of the tawa provides slow radiating heat, creating a crispy exterior while maintaining softness inside. Flip and cook until golden brown on both sides.

name: Kharbooja Shake
instructions: Peel and de-seed the muskmelon. Cut into chunks. Blend muskmelon chunks with milk and sugar until smooth. Add ice cubes and blend again until the shake becomes chilled and frothy. Pour into glasses and serve immediately. Can be garnished with a melon slice on the rim.

name: Bhel Puri
instructions: Make dry green chutney: Grind coriander, mint, green chillies, ginger, roasted chana, black salt, jeera powder and black pepper until fine powder. Store in airtight jar. Make wet green chutney: Grind coriander, mint, curry leaves, raw mango, green chillies, ginger, roasted chana dal with salt and ice. Make red garlic chutney: Soak red chillies, grind with garlic, jeera powder, black salt and water into paste. Make sweet tamarind chutney: Soak tamarind and dates, strain pulps, add jaggery and spices, cook 30 minutes on medium heat until thin syrup. For sukha bhel: Roast puffed rice on medium-high heat, mix with roasted chana, masala chana dal, peanuts, papdi, potatoes, tomatoes, onions, raw mango, dry chutney, chaat masala, sev, coriander and lemon. For geeli bhel: Same base with wet and sweet chutneys mixed in. For sev puri: Layer papdi with potatoes, tomatoes, onions, raw mango, chutneys, sev and spice powder. Serve immediately.

name: Vegetable Biryani
instructions: Prepare marination: Mix diced vegetables with turmeric, chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste, curd, mint leaves and aromatic spices. Boil rice separately with cardamom, cinnamon, green chillies and salt until 70% cooked. In a heavy-bottomed pot, layer the marinated vegetables and par-cooked rice alternately. Sprinkle fried onions, saffron soaked in milk, and remaining mint leaves between layers. Top with rose water and kewra water. Seal the pot with dough to trap steam. Cook on high heat for 2-3 minutes until steam forms, then reduce to low heat and cook for 45 minutes using dum technique.

name: Besan Barfi
instructions: Prepare sugar syrup by dissolving sugar in water and bringing to a boil, then simmer to get one-string consistency. In a separate heavy-bottomed pan, heat ghee and add besan gradually, stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Roast besan in ghee on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until light golden and aromatic, stirring often. Add turmeric and cardamom powder while roasting. Pour the prepared sugar syrup into the besan mixture and stir well to combine. Continue cooking and stirring until the mixture thickens and starts leaving the sides of the pan. Spread on a greased tray and cool. Once set, cut into square pieces and garnish with chopped pistachios.

name: Khatti Meethi Aamras
instructions: Select ripe sweet mangoes and some raw mangoes to balance sweetness with tartness. Wash and deseed the mangoes, extracting the pulp. Blend the mango pulp together until smooth. Pass the blended mixture through a fine sieve or strainer to remove any fibers, ensuring a smooth consistency. If using very sweet mangoes, the drink may not need added sugar. Adjust sweetness by adding sugar if desired, stirring well. Add water if the mixture is too thick. Serve immediately or chill thoroughly. Serve cold, preferably with crushed ice.

name: Coastal Fish Curry
instructions: Combine fresh grated coconut, dry red chillies, peppercorns, shallots, garlic cloves and ginger in a food processor. Grind into a fine paste, adding water as needed. Heat coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add the coconut paste and cook on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant and the raw smell disappears. Add turmeric powder and mix well. Add pomfret slices carefully and coat with the coconut paste. Simmer for 8-10 minutes until the fish is partially cooked. Add diced raw mango and kokum for tartness. Add curry leaves and adjust salt. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the curry has thickened slightly. Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Semiyan
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan on medium heat. Add dry vermicelli and roast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and fragrant (about 3-4 minutes). Be careful not to burn it. Add water first to prevent oil splatter, then add milk gradually. Crush cardamom pods and add to the milk. Add sugar and stir well. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the vermicelli is cooked through and the milk is mostly absorbed (about 8-10 minutes). Add the chopped nuts and raisins, mix well. Cook for another 1-2 minutes. Serve warm as a dessert.

name: Mango Jam
instructions: Combine raw and ripe mango with sugar. Cook on medium heat for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally until mixture thickens and reaches jam consistency. Cool and store in bottles.

name: Matar Mushroom Masala
instructions: Heat oil, temper bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and cumin. Fry onions until golden. Add garlic and ginger. Add green chilli and spice powders. Cook tomatoes until soft. Add curd and simmer. In separate pan, cook mushrooms in oil and butter, add peas. Combine both and finish with kasoori methi and garam masala.

name: Malai Paneer Korma
instructions: Boil onions with ginger, garlic, and spices until soft. Grind to fine paste with cashewnuts. Combine paste with curd. Heat ghee, add this mixture, simmer. Add milk gradually. Add paneer cubes and cook until tender. Finish with rogan, pepper powder, and cardamom powder.

name: Rose Mojito
instructions: Mix rooh afza with lemon juice. Add salt, black salt, and pepper powder. Add soaked chia seeds and mint leaves. Add ice cubes. Top with chilled soda water. Stir well and serve immediately.

name: Watermelon Chutney
instructions: Heat oil, add dry red chilli, mustard seeds, fennel seeds, and cumin. When seeds crackle, add chopped ginger. Add kashmiri chilli powder. Add watermelon peel puree. Stir in salt, black salt, vinegar, and sugar. Cook on medium heat for 30-40 minutes until thick. Cool and store.

name: Masala Macaroni
instructions: Boil water with salt. Cook macaroni pasta until al dente. Drain well. In a pan, heat oil and butter. Add cumin, garlic, ginger, green chilli. Add onion and capsicum. Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder. Add tomato and cook until soft. Add tomato ketchup. Toss cooked pasta into sauce. Add kasoori methi powder and cilantro. Top with mozzarella cheese and mix well.

name: Cheese Stuffed Onion Pakora
instructions: Slice onions thinly and soak in water with turmeric and salt. Drain well. Cut cheese into cubes. Make a batter with besan, water, ginger, green chilli, chaat masala, chilli powder, ajwain, salt and coriander. Dip onion slices in batter. Take a spoonful of battered onion, place a cheese cube in the center, cover with more battered onion to form a ball. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on medium-high heat. Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

name: Pasta in White Sauce
instructions: Boil water in a large pot with salt. Add pasta and cook until al dente, then drain. In a separate pan, heat butter, add sliced garlic and cook for a minute. Add flour and stir to form a roux, cook for 1-2 minutes without browning. Slowly add milk while stirring to avoid lumps. Keep stirring until sauce thickens. Add grated cheese, salt, pepper powder, and italian seasoning. Mix well. Add cooked pasta to the sauce and toss gently. Garnish with fresh basil and serve hot.

name: Crispy Lotus Stem
instructions: Clean and peel the lotus stem. Slice thinly into round slices. Soak in water to prevent browning. Make a coating mixture with gram flour, corn starch, salt, black salt, turmeric, chilli powder, green chilly paste, ginger garlic paste, chaat masala and mint powder. Add minimal water to form a paste-like coating. Heat oil in a deep pan. Dredge lotus stem slices in the coating mixture. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on both sides. Drain on paper towel. Serve hot with chaat masala and tamarind chutney.

name: Strawberry Chocolate Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and line a cake pan. Cream together softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs one at a time, adding vanilla extract. In a separate bowl, sift together flour and baking powder. Gently fold dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined. Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth the top. Arrange strawberry halves on top of batter, pressing gently. Bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely. Optional: prepare chocolate ganache and frosting as per written recipe and layer accordingly.

name: Atta Pinni
instructions: Roast wheat flour in ghee over medium heat until light golden. Add sugar and mix well. Add black cardamom powder, cardamom powder, and gond (if using). Mix in all the chopped dry fruits, almonds, cashews, walnuts, and raisins. Mix everything together until well combined. Shape into small laddoos or patties. Serve with warm milk during winter.

name: Phirni
instructions: Soak basmati rice for 1 hour, then grind to a fine powder. Bring full fat milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Slowly add rice powder while stirring continuously to prevent lumps. Cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens. Add cardamom powder and desi ghee. For Plain Firni: continue cooking until desired consistency. For Mango Firni: add fresh mango puree and mix well. For Chocolate Firni: add dark chocolate chips and stir until melted and combined. Pour the firni into bowls or traditional moulds. Chill in refrigerator for 2-3 hours until set. Garnish with chopped nuts and fresh mint sprigs before serving.

name: Amritsari Chur Chur Naan
instructions: Make dough: Mix flour, salt, sugar, baking soda in a bowl. Add ghee, curd, and warm water gradually. Knead into soft dough and let rest 20 mins. Make filling: Mix mashed potato, grated paneer, onion, green chilli, coriander, cumin, coriander seeds, garam masala, red chilli, chilli flakes, anardana, and salt. Roll dough into circles, fill with stuffing, seal edges, flatten gently. Heat tawa with ghee on high heat. Cook naan until golden and crispy, flipping multiple times. The bread should be crumbly and crackly when done. Serve hot with pyaz chutney (onion chutney).

name: Cheese Potato Balls
instructions: Mix boiled mashed potatoes with grated cheese, onion, corn, bell peppers, green chilli, coriander, mint, ginger, salt, pepper. Form into balls with a cheese cube center in each ball. Make coating: Mix flour with water to form paste. Dip each ball in flour paste, then roll in bread crumbs to coat evenly. Deep fry in hot oil (350°F) until golden brown on all sides. Drain on paper towel. Serve hot with green chutney or sauce.

name: Sarson da Saag
instructions: Blanch mustard leaves, spinach, methi, bathua, radish leaves in boiling salted water for 5 minutes. Drain and grind to smooth paste. In heavy-bottomed pot, heat ghee. Add onion, sauté until golden brown. Add ginger, garlic, green chilli, cook for 2 mins. Add turmeric, salt, chilli powder. Add channa dal and water, bring to boil. Simmer for 15 mins. Add ground greens paste and makki atta dissolved in water. Cook for 20-25 mins, stirring occasionally. Finish with second tempering: heat ghee with chilli powder and pour over saag. Serve hot with makki di roti or bajra roti.

name: Chocolate Dalgona Coffee
instructions: In a bowl, take equal parts instant coffee powder, hot chocolate powder, and sugar (2 tbsp each). Add hot water (2 tbsp) and whisk vigorously for 3-4 minutes until the mixture becomes frothy, creamy, and resembles whipped cream. Pour cold or hot milk into a cup (1 cup). Gently pour the whipped coffee-chocolate mixture on top of the milk. Top with a sprinkle of cocoa powder or coffee powder and optional crumbled biscuits. Stir well before drinking.

name: Kathal Biryani
instructions: Prepare kathal: Boil kathal chunks until soft and shredded. Heat oil, sauté kathal with turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, ginger paste, garlic paste, salt. Add bhuna besan and mix well. For gravy (jhol): Heat oil, temper with shahi jeera, cardamom, cinnamon stick. Sauté sliced onion until golden brown. Add ginger paste, garlic paste, cook 2 mins. Add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder. Add yogurt and cook 3-4 mins. Add prepared kathal, salt, cardamom powder, mace powder. Simmer 10 mins. Prepare rice: Soak basmati rice 30 mins. Boil salted water with cardamom, cinnamon, green chilli. Cook rice until 70% done, drain. Layer in heavy pot: Rice, then kathal jhol. Sprinkle remaining cardamom, mint, fried onion. Add rose water, kewra water, saffron. Seal pot with dough. Cook on high heat 2 mins for steam formation, then low heat for 15-20 mins. Do not stir. Serve hot.

name: Veg Burger
instructions: Mix chopped beans, grated carrots, mashed potatoes, green peas with cumin, ginger, green chilli, and all spices. Add grated cheese and paneer. Form into patties and coat with breadcrumbs. Fry on oil until golden brown. Prepare chilli-mint mayo and spread on toasted buns along with mustard sauce. Layer with fried patty, tomato slices, onion slices, cheese slice, salad leaves, and pickled gherkin. Serve with french fries.

name: Makki Ki Roti
instructions: Mix maize flour with chopped radish leaves, optional grated radish, chopped green chilli, and salt. Slowly add water to form a dough that is slightly softer than regular roti dough. Divide into portions and knead well. Heat a tawa (griddle) and roast each portion on medium-high heat until brown spots appear on both sides. Apply desi ghee on the hot roti. Serve immediately while warm.

name: Mint Lemonade
instructions: Crush mint leaves lightly to release flavors. Squeeze juice from 2 lemons. In a pitcher, combine lemon juice, water, and sugar. Stir well to dissolve sugar.
