Add crushed mint leaves and ice cubes. Stir again and serve immediately. You can strain if preferred or serve with mint sprigs as garnish.

name: Tawa Masala Pulao
instructions: Heat oil in a tawa or flat griddle on high heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add sliced onions and fry until golden. Add diced vegetables (carrots, peas, capsicum) and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add green chilli and turmeric. Add the cold leftover rice, breaking any clumps, and spread on the tawa. Sprinkle garam masala and chilli powder. Toss continuously until the rice is heated through and lightly browned. Season with salt and garnish with coriander. Serve hot.

name: Tawa Pulao Mumbai Style
instructions: Heat oil on a tawa (flat griddle) over high heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add sliced onions and fry until golden brown. Add diced vegetables (carrots, peas, capsicum) and green chilli, cook for 2-3 minutes. Add turmeric powder and pav bhaji masala, mixing well. Add the cold leftover rice, breaking clumps with your spatula. Spread it on the tawa and cook, stirring continuously, until rice is heated through and edges get slightly browned (approximately 8-10 minutes). Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon juice. Garnish with chopped coriander. Serve hot as a street food style dish.

name: Kofta Kebab
instructions: Mix lamb with salt, chilly powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, nutmeg powder, minced ginger, and minced garlic. Stuff cheese cubes into portions of the mixture and form into long koftas. Heat oil in a pan and fry koftas until cooked through and golden. For the sauce: heat oil, add chopped onion, ginger, garlic, and green chilly, cook until soft. Add chilly powder, coriander powder, chopped tomato, tamarind pulp, jaggery, salt, and water. Simmer until sauce thickens. Submerge the cooked koftas in the tamarind sauce. Garnish with fresh coriander and mint leaves. Serve hot.

name: Rajgira ka Halwa
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add rajgeera atta and roast for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly until fragrant and light brown. Slowly add water while stirring to avoid lumps. Keep stirring as the flour cooks and absorbs the ghee and water. Cook until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan and becomes thick and creamy. Add sugar and mix well. Cook for another 1-2 minutes. Transfer to serving dishes and garnish with chopped nuts. Serve warm.

name: Samak Chawal ki Kheer
ingredients: dry fruits and nuts chopped handful
instructions: Rinse samak rice thoroughly under running water. Heat ghee in a pan and lightly roast the rice for 1-2 minutes, stirring frequently. Slowly add milk and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer gently until the rice is cooked and soft, about 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add condensed milk and sugar to taste, stir well. Cook for another 2-3 minutes. Add cardamom powder and mix. Transfer to serving bowls. Garnish with chopped dry fruits and nuts. Serve warm or chilled as preferred.

name: Honey Chilli Potato
instructions: Cut potatoes into thin fries. Coat with cornstarch and salt. Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the potatoes until crispy and golden. Drain on paper towels. In a separate pan, heat oil and add chopped ginger, garlic, onion, and capsicum. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add tomato ketchup, chilli sauce, soya sauce, and honey. Mix well and cook for 1 minute. Make a slurry with cornstarch and water, add to the sauce to thicken it. Cook for 1 minute more. Add the crispy fried potatoes to the sauce and toss quickly to coat evenly. Garnish with sesame seeds and serve immediately while the potatoes are still hot and crispy.

name: dal makhni
instructions: Soak and cook urad dal and rajma in water until soft. Make ginger-garlic paste and fry in butter. Add kashmiri chilli powder and tomato puree, cook until oil separates. Add cooked dal and cream. Temper oil with chopped garlic and pour over. Garnish with methi leaves and serve hot.

name: veg biryani kebab
instructions: Mash boiled potatoes with grated cheese. Mix with cooked biryani, add chopped green chilli and coriander. Form kebabs, coat with maida slurry and bread crumbs. Deep fry until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Serve hot.

name: kurkuri bhindi chaat
instructions: Dry okra and coat with besan, amchur, rice flour, chaat masala, corn starch and spices mixed with water. Deep fry until golden and crispy. Layer on a plate with curd, chutneys, onion, tomato, pomegranate and sev. Sprinkle chaat masala and serve immediately.

name: green coconut chutney
instructions: Grind coconut, mint, coriander, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves and roasted channa dal into a smooth paste. Heat oil and temper with urad dal, red chilli and mustard seeds. Add to the ground chutney and mix well. Serve with dosa, idli or as a condiment.

name: dhaba style laccha pyaz
instructions: Slice onions into thin rings and soak in ice-cold water for 10-15 minutes to make them crisp and mild. Drain well. Mix kashmiri chilli powder, salt, black salt, chaat masala, coriander powder and garam masala. Toss onions with the spice mix, add green chillies and coriander. Serve with lemon juice.

name: instant mango chunda
instructions: Grate raw mango and add to a pan with water. Cook until softened. Add sugar and cook until chutney reaches a thick consistency. Add salt, black salt, chilli powder and roasted cumin. Cook for a few more minutes until well combined. Cool and store in a jar.

name: spicy chicken wings
instructions: Toast coriander seeds, cumin, fennel seeds, peppercorn, dry red chilly and cinnamon. Grind to a paste with garlic and salt. Mix hung curd with the spice paste and lemon juice. Marinate chicken wings for 2 hours. Roast or grill until cooked through and caramelized. Garnish with mint and serve with lemon wedges.

name: malpua with rabri
instructions: Prepare sugar syrup by cooking water and sugar to single string consistency, add rose water and cardamom. Mix khoya, maida, semolina and cornflour, add water and saffron, whisk to smooth batter. Add fennel and cardamom powder. Heat oil and spread batter in pan, fry until floating then on high flame until cooked. Soak in sugar syrup. For rabri, reduce full fat milk, add sugar, rose water and fennel. Serve hot malpua topped with thick rabri.

name: watermelon peel sabzi
ingredients: watermelon rind peeled and diced 2 cups
instructions: Heat mustard oil and temper with mustard seeds, dry red chilli, cumin, and fennel seeds. Add ginger, garlic, and green chilli. Add chopped onion and cook until soft. Add turmeric, chilli powder, and coriander powder. Add watermelon rind pieces and cook until tender. Add dry methi leaves, amchur powder, and season with salt. Cook until well-combined and serve hot with coriander leaves garnish.

name: boondi ladoo
instructions: Mix besan with turmeric, yellow and orange colour and water to make a smooth batter. Heat oil for frying. Drop besan batter using a boondi maker to create small round droplets in hot oil, fry until golden. In a separate pan, make sugar syrup with sugar and water. Add cardamom powder and back cardamom to the syrup. Dip fried boondi in syrup and coat well. Add melon seeds and mix. Shape into round balls (ladoos) and let cool.

name: cream of cauliflower soup
instructions: Heat butter in a pan and temper with kalonji seeds and bay leaf. Add chopped garlic and onion, cook until golden. Add cauliflower florets and water, cook until soft. In a separate pan, make a roux with flour and butter. Add this to the cauliflower mixture along with milk and cheese. Simmer until desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Blend if a smoother texture is preferred. Serve hot.

name: dal ke kebab
instructions: Boil soaked dals with turmeric and salt until cooked. Drain and dry. Heat ghee and temper with asafoetida, cumin, green chilli, and ginger. Add cooked dals and spices. Mix with mashed potato and breadcrumbs. Cool mixture. Make filling with hung curd, onion, mint leaves, and salt. Shape dal mixture into patties with filling inside. Coat with breadcrumbs and deep fry until golden brown. Serve hot with chutney.

name: chicken sausage pulao
instructions: Heat ghee and add bay leaf, cumin, cloves, and cinnamon stick. Add chopped onion and cook until golden. Add ginger garlic paste and green chilli. Add sliced chicken sausage and cook until lightly browned. Add washed rice and mix well. Add salt and water. Cover and cook on high heat until steam forms. Reduce heat and cook until rice is tender and water is absorbed. Fluff with fork. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: lucknowi chicken biryani
instructions: Fry onions until golden. Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger paste, garlic paste, and spices. Layer rice and chicken alternately in heavy-bottomed pot. Seal with dough and cook on high heat until steam forms, then low heat for 45 minutes. Let rest before serving.

name: veg chowmein or hakka noodles
instructions: Boil noodles and set aside. Heat oil in wok, add ginger and garlic. Stir-fry onion until translucent. Add cabbage, carrot and peppers. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Add noodles, soya sauce and green chilly sauce. Toss well for 1-2 minutes and serve hot.

name: paneer kathi kebab
instructions: Prepare dough with maida, atta, salt, oil and water. Let rest. Make filling: temper oil with cumin and coriander seeds, sauté ginger, garlic, green chilli. Add spices, tomato puree. Cook onions and capsicums until soft. Add paneer, kasoori methi and coriander. Roll dough thin, fill with paneer mixture, cheese and salad leaves. Fold into roll. Make paneer tikkis from leftover mixture and fry. Serve rolls with salad and tikkis.

name: masala cucumber lemonade
instructions: Peel and dice cucumber. Squeeze lemon juice. In a blender, combine cucumber, lemon juice, mint leaves, sugar, salt and black salt. Blend until smooth. Strain into glasses. Add coriander powder, roasted cumin powder and chaat masala. Top with ice cubes and chilled soda water. Stir well and serve immediately.

name: banana chia smoothie
instructions: Soak chia seeds beforehand. Peel and chop bananas and strawberries. In a blender, combine soaked chia seeds, coconut milk, bananas, strawberries, and honey. Blend until smooth. Pour into serving glasses and top with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Garnish with crushed assorted nuts. Serve immediately.

name: afghani egg curry
instructions: For paste: Heat oil and ghee in kadai. Add sliced onions, ginger, garlic, green chillies; saute for 2-3 minutes until translucent. Add green cardamom, black peppercorns, tender coriander stems; cook for 1 minute. Add mint leaves, coriander leaves, coriander powder, turmeric powder, beaten curd, and salt to taste. Transfer to mixer grinder and blend into smooth paste. For curry: In handi, heat ghee; add bay leaf, black peppercorns, cinnamon stick and let splutter. Add prepared paste and cook until thick and well-combined. Add water and bring to quick boil. For eggs: Heat oil in separate pan. Add sliced garlic and boiled eggs (halved if desired). Add dry fenugreek leaves, degi red chilli powder, diced tomato; saute for 2-3 minutes. Add crushed black peppercorns. Transfer curry to serving dish. Gently place sauteed eggs on top. Garnish with fresh coriander sprig. Serve hot with roti or rice.

name: Paneer Angara
instructions: Heat oil, temper with cloves and peppercorns. Add ginger-chili paste, sauté 2-3 minutes. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until soft. Add almonds and curd, cook 5-6 minutes on high. Add water, cover and cook 8-10 minutes on medium. Blend gravy smooth. Add fried paneer cubes, cook 2-3 minutes. Smoke with hot coal and green cardamom in ghee for 4-5 minutes. Serve hot with roti.

name: Mango Custard Trifle
instructions: Boil milk, add sugar and cornstarch slurry, whisk well on low heat. Add saffron color. Cool and blend with mango, refrigerate 1-2 hours. Make pancake batter, cook pancakes on nonstick pan with ghee, sprinkle sugar and caramelize. Dice pancakes. Layer in glass: mango, pancake, sugar, biscuit crumbs, custard. Garnish with whipped cream, pomegranate, mango, biscuits, mint. Serve chilled.

name: Shahi Matar Pulao
instructions: Make besan kofte: mix gram flour, chili, curd, ginger-garlic, paneer, spices; fry until golden. Fry paneer cubes. In handi, temper ghee and oil with whole spices. Add peas, sauté. Add curd and more ghee. Layer rice, fried paneer, onions, saffron. Add more rice, chili, warm water, peas, kofta. Cover with foil, dum cook on low 10-15 minutes. Finish with ghee, herbs, serve with matar raita.

name: Double Dal Tadka
instructions: Wash dals. In pressure cooker, heat ghee, add cumin, dals, ginger, chili, spices, water. Cover and cook 3-4 whistles on medium-high. Add water and salt. Prepare jeera rice: heat oil, add cumin, chili, herbs, cooked rice, butter, toss well. For tadka: heat oil and ghee, add bedgi chili and asafoetida, sauté well, add ginger, chili, degi powder. Pour tadka over dal. Serve hot with jeera rice.

name: Dahi Wala Chicken
instructions: Prepare ginger-garlic paste. Marinate chicken with chili, coriander stem, mint, ginger-garlic paste, salt, oil, lemon juice, coriander. Dry roast peppercorns, cloves, black cardamom, fenugreek for masala. In kadai, heat oil and ghee, add bay leaf, cloves, black cardamom, cumin. Sauté onion until translucent. Add marinated chicken and ginger-garlic paste, cook until tender. Add curd and cashew paste, simmer until thickens. Garnish with prepared masala, mint, coriander. Serve hot with roti.

name: Veg Schezwan Fried Rice
instructions: Make instant schezwan sauce: cook dry chillies, chili flakes, sugar, salt, oil, garlic, ginger, water in pressure cooker 2-3 whistles. Simmer 4-5 minutes on low. In wok, heat oil, sauté finely chopped ginger and garlic 2-4 minutes. Add carrot, baby corn, mushroom, coriander stem, cabbage, stir-fry 1 minute on high. Add schezwan sauce, mix well. Add cooked rice, soy sauce, red chili sauce, spring onion, toss on high heat. Garnish with spring onion and coriander. Serve hot.

name: Lasaniya Batata
ingredients: degi red chili powder 1.5 tsp + 2 tbsp
instructions: Marinate boiled diced potatoes with degi chili powder and salt. Make garlic chutney: grind garlic, chili powder, salt, ginger coarsely. In handi, heat oil, add cumin, cloves, black cardamom, green cardamom, bay leaf, let splutter. Add onion, sauté until translucent. Add garlic chutney, cook 5-6 minutes on medium. Add tomato puree, coriander powder, cook until thickens. Add water, boil. Add marinated potatoes, cook 2-3 minutes on low. Serve hot with roti. For raita: mix boiled potato, tomato, chili, carrot, coriander, curd, salt, sugar.

name: Mixed Vegetable Soup
instructions: For the soup base: In a sauce pot, add butter and oil. Heat, add bay leaf, ginger, onion, and sauté until golden. Add coriander stems, carrots, cauliflower, cabbage, mushrooms and sauté 1 minute. Add water, cover and boil 20-30 minutes on medium heat. Add peas, noodles, ginger, coriander leaves, peppercorns, and cornstarch slurry. Simmer 5-6 minutes until cooked. For chili oil: Add oil and sesame oil to a small pan, once slightly hot add garlic, cloves, star anise, chili flakes, sesame seeds, and chili powder. Cook on low heat 15-20 minutes until aromatic. For dough: Knead whole wheat flour with salt and water to a semi-soft dough. Let rest 10-15 minutes. Flatten lemon-sized portions and cut into desired shapes. To serve: Add spinach and soup ladleful to bowl, drizzle chili oil, garnish with lemon wedge and coriander. Serve hot.

name: Lahori Paneer
instructions: For paneer marination: Mix paneer cubes with salt and degi chili powder. Set aside. For masala: Dry roast cumin, coriander seeds, peppercorns, cloves, black cardamom, and salt. Grind smoothly in mixer and set aside. Fry paneer: Heat oil in pan, add marinated paneer and fry until golden. Set aside. For lahori paneer: Heat oil and ghee in handi, add cloves and black cardamom. Add onions and sauté. Mix in coriander powder, chili powder, ginger-garlic paste, and curd. Cook 2-3 minutes on high flame. Add tomato puree and cook on medium flame. Add prepared masala, sauté 1 minute, and transfer excess oil to bowl. Add coriander stems and water, bring to boil. Add fried paneer and fenugreek leaves, mix well. Transfer to serving dish, garnish with cream, green chillies, and coriander. Serve hot with roti.

name: Bhindi Butter Masala
instructions: For ginger-garlic paste: Grind green chillies, garlic, and ginger together coarsely. For sautéing bhindi: Heat mustard oil until smoky, add cumin seeds and let splutter. Add onions, bhindi, salt, turmeric, and chili powder. Cook 5-6 minutes on low heat until golden. Add diced tomatoes and mix. Set aside. For bhindi butter masala: Heat oil and butter in kadai, add ginger-garlic paste and sauté 1 minute. Add onions and bay leaf, sauté until golden. Add turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder and cook 1 minute. Add curd, mix well, add tomato puree and salt. Sauté until cooked. Add butter and tender coriander stems, cook well. Add water and cream, simmer 3-4 minutes until thick. Add sautéed bhindi, coriander leaves, mix well. Finish with butter and fenugreek leaves. Transfer to serving dish, garnish with coriander, butter, and ginger juliennes. Serve hot with roti.

name: Railway Mutton Curry
instructions: For mutton marination: Mix mutton with salt, ginger-garlic paste, mustard oil, and crushed peppercorns. Marinate 10-15 minutes. For potato marination: Mix diced potatoes with salt and turmeric powder. For frying potatoes: Heat mustard oil in pressure cooker, add marinated potatoes and fry until half cooked. Set aside. For masala: Dry roast black cardamom, peppercorns, fennel, coriander seeds, cinnamon, green cardamom, and stone flower. Grind smoothly and set aside. For curry: Heat oil in pressure cooker, add black and green cardamom, bay leaf. Add onions and salt, sauté until translucent. Add marinated mutton and cook until half done. Add coriander powder, turmeric, and tomato puree. Cook 6-7 minutes on high heat. Add water, salt, and tamarind paste. Bring to boil, cover and cook 6-7 whistles on medium-high heat. Add coriander stems, fried potatoes, and prepared masala. Simmer until thick. Transfer to serving dish, garnish with coriander. Serve hot with bread.

name: Lehsuni Palak Paneer
instructions: For blanching spinach: Bring water to boil with salt and baking soda. Add spinach, green garlic, and green chili. Boil 1 minute, transfer to ice water to cool. Squeeze excess water, grind spinach mixture smoothly in mixer. Set aside. For masala: Dry roast coriander seeds, peppercorns, cumin, and salt. Grind coarsely in mortar-pestle. Set aside. For shallow frying paneer: Heat oil in pan, add paneer cubes and fry until golden brown on both sides. Set aside. Soak fried paneer in water 10-15 minutes. For tadka: Heat oil in small pan, add dry red chili and garlic. Sauté well. Set aside. For lehsuni palak paneer: Heat oil in kadai, add dry red chillies, cumin seeds. Let splutter. Add sliced garlic, sauté 1 minute until golden. Add spinach paste, ghee, salt, and pinch of sugar. Sauté well. Add water and coriander stems, cook 2-3 minutes on medium heat. Adjust consistency with water, add salt and masala. Add fried paneer and diced tomato, simmer. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with cream, tadka, and coriander. Serve hot with roti or naan.

name: Kashmiri Paneer Masala
instructions: For cooking paneer: Simmer paneer with water, turmeric, salt, and degi chili powder 7-8 minutes on medium heat until cooked. Set aside. For masala: Heat mustard oil, add tomato puree, kashmiri chili powder, salt, and sugar. Cook 4-5 minutes until cooked well. Add ginger powder, fennel powder, and fried onions paste. Cook 2-3 minutes on medium heat. Set aside. For frying paneer: Heat mustard oil in pan, add cooked paneer and fry on both sides until golden brown. Set aside. For yakhni: Simmer water with fried onions, chili powder, ghee, asafoetida, bay leaf, cinnamon, and black cardamom. Add fried paneer and cook 5-6 minutes. Add prepared masala and cook well. Finish with coriander leaves and mix. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with coriander sprig. Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Lucknowi Chicken Masala
instructions: For marination: Mix chicken with salt, oil, chili powder, and lemon juice. Set aside. For curd mixture: Mix curd with coriander powder, turmeric, and chili powder. Set aside. For dry masala: Dry roast peppercorns, cardamom, mace, green cardamom, and salt 2-4 minutes. Grind, add roasted gram flour and mix. Set aside. For boiling cashews: Boil water with salt, add cashews and boil. Strain and grind to smooth paste. Set aside. For tadka: Heat oil and ghee, add green chili and onion. Sauté until translucent. Add chili powder, masala, kewra water, rose water, and fenugreek leaves. Sauté well. Set aside. For chicken masala: In handi, heat ghee and oil. Add green chili and onions, sauté until translucent. Add bay leaf, cinnamon, black and green cardamom. Sauté well. Add salt and water, cover and cook 8-10 minutes on medium heat. Blend onions with hand blender. Add water, ginger-garlic paste and sauté. Add curd mixture and salt, cook 5-6 minutes. Add coriander stems, marinated chicken, and water. Simmer. Add water and cashew paste, bring to boil. Add tadka and shredded chicken, mix well. Transfer to bowl, garnish with green chili and coriander. Serve hot with roti or naan.

name: Aloo Ki Katli
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a kadai. Add cloves, black peppercorns, fenugreek seeds, cardamom, red chillies, and cumin seeds; let them splutter. Add ginger and potatoes with salt; saute until half cooked. Add onions, degi red chili powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder; cook for 2-3 minutes. Add tomato puree, cover and simmer until potatoes are fully cooked. Finish with ghee and tender coriander stems. Transfer to serving dish and garnish with fresh coriander. Serve hot with roti.

name: Chicken Double Masala
instructions: For marination: Mix tender coriander stems, ginger, green chillies, curd, salt, oil, coriander powder, and turmeric powder with chicken. Set aside to marinate. For onion-tomato masala: Heat ghee and mustard oil in kadai. Add black peppercorns, cinnamon, bay leaves and let splutter. Add onions and saute until golden. Add degi red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and tomatoes. Cook well on medium flame. For chicken: In handi, heat ghee and add marinated chicken; saute 2-4 minutes. Add water and cook. Add fresh coriander leaves and mint. Add prepared onion-tomato masala and mix. Cover and cook 5-6 minutes until cooked well. Finish with dry fenugreek leaves and garam masala. Garnish with coriander sprig and lemon wedges. Serve hot with roti.

name: Methi Kadai Paneer
instructions: For paneer: Simmer milk for 10-15 minutes. Add vinegar and ghee, stir until curdles. Rest and strain through muslin cloth. Rinse paneer and shape into block with weight. Cut into cubes when set. For ginger-garlic paste: Grind ginger, garlic, and salt in mortar pestle. For gravy: Heat ghee and oil, add ginger-garlic paste and saute 1 minute. Add onions and capsicum, saute until translucent. Add degi red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and tomatoes. Cook 10-15 minutes. Blend into smooth paste with hand blender, add water and boil. For fenugreek leaves: Soak in salted water for 10-12 minutes. For masala: Dry roast fennel seeds, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, coriander seeds, and chilli flakes. Grind coarsely. For whey juice: Crush tulsi leaves and black peppercorns. Mix with jaggery, whey, and salt. Serve hot. For kadai: Heat oil and ghee, add soaked methi and saute 2-3 minutes. Add onion and prepared gravy. Mix in tomato ketchup. Add paneer cubes, tomatoes, and capsicum; cook 5-6 minutes. Finish with coriander leaves, green chillies, ginger, and masala. Garnish and serve hot.

name: UP Style Aloo Matar
instructions: For paste: Grind ginger, garlic, tender coriander stems, green chillies, salt, small mustard seeds, and cumin seeds coarsely. For aloo matar: Heat mustard oil in kadai. Add bay leaf, onion seeds, fennel seeds, and cumin seeds; let splutter. Add prepared ginger-garlic paste and saute 1 minute. Add onion and saute until golden. Add degi red chili powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder; cook 1 minute. Add tomatoes and potatoes. Cook until half cooked. Add water, cover and cook 10-12 minutes on medium flame. Mash one potato piece. Add more water, salt, ghee, and coriander leaves. Simmer until thick. For achaar: Heat mustard oil in pan. Turn off flame and add asafoetida, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, mustard seeds, onion seeds, and fenugreek seeds. Transfer to bowl. Add garlic, ginger, green chillies, salt, sugar, dry mango powder, and lemon juice. Set aside 30-40 minutes for flavors to develop. Serve aloo matar hot with achaar and roti.

name: Mango Shrikhand with Poori
instructions: For mango pulp: In pan, cook mangoes with sugar and water for 5-6 minutes on medium flame until cooked well. Grind smoothly with hand blender. Cook 2-3 minutes on low to medium flame until thickens. Transfer to bowl and refrigerate for 30-35 minutes. For mango shrikhand: Whisk hung curd until smooth. Add prepared mango pulp and mix well. Transfer to serving bowl. Garnish with cardamom powder, mango cubes, pistachios, almonds, and fresh mint sprig. Serve chilled. For dough: Mix wheat flour, salt, semolina, powdered sugar, and ghee. Add chilled water and knead into semi-soft dough. Cover with muslin cloth. Take lemon-size ball and roll. Heat oil in kadai. Fry puri until golden. Transfer to absorbent paper. Serve hot poori with prepared mango shrikhand.

name: Chicken Kabsa Pulao
ingredients: 1 heaped tbsp degi red chili powder
instructions: For chicken marination: Place chicken in tray with salt and marinate. For masala: Dry roast black peppercorns, green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, mace, and black cardamom for 1 minute. Add saffron strands and grind into fine powder. For pulao: Heat ghee and oil in handi. Add cinnamon stick, bay leaf, and black peppercorns; let splutter. Add onions and saute 3-4 minutes until golden. Add salt, turmeric powder, degi red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder; saute 1 minute. Add tomato puree with salt and cook well. Add marinated chicken and mix well. Cover and cook until half cooked. Add water and simmer. Remove cooked chicken to tray. Add raisins, sella basmati rice, carrots, and prepared masala. Cover and cook until rice is cooked well. Finish with remaining chicken oil and tender coriander stems. For second marination of chicken: Mix oil, ginger-garlic paste, curd, degi red chili powder, prepared masala, and half-cooked chicken with salt. Marinate. Heat oil in pan and sear marinated chicken until golden brown. Serve pulao garnished with almond slivers and mint sprig. Serve with seared chicken on the side.

name: Easy Egg Pulao
instructions: For cooking rice: Bring water to boil. Add salt, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and sella basmati rice. Get quick boil. Cover and cook 7-8 minutes on high flame. Strain and transfer to tray for resting. For egg masala: Heat ghee and oil in handi. Add bay leaf, cinnamon stick, black cardamom, green cardamom, and mace; let splutter. Add onions, green chillies, and ginger; saute 2-3 minutes until golden. Add turmeric powder, degi red chili powder, and coriander powder; cook 1 minute. Add curd and cook well. Add hard boiled eggs, salt, tender coriander stems, and saffron water. Cook well. Transfer half of the masala to bowl for later use. For egg mixture: Mix grated boiled eggs, green chillies, coriander leaves, mint leaves, salt, and degi red chilli powder. For assembling: In same handi, layer cooked rice evenly. Add ghee and spread prepared egg mixture. Layer cooked rice and spread remaining prepared egg masala evenly. Cover and cook 10-12 minutes on low flame. For raita: Mix curd, green chilli, ginger, tomato, saffron water, and salt. Garnish egg pulao with green chilli and coriander sprig. Serve hot with prepared raita. Garnish raita with roasted cumin powder, degi red chili powder, and coriander sprig.

name: dal chawal
instructions: For dal: Heat ghee and oil, add onion seeds, fennel, fenugreek, cumin, mustard seeds, and ginger-green chili paste, saute 1 minute. Add toor and moong dal and saute well. Add asafoetida, red chili powder, turmeric, salt, and 2.5 cups water. Cover and cook 20-25 minutes on medium flame. Add raw mango and jaggery, cook 2-3 minutes more. For rice: Boil 3 cups water with salt and green cardamom. Add 2 cups washed rice and cook 10-15 minutes covered on low-medium flame. Serve dal and rice together, garnished with fried red chillies, lemon, and coriander.

name: mango kulfi and falooda
instructions: For falooda sev: Mix water and cornstarch, cook 2-3 minutes until translucent on medium-low flame. Pipe into iced water using a mold and refrigerate. For kulfi: Blend 5 mangoes with condensed milk and rabdi. Pour into kulfi molds and freeze 6-7 hours. For assembly: On serving dish, arrange mango slice, almonds, kulfi, falooda sev, rose syrup, basil seeds, condensed milk and pistachios. For falooda: In glass add rose syrup, falooda sev, mango cubes, basil seeds, chilled milk, almonds, kulfi, and tutti frutti. Garnish with almonds, mint and mango.

name: bhopali chicken rezala
instructions: For boiling: Boil water with salt, sugar, and onions 7-8 minutes. Grind boiled onions into smooth paste. For marination: Mix chicken with salt, oil, green chillies, ginger-garlic paste and turmeric, marinate 10-15 minutes. For rezala: Heat ghee and oil, add cumin, cardamom, bay leaf, cinnamon and splutter. Add marinated chicken and saute. Add boiled onion paste and cook well. Add green chillies, coriander powder, turmeric, red chili powder and saute 1 minute. Add curd, simmer 1 minute, cover and cook 5-6 minutes. Add water, fresh coriander, black cardamom-peppercorn powder, simmer. Finish with fried onions-cashew paste. Serve hot with roti, garnished with coriander and boiled egg.

name: Punjabi Mutton Masala
instructions: First prepare fresh homemade garam masala: Set a pan on low heat and add cloves, black cardamom, coriander seeds, cinnamon, cumin seeds, black peppercorns, and fennel seeds. Roast until fragrant. Remove to a plate to cool. Transfer roasted spices with a pinch of salt to a mortar and pestle and grind to a fine powder. For mutton: Add 2 tbsp salt to mutton and mix to coat every piece well. Marinate for a minimum of 1 hour. Heat oil and ghee together in a deep heavy-bottomed vessel on medium heat. Add sliced onions and cook on medium-low heat, stirring at short intervals, until golden brown (about 30-35 minutes). Do not rush this step. While onions brown, make a paste of garlic, ginger, and green chillies. Once onions are browned, add the ginger-garlic-chilli paste and lower flame. Cook for 7-8 minutes. Lower heat, add turmeric powder and cook for 1-2 minutes. Add coriander powder, degi mirch powder, kashmiri red chilli powder, and jeera powder. Stir well and add 500 ml hot water to prevent spices from burning. Cook on low heat until ghee/oil separates. Increase flame to medium-high, add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook until tomatoes are mushy, stirring frequently. Once completely disintegrated, add another 500 ml hot water and cook until ghee/oil separates. Add salt-marinated mutton pieces, mix, and cook on medium-low heat, stirring at short intervals to prevent sticking. Cook until mutton releases its water and ghee/oil separates. Reduce flame to low and keep it low throughout. Once ghee/oil separates from masala, add 1-1.5 liters hot water and 1-2 tbsp ghee, mix well and bring to boil. Cover and continue cooking on low heat until mutton is tender (45-50 minutes or longer depending on quality), stirring frequently. Check tenderness by cutting a piece - it should cut easily. Add slit green chillies, ginger juliennes, and freshly prepared garam masala. Mix gently and cook 10-12 minutes uncovered. Add kasuri methi and lemon juice, stir and cook for 2-3 minutes. Check seasoning and adjust. Finish with freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot with chapati, naan, pav, or rice.

name: laal mirch gosht
instructions: In handi, heat mustard oil, add cinnamon and bay leaf and splutter. Add mutton and onions, cook until golden. Add salt, soaked red chillies, and ghee, saute on medium flame. Add coriander seeds and curd with salt, cook 10-12 minutes until cooked well. Add water and mix, cover with lid and cook 30-40 minutes on medium flame. Finish with tender coriander stems. Place small steel bowl in handi, add charred coal, dry red chili, pour ghee and smoke 2-3 minutes. Transfer mutton to serving bowl and garnish with coriander sprig. Serve hot with roti.

name: Eggless Christmas Cake
instructions: Caramelize jaggery with water and butter until dark golden. Mix caramelized mixture with desiccated coconut, peppercorns, tutti frutti, raisins, and orange rind. Add flour, milkmaid, and cashew nuts to make smooth batter. Fold in tutti frutti and raisins with baking soda. Transfer to greased tray and bake at 170°c for 35-40 minutes. Demold and garnish with tutti frutti, icing sugar, candied cherries, and mint.

name: Nagori Dal Tadka
instructions: Soak akkha masoor and toor dal for 5-10 minutes, then pressure cook with water and salt until 2-3 whistles. In a separate handi, heat oil and ghee, add dried chillies, asafoetida, ginger, garlic, onions and sauté until translucent. Add green chillies, coriander stems and sauté for a minute. Add turmeric, degi chili powder, tomatoes, and soaked fenugreek leaves. Add water and cooked dal, simmer for 15-20 minutes. Finish with jaggery and salt. Add fried chillies and garnish with coriander.

name: Hyderabadi Dum Aloo
instructions: Fry potatoes and onions in oil and ghee until golden and half-cooked. Separately prepare masala by roasting sesame seeds, cashewnuts, peppercorns, and spices, then grind to powder. Mix fried potatoes with prepared masala, curd, tamarind paste, chili powder, ginger, green chillies, and coriander leaves. Transfer to handi, add water, cover and cook on low to medium flame for 15-20 minutes. Finish with prepared tadka of fried red chillies in oil.

name: Cooker Chicken Curry
instructions: Marinate chicken with curd, degi red chili powder, turmeric, coriander, garam masala, cumin, salt, lemon juice, oil, and fried onions for 30-40 minutes. In pressure cooker, heat mustard oil and oil, add black cardamom, green cardamom, bay leaf, cinnamon stick and let splutter. Add garlic, onions and sauté until golden. Add turmeric, degi chili, coriander powder, ginger, coriander stems and sauté for a minute. Add tomato, cover and cook for 2-3 whistles. Mash tomato and cook further. Add marinated chicken, water, salt, ghee, masala, and coriander. Cook for 4-5 whistles until chicken is well-cooked.

name: Banarasi Chutney Wala Paneer
instructions: Prepare chutney by sautéing onions, ginger in oil and ghee until translucent, then grind with coriander, mint, cashew nuts, green chillies, and tomato to smooth paste. Fry paneer cubes in oil and ghee until golden, soak in water for 15-20 minutes. Mix curd with degi chili, turmeric, and coriander powder. In a handi, add oil, temper with asafoetida, cloves, peppercorns, cardamom, fennel, cumin, fenugreek seeds, and red chilli. Add curd mixture and cook for 4-5 minutes. Add prepared chutney, salt, sugar, and cook. Add mango powder and fresh cream. Finish with roasted nuts and paneer. Garnish with pomegranate pearls and coriander.

name: Chicken Tikka Lazeez
instructions: Marinate chicken breast with curd, ginger garlic paste, salt, turmeric, and degi chili powder for 10-15 minutes. Prepare onion paste by boiling onions, green chillies, garlic, cashews with ghee and sugar, then grinding. Sauté marinated chicken in oil for 3-4 minutes on both sides until tender. In handi, heat oil and ghee, add bay leaf, green and black cardamom, let splutter. Add onion paste and ginger garlic paste, sauté. Add coriander powder, turmeric, degi chili, ghee and mix well. Add curd and crushed peppercorns. Add tomato puree, green chilli, coriander stems, cover and cook 5-6 minutes. Add water, adjust consistency, add sautéed chicken, sugar, and cook 7-8 minutes. Finish with fenugreek leaves and butter.

name: Pepper Chicken Fry
instructions: Prepare ginger garlic paste by grinding ginger, garlic, green chillies with salt in mortar pestle to coarse paste. Marinate chicken with crushed black peppercorns, curry leaves, ginger garlic paste, and oil. In handi, heat oil, add curry leaves and onions with salt, cook until translucent. Add marinated chicken and cook for 7-8 minutes on medium flame. Add curd and prepared masala, cook together for a while. Once chicken is well-cooked, add black pepper powder and mix well. Serve hot with garnish of coriander and lemon wedge.

name: Amritsari Mutton Curry
ingredients: degi red chili powder 2 heaped tbsp
instructions: In handi, heat oil and mustard oil, add cinnamon stick, bay leaf, cloves, and sliced onions, sauté for a minute. Add mutton with bones and sauté until onions are cooked well. Add coriander powder, degi chili powder, turmeric, and coriander powder, cook for a while. Add curd and cook for 5-6 minutes on medium flame. Add water to adjust consistency, cover with lid and cook for 30-40 minutes on medium flame. Finish with prepared masala and salt, cook for 5-6 minutes more. Prepare masala by roasting peppercorns, cloves, cardamom, mace, cumin, cardamom, fennel, coriander seeds and carom seeds, then grinding smooth. Transfer to serving dish, garnish with ginger, green chillies, and coriander leaves with stems.

name: Mustard Fish Curry
instructions: Boil mustard seeds in water with salt. Grind onion, green chillies, garlic, ginger, boiled mustard seeds, red chili powder, turmeric and coriander powder with mustard oil into a paste. Marinate fish with salt and turmeric for 10-12 minutes. Fry marinated fish and potatoes in mustard oil until golden. In a kadai, heat mustard oil, splutter fenugreek and fennel seeds, add curry paste and cook. Add coriander stems, fried potatoes and water, simmer for 2-3 minutes. Add tomato, sugar, green chillies, coriander leaves, fried fish and boiled eggs, boil briefly. Finish with lemon juice and serve hot with rice.

name: Afghani Chicken Biryani
instructions: Marinate chicken with salt, ginger garlic paste, green chillies, oil, curd, coriander and mint leaves for 15-20 minutes. Prepare jhol by heating ghee, adding saffron, cream, cardamom, salt, sugar, then mix in green chillies, fried onion, mint, coriander. Dry roast masala spices and grind. Boil rice in water with salt, ghee, bay leaf and cinnamon for 4-5 minutes, then drain. In a handi, heat oil and ghee, add green chillies and onions, add marinated chicken and cook covered 8-10 minutes. Layer with apricot, fried onion, mint, first batch rice, jhol, masala, then second batch rice, jhol, saffron and masala. Seal edges with dough and cook on low flame 15-20 minutes. Rest a few minutes and serve garnished with coriander and mint.

name: Assam Fish Curry (Masor Tenga)
instructions: Coat fish with salt and turmeric, marinate 5-10 minutes. Heat mustard oil, fry marinated fish for 2-3 minutes each side and transfer to plate. In same pan, fry potatoes until golden and half cooked, transfer to plate. In kadai, heat mustard oil, splutter fenugreek, mustard and onion seeds with dry red chillies. Add green chillies and tomatoes, cook 5-6 minutes until mushy. Add turmeric and red chili powder, add fried potatoes and cook until tender. Add water and bring to boil. Add coriander leaves and fried fish, cook 5-6 minutes on low flame. Finish with lemon juice and mix gently. Transfer to serving bowl and garnish with coriander sprig. Serve hot with rice.

name: Maharaja Mutton Curry
instructions: Fry cashew nuts in hot oil and ghee until golden, grind to paste. In handi add remaining oil and ghee, saute onions until golden brown. Add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf, mutton and salt, saute until half cooked. Add chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and jaggery, mix well. Add curd and saffron, simmer. Add water to adjust consistency, cover and cook 30-40 minutes on medium flame. Add peppercorns, saffron, cardamom powder and cashew paste, bring to boil. Smoke with coal and cloves for 7-8 minutes. Finish with coriander leaves and lemon juice. Serve hot with roti.

name: Peshawari Chicken Karahi
instructions: Prepare kadhai masala by grinding black peppercorns, cumin seeds, coriander seeds and black cardamom coarsely. Heat oil in handi, add sugar and chicken with salt, cook on high flame until golden. Add tomatoes and saute until mushy, remove skins. Add green chillies, cook 7-8 minutes until done. In separate pan, heat oil and fry ginger briefly, add onions and saute 1 minute. Add capsicum, tomato, prepared kadhai masala, salt and sugar, saute on high flame. Transfer sauteed veggies to the chicken. Garnish with ginger, green chili and coriander. Serve hot with roti.

name: Kurkuri Dahi Bhindi
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling salted water 1 minute, cool in ice water, grind to puree. Make garlic-green chili paste in mortar pestle. Heat ghee in sauce pot, add paste, saute well. Add dill, gram flour and salt, cook well, add spinach puree, saute. Add water and simmer on low flame, season with peppercorns, sugar, salt and ghee. For bhindi: Mix gram flour, rice flour, salt, chili powder and asafoetida. Coat lady fingers, let sit 5-6 minutes. Fry in hot oil until crispy. For tadka: Heat oil, add dry chillies, asafoetida, curry leaves, mustard and cumin seeds, splutter 30 seconds. Mix curd with salt, sugar, peppercorns and tadka. Assemble: Layer spinach puree, add fried bhindi, top with curd mixture. Garnish with pomegranate, fried chillies, curry leaves, lemon and coriander. Serve hot.

name: Kashmiri Chicken Rogan Josh
ingredients: degi red chili powder 3 heaped tbsp
instructions: Grind garlic, onions, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves into coarse paste. Mix paste with coriander powder, chili powder, fennel powder, ginger powder, salt and mustard oil to make ver masala. Marinate chicken with chili powder, salt, caraway seeds, curd and mustard oil. Melt butter in handi, add ver masala and mustard oil, saute 1 minute until aromatic. Add marinated chicken, saute 2-3 minutes. Add tender coriander stems, curd and butter, mix well. Cover and cook 10-12 minutes until cooked through. Garnish with coriander leaves. Serve hot with roti.

name: Ginger Chicken Curry
instructions: Marinate chicken with salt, ginger slices, green chilli, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste and oil for 10-15 minutes. Heat ghee and oil in handi, add mace and cardamom. Add onions and saute until golden. Add chopped ginger, salt, coriander powder, chili powder and turmeric, cook 1 minute. Add curd and saute well. Add marinated chicken and cook 15-20 minutes on medium flame until done. Finish with honey, ginger, fresh mint, peppercorns and ghee, mix well. Transfer to serving dish and garnish with ginger and coriander leaves. Serve hot with tandoori roti or naan.

name: dal moradabadi ki chaat
instructions: In pressure cooker add water, moong dal, salt, asafoetida, turmeric, butter and cook for 3-4 whistles. Mash well. Dry roast cumin, peppercorns, black cardamom for 2-3 minutes and grind. Heat oil and ghee, add dry red chillies and asafoetida, toss for a minute, add red chilli powder. In kadai add water, butter and dal, simmer until thick. Transfer to bowl, add butter, lemon juice, prepared tadka, chaat masala, green chillies, onions, prepared masala, papdi and crushed papdi. Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

name: bihari chicken curry
instructions: Marinate chicken with turmeric, salt, red chilli powder and mustard oil. Make ginger garlic paste. Heat mustard oil in handi, add marinated chicken and cook 7-8 minutes until golden, set aside. In same handi, add mustard oil, heat, add dry red chillies, bay leaf, cinnamon, black cardamom, cloves, let splutter. Add onions and saute 2-3 minutes until translucent. Add salt and whole garlic, saute 1 minute. Cover and cook 5-6 minutes. Add ginger garlic paste, mix well. Add turmeric, red chilli powder, cumin and coriander powders. Add water, cooked chicken, coriander stems and simmer covered for 10-15 minutes. Add prepared garam masala. Garnish with coriander and serve hot with roti or rice.

name: egg chowmein
instructions: Boil water with salt and oil, add noodles and cook 7-8 minutes until 70-80% cooked. Strain and cool on tray. Mix ginger, coriander stems, schezwan sauce, green chili sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, red chili sauce and oil in bowl for sauce. In bowl beat eggs with salt and water. Heat nonstick pan, pour egg mixture and cook 2-3 minutes on both sides, roll and cut into strips. In wok add oil, when smoky hot add onions, carrots, toss 1 minute. Add cabbage, salt, french beans, peppers and toss on high flame. Add prepared sauce and noodles, mix gently. Finish with more sauce and spring onion bulbs. Combine with egg omelet strips. Serve hot with spring onion garnish.

name: dal nizami
instructions: Wash green moong dal, chana dal and toor dal. Soak 10-15 minutes. In pressure cooker add water, ghee, salt, turmeric, dals. Cook until 3-4 whistles. Mash 20% of dal with ladle. In mixer grinder add onions, green chillies, coriander leaves, salt, oil, ginger and grind smoothly. In handi add oil, when hot add paste and saute 5-6 minutes until golden. Add asafoetida, coriander powder, turmeric, curd and saute. Add red chilli powder, cumin powder, fried onions and dal. Cook 4-5 minutes. Finish with fried onions, ginger, coriander leaves and prepared tadka. For tadka: heat oil and ghee, add red chillies and cumin seeds, splutter. Garnish and serve hot with roti or naan.

name: sabudana tikki chaat
instructions: Mix potatoes, sabudana, green chillies, ginger, coriander leaves, prepared masala, salted boondi, dal moth and red chilli powder. Sprinkle dal moth in greased tray, add mixture and flatten. Refrigerate 20-30 minutes. Demold and cut into shapes. Fry until half cooked then refry until crispy. For masala: dry roast coriander, cumin, peppercorns and salt 2-3 minutes. Grind coarsely. For chutney: saute green chillies, ginger, roasted peanuts, curry leaves. Add mint, coriander leaves, green chilli and curd. Grind to paste. For seasoned chutney: mix curd, salt, sugar with prepared chutney. For assembly: add green chutney in dish, place fried tikki, add pomegranate, sev, tamarind chutney, dal moth, sweetened curd and coriander. Serve hot.

name: punjabi chole
instructions: Cook chickpeas in pressure cooker with ginger, kashmiri chilli, bay leaf, cinnamon, salt, water, turmeric and red chilli powder. Mash 20% of cooked chickpeas. For masala: dry roast coriander seeds, black cardamom, peppercorns, cumin, cloves, mace, green cardamom, carom seeds, asafoetida and bedgi chilli 2-3 minutes. Add pomegranate seeds, fenugreek leaves and salt. Toss 1 minute and grind to fine powder. Heat oil and ghee in kadai, add cumin seeds and let splutter. Add garlic, ginger, onions and saute until golden. Add green chillies, coriander stems and prepared masala. Cook briefly. Add turmeric, red chilli powder and curd, cook well. Add cooked chickpeas and water. Cover and cook 10-15 minutes on medium flame. Finish with coriander leaves and tomato. Serve hot with puri or roti. Garnish with coriander.

name: Egg Tikka Masala
instructions: For egg mixture: Mix eggs, salt, red chili powder, turmeric, oil. For cooking: Heat oil in pan, pour egg mixture, cover with lid, cook on low 15-20 minutes. Flip and cook another 10-15 minutes on low flame. Cool. For tikka masala: Heat oil and ghee in handi, add bay leaf and cardamom, add chopped onions, saute until translucent. Add ginger garlic paste, cook until golden. Add turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, saute 1 minute. Add water and tomato puree, salt, cook well. Adjust consistency with water, add salt, sugar, fresh cream, stir. Add coriander stems and cooked eggs. For marination: Mix mustard oil, salt, ginger garlic paste, turmeric, red chili powder, lemon juice, hung curd with egg frittata cubes, capsicum, tomato. Marinate well. For frying: Heat oil in pan, fry marinated eggs and vegetables until golden brown on both sides. Add to curry, simmer with butter and kasuri methi. Serve hot garnished with cream, kasuri methi, and coriander.

name: Tari Wala Chicken
ingredients: chicken drumstick and thigh with bones - 900 gms
instructions: For marination: Mix chicken with turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, salt, kasuri methi, yogurt. Let marinate 10-15 minutes. For curry: Heat oil in handi, add cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, ginger, green chillies, garlic, saute 1 minute. Add chopped onions, cook 5-6 minutes until golden. Add coriander stems and tomato, saute well. Add coriander powder and red chili powder, mix well. Add marinated chicken, cook until pieces are seared. Add water, cover with lid, cook on medium flame 15-20 minutes. For masala: Dry roast black peppercorns, coriander seeds, cloves, green and black cardamom on medium heat 2-3 minutes until fragrant, grind to fine powder. Finish curry with prepared masala powder and coriander leaves, give quick boil. Transfer to serving dish, garnish with coriander and julienned ginger. Serve hot with rice.

name: Soya Chaap Makhani
instructions: For grilling soya chaap: Wash and remove sticks from soya chaap. Deep fry in hot oil on medium-high heat until crisp and golden. Cut diagonally into 3-4 pieces. Mix mustard oil with red chili powder to extract color, add other powdered spices, besan, ginger garlic paste, hung curd, coriander, salt, lemon juice. Coat fried soya chaap in marinate. Smoke with live charcoal and ghee for 3-4 minutes. Grill on open flame or pan until golden brown, brush with butter. For makhani gravy: Heat oil and butter, add cumin and green cardamom, saute 1 minute. Add sliced onions, saute 3-4 minutes on medium-high until caramelized. Add whole red chillies, tomatoes, salt, stir 1-2 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, cashew nuts, powdered spices, mix and cook 8-10 minutes. Add water, cover and cook 10-12 minutes. Cool and grind to fine puree. For final dish: Heat oil and butter, add julienned ginger, chopped garlic, green chillies, onions, cook 3-4 minutes. Lower flame, add red chili powder briefly 30 seconds. Add makhani gravy, cook 5-6 minutes. Add sugar and hot water, cook 7-8 minutes, add grilled soya chaap, cook 2-3 minutes. Lower flame, add cream, cook 2-3 minutes more. Add salt, garam masala, kasuri methi, coriander, lemon juice. Serve hot with naan or roti.

name: Veg Spring Roll
instructions: For vegetable filling: Heat oil in wok, add garlic, ginger, spring onion bulbs, stir and cook on high heat 1-2 minutes. Add remaining vegetables, stir and cook on high heat 1-2 minutes. Sprinkle cornflour and mix well, finish with spring onion greens, mix and switch off flame. Cool filling completely. For spring roll sheets: Mix maida, cornflour, salt. Add water in batches to make smooth, lump-free batter. Whisk well to proper consistency where coated spoon flows. Rest batter 12-15 minutes. Heat non-stick pan moderately hot. Pour ladle of batter, immediately swirl pan to spread thin sheet evenly (do not use spoon). Cook 30-40 seconds on medium flame. Use spatula to remove sheet efficiently. Place cooked sheets on plate dusted with cornflour, dust cornflour between sheets to prevent sticking, cover with moist cloth until use. For spring roll assembly: Mix maida and water to make slurry. Take sheet, add sufficient filling, fold both ends inwards to seal, roll tightly to keep filling intact. Apply slurry on edges and seal. Deep fry on medium heat until crisp and golden brown. Cut into pieces and serve hot with ketchup or dip of choice.

name: Desi Masala Anda
instructions: Heat ghee in pan on medium heat. Add jeera, onions, green chillies and ginger garlic paste. Saute until onions turn translucent. Add chopped tomatoes, salt and powdered spices. Cook well until tomatoes are mushy. Add water to prevent burning, cook for 2-3 minutes. Lower heat and add fresh cream, mix and cook for a minute. Make cavities in the masala with spatula and break eggs directly into pan. Sprinkle salt and pepper over eggs. Cover and cook on low flame until egg whites are set and yolks remain slightly runny. Finish with fresh coriander. Serve hot with bread.

name: Palak Paneer Naanza
instructions: For palak naan: Mix maida, salt, sugar and baking soda. Add dahi and spinach puree, gradually add water to form soft dough. Knead for 10-12 minutes until smooth, cover with damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. Divide into dough balls, flatten and stretch into naan shape. Spread garlic butter on naan, place on baking pan. Half-cook on grill + convection at 200C for 7 minutes. For pizza sauce: Heat oil, add garlic, ginger, green chillies and coriander stems. Cook 1-2 minutes. Add onions, cook until golden. Lower heat, add spices, then tomato puree and salt. Simmer covered for 10-12 minutes, finish with coriander. Dice paneer, toss with chaat masala and lemon juice. Assemble: Spread sauce on half-cooked naan, add cheese, toppings and paneer. Cook on convection + grill at 200C for 7 minutes. Cut into slices, drizzle garlic dip and garnish with spring onions.

name: Paneer Makhani Biryani Cups
instructions: Wash basmati rice thoroughly until starch is removed, soak for 15-20 minutes. Boil water with salt, spices, lemon and ghee. Add rice and herbs, cook until 3/4 done, drain excess water. For makhani base: Combine tomatoes, onions, garlic, ginger, chillies, cashews and spices in microwave-safe bowl. Microwave 10 minutes at 100% power. Cool to room temperature, transfer to blender and grind to fine puree. Mix puree with curd, cream, kasuri methi, garam masala, fried onions, mint and coriander. Dice paneer and add gently. Add live charcoal with ghee to a bowl and cover to impart smoky flavor. Assemble: Fill microwave-safe mug halfway with paneer makhani, add fried onions and herbs. Fill with cooked rice, top with coriander, mint, fried onions and saffron milk. Can wrap in cling film and refrigerate. Reheat in microwave for 2 minutes before serving with raita.

name: Vegetables in Red Sauce with Butter Garlic Herbed Rice
instructions: For herbed rice: Heat oil and butter in wok on medium-high heat. Add garlic and green chillies, cook 1 minute. Add fresh coriander, herbs and chilli flakes. Quickly stir on medium-high and add cooked rice, salt and pepper. Toss for 2-3 minutes on high flame. Set aside. For red sauce: Wash and quarter tomatoes, transfer to blender and blend to puree. Heat oil in saucepan on low heat, add sliced garlic and cook until light brown. Add onions and cook on medium until translucent. Lower heat and add red chilli powder and coriander stems, cook 15-30 seconds. Add tomato puree, salt, pepper, ketchup, sugar, oregano and chilli flakes. Stir and cook 2-3 minutes on medium-high, then cover and cook 8-10 minutes on medium. For stir-fried veggies: Heat oil in wok on medium heat with garlic and chilli flakes, cook 1-2 minutes. Add baby corn and carrot, cook 2-3 minutes. Add remaining veggies, salt, pepper and lemon juice. Cook 1-2 minutes. Combine stir-fried veggies with red sauce and cook 1-2 minutes more. Serve hot with herbed rice.

name: Chilli Paneer Sizzler
instructions: For fried rice: Heat oil in pan on high heat with onions and veggies. Stir and cook 1-2 minutes. Add rice, salt, pepper, sugar, vinegar, soy sauce and spring onions. Stir and cook 2-3 minutes, do not stir vigorously to avoid breaking grains. For hakka noodles: Heat oil in wok on high, add sliced onions and garlic. Stir and cook 1-2 minutes. Add julienned veggies and cook 1-2 minutes. Add noodles, spring onions, salt, pepper, sugar, vinegar and soy sauce. Mix well and cook 2-3 minutes on high. For grilled paneer: Cut paneer into 1cm thick squares. Marinate with salt and pepper. Heat oil in grill pan on medium, grill paneer from both sides until marks appear. For chilli sauce: Heat oil in wok on medium with onion bulbs, garlic, ginger and green chillies. Cook 1 minute. Add thickly sliced onions and capsicum, cook 1 minute. Add vegetable stock, sauces, chilli paste, sugar, salt, pepper, coriander and spring onions. Bring to boil. Mix cornstarch with water to make slurry, add to stock and cook until thickened. For assembly: Heat sizzler plate until smoking hot. Spread cabbage leaves on plate. Arrange fried rice, hakka noodles, stir-fried veggies, charred onions, french fries and grilled paneer. Pour hot chilli sauce and add cold butter for sizzling sound. Serve immediately.

name: vegetable wonton clear soup
ingredients: spring onion greens 1/4 cup finely chopped
instructions: For wonton wrappers: Mix refined flour and salt, add water gradually and combine. Cover with damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. Knead dough by stretching until smooth. Rest another 30-60 minutes. Knead again and divide into 4 equal parts. Coat with cornstarch and flatten. Roll very thin sheets with rolling pin, dusting cornstarch frequently. Check thinness by placing hands beneath sheet. Cut sheets into 10cm x 10cm squares. Dust cornstarch on wrappers. For paneer filling: Mix crumbled paneer, carrots, french beans, cabbage, ginger, spring onion greens, soy sauce, salt and white pepper in bowl. For wontons: Place small spoonful of paneer filling in center of wrapper, apply water on edges, fold diagonally into triangle, apply water on ends and bring together, seal. Sprinkle flour to avoid sticking. For soup: Add vegetable stock to pot with sliced ginger and crushed garlic, add spring onion greens, green chillies, soy sauce, sugar and vinegar. Bring to boil and simmer for 15-20 minutes. Strain stock into another pot. Bring to boil, remove scum. Add broccoli, mushroom and carrots 4-5 minutes before serving. In separate pot, boil wontons for 5-6 minutes. Place cooked wontons in serving bowl and add boiled soup with vegetables. Garnish with spring onion greens. Serve hot with soy chilli on side.

name: mumbai veg grill sandwich
instructions: For special sandwich masala: Dry roast jeera, cloves, peppercorns and fennel seeds on medium heat until fragrant. Cool and transfer to grinding jar. Add amchur powder, anadana powder, ginger powder, hing, black salt and salt. Grind into fine powder. For special spicy green chutney: Wash coriander leaves and transfer to grinding jar. Add blanched spinach, green chillies, garlic, curry leaves, sandwich masala 1/2 tsp, salt and roasted chana dal. Grind into fine paste. Chutney should be thick enough to apply on bread. For special garlic red chutney: Soak kashmiri red chillies and spicy red chillies. Add garlic, jeera powder, black salt, salt, lemon juice and water to grinding jar and grind to fine paste. Adjust consistency with water to avoid sogginess. For sandwich assembly: Finely chop onions and capsicum, thinly slice tomatoes. Apply butter on one side of bread slice, then green chutney. Grate medium boiled potato over bread, sprinkle sandwich masala and chopped onions. Take another bread slice, apply butter on both sides. Apply green chutney on one side and red chutney on other. Place green chutney side facing onion side. Place tomato slices over red garlic chutney side and sprinkle sandwich masala. Add chopped capsicum and more sandwich masala. Grate processed cheese over it. Apply butter and green chutney on another bread slice and close sandwich. Heat grill pan until hot, apply butter on sandwich and grill both sides until grill marks appear and golden brown. Serve hot with ketchup, chutney and potato chips.

name: schezwan chicken frankie
instructions: For half-cooked frankie roti: Mix refined flour, salt and curd in bowl. Transfer to platform and knead well for 10-15 minutes with stretching. Oil the dough surface and cover with damp cloth. Rest 30 minutes. Divide into equal dough balls, coat with flour, flatten and roll into thick chapati using rolling pin. Heat tawa on medium high, add little oil and cook roti briefly on both sides for 20-30 seconds each. Do not burn. Stack cooked rotis and keep covered in cloth or insulated casserole. For homemade frankie masala: Mix kashmiri red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, black salt, anadana powder, aamchur powder, cumin powder, garam masala, black pepper and salt in mixing jar. Store in airtight container. For schezwan chicken filling: Slice chicken thinly and cut into thin strips. Mix salt, pepper, soy sauce, vinegar, egg white and cornstarch with chicken strips. Heat oil on medium heat and deep fry marinated chicken strips until light golden brown. For red chilli paste: Soak kashmiri red chillies in hot water for 10-15 minutes. Cool and grind to fine thick paste with little water. For sauce: Heat wok on high, add oil and chilli paste, cook until oil separates. Add chopped garlic, ginger, green chillies, green chilli paste, coriander stems and spring onion bulbs. Stir and cook 1-2 minutes. Add tomato ketchup, red chilli sauce, vinegar and soy sauce. Stir and cook 1-2 minutes. Add chicken stock, salt, pepper and sugar. Add spring onion greens, onions, capsicum and fresh coriander. Cook 1-2 minutes. Add fried chicken and mix to coat with sauce. Make cornflour slurry with water and add to wok. Cook until sauce thickens. Finish with spring onion greens. For assembly: Break egg in bowl, add salt and whisk. Heat tawa on high, add blob of butter and cook half-cooked roti on both sides until golden brown spots appear. Pour whisked egg over roti, flip and cook until egg is cooked and stuck to roti. Sprinkle frankie masala, add sufficient schezwan chicken filling, onions, fried noodles and more frankie masala. Roll and serve immediately.

name: schezwan paneer paratha
ingredients: gehun ka atta wheat flour 2 cups
instructions: For half roti/paratha: Mix wheat flour and salt in bowl. Add water in batches to knead semi-soft dough. Knead well for 7-8 minutes. Oil dough surface, cover with damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. Divide into equal dough balls, flatten, coat with flour and roll into thin chapati using rolling pin. Cook chapati from both sides until almost cooked with brown spots appearing. Make all chapatis. For schezwan paneer filling: Heat wok on high heat. Add oil, spring onion bulbs, garlic, ginger, coriander stems and green chillies. Stir and cook on high flame 1-2 minutes. Add schezwan sauce, red chilli sauce, ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper, salt and sugar. Stir and cook 1-2 minutes. Add capsicum, onions, spring onion bulbs, paneer and spring onion greens. Stir gently and cook 1-2 minutes on high flame. Make cornstarch slurry with water in separate bowl. Add slurry to wok and cook until sauce thickens. Finish with freshly chopped spring onion greens. For tom mayo: Mix mayonnaise, ketchup and red chilli sauce in mixing bowl and refrigerate. For schezwan paneer paratha: Place half-cooked roti and add sufficient schezwan paneer filling. Grate processed cheese as preferred. Sprinkle frankie masala. Place another cooked roti over it to sandwich. Set grill pan on medium heat, add oil and spread evenly. Place paratha on hot pan and grill both sides until grill marks appear or golden brown. Be careful while flipping. Schezwan paneer paratha is ready. Cut into slices and serve hot with tom mayo.

name: crispy threaded paneer
instructions: For threaded paneer: Cut paneer into 3 by 2 inch strips or cuboid shape. Mix red chilli sauce, soy sauce, ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder, salt and pepper. Sprinkle water if marinade too thick. Coat paneer strips with marinade. Roll spring roll sheets and cut thinly with sharp knife to make flat noodles. Wrap these noodles around marinade coated paneer. Alternatively use boiled noodles coated with refined flour and cornstarch. Deep fry noodle wrapped paneer in hot oil on medium high from both sides until crisp and golden brown. For sweet chilli garlic dipping sauce: Heat pan on medium high, add oil, chopped garlic and chopped green chillies. Sauté briefly for about a minute. Add ketchup, red chilli sauce, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper. Stir and cook 1-2 minutes on medium high flame. Add water and simmer until sauce bubbles. Make cornflour slurry with water in small bowl and mix well. Add slurry to sauce while stirring continuously. Cook 1-2 minutes on medium high flame until sauce thickens. Serve threaded paneer hot and crispy with sweet chilli garlic dipping sauce.

name: soya kheema pav
instructions: Set water for boiling in stock pot. Add pinch of salt and soya granules. Cook soya for 1-2 minutes and strain. Pass through tap cold water and squeeze out excess moisture. Heat wok on medium high, add ghee and oil with whole spices. Sauté spices for a minute until aromatic. Add chopped onions and cook until golden brown. Add ginger garlic paste and green chillies. Sauté for a minute. Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook until oil separates. Add powdered spices and mix well. Add hot water to avoid masalas from burning. Cook until oil separates. Keep adding hot water as required to adjust consistency and make slight gravy. Add cooked soya granules and mix well with masala. Cook for 25-30 minutes on medium low heat. The longer you cook, the better and more intense the flavour. Make sure ghee separates from kheema indicating it is cooked. If not, cook longer. Add kasuri methi, garam masala, slit green chillies and julienned ginger. Mix well and cook one more minute. Finish with freshly chopped coriander leaves and check for seasoning. Serve hot with toasted pav.

name: khao swe burmese veg noodle soup
instructions: For fresh coconut milk: Roughly chop fresh coconut and transfer to grinding jar with water. Grind as fine as possible. Use sieve and muslin cloth to transfer coconut paste. Squeeze well to extract coconut milk. Reuse pulp in grinding jar with additional water and repeat process to extract maximum coconut milk. Yields approximately 800ml coconut milk. For soup: Add onions, garlic, ginger, green chillies and coriander stems to grinding jar with little water. Grind into fine paste. Set wok on medium high heat, add oil and onion ground paste. Stir and cook 2-3 minutes. Lower flame and add powdered spices. Add little water and cook spices until it releases oil. Add veggies and stir well. Add vegetable stock/hot water, jaggery and salt. Stir and bring to boil. Cook 5-6 minutes on medium flame. Lower flame. In separate bowl, add besan and few tablespoons of coconut milk. Mix well to make lump-free besan slurry. Add slurry to coconut milk and stir well ensuring no lumps. Add slurry-mixed coconut milk to wok and stir well. Increase flame to medium heat and simmer soup 5-6 minutes. Stir regularly. Taste for salt and adjust seasoning. Finish by adding lemon juice. For assembly: Place boiled noodles in bowl. Pour hot soup over noodles. Top with roasted crushed peanuts, fresh onion slices, fried noodles, fried onions, fried garlic, freshly chopped coriander and spring onion greens. Add chilli oil and lemon wedge on side. Serve hot and tweak addition of components as per preference.

name: aloo tikki burger
instructions: Make creamy tangy mayo by mixing mayonnaise, ketchup and red chilli sauce. For aloo tikki: sauté ginger, green chillies and peas in butter and oil for 1-2 minutes. Add powdered spices, sauté briefly, add grated boiled potatoes and salt, cook for 2-3 minutes. Transfer to bowl, add softened poha, fresh coriander and lemon juice, cool to room temperature. Shape mixture into sausage on plastic wrap using freezer for 2-3 hours. Slice into 1cm discs. Make slurry with refined flour, cornstarch, salt and water. Coat tikkis with flour, dip in slurry, coat with seasoned bread crumbs. Deep fry until golden brown on medium-high heat. For assembly: toast burger buns with butter, spread mayo on top bun, place tikki on bottom bun, add cheese, tomato and onion slices, close with top bun. Serve with french fries.

name: pithala bhakri
instructions: For pithala: Make kharda/thecha by crushing green chillies, garlic and salt in mortar-pestle. Mix besan, salt, turmeric and 2 tbsp kharda with water for smooth mixture. Heat wok with oil, add mustard seeds and cumin, sauté briefly. Add curry leaves, onions, asafoetida and slit green chillies, cook until onions turn translucent. Add besan mixture and 500ml water, stir continuously to avoid lumps, cook until semi-thick consistency. Cover and cook on low flame for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add fresh coriander leaves and check seasoning. For bhakri: Mix jowar flour with salt and warm water to make soft, moist dough. Divide into small balls, sprinkle dry flour, flatten and shape traditionally with hands or rolling pin. Cook on hot tawa, sprinkle water, flip when dry. Cook on open flame until brown spots appear. Pour ghee over hot bhakri. Serve hot pithala with bhakri, onions, green chillies, kharda and yogurt.

name: pineapple sheera
instructions: Core pineapple slices using cookie cutter or bottle lid. Coat with salt, sugar and lemon juice. Grill on medium-high heat on both sides until grill marks appear and pineapple caramelizes, roughly chop while keeping chunky. Toast cashews and chopped nuts in 2 tbsp ghee on low heat until light golden, set aside. In same pan, add 1-2 tbsp ghee and semolina, roast on medium-low flame until aromatic and light golden, remove to plate. In another wok, bring water, saffron and cardamom powder to boil with caramelized pineapple chunks. Add roasted semolina in stream while stirring continuously to avoid lumps, cook for 4-5 minutes on medium-high flame. Add 3/4 cup sugar, stir until dissolved. Add 1/4 cup ghee in batches, stir and cook until sheera leaves pan and ghee separates. Fold in roasted nuts and mix well. Serve hot, garnish with chopped or slivered nuts.

name: kolkata style egg roll
instructions: Mix maida, sugar, salt and ghee lightly. Add warm water gradually and knead on platform, pulling and stretching well for 4-5 minutes until soft and stretchy. Tuck inwards, shape smooth surface, apply oil, cover and rest for 30 minutes. Divide dough into equal balls. For parotta: Flatten dough ball, roll into thin chapati, brush oil/ghee and sprinkle dry flour. Make slit from centre, roll sideways in circular motion to form cone, press into thick disc, coat with dry flour and roll into thick paratha. Alternatively: fold chapati while making pleats, roll and tuck to seal, oil, cover and rest 10 minutes, press and roll. Set tawa on medium-high heat with oil. Place parotta, break 2 eggs into bowl with salt, whisk well and pour over paratha. Flip and cook until egg is cooked and parotta is golden brown. For salad: Mix sliced onions, julienned cucumber and lemon juice, rest for 15-20 minutes. For assembly: Place egg parotta, top with salad, add chopped green chillies, black pepper, chaat masala, red chilli sauce and ketchup. Roll and serve hot.

name: paneer makhani naanza
ingredients: sabut kashmiri lal mirch (red chillies) 4-5 nos.
instructions: For makhani sauce: Heat wok with oil and butter, add jeera and cardamom, sauté for 1 minute. Add sliced onions, sauté for 3-4 minutes until caramelized. Add red chillies, tomatoes and salt, stir for 1-2 minutes. Add garlic cloves, ginger, cashew nuts and powdered spices, cook for 8-10 minutes. Add water, cover and cook for 10-12 minutes. Cool to room temperature, grind to fine puree, strain and keep aside. For paneer tikka: Mix mustard oil with red chilli powder to extract color. Add remaining powdered spices, coriander, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste and hung curd. Add diced onions, capsicum and paneer cubes, marinate gently. Place live charcoal on marinade and pour ghee over it, cover for 3-4 minutes to smoke. Skewer paneer, onions and capsicum, char on open flame. Apply melted butter, cook again briefly, remove from skewer, cut into bite-size pieces. For naan: Mix flour, salt, sugar, baking soda, dahi and water to sticky dough. Knead with oil for 10-12 minutes until smooth and not sticky. Cover with damp cloth for 30 minutes. Shape into dough balls, flatten and stretch with rolling pin into thick naan. Apply water on back of naan and stick to hot iron tava water-side down. Cook until bubbles appear (half minute), invert tava and cook over direct flame from different angles. Remove when cooked. For assembly: Spread makhani sauce on naan base, top with paneer tikka pieces, mozzarella cheese, diced onions, capsicum and bell peppers. Serve immediately.

name: pasta in creamy peri peri sauce
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water with oil for 7-8 minutes until al dente. Drain excess water, cool to avoid overcooking, drizzle oil and sprinkle salt & pepper, toss well. For stir-fried veggies: Heat 1 tbsp oil in pan on high flame, add chopped garlic, sauté for 1-2 minutes. Add blanched broccoli, mushroom quarters, bell pepper triangles, corn kernels, salt, pepper, oregano and red chilli flakes. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, squeeze fresh lemon and sauté again, keep aside. For peri peri spice mix: Mix red chilli powder, black salt, cinnamon powder, garlic powder, ginger powder, oregano, powdered sugar and salt in bowl. For pasta sauce: Heat butter in pan on medium heat and melt. Add refined flour, stir and cook on low flame for 2-3 minutes until light golden. Slowly add milk in batches while whisking continuously to avoid lumps. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Add salt, pepper, and 2 tbsp peri peri spice mix, cook for 1-2 minutes. Add stir-fried veggies, boiled pasta and processed cheese, stir and cook for 2-3 minutes until cheese blends well. Add tomato ketchup, adjust consistency with milk if too thick. Serve hot immediately with toasted garlic bread.

name: Kaala Mutton
instructions: Wash mutton thoroughly. Make hirva vatan paste: grind green chillies, garlic, ginger and fresh coriander. Marinate mutton with salt, turmeric powder, hirva vatan and curd for minimum 1 hour or overnight. Make special garam masala: lightly toast coriander seeds, sesame seeds, red chillies, black cardamom, cloves, peppercorns, sichuan peppercorns, naag kesar, star anise, bay leaf, cinnamon and mace on low flame until fragrant, cool and grind to fine powder with salt. Make kala masala: char onions and dry coconut on direct flame until dark, roughly cut and grind with charred green chillies, garlic, ginger, coriander and garam masala to make paste. Heat iron wok, add oil and red chilli powder, add kala masala paste and cook on medium flame for 30 minutes while stirring regularly until oil separates and masala turns dark. Heat large vessel on high flame, add oil, sauté onions until light golden. Add marinated mutton, stir for 1 minute, cook on high flame for 10 minutes until water releases. Lower flame, cover and cook for 60-90 minutes until mutton is 90% cooked. Separate mutton from stock using strainer; use stock for rassa and mutton pieces for kala masala preparation.

name: Mysore Masala Dosa
ingredients: onions 1/2 cup sliced and 1/2 cup chopped
instructions: Wash moong dal well and soak for minimum 1-2 hours. Wash soaked dal with fresh water, transfer to grinding jar with green chillies, ginger and salt. Grind to fine smooth paste, add water while grinding to make thick dosa-like batter. For aloo filling: heat oil, add chana dal and urad dal, sauté for 1 minute until golden. Add mustard seeds, chopped ginger, chopped green chillies, curry leaves and asafoetida, sauté briefly. Add sliced onions, sauté on high flame until translucent. Add turmeric and salt, sauté for 1 minute. Add boiled diced potatoes, mix well and mash lightly with spoon. Add splash of water to make moist. Squeeze lemon juice and add fresh coriander, mix well. For mysore chutney: heat oil, add chana dal and urad dal, sauté on low flame for 1 minute. Add garlic, ginger and kashmiri red chillies, sauté for 1-2 minutes on low flame. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Cool mixture to room temperature, transfer to grinder, add tamarind pulp, salt and water, grind to fine paste. To make dosa: heat seasoned iron tawa, sprinkle little water to control temperature. Pour efficient batter and spread evenly to 3-4 inch circle. Add ghee and cook on medium heat until crispy and golden brown. Lower flame, spread mysore chutney and aloo mixture in center, add chopped onions and fresh coriander. When dosa starts to leave side, fold in half. Serve with hot sambar and coconut chutney.

name: Mango Phirni
instructions: Wash rice couple of times. Soak rice in water for 45 minutes, drain water and air dry the soaked rice. Cut mangoes and remove flesh, transfer to grinding jar to make puree. Once rice is completely dried, transfer to mixer grinder and grind to coarse texture, taking care not to grind too much. Soak ground rice in 200 ml milk from 1 liter total, keeping remaining 800 ml milk for cooking phirni. Set heavy bottom vessel on medium heat, add remaining 800 ml full fat milk, stir and bring to light simmer. Once milk boils, add milk-soaked rice while stirring, cook for 10 minutes on medium flame while stirring at short intervals. Scrape off sides while cooking and stir continuously throughout. Once phirni starts to thicken, lower flame and stir continuously until rice grains are cooked. Once thickened, add mango puree and chopped nuts, stir well. Taste for sweetness and add sugar accordingly. Add pinch of elaichi powder, stir and cook on medium-low flame for another 5-7 minutes until consistency is thick. Finish with pinch of salt and stir well. Transfer immediately to sakora or kullhad while warm for setting. Ensure phirni is warm enough while setting. Set in fridge for minimum 3-4 hours or overnight. Remove and serve chilled with some mango pieces as garnish and few fresh mint leaves.

name: Halwa Puri Chana
instructions: Wash black chana thoroughly and soak overnight for 7-8 hours. After soaking, strain and rinse with fresh water. Transfer soaked chana to pressure cooker with salt to taste and pressure cook for 4-5 whistles on medium flame. After cooking, strain water and reserve for later use. In a bowl, mix red chilli powder, coriander powder, amchur powder and jeera powder, add little water to make lump-free paste, keep aside. Set wok on medium heat, add oil and jeera, let jeera splutter. Further add prepared spice paste and stir continuously while cooking. Add turmeric powder and cook on medium flame until oil separates. Now add cooked chana, salt to taste and garam masala, mix to coat well with spices. Add reserved chana water (100-200 ml), stir and cook on medium flame for 10-15 minutes until water evaporates completely and masala coats well. For halwa (sheera): set wok on high heat, add sugar, water and crushed cardamom, stir until sugar dissolves completely. Once dissolved bring to boil and cook for 4-5 minutes. In another wok, set on low flame, add ghee and semolina, stir and cook sooji until it starts to get color and is aromatic. Cooking of sooji is very important. As sooji is almost roasted, add roasted almonds and roast briefly for 30 seconds. Further add prepared sugar syrup carefully while stirring, cook on medium flame while stirring continuously for 8-10 minutes until water is absorbed and ghee has separated. Switch off flame, cover and rest for 5-10 minutes. For puri: in mixing bowl, add wheat flour, semolina, ajwain, salt and ghee, mix well.
