Add water gradually to knead soft dough, knead well for 3-4 minutes. Apply ghee over dough surface, cover with damp cloth and rest for minimum 30 minutes. After resting, knead once again and divide into small equal roundels. Apply oil and roll each into thin chapati. Heat oil for frying, slide puri into hot oil, push down with puri maker to fluff it up, flip and fry on both sides until fluffed up nicely and golden brown. Serve hot fluffy puri with hot halwa and kale chane.

name: Falafel Wrap
instructions: Make tahini by toasting sesame seeds and blending with olive oil. Make hummus by soaking and cooking chickpeas, then blending with tahini, lemon, and oil. Make falafel by soaking chickpeas, grinding with onions, garlic, herbs and spices, refrigerating, then deep frying until golden. Prepare salad by mixing fresh vegetables. Assemble by spreading hummus on pita bread, adding fried falafel, salad, and sauces, then roll and serve.

name: Tandoori Soya Chaap Tikka
instructions: Fry canned soya chaap pieces in hot oil until crisp and golden. Cut into 2-3 pieces. Divide into two portions for afghani and achari marination. Mix curd, cashew paste, cream, ginger garlic paste, spices for afghani marinade and marinate 15-20 minutes. For achari version, add mango achar to marinade. Skewer marinated chaap with capsicum and onions. Cook on open flame or oven at 200°C for 7-8 minutes. Brush with melted butter and recook briefly. Serve with chutney and garnish.

name: Idli Chilli
instructions: Cut leftover idlis into strips. Make batter with maida, cornflour, salt, pepper powder and ginger garlic paste. Coat idli strips with batter and deep fry in hot oil on medium high heat until crisp and golden. Heat oil in wok on high heat, add onions, ginger, garlic and green chillies, cook 1 minute. Add vegetable stock and stir. Add soy sauce, capsicum, onions and spring onion bulbs, cook 1 minute. Add coriander, sugar, salt and pepper. Mix cornstarch with water to make slurry, add and cook until sauce thickens. Add fried idlis and toss gently to coat with sauce. Finish with spring onion greens and serve immediately with schezwan sauce.

name: Paneer Schezwan Frankie
instructions: 1. Make frankie dough: Mix maida, salt, and curd. Knead well for 10-15 minutes. Rest 30 minutes. 2. Divide into balls, flatten and roll thick chapatis. Cook briefly on both sides (20-30 seconds each) on tawa with oil. Stack and keep warm. 3. Make frankie masala: Mix all powdered spices in a jar. 4. Prepare schezwan paneer filling: Fry paneer cubes coated in corn flour and refined flour batter until golden. 5. Make chilli paste by soaking red chillies in hot water and grinding. 6. In a wok, cook chilli paste in oil until oil separates. Add garlic, ginger, green chillies, and coriander stems. Cook 1-2 minutes. 7. Add ketchup, chilli sauce, vinegar, and soy sauce. Cook 1 minute. 8. Add vegetable stock and bring to boil. Add cornstarch slurry to thicken. 9. Add fried paneer, onion petals, and capsicum. Mix gently to coat. Finish with spring onion greens. 10. Assemble frankies: Butter a half-cooked roti on tawa until golden spots appear. Sprinkle frankie masala, add schezwan paneer, onions, cabbage, and fried noodles. Roll and serve hot.

name: Chatpate Tandoori Aloo
instructions: 1. Boil cubed potatoes with salt until 80% cooked. Cool to room temperature. 2. In a mixing bowl, whisk mustard oil with red chilli powder to bleed color. 3. Add remaining powdered spices, ginger-garlic paste, hung curd, and salt. Mix well. 4. Add par-boiled potatoes, capsicum, and onions. Mix well. 5. Smoke potatoes by placing live charcoal on them and pouring ghee over it. Cover and smoke 4-5 minutes. 6. Skewer potatoes and capsicum on bamboo skewers. Grill on all sides until crisp and golden, applying melted butter while grilling. 7. For chaat: In a mixing bowl, combine tandoori aloo with sliced onions, ginger julienne, chopped green chillies, lemon juice, green chutney, tamarind chutney, melted butter, fresh cream, whisked curd, chaat masala, and coriander. Mix gently without breaking potatoes. 8. Serve immediately with fresh cream and sliced onions.

name: Paneer Rajma
instructions: 1. Soak rajma for 4-5 hours or overnight. Drain water. 2. In pressure cooker, add soaked rajma, whole spices, salt, and water (1 cm above surface). 3. Pressure cook on high for 5 minutes, then on low until 2 whistles. Let cool naturally. 4. Meanwhile, cut paneer into preferred shapes and shallow fry in hot oil on both sides until golden. Submerge in salted lukewarm water for 10 minutes. 5. Strain cooked rajma and reserve the water. 6. Heat wok on medium, add oil and ghee, cumin seeds, and sliced onions. Cook until golden brown. 7. Add garlic, ginger, green chillies, cashew nuts, and turmeric. Mix and cook 3-4 minutes. 8. Add tomatoes and salt. Cook until mushy. Cool to room temperature and grind to fine paste. 9. In another pan, heat oil and ghee. Sauté ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute. 10. Add powdered spices and cook on low heat for 1-2 minutes with some water to prevent burning. 11. Add ground paste and cook on medium heat 10-12 minutes, covered. 12. Add cooked rajma and stir. Cook 7-8 minutes. 13. Add reserved rajma water as needed. Add julienned ginger, slit chillies, kasuri methi, and garam masala. Cook 10-12 minutes. 14. Add fried paneer gently and cook on low heat for 5 minutes. Finish with fresh coriander. Serve with rajma or roti.

name: Makai Dum Angara
instructions: 1. Onion-tomato gravy: Heat wok on medium, add oil and whole spices. Cook until onions translucent. Add tomatoes and remaining ingredients. Add salt, cook 3-4 minutes on medium flame. 2. Lower heat, add water, cover and cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. 3. Cool to room temperature. Remove bay leaf and grind to fine puree. 4. Making final sabzi: Heat wok on medium, add ghee, chopped onions, garlic, ginger, and slit green chillies. Cook until onions turn translucent. 5. Lower flame, add powdered spices with some water to prevent burning. Cook 2-3 minutes on medium-high heat. 6. Add pureed onion-tomato gravy and pinch of sugar. Cook 4-5 minutes on medium flame. 7. Add sweet corn kernels and stir well. 8. Smoke the gravy: Burn charcoal on open flame. Place steel bowl in gravy and put burning charcoal in bowl. Pour ghee over charcoal, cover immediately with lid and lower flame. Cook 10 minutes while gravy absorbs charcoal flavor. 9. Cut capsicum and tomatoes into julienne. 10. After 10 minutes, open lid, discard charcoal. Stir gently. Add grated paneer, kasuri methi, and garam masala. 11. Add julienned capsicum and tomatoes. Cook 2-3 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. Finish with fresh coriander. Serve hot with roti or naan.

name: Veg Diwani Handi
instructions: 1. Base Gravy: Slice onions thinly and separate layers. Heat wok/handi on medium, add oil and cook onions until golden brown (like birista). Remove on paper towel. Transfer to grinding jar. 2. In same pan, remove 80% oil. Roast cashew nuts on medium-low flame until golden. Remove and keep aside. 3. Add tomatoes, ginger, garlic, Kashmiri red chillies, salt, and green chillies. Cook 2-3 minutes. Add water and stir. 4. Cover and cook 10 minutes on medium-low flame. Cool to room temperature. Grind along with roasted cashews and fried onions with water into fine paste. Keep aside. 5. Half-cooked veggies: Boil water with turmeric and salt. Blanch cauliflower florets for 30 seconds. Keep aside. 6. In wok/handi, add reserved oil from frying onions. Fry carrots, peas, blanched cauliflower, and french beans on high flame for 3-4 minutes, keeping them crunchy. Remove and keep aside. 7. Making sabzi: Heat wok/handi, add ghee, chopped garlic, and green chillies. Cook on medium-low until garlic turns slightly golden. 8. Lower heat, add whole spices and powdered spices. Add some water to prevent burning. Increase flame to medium and cook until oil/ghee separates (2-3 minutes). 9. Add blended base gravy. Add hot water for desired consistency. Stir well and cook 10-15 minutes on medium flame, stirring regularly. 10. Add half-cooked veggies and julienned ginger. Mix well, taste, and adjust salt. Cook 7-8 minutes on high flame. 11. Lower flame, add fresh cream, garam masala, and kasuri methi. Cook 1 minute on low flame. 12. Finish with fresh coriander and 2 drops of kewda water (don't overdo). 13. For tadka: Heat tadka pan with ghee. Fry almonds and cashews until golden. Top over sabzi. Serve hot with roti or naan.

name: Capsicum Pakora Chaat
instructions: For aloo mixture: Heat oil, add jeera, mustard seeds, hing, curry leaves and ginger garlic paste, sauté for 1 minute. Add turmeric, green chilli paste and cook for 30 seconds. Add boiled mashed potatoes, garam masala, salt and lemon juice, cook for 2-3 minutes. Add coriander and cool to room temperature. For pakora: Mix besan, ajwain and salt. Add water gradually to make semi-thin batter and rest for 10-15 minutes. Remove stem from capsicum and cavity using small spoon. Fill with potato mixture and coat with besan batter. Deep fry on medium-high flame until crisp and golden brown. Remove on absorbent paper. For chaat assembly: Cut pakoras into pieces, top with green chutney, red garlic chutney, chopped onions, tomatoes, aloo bhujiya, chaat masala and coriander. Serve immediately.

name: Aloo Tikki Sandwich
instructions: For red garlic chutney: Grind soaked kashmiri red chillies, garlic, jeera powder, black salt and salt with water to make thick paste. For green chutney: Grind coriander leaves, spinach, green chillies, curry leaves, garlic, roasted chana dal, sandwich masala and salt with water to make thick spread. For aloo tikki: Heat oil, add jeera and hing, sauté briefly. Add ginger garlic paste and green chillies, cook for 1 minute. Add turmeric, cook for 1 minute. Add boiled mashed potatoes, salt, lemon juice and coriander, cook for 2-3 minutes and cool. Shape into tikkis. Shallow fry on grill pan or pan on both sides until golden brown. Remove on absorbent paper. For sandwich: Trim bread edges and spread butter. Apply green chutney and red garlic chutney on both slices. Place aloo tikki on one slice and mash. Add aloo bhujiya sev and sliced vegetables. Sprinkle sandwich masala. Top with second buttered slice, cut into pieces, apply butter on top and sprinkle sev. Serve with ketchup and chutneys.

name: Baida Roti
ingredients: oil 1 tsp plus 2 tbsp for cooking
instructions: For dough: Add flour and salt, gradually add water until dough forms. Knead for 10 minutes on platform with dry flour. Add 1 tsp oil and knead for 2-3 minutes. Apply oil on surface, cover with damp cloth and rest 30-60 minutes. Divide into small dough balls. For chicken mixture: Mince boneless chicken. Heat oil, add jeera, ginger garlic paste, green chillies, cook for 1-2 minutes on medium flame. Add powdered spices and little water, cook for 1-2 minutes. Add minced chicken and salt, cook for 7-8 minutes on medium flame until moisture dries. Add coriander and lemon juice. For baida roti: Roll dough ball into thin translucent sheet. Break egg in bowl, add fresh coriander, green chillies, onions, chicken mixture and whisk. Pour over thin dough sheet. Fold all sides to seal and make square pocket. Heat oil in pan, shallow fry until crisp and golden brown. Lift edges and fry all sides. Serve hot with chutneys.

name: Mexican Tomato Corn Soup
instructions: For salsa (Pico De Gallo): Mix chopped tomatoes, onions, green chillies, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, black pepper and coriander in mixing bowl. Refrigerate until served. For soup: Wash tomatoes and cut in quarters. Blend into fine puree. Set wok or stock pot on medium heat, add oil and onions, cook until translucent. Add garlic and cook on medium flame for 2-3 minutes. Lower heat, add powdered spices and hot water to prevent burning, cook for 2-3 minutes. Strain tomato puree and add to wok (or add without straining for chunky soup). Add salt, black pepper and oregano, stir and cook for 1-2 minutes. Add coriander stems and green chillies, cover and cook on medium flame for 5 minutes. Add sweet corn, rajma and vegetable stock. Adjust consistency as desired. Cook for 7-8 minutes on medium flame. Add lemon juice and fresh coriander. Serve hot with crushed nachos, salsa, cheese and coriander garnish.

name: Eggless New York Style Cheesecake
instructions: Crush biscuit using food processor or clean cloth. Add melted butter and mix well. Set 8-inch spring form mould with base tray upside down and lock the spring form. Transfer butter-biscuit mixture to mould and press evenly using pav bhaji masher or flat-bottomed glass. Bake in preheated oven at 165°C for 10-12 minutes. Cool and prepare cheese mixture. In mixing bowl, add cream cheese and sifted powdered sugar, beat with electric beater or hand whisk until creamy. Add fresh cream, condensed milk, vanilla extract, thick curd, lemon zest, lemon juice and sifted cornstarch. Fold and mix with spatula, do not over-mix. Pour mixture over baked base, tap to remove air pockets. Wrap mould with foil and butter paper. Fill water in baking tray and place wrapped cheesecake in it. Bake at 165°C for 45-50 minutes until slightly wobbly. Run clean knife around sides and cool. Remove foil and butter paper. Refrigerate for 5-6 hours. Carefully unlock spring form mould using thin wide spatula. Serve as is or with berry compote.

name: Atom Bomb Chaat
ingredients: green chillies 5-6 spicy plus 10-12 less spicy
instructions: For green chutney: Grind coriander leaves, mint, curry leaves, black salt, raw mango, green chillies, ginger, roasted chana dal and salt with ice cubes and water into fine chutney. Refrigerate. For red garlic chutney: Grind soaked kashmiri red chillies, garlic, jeera powder, black salt and salt with water into fine paste. For sweet tamarind chutney: Soak tamarind and dates in hot water for 15-20 minutes. Squeeze tamarind pulp. Grind tamarind and dates into fine paste. Strain through sieve. Add jaggery and remaining spices, let jaggery melt. Remove scum and cook for 30 minutes on medium flame, stirring occasionally, until thin syrup consistency. Cool and store. For special spice mix: Dry roast jeera on low heat until dark and aromatic. Cool, transfer to grinding jar with remaining ingredients and grind to fine powder. For assembly: Cut boiled potatoes in halves, make a base, cut tip and scoop out using small spoon to make cavity. Mix scooped potato, sprouted moong, boiled chana, raw mango, onions, pomegranate seeds, peanuts, lemon juice, spice mix and coriander for filling. Fill potato cavities. Place on plate and top with green chutney, red garlic chutney, sweet tamarind chutney, nylon sev, lemon juice, spice mix, coriander, peanuts, raw mango and anardana. Serve immediately.

name: Veg Hyderabadi Nizami Handi
instructions: Make quick makhani sauce by cooking tomatoes, green chillies, ginger, garlic, cashew nuts, bay leaves and salt for 10-15 minutes, then grind to smooth paste. Boil vegetables (cauliflower, french beans, carrots, peas) with salt and turmeric until 80-85% done. Boil and grind cashew nuts into fine paste. In final cooking: heat oil and ghee, add ajwain and jeera to crackle, add whole spices (cardamom, bay leaves, cinnamon), add chopped onions until translucent, add ginger-garlic paste, cook until rawness goes, add turmeric powder, add chopped tomatoes and cook until mushy, add powdered spices, cook until ghee is released, add cashew paste and cook 4-5 minutes while stirring continuously, add makhani gravy and cook 4-5 minutes on high flame, add partially cooked vegetables and spinach, cook 4-5 minutes more, lower flame and add fresh cream and toasted kasuri methi, finish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

name: Aloo Tikki Makhani Sizzler
instructions: For aloo tikki: heat butter and oil, add ginger, green chillies, green peas, sauté 1-2 minutes, add powdered spices, sauté briefly, grate boiled potatoes directly into pan, mix and cook 2-3 minutes, transfer to bowl, wash poha and add to mixture with fresh coriander and lemon juice, shape into medium tikki, coat with flour, dip in slurry (refined flour, corn starch, salt, pepper, water), then coat with seasoned bread crumbs, deep fry on medium-high heat until golden. For makhani sauce: cook tomatoes, onions, kashmiri chillies, ginger, garlic, cashew nuts and spices for 10 minutes, add water and cover for 15 minutes, cool and grind to fine puree, then make tadka with butter, oil, garlic, ginger, green chillies, onions, add kashmiri chilli powder, add pureed gravy and sugar, cook 5-6 minutes, add fresh cream, garam masala, kasuri methi and coriander. For jeera rice: heat ghee, add jeera, add cooked rice with salt, toss and add coriander. Sauté veggies: heat oil and butter, add garlic, add french beans and carrots, cook 1-2 minutes on high heat. Assembly: heat sizzler plate until smoking hot, spread cabbage leaves, place jeera rice, sautéed veggies, caramelized onions and crispy aloo tikki, pour hot makhani sauce, add cold butter pieces on sizzler for sizzling effect.

name: Mumbai Street Style Sandwich
instructions: For sandwich masala: dry roast jeera, cloves, peppercorns, fennel seeds on medium-low flame until aromatic, cool to room temperature, add aamchur powder, anardana powder, ginger powder, hing, black salt, salt and grind in blending jar. For green chutney: grind fresh coriander, blanched spinach, green chillies, garlic, curry leaves, sandwich masala (1/2 tsp), salt, roasted chana dal and ice cubes to fine chutney. For red garlic chutney: soak kashmiri and spicy red chillies, grind with garlic, jeera powder, black salt, salt, lemon juice and water to fine paste. For aloo masala: heat oil, add jeera, mustard seeds and curry leaves to splutter, add ginger, green chillies, hing and curry leaves, sauté 1 minute, add onions until translucent, add turmeric, sauté 30 seconds, add boiled potatoes, salt, coriander and lemon juice, cook 1-2 minutes while mashing slightly. Spread chutney over bread, place tandoori aloo, add onions, ginger, green chillies, lemon juice, chaat masala and coriander, mix gently without breaking potatoes and serve immediately.

name: Strawberry Jam
instructions: Wash strawberries thoroughly and pat dry, trim the head with leaves, cut strawberries into quarters or smaller chunks (chunkier is fine). Transfer chopped strawberries to non-stick wok, add sugar, salt pinch and vinegar, mix well and switch on flame to low heat. Lightly stir until sugar dissolves completely, continue cooking on low flame while stirring regularly. By now mixture will turn slightly watery. Once strawberries have softened, mash them with spatula. After 10 minutes of cooking increase flame to medium heat. Continue cooking 45-60 minutes total, stirring regularly. Remove and discard froth formed on top while cooking. Check readiness by dropping dollop of jam on plate, allow to cool and tilt the plate - if jam slides it is runny and needs more cooking, if it stays it is done. Do not overcook as jam will thicken as it cools. Store in well-sterilized glass jar: boil glass jar, spoon and tong in stock pot for few minutes, remove and let steam escape and jar dry completely. Add jam (can be warm), close lid and re-dip in boiling water for few minutes to increase shelf life. Allow to cool to room temperature and refrigerate for good 6 months.

name: Almond Tea Time Cake
instructions: Grind whole almonds in grinding jar well to make almond flour/powder, keep aside. In bowl add softened salted butter and powdered sugar, whisk well with electric beater until soft, pale and fluffy. Add milk and vanilla extract to beaten sugar and butter mixture slowly and gradually to avoid lumps, mix well. Add almond flour/powder and mix well. Sift refined flour and baking powder together and add to mixture, mix and fold well - just mix until ingredients come together and avoid overmixing at this stage. Add slivered almonds to mixture and mix well. Line loaf pan with butter paper and transfer cake mixture into it, tap to release excess air. Top with slivered almonds. Bake in preheated oven at 180°C for 30-35 minutes. Check doneness by pricking toothpick in centre - if it comes out clean it is done, otherwise bake further. Remove from oven and cool down to room temperature before removing from pan. Slice and enjoy with family with tea or coffee. Optional: top with chocolate ganache and chopped nuts.

name: Pindi Chole Bhature
instructions: For bhatura: Mix dry ingredients, add curd and ghee, knead with water for 10-15 minutes to make soft dough. Rest dough with ghee for 1 hour. Shape into balls, rest 10 minutes, flatten and roll. Heat oil until smoking, fry bhature until golden and fluffy. For chole masala: Roast whole spices, make masala potli with tea and spices. Soak chickpeas overnight, pressure cook with potli and salt for 3-4 whistles. Strain, discard potli. In iron wok, add hing, green chillies, ginger, masala and salt, rest 30 minutes. Heat ghee until smoking, mix with chickpeas, cook on low with reserved water for 15-20 minutes until semi-thick. For aloo: Fry cubed potatoes, toss with masala spices and ghee. For chutney: Grind pudina, coriander, green chillies, ginger, anardana with black salt and amchur. Serve bhature hot with chole, aloo, and chutney.

name: Tandoori Vegetable Grill Sandwich
instructions: Make green spicy chutney: Grind coriander, spinach, green chillies, garlic, curry leaves with sandwich masala and roasted chana dal until thick paste. Make red garlic chutney: Soak chillies, grind with garlic, jeera powder, black salt and lemon juice. Make tandoori sauce: Bleed kashmiri chilli powder in mustard oil, add spices, ginger garlic paste, red chutney, curd, mayo. Smoke sauce with ghee over live charcoal. Prepare paneer vegetable filling: Mix chopped tomatoes, capsicum, onions, corn, paneer, mint and coriander. Assembly: Apply butter on bread, layer with tandoori sauce, paneer filling, sandwich masala, cheese. Repeat with another slice using green and red chutneys. Grill both sides until golden with grill marks. Serve hot with ketchup, chutney and chips.

name: Mushroom Ghee Roast
instructions: Soak Byadgi red chillies and cashew nuts in hot water for 15-20 minutes. Set pan on medium-low heat, dry roast whole spices until aromatic, cool to room temperature. Grind roasted spices, soaked chillies and cashews with garlic, tamarind pulp, jaggery and salt into thick paste. This is the ghee roast masala. Set pan on medium heat, add 2 tbsp ghee with halved mushroom and turmeric powder, saute for 3-4 minutes and set aside. In another pan, add 2 tbsp ghee with ghee roast masala paste, cook for 10-15 minutes until ghee separates and turns dark. Add sautéed mushroom, mix and cook on medium flame for 5-6 minutes until ghee separates. Add curry leaves, salt, coriander powder and lemon juice. Cook for 1 minute and serve hot.

name: Maa Ki Dal
instructions: Wash kaali urad dal and chana dal 3-4 times until water is clear, soak overnight. After soaking, rinse with fresh water and transfer to pressure cooker. Coarsely crush green chillies and ginger with hamam dasta, add to dal with turmeric, salt and onions. Add water and stir once. Close lid and pressure cook for 4-5 whistles on medium-low flame. Allow pressure cooker to depressurize naturally. Open lid and check if dal is cooked by mashing. Use muddler to mash dal completely - chana dal should be fully mashed while keeping urad dal chunky. For tadka: Heat ghee, add jeera, ginger and garlic, cook until garlic gets colour. Add onions and cook until light golden. Add powdered spices, red chillies, tomatoes, salt and coriander. Cook 2-3 minutes. Add little water and cook until tomatoes turn mushy. Add cooked dal, stir and cook. Add hot water to adjust consistency. Taste and adjust salt. Add garam masala and finish with fresh coriander. Serve hot with ghee on top.

name: Kurkuri Aloo Tikki Chaat
instructions: For masala chana filling: Wash and soak chana dal 4-5 hours. Boil with salt until almost cooked but grains intact (6-7 minutes), drain and cool. Lightly mash 25% while keeping rest intact. Heat ghee, add cooked chana dal, ginger chilli paste, and powdered spices, cook 4-5 minutes on low flame. For aloo tikki: Grate boiled potatoes using bigger hole, add jeera, salt, oil and cornflour, mix gently without mashing much. Take spoonful, shape into cup, fill with chana dal mixture, bring ends together and seal. Shape into ball and flatten gently into tikki. Heat ghee on tawa on medium-low flame, fry tikki slowly on one side until light golden. Flip and cook other side until crisp and golden. Can re-fry briefly on medium-high flame for extra crispiness. For assembly: Place tikki on plate, top with green and sweet chutneys, chaat masala, ginger juliennes, beetroot, green chillies, coriander. Mix curd with black salt and sugar, drizzle on top. Serve immediately.

name: Aloo Chaat
instructions: Wash potatoes of equal size, par boil until 70-80% cooked (fork should prick with some resistance). Cut while hot into halves to release steam, cool, peel and cut into quarters. Rest 10-15 minutes. Heat oil for deep frying, add par boiled potato quarters in batches. Let outer layer form on high flame, then reduce to medium flame and fry slowly until crisp and golden brown. Remove and toss with salt immediately. For hari chutney: Grind coriander, mint, green chillies, ginger, jeera powder, amchur powder, black salt with ice until fine chutney. For tandoori marinade: Bleed mustard oil with kashmiri red chilli powder, add all remaining spices, ginger garlic paste, curd, fresh cream and mayonnaise. Smoke over live charcoal with ghee for 2-3 minutes. For classic aloo chaat: Mix fried potatoes with red chilli powder, black salt, ginger juliennes, green chillies, coriander, lemon juice, green chutney and sweet chutney. Garnish with ginger and coriander. For tandoori aloo chaat: Mix fried potatoes with tandoori marinade, onions, ginger, green chillies, coriander, mint, lemon juice and fresh cream. Garnish with onion rings and cream. For schezwan aloo chaat: Mix fried potatoes with schezwan sauce, ketchup, cabbage, capsicum, spring onions and black pepper. Garnish with spring onion greens. Serve immediately.

name: Chole Pattice
instructions: For chana dal: Soak and pressure cook chana dal with water, turmeric and salt for 1 whistle. Drain and mix with salt, chopped green chillies, fresh coriander and powdered spices (amchur, chilli, jeera, coriander, black salt). For pattice: Grate boiled potatoes, add soaked poha, salt, bread crumbs and cornflour, mix well. Use heart-shaped cookie cutter, fill halfway with potato mixture, add spoonful of masala chana dal in center, fill top half with potato mixture, press to hold shape. Coat with breadcrumbs, shallow fry in hot oil/ghee until crisp and golden brown. For chole: Grind green chutney ingredients to fine paste. Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with bay leaf, salt and baking soda for 2 whistles until cooked. Drain, reserve water. Heat ghee and oil with jeera, add green chutney, turmeric and jeera powder, cook 4-5 minutes. Add cooked chickpeas, mix well, cook 2-3 minutes. Add reserved chickpea water for gravy, add jaggery, tamarind, salt and garam masala, cook 10-15 minutes on medium-low. Crush boiled potatoes directly into chole, cook 10 minutes. Check seasoning, adjust consistency with reserved water, finish with fresh coriander. Assemble by placing fried pattice on plate, pour chole over it or serve separately with chutneys and pickled onions.

name: Peri Peri Chicken Popcorn
instructions: For peri peri spice mix: Add red chilli powder, black salt, cinnamon powder, garlic powder, ginger powder, oregano and salt to jar and shake well. For chicken popcorn: Cut boneless chicken into cubes. In mixing bowl, add chicken cubes with salt, pepper, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice and 1 tbsp peri peri spice mix, mix and coat well, marinate 10 minutes. Coat chicken cubes individually with dry refined flour, then dip in whisked eggs, give final coating of dry refined flour. Massage chicken in final flour coating and dust off excess to form crumbs. Heat oil for deep frying, fry coated chicken in hot oil on medium flame until crisp and golden brown. Remove fried chicken to mixing bowl and toss with additional peri peri masala as desired, toss well until peri peri coats evenly. Serve hot and crispy immediately.

name: cheese chilli toast sandwich
instructions: For green chutney: Wash coriander leaves and transfer to grinder. Add blanched spinach, green chillies, garlic, curry leaves, sandwich masala and roasted chana dal. Grind to fine paste, adjust consistency with water. For sandwich masala: Dry roast whole spices (jeera, peppercorns, cloves, fennel, star anise) and anardana powder until fragrant. Cool, then add to grinder with powdered spices (amchur, hing, anardana, ginger powder, black salt, salt). Grind to fine powder. For sandwich: Chop capsicum and onions finely. Mix in bowl with grated cheese, sandwich masala and green chutney. Assemble sandwich with filling between bread slices, apply butter and toast in toaster or on tawa until golden. Press gently while toasting to keep filling intact. Serve hot with green chutney and ketchup.

name: crispy chana chilli
ingredients: oil 2 tbsp plus oil for frying
instructions: For crispy fried chana: Soak chana 4-5 hours, drain and rinse. Pressure cook with cinnamon, bay leaf, black cardamom, baking soda and salt for 1-2 whistles on medium heat. Cool and strain. Mix cooked chana with batter ingredients (maida, cornflour, salt, pepper, ginger garlic paste, baking powder, water) to coat. Deep fry in hot oil on medium-high heat until crispy and golden. Remove on absorbent paper. For crispy chana chilli: Heat oil in wok, add onions, garlic, ginger and coriander stems, cook 1 minute on high heat. Add veg stock, green chillies, green chilli paste, capsicum, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper. Cook 1 minute. Mix cornflour slurry, add and cook until sauce thickens. Lower heat, add crispy chana, fresh coriander and spring onion greens. Toss gently. Garnish with spring onion greens and serve hot.

name: aloo tuk chaat
instructions: For aloo tuk: Peel and wash raw potatoes. Cut into halves or quarters if large. Soak in salted water for 5-10 minutes, then drain and pat dry. Heat oil in wok, add pinch of salt. Deep fry potatoes for 2 minutes in hot oil to form crust, then lower heat and continue frying for 8-10 minutes until almost cooked (test with toothpick). Remove on absorbent sheet and cool slightly. Gently smash with hands to keep intact. Once cooled, heat oil to high temperature and flash fry mashed potatoes until crisp and golden brown. Remove on absorbent paper. Heat 1 tsp oil, add turmeric and sauté briefly. Add red chilli powder, cumin powder, amchur powder, coriander powder, salt and pepper. Add crispy fried potatoes and toss to coat. For chaat: Transfer spiced aloo tuk to mixing bowl and break into chunks. Add chutneys, pomegranate seeds, fresh coriander and ginger. Mix gently. Top with whisked curd, ginger juliennes, beetroot juliennes, more chutneys, black salt, jeera powder, chaat masala and sev. Serve immediately.

name: palak rajma with paneer
instructions: Soak rajma for 4-5 hours or overnight, drain and wash. Boil water, blanch palak for 15-20 seconds, transfer to ice-cold water. Drain and grind with coriander, mint, green chillies and ginger to fine puree. Pressure cook soaked rajma with bay leaf, black cardamom, pinch of salt and water for 1-2 whistles. Cool, drain and reserve water. Heat ghee and oil, add jeera, garlic, ginger and green chillies, sauté for 1-2 minutes. Add onions and cook until translucent. Add hing, kasuri methi, chopped tomatoes and salt, cook for 8-10 minutes until mushy and ghee separates. Add powdered spices (haldi, red chilli, coriander), mix and cook 2-3 minutes. Add boiled rajma, cook gently 2-3 minutes. Add reserved rajma water to adjust consistency, cook 8-9 minutes stirring. Add spinach puree, cook until boiling. Add wheat flour and nutmeg powder, cook 4-5 minutes. Add paneer cubes, cook 2-3 minutes. Add fresh cream and butter, cook 1-2 minutes. Check seasoning, add lemon juice. For tadka: Heat ghee, add garlic until golden, add whole red chillies, add red chilli powder, pour immediately over rajma. Serve hot with paratha or Indian bread.

name: tandoori creamy pasta
instructions: Boil water in pot, add salt, add spaghetti and cook for 10-12 minutes or al dente. Drain excess water, cool with running cold water to stop cooking. Add little oil and black pepper, toss well to prevent sticking. For tandoori spice mix: Mix kashmiri red chilli powder, coriander powder, black salt, jeera powder, amchur powder, garam masala and kasuri methi. For sauce: Heat butter in pan on medium heat. Add green chillies and sliced garlic, sauté 1 minute. Add refined flour, stir and cook on low heat 2-3 minutes until light golden. Slowly and gradually add milk while whisking continuously to make lump-free sauce. Cook 2-3 minutes until thickens slightly. Add tandoori spice mix, oregano and chilli flakes, mix well and cook 1-2 minutes. Add boiled spaghetti, salt to taste, cream and cheese, mix gently until cheese melts. Finish with freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil and fried garlic. Smoke the pasta by placing burning charcoal in a bowl, adding ghee drops, and covering briefly with a cloche.

name: triple schezwan fried rice
instructions: For cooked red chilli paste: Remove stems from kashmiri red chillies and cut from center to remove seeds. Discard seeds and soak chillies in hot water for 30 minutes (or overnight). Grind soaked chillies to fine paste, adding water as needed. Heat oil in wok on high flame until very hot. Add red chilli paste and cook on medium-high heat, stirring continuously. Initially the paste will absorb oil; continue cooking until oil separates completely from paste and texture becomes grainy. Add vinegar to increase shelf life, mix well and cook 1 minute. Set aside (chilli oil on top can be used for cooking). For fried noodles: Coat boiled noodles with cornflour, mix salt. Fry in hot oil until crisp and golden brown. Remove on absorbent paper. For schezwan fried rice: Heat oil in wok on high flame. Add chopped onions, garlic, ginger and green chillies, cook 1-2 minutes. Add carrots and french beans, stir and cook on high 1-2 minutes. Add cooked red chilli paste, ketchup, light soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, salt and white pepper, cook 1 minute on high heat. Add cooked rice and boiled noodles, stir well and cook 1 minute. Mix in spring onion bulbs and greens. Finish with fresh spring onion greens as garnish. Serve hot with schezwan manchurian.

name: Veg Masala Hot Dog
instructions: For aloo filling: Heat oil and butter, add jeera and ginger garlic paste with green chillies, cook 1-2 min. Add powdered spices and water to prevent burning, cook 1-2 min. Add ketchup, red chilli sauce, vinegar, cook until oil separates. Add boiled mashed potatoes, salt, coriander, lemon juice, mash while cooking 2-3 min. For chutneys and sauce: Grind coriander, mint, green chillies, ginger, tamarind pulp with spices to make green chutney; grind soaked kashmiri chillies with garlic, jeera powder, spices, vinegar, lemon for red garlic sauce. Assembly: Toast buttered hot dog buns on tawa, apply red garlic sauce, fill with aloo mixture, top with green chutney, onions, farsan, cheese, chaat masala, close and serve immediately.

name: Paneer Tikka Rumali Roll
instructions: For paneer tikka: Mix mustard oil with kashmiri chilli powder, add spices, ginger garlic paste, hung curd. Add capsicum and paneer cubes, marinate. Smoke with live charcoal for 3-4 min. Skewer and char over open flame, brush with butter, finish on flame. For rumali roti: Mix refined flour, wheat flour, sugar, salt, oil with lukewarm milk to make soft dough, rest 30 min. Heat kadhai upside down, sprinkle salt water. Roll dough paper-thin, place on hot kadhai with salt water, cook briefly each side until light golden and folded. For roll assembly: Mix charred paneer tikka with butter, green chutney, dahi, onion rings, coriander, chaat masala. Unfold rumali roti, place paneer tikka filling, fold tightly, brush with butter, char on flame, cut in half, serve hot.

name: Layered Spaghetti Bake
instructions: For red sauce spaghetti: Boil water with salt, cook spaghetti 10-12 min al dente, strain and toss with oil and black pepper. Blend tomatoes into puree. Heat oil, cook sliced garlic until colored. Add onions, cook translucent. Add red chilli powder briefly, add tomato puree, salt, ketchup, cover and cook 10 min. Add oregano, chilli flakes, black pepper, mix spaghetti into sauce. For white sauce veggies: Heat oil, add garlic and chilli flakes 2-3 min. Add baby corn and carrot 2-3 min, add remaining veggies with salt and pepper, cook 2-3 min. For white sauce: Melt butter, add flour, cook 2-3 min (light brown). Add milk in 3 batches while whisking. Add salt, black pepper, oregano, nutmeg, processed cheese until melted. Add sauteed veggies, cook 1-2 min. Assembly: Layer spaghetti in red sauce halfway in baking dish, top with veggies in white sauce, grate processed cheese, sprinkle oregano and chilli flakes. Bake at 180°C for 10-12 min until cheese colors. Serve hot with garlic bread.

name: Garlic Laccha Paratha
instructions: For mint and curd dip: Grind coriander, mint, green chillies, ginger, garlic, amchur, sugar, salt, black salt, black pepper with water and ice to fine paste. Mix with thick curd. For cheesy dip: Use double boiler, melt processed cheese with butter and milk gradually, whisk until desired consistency. For garlic dip: Mix thick curd, mayonnaise, garlic paste, salt, black pepper, fresh coriander. For garlic mixture: Mix chopped garlic, green chillies, coriander, mint, chilli flakes, imli water, melted butter, salt, black pepper. For paratha: Mix wheat flour and salt, add water to make semi-soft dough, oil surface, rest 30 min. Divide into balls, roll thin chapati, spread garlic mixture, cut into strips with pizza cutter, collect into sausage shape, roll into thick paratha. Cook on hot tawa until light golden, flip, cook again, add ghee/oil/butter, cook both sides until golden and fluffed. Serve hot with dips.

name: Paneer Ka Paratha
instructions: For homemade paneer: Heat milk to light boil on medium-low heat stirring constantly. Mix vinegar with water, gradually add to boiling milk to curdle. Once curdled, switch off flame. Strain through muslin cloth, rinse with fresh water to remove vinegar sourness, squeeze excess moisture. For thecha: Grind fresh coriander, garlic, green chillies, salt to coarse paste. For filling: Mix paneer crumbles with thecha, chopped ginger, mint, coriander, powdered spices (red chilli, coriander, jeera, anardana, aamchur, black salt, kasuri methi, ajwain), salt. Add chopped onions just before use. For paratha: Mix wheat flour and salt, add water for semi-soft dough, add oil, knead smooth, cover, rest 30 min. Divide into balls, flatten, make cup shape with thumb, fill with paneer mixture, seal ends, flatten gently, roll counter-clockwise without hard pressure. Cook on hot tawa light golden, flip, cook briefly, add ghee/oil/butter, cook both sides until golden and fluffy. Serve hot with fresh thecha and butter.

name: Taco Chaat
instructions: For taco shells: Mix wheat flour, semolina, ghee until incorporated. Add carom seeds, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, salt, fresh coriander. Add water gradually to knead tight dough, rest 30 min. Divide into balls, flatten, roll thin chapati. Cut into mini circles with cookie cutter or jar lid, prick with fork. Heat oil, deep fry on low heat, fold in half while frying until crisp and golden, drain on absorbent paper, cool to room temperature, store in airtight container. For chaat filling: Mix boiled diced potatoes, chopped tomatoes, boiled corn, pomegranate seeds, masala chana dal, toasted oats, chopped green chillies, gud/khajoor/tamarind chutney, mint chutney, fresh coriander, lemon juice, chaat masala. Assembly: Fill taco shells with chaat mixture, top with more tamarind chutney, mint chutney, whisked curd, sev, chaat masala. Serve immediately before it gets soggy.

name: Punjabi Aam Ka Achaar
instructions: Select ladwa variety raw mangoes, wash thoroughly with scrubber to remove residues. Cut into 1-inch cubes and pat dry completely. Spread on clean cloth, cover with net, sun dry 5-6 hours. Grind mustard seeds into powder. Grind fennel seeds only 15-20% in pulse mode keeping seeds mostly intact. Mix mustard powder, crushed saunf, kashmiri red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt, crushed methi, 400 ml mustard oil with sun-dried mangoes. Heat 100 ml mustard oil in separate pan until it smokes, cool slightly, add 1 tbsp asafoetida. Cool oil completely, pour over mango mixture, mix well. Use clean, completely dried airtight container or ceramic jar. Pour some mustard oil in jar, fill 3/4 with mango achaar, pour additional 100ml mustard oil on top for preservation. Seal jar or cover with cloth. Keep in direct sunlight for 3-4 days to mature, mix daily so oil and masala distribute evenly. After minimum 3 days, achaar is ready; flavor improves with longer storage. Serve as condiment with paratha, dal rice, or preferred dishes.

name: Loaded Nachos
instructions: Make tortilla chips dough from cornmeal, refined flour, salt, turmeric and water. Rest for 10 mins. Prepare spice mix by combining jeera, dhaniya, lal mirch, oregano, aamchur, garlic powder, kala namak. Make cheese sauce: melt butter, add cheese and milk until thick. Prepare pico de gallo salsa: chop tomatoes, onions, chillies, coriander, add lemon juice. Make mango salsa: combine salsa, raw mango, ripe mango, black salt, boiled corn. Pickle chillies in water, vinegar, sugar, salt. Make masala beans: cook ginger garlic paste with onions, dhaniya, jeera, garam masala, lal mirch, tomato puree, then add rajma beans. Deep fry tortilla chips until golden. Top with cheese sauce, salsas, pickles, beans and masala.

name: Cheese Garlic Naan
instructions: Mix dry ingredients: flour, salt, sugar, baking soda. Add yogurt and water gradually to make sticky dough. Add oil and knead for 10-12 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest 30 minutes. Make oregano seasoning from garlic powder, oregano, basil, black pepper, red chilli powder, rosemary. Combine cheese, garlic, oregano mix for filling. Shape dough into katori (cup shape), fill with cheese-garlic mixture, seal and flatten. Roll into elongated naan shape. Apply water on back, stick on hot iron tava water-side down. Cook until bubbles appear, then invert and cook over flame directing from different angles. For cheesy dip: heat milk and butter over double boiler, add cheese and whisk until melted and thick. Serve naan with cheesy dip.

name: Matar Ka Paratha
instructions: For filling: heat ghee and oil, add jeera, green chillies, garlic and cook 1-2 minutes. Add hing and peas, cook 2-3 minutes on high, then medium-low covered for 12-15 minutes. Increase heat and dry out moisture for 2-3 minutes. Cool to room temperature, coarsely grind and mix with thecha (crushed green chillies, garlic, coriander), amchur powder and chopped coriander. For paratha: mix wheat flour with salt, add water to make semi-soft dough, add oil and knead smooth. Rest 30 minutes. Divide into balls, flatten into cup shape, fill with pea mixture, seal. Flatten and roll gently in counter-clockwise direction. Cook on hot tawa until light golden, flip, add ghee and cook on both sides until fluffy and golden. Serve with thecha and butter.

name: Kaju Masala
instructions: Boil onions and cashews in water for 10-12 minutes, drain and rinse. Grind into fine paste with little water. Heat ghee, shallow fry cashews until golden on low flame, remove to paper towel. In same ghee, add oil, jeera, cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf, garlic and green chillies. Cook 1-2 minutes on low flame. Add chopped onions, cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and spice powders (turmeric, kashmiri red chilli), cook 1-2 minutes. Add coriander and cumin powder with little water. Add tomatoes, salt, cover and cook 10-15 minutes on low until ghee releases. Add cashew-onion paste, stir and cook 8-10 minutes on medium flame. Add fried cashews, kasuri methi, garam masala, butter and cream. Cook 2-3 minutes. Finish with coriander. Serve with naan or roti.

name: Crispy Corn
ingredients: oil for deep frying and tossing
instructions: Boil sweet corn kernels in water for 3-4 minutes, transfer to bowl and cool. Add salt, ginger-garlic paste, black pepper, refined flour and corn flour. Mix lightly with hands, add water splash and recoat with flour 3-4 times for even coating. Rest corn kernels. Heat oil for deep frying, sift coated corn with sieve to remove excess flour. Test oil temperature with one kernel (bubbles should form). Deep fry corn in batches on medium heat until crispy golden. Drain on strainer. For sauce: heat wok on high, add oil, onions, garlic, ginger, coriander stems and green chillies for 1-2 minutes. Add capsicum and spring onion bulbs, cook 1-2 minutes on high. Add schezwan sauce, ketchup, red chilli sauce, soy sauce, salt, white pepper, sugar. Toss crispy corn in sauce quickly. Finish with spring onion greens and coriander. Serve hot.

name: Cheese Garlic Bread Pizza
ingredients: fresh coriander or parsley 2 tbsp chopped
instructions: Make oregano mix: combine garlic powder, dried oregano, dried basil, black pepper powder, red chilli powder, dried rosemary and salt in jar, shake well. Store in airtight container. Make cheese-garlic filling: mix grated cheese, chopped garlic and oregano mix. Make garlic butter: combine melted butter, chopped garlic and fresh coriander leaves. Assembly: apply spoonful of cheese-garlic filling on one bread slice, place another slice on top. Heat pan on medium-high, add garlic butter and toast sandwich on both sides until crisp and golden. Remove from flame, apply pizza sauce on top, sprinkle grated cheese, add toppings of choice. Return to medium heat and toast until cheese melts (or use microwave for 30 seconds). Cut into desired pieces and serve with ketchup or mayonnaise.

name: Egg Chowmein Frankie
instructions: 1. Knead dough with refined flour, salt, curd, water, and oil until very soft and stretchy. Apply oil, cover and rest 30 minutes, then knead again. 2. Divide dough into balls, flatten and make thick rotis. 3. Heat tawa with oil and cook roti briefly on both sides (20-30 seconds each), stack in cloth. 4. For chowmein: heat wok with oil, add garlic, ginger, spring onion bulbs, green chillies and sauté. 5. Add onions and sauté. Add capsicum, carrots, cabbage - keep crunchy. 6. Add boiled noodles and mix gently. Add soy sauce, green chilli paste, red chilli sauce, vinegar, ketchup, salt, white pepper, and sugar. Toss and finish with spring onion greens. 7. For assembly: heat pan with oil and butter, cook half-cooked frankie roti until golden spots appear. Pour whisked egg on one side, flip and cook until egg is set. 8. Spread schezwan sauce on roti, sprinkle frankie masala, add chowmein, chopped onions, chilli vinegar, grated cheese. Roll and serve immediately.

name: Idli Sambar
instructions: 1. For idli batter: soak urad dal and idli rice separately for 4-5 hours. Grind urad dal to fluffy batter. Grind idli rice to paste. Mix both, add methi seeds and salt. Ferment 8 hours or overnight. 2. For sambar masala: heat oil with hing, mustard seeds, and cumin. Add urad dal, chana dal, black peppercorns, methi seeds, coriander seeds, curry leaves, and kashmiri chillies. Roast until aromatic. Add grated coconut, garlic, ginger, shallots, and green chillies. Cool and grind with toor dal and turmeric to paste. 3. For sambar: heat oil, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds. Add diced onions and tomatoes. Add salt, turmeric, and red chilli powder. Cook until tomatoes soften. 4. Add sambar masala paste and cook well. Add chopped drumstick, pumpkin, ash gourd, brinjal, bottle gourd, and shallots. Cook until vegetables are tender. 5. Soak tamarind in water and add juice. Add jaggery. Cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes. 6. Add lady finger and cook 5 more minutes. Adjust salt and jaggery balance. 7. For tadka: heat oil, add chana dal, methi, mustard seeds, boriya chillies, curry leaves, and hing. Add to sambar. 8. For coconut chutney: grind coconut, roasted chana dal, green chilli, cumin powder, black pepper, and salt with water to paste. Heat oil, add chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds, dry red chillies, and curry leaves. Pour over chutney. 9. Steam idlis using batter. Serve hot idlis with sambar and coconut chutney.

name: Mutton Rara
instructions: 1. Make homemade garam masala: dry roast cumin seeds, coriander seeds, green cardamom, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, black peppercorns, and fennel seeds on low flame until aromatic. Cool and grind with salt to fine powder. 2. Wash mutton pieces and mutton keema. Marinate with salt, turmeric, red chilli powder, ginger garlic chilli paste, and curd. Mix well and refrigerate. 3. Heat ghee and oil in wok. Add cumin seeds, cinnamon, green cardamom, cloves, black cardamom, and bay leaves. 4. Add 700 gm chopped onions and salt. Cook on medium flame until onions turn golden brown. 5. Add ginger garlic chilli paste and cook 3-4 minutes. 6. Lower flame, add turmeric powder and red chilli powder. Stir briefly. Add spicy red chilli powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Stir briefly. 7. Add 300-400 ml hot water and increase flame to high. Cook until oil separates. 8. Add finely chopped tomatoes and salt. Cover and cook on medium-low flame 8-10 minutes, stirring to prevent burning. Cook until tomatoes break down and oil releases. 9. Add marinated mutton pieces and keema. Cook on high flame for 10 minutes. Lower to lowest possible flame and cook 1-1.5 hours until mutton is completely tender. Stir occasionally. 10. Add garam masala, kasuri methi, ginger julienne, green chillies, and fresh coriander. Cook 10 more minutes on medium-high flame. Taste and adjust salt. Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander. 11. Serve hot with tandoori roti or any Indian bread.

name: Chicken 65
instructions: 1. Wash and cut chicken into 1-inch cubes, slicing at 45-degree angle for better marination. 2. Apply salt to all chicken pieces. 3. Mix ginger garlic paste, chopped curry leaves, kashmiri red chilli powder, jeera powder, garam masala pinch, green chilli paste, black pepper powder, and curd. 4. Add marinade to chicken and mix well. Marinate for 30-35 minutes in refrigerator. 5. After marination, add rice flour, cornflour, and hot oil to chicken. Mix thoroughly until flour coats evenly. Add more flour if needed. 6. Heat oil for deep frying to high temperature. Fry chicken for 2 minutes on high flame initially. 7. Lower heat to medium-low and continue frying until chicken is crisp, cooked, and tender, about 8-10 minutes total. 8. Remove from oil and drain on paper towel. 9. Heat 1 tbsp oil in wok on medium-high flame. Add chopped garlic, diagonally sliced green chillies, and curry leaves. Sauté lightly. 10. Add fried chicken to the wok and toss well with the aromatics. 11. Add black pepper powder pinch and toss again. 12. Serve hot and crispy immediately.

name: Cheesy Peri Peri Toast Sandwich
instructions: 1. For red garlic chutney: soak kashmiri red chillies in water for 10 minutes. Grind soaked chillies with garlic cloves, jeera powder, black salt, salt, and 50 ml water to fine paste. Keep aside. 2. For peri peri spice mix: combine red chilli powder, black salt, cinnamon powder, garlic powder, ginger powder, oregano, and salt in a jar. Shake well. 3. For filling: chop capsicum and onions finely. Dice paneer into small cubes. Chop green chillies. 4. In a mixing bowl, combine chopped capsicum, onions, corn kernels, paneer, green chillies, mayonnaise, red garlic chutney, and peri peri spice mix. Mix and combine well. 5. Apply sufficient filling on one bread slice and close with another bread slice to form sandwich. 6. Apply butter on both outer sides of sandwich. 7. Place on hot tawa or griddle and toast both sides until crisp and golden brown. 8. Optional: open the toasted sandwich, cut into desired shape, grate extra cheese on top, sprinkle peri peri masala, and serve immediately with ketchup or dip. 9. Alternative: keep sandwich intact, grate cheese and sprinkle peri peri masala on top while still warm. Serve immediately.

name: Mutton Keema
instructions: 1. Wash mutton mince well and squeeze out excess water. 2. In a mixing bowl, combine minced mutton with salt, ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder, garam masala, fresh coriander, green chilli paste, and ghee. Mix well. 3. Add thoroughly whisked curd and mix. Marinate for 30 minutes to 1 hour. 4. For onion masala: heat pan with ghee and oil. Add ginger garlic paste and chopped coriander stems. Cook 3-4 minutes. 5. Add chopped onions and cook until golden brown. When almost golden, add water 2-3 times and continue cooking until onions are deep dark brown. 6. Lower heat and add powdered spices (turmeric, red chilli, coriander, cumin, black pepper). Add hot water to prevent burning. Cook 4-5 minutes. 7. Remove onion masala and keep aside. 8. In the same wok, add oil and ghee with whole spices (cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, black pepper, cloves, green cardamom). Cook 1-2 minutes. 9. Add marinated mutton keema and mix. Cook on high flame 10-15 minutes while stirring continuously. 10. Mutton and curd will release moisture. Let cook in its own water for 30 minutes while stirring continuously. 11. After 30 minutes, fat will form on top. Add prepared onion masala and stir well. Cook 10-15 minutes. 12. Add 200-300 ml hot water and cook on low flame 25-30 minutes. 13. When moisture decreases and fat forms again, add 500 ml more hot water. Bring to boil and cook on medium-low flame 30-45 minutes. Cover for faster cooking. Check if keema is tender. 14. Add garam masala pinch, kasuri methi, and lemon juice. Mix well. Add green chillies. Finish with fresh coriander leaves. 15. Serve hot with toasted pav or pav bread with onion rings and lemon wedges.

name: Crispy Chilli Potato
instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into 1cm thick 3-inch batons. Blanch in salted boiling water until 80% cooked. Cool. Mix cornflour, maida, salt, baking powder with water to make thick batter. Deep fry blanched potatoes in hot oil until golden and crispy on medium heat. For chilli sauce: heat oil in wok on high, add onions, garlic, ginger, coriander stems, cook 1 minute. Add green chillies and paste, vegetable stock, bring to boil. Add soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, salt, white pepper. Add capsicum, onions, spring onion bulbs, coriander. Mix cornflour with water to slurry, add to thicken sauce. Add spring onion greens. Toss in crispy fried potatoes briefly, don't overmix.

name: Onion Samosa
instructions: For patti: mix maida and salt, add water gradually to knead soft dough. Knead well 8-10 minutes until smooth. Oil and cover, rest 30 minutes. Divide into dough balls. Flatten and roll mini chapatis. Apply oil and flour between each chapati. Stack 3-4 and roll thin as one sheet. Cook on hot tawa briefly 10-15 seconds per side, separate sheets. Cut into 2x8 inch strips. For filling: mix onions, green chillies, curry leaves, coriander, chilli paste, ginger paste, turmeric, garam masala, cumin, salt. Add poha in batches for moisture control. Rest 10-15 minutes. Add oil and mix. For assembly: make flour-water slurry. Take sheet, fold corner to make triangle, fill pocket with onion mixture. Fold and seal edges with slurry. Deep fry in medium-high oil until golden and crispy.

name: No Onion No Garlic Paneer Tikka Masala
instructions: For roasted besan: heat ghee, add besan, stir constantly until aromatic and color changes slightly. Cool in bowl. For tikka: mix mustard oil and kashmiri red chilli powder to bleed color. Add roasted besan, remaining powdered spices, hung curd, salt, black pepper, tomatoes, capsicum, paneer cubes. Mix gently without breaking paneer. Place live charcoal in center, pour ghee drops, cover 4-5 minutes to smoke. Skewer paneer, tomatoes, capsicum. Cook on open flame and char. Brush with melted butter, cook briefly on flame again. For gravy base: heat oil, add jeera, tomatoes, green chillies, coriander stems, kashmiri chillies, cashew nuts, salt. Add water, cover, cook 10-15 minutes until mushy. Cool and grind fine. For gravy: heat oil and butter, add jeera until crackling. Add bay leaves and chopped tomatoes, cook 2-3 minutes. Add powdered spices and little water, stir until oil separates. Add tomato puree and reserved marinade, cook 8-10 minutes. Add paneer tikka gently, adjust consistency with water. Add garam masala, kasuri methi, sugar, fresh cream. Finish with fresh coriander.

name: Paneer Shawarma
instructions: For pita bread: mix warm water, milk, curd, olive oil, sugar. Sift and add refined flour, wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt. Knead dough 10-12 minutes until smooth. Oil bowl, place dough, oil surface, cover, let proof 1 hour in warm place. Knead again, roll into log, divide into 7-8 dough balls. Rest 5-6 minutes. Roll into thick chapatis. Cook on hot tawa both sides until golden spots appear, press gently to fluff. Keep covered until use. For pickle: boil beetroot, carrots, green chillies until crunchy. Make brine with water, vinegar, sugar, salt, cool. Add blanched veggies, store in glass jar refrigerated. For hummus: use mixer grinder, add boiled kabuli chane, garlic, tahini, lemon juice, salt, black pepper, reserved chickpea water, ice cubes, virgin olive oil, optional curd. Pulse until fine, adjust consistency with chickpea water. For grilled paneer: mix paneer with olive oil, kashmiri red chilli, coriander, garam masala, elaichi powder, jeera powder, garlic paste, lemon juice, salt, black pepper, hung curd. Grill marinated paneer on hot pan both sides until golden with grill marks. Cut into strips or dices. For hot sauce: soak kashmiri red chillies, grind with garlic, sugar, olive oil, black salt, vinegar, jeera powder, lemon juice, salt, black pepper to paste consistency. Assemble shawarma.

name: Soya Chaap Tikka Dum Biryani
instructions: For soya tikka: deep fry soya chaap until golden brown, cut diagonally into 2-3 pieces. Mix kashmiri red chilli powder and mustard oil to bleed color. Add remaining powdered spices, besan, ginger garlic paste, thick curd, chopped coriander and mint, salt, lemon juice. Add capsicum, tomatoes, onion petals and fried soya chaap, coat well with marinade. Place live charcoal in bowl, pour ghee drops, cover and smoke 3-4 minutes. Skew soya chaap on skewers, cook on open flame, dab with melted butter, cook briefly on open flame. For gravy: heat oil and ghee, add whole spices, sauté 30 seconds. Add onions cook until golden brown. Add ginger garlic paste and chopped green chillies, cook 1-2 minutes. Lower heat, add powdered spices and hot water, cook until ghee separates. Add tomatoes and salt, increase flame to medium, cook until mushy. Add whisked curd slowly (lower heat while adding), increase heat to medium-high, cook 5-6 minutes until ghee releases. Add soya tikka gently, cook 3-4 minutes medium flame. Adjust consistency with water. Season with garam masala, kasuri methi, coriander and mint. For boiled rice: wash rice 3 times until water clear, soak 15-20 minutes. Boil water with salt, whole spices, ghee, mint, coriander. Add soaked basmati rice, cook 7-8 minutes. Strain and keep aside. For assembly: add birista, coriander, mint, ghee to soya tikka masala. Layer cooked rice. Repeat layers with birista, coriander, mint, garam masala, saffron infused milk, ghee, kewda water. Cover with dough seal and lid. Cook on thick tawa high flame 10 minutes, then low flame 15 minutes.

name: Schezwan Veg Crispy
instructions: For batter: mix refined flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt, black pepper. Add water gradually to make smooth thick batter. Add all blanched vegetables to batter and coat well. Heat oil in wok on medium heat. Deep fry batter-coated vegetables until crisp and light golden brown. Remove on kitchen tissue and keep aside. For tossing: heat oil in wok on medium-high flame. Add chopped garlic, ginger, green chillies and onions. Cook 2-3 minutes while stirring. Add 50ml water and bring to boil. Add all sauces (schezwan, ketchup, red chilli sauce), light soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, salt and white pepper to taste, aromat powder. Cook 1-2 minutes. Lower heat, add fried vegetables and toss well to coat with sauce. Do not cook longer or it will turn soggy. Garnish with fresh chopped spring onion greens and serve hot and crispy.

name: Goan Egg Curry
instructions: Make coconut paste by grinding fresh coconut, kashmiri chillies, black pepper corns, jeera, coriander seeds, ginger, garlic, turmeric powder and tamarind pulp with water. For frying eggs: heat oil, add boiled eggs, sprinkle salt, black pepper and turmeric powder, cook until golden brown. For curry: heat oil, add onions and green chillies, cook until light golden. Add coconut paste, cook 2-3 minutes. Add hot water and bring to boil. Add kokum and simmer 10-12 minutes until gravy thickens. Add fried eggs, cook 2-3 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. Cover and cook 2-3 minutes more. Add coconut milk if desired. Serve hot with rice or neer dosa.

name: Veggie Burger with Rajma Patty
ingredients: oil 1 tsp + butter 1 tbsp for onions
instructions: For raw mango salsa: blend raw mango, onions, tomatoes, ripe mango, fresh coriander, salt and pepper to coarse texture. Mix in red chilli powder, olive oil, green chillies, fresh coriander and additional mango. Chill. For mint garlic dip: mix curd, mayonnaise, grated garlic, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, powdered sugar and mint leaves. Chill. For charred onions: sauté thick onion rings with oil and butter, sugar and salt on high flame until charred. For rajma patty: soak rajma overnight, pressure cook until done. Mash hot rajma with potato masher. Mix with spices, ginger, garlic, chillies, herbs. Soften poha with water, add to mixture and knead. Shape into patties. Grill patties on both sides until crisp, top with cheese slice and cover until cheese melts. Assembly: toast burger buns with butter, spread mint garlic dip on bottom bun, add lettuce, rajma patty, mango salsa, tomato slices and charred onions. Top with upper bun and serve.

name: Burnt Chilli Garlic Noodles
instructions: Boil noodles in water with salt and oil. Once noodles separate, switch off flame and let sit 2-3 minutes in hot water. Drain and refresh with cold water. Drizzle oil and coat well to prevent sticking. Soak kashmiri red chillies in hot water for 10-15 minutes, cool and grind to fine paste. Heat oil in wok on medium heat, add chopped garlic and ginger, cook 1-2 minutes. Add broken red chillies and cook until garlic and chillies turn brown. Add red chilli paste and cook until oil separates. Increase flame to high for burnt flavour. Add green chillies and green chilli paste. Add all vegetables, soy sauce, salt, white pepper, aromat powder and sugar. Saute on high flame 1-2 minutes. Add boiled noodles, spring onions, coriander and vinegar. Stir and toss well on high flame for 1 minute. Serve immediately garnished with spring onion greens and schezwan sauce on the side.

name: Chana Garlic Koliwada
instructions: For chutney: grind fresh pudina, coriander, spring onion greens, green chillies, spring onion bulbs, ginger, garlic, jaggery, black salt, anardana powder and salt to fine paste with ice cubes and water. Chill in refrigerator. For chana koliwada: pressure cook soaked chickpeas with bay leaf, salt, baking soda and water until cooked. Drain and cool. Mix mustard oil with kashmiri chilli powder to bleed color. Add remaining spice powders, chilli pastes, salt and pepper. Coat cooked chickpeas well. Marinate remaining spices on garlic cloves. Mix cornflour, refined flour and besan. Deep fry coated chickpeas in hot oil on medium-high heat until crisp and golden. Briefly deep fry masala-coated garlic cloves. Serve hot with chutney, or mix with fresh coriander, green chillies, onions, chaat masala, red chilli powder and lemon juice.

name: Chicken Chilli Wontons
instructions: Make dough: Mix flour, eggs, salt and water to form a stiff dough. Knead well for 5-7 minutes, cover with damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. Divide into 4 parts, flatten and roll into very thin sheets, dusting flour to prevent sticking. Cut into 10cm x 10cm squares. For filling: Mince boneless chicken with food processor or knife. Mix minced chicken with spring onion greens, ginger, garlic, white pepper, salt, soy sauce, chicken stock, whisked egg and corn starch. Wrap: Place wonton wrapper diagonally, add small spoonful of filling, roll 3/4 way, press edges, apply water and seal sides together. Boil: Bring water to boil, add wontons and boil 5-6 minutes, remove and set aside. For chilli gravy: Heat oil in wok on high heat, add chopped garlic, spring onion bulbs, ginger and green chillies, sauté 1 minute. Add hot stock/water and bring to boil. Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, green chilli paste, vinegar, sugar, salt and white pepper. Add onion petals and diced capsicum, mix gently. Add spring onion greens and fresh coriander leaves. Mix corn flour with water and add to wok, cook until sauce thickens. Place cooked wontons on plate, pour chilli gravy over and serve immediately.

name: Soya Nargisi Kofta
instructions: For kofta: Boil water in stock pot, add pinch of salt and soya granules. Boil for 4-5 minutes. Strain out boiling water and wash with fresh tap water. Squeeze out excess water from cooked soya granules. Transfer to food processor or grinding jar and grind well to make soya mince. In mixing bowl, add minced soya granules, chopped ginger, garlic, green chillies, fried onions, powdered spices (red chilli powder, coriander powder, jeera powder, garam masala, kasuri methi, amchur powder, black salt), besan, salt to taste, freshly chopped coriander and mint leaves. Mix and combine well. Place live charcoal in center and add few drops of ghee. Cover and smoke for 4-5 minutes. Take large spoonful of soya mixture and flatten on greased palms. Place boiled egg in center and cover completely with soya mixture. Shape nicely like an egg. Fry soya coated egg on medium-high heat from all sides until crisp and golden brown. For gravy: Heat ghee and oil in wok. Add whole spices (jeera, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, black cardamom, green cardamom, black peppercorns, cloves) and cook until they release aroma. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook on low flame 1-2 minutes. Add tomato puree and whisked curd. Cook on high flame until ghee separates. Add powdered spices (red chilli powder, coriander powder, jeera powder, turmeric powder) and cook on low flame 2-3 minutes. Add 1 cup water and continue cooking 4-5 minutes. Add ground fried onions and cashew paste. Cook on medium flame until ghee separates. Add 500ml water to adjust consistency of gravy. Cook for 10-15 minutes. Add garam masala and kasuri methi and mix well. Add fried kofta, cover and cook 1-2 minutes on low flame. Add freshly chopped coriander leaves and mix gently. Cook for 1 minute. Serve hot with roti or paratha.

name: milk barfi
instructions: Whisk together condensed milk, milk powder and curd to make a lump-free mixture in a microwave-safe bowl. Microwave at 100% power for 3 minutes, remove and whisk well. Microwave again for 2 minutes at 100% power. Remove, whisk, add ghee and mix well. Lower power to 50% and microwave for final 2 minutes. Once the base is ready and hot, add chosen flavorings (cardamom and nuts for classic version). Mix well and transfer to a butter paper-lined tray. Top with slivered nuts. Set at room temperature for 2 hours without refrigerating to maintain creamy texture. Cut into desired shapes and serve.

name: butter chicken pasta
instructions: Marinate sliced chicken with oil, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, dry mango powder, black salt, garam masala, dry fenugreek, ginger garlic paste, curt, salt and pepper for 30 minutes. Heat ghee and oil in a pan on medium-high heat, cook marinated chicken 3-4 minutes per side until done, then cut into thin strips. For makhani sauce: heat oil with whole spices (cumin, green cardamom, bay leaf), sliced onions, whole red chillies, ginger and garlic. Add diced tomatoes, powdered spices, sugar, cashew nuts, salt and butter. Cook on medium-high for 10 minutes. Add water, cover and cook 15 minutes. Cool, grind to smooth puree and strain. In a new pan, heat oil and butter, add chopped garlic, julienned ginger and chopped green chillies. Cook 1-2 minutes, then add red chilli powder with a splash of water. Cook 20-30 seconds, then add makhani gravy and hot water to adjust consistency. Simmer 5-6 minutes. Stir in fresh cream, a pinch of garam masala and dry fenugreek. Add boiled spaghetti and grilled chicken strips along with fresh coriander. Mix gently and cook 1-2 minutes. Adjust seasoning, add lemon juice, finish with fresh coriander and serve hot with garlic bread.

name: smoked chicken tikka sandwich
instructions: For chilli garlic dip: whisk curd ensuring no lumps, add mayonnaise, finely chopped green chillies, garlic paste, salt and black pepper. Mix well and refrigerate. For chicken tikka: thinly slice chicken breast, mix with salt, red chilli powder, lemon juice and ginger garlic paste. Marinate briefly. For second marinade: heat mustard oil, add kashmiri red chilli powder and mix to bleed color, add ginger garlic paste, all powdered spices, fresh herbs, salt and thick curd. Mix well. Add pre-marinated chicken, onion petals, diced tomatoes and diced capsicum. Marinate 30-60 minutes. Smoke chicken by placing live charcoal in a bowl, pour ghee over coal, place in center of marinade and cover for 4-5 minutes. Skewer chicken with vegetables. Grill on hot tawa or grill pan with ghee, cooking from all sides until tender. Drizzle melted butter and char on open flame. Chop grilled chicken and vegetables roughly, sprinkle chaat masala, add lemon juice, chopped mint and coriander, fried onions and chilli garlic dip. Mix well. Spread generous amount of filling on bread slice, close with another slice. Apply butter and toast both sides until crisp and golden brown. Cut in preferred shape and serve hot with ketchup or chilli garlic dip.

name: tandoori pudla sandwich
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
live charcoal and ghee for smoking
instructions: For tandoori marinade: heat mustard oil, add kashmiri red chilli powder and mix well to bleed color, add ginger garlic paste, all powdered spices, salt and black pepper, stir in hung curd and mix well. Smoke marinade by placing live charcoal in small bowl inside marinade, pour ghee over coal, cover and smoke 3-4 minutes. For vegetable salad filling: shred cabbage, julienne tomatoes, slice onions, julienne capsicum, grate beetroot, chop green chillies. Combine all in bowl with lemon juice and fresh coriander. Do not add salt to avoid vegetables releasing moisture. For besan batter: mix besan, coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, ajwain, chopped coriander and green chillies with salt. Add water to make semi-thick batter. Rest 15-20 minutes. For vegetable pudla sandwich: heat tawa on medium heat, dip bread slice in batter and coat nicely, place on tawa and cook until light golden. Flip and cook other side. Apply tandoori marinade, add vegetable mixture, sprinkle chaat masala, add butter and flip. Cook briefly 1-2 minutes, then flip again with vegetable side facing up. Cook until bread becomes golden, lift one bread and place on top to make sandwich. Cut and serve with chutney or ketchup. For cheesy version: dip and coat bread with batter, place on tawa and cook until light golden on both sides. Apply butter and flip, cook briefly on medium flame. Flip again and grate cheese over it. Lift one bread and place on top to make sandwich. Cook both sides until golden brown and cheese melts. Cut and serve.

name: masala paneer pakora
instructions: For masala spice blend: set pan on medium-low heat, add jeera, coriander seeds, black peppercorns and fennel seeds, dry roast until fragrant. Cool to room temperature, transfer to mortar and pestle and grind coarsely. Add salt and red chilli flakes. For paneer: set deep vessel on medium-low heat, add milk and bring to boil while stirring at intervals. Lower flame, add ground spices, chopped green chillies and fresh coriander, stir well for 1-2 minutes. In separate bowl, mix vinegar and water. Slowly add this mixture to milk while stirring continuously until milk solids separate completely. Strain through muslin cloth without using hands (very hot). Wash paneer with fresh water to remove vinegar taste. Fold muslin cloth and place heavy weight on top for at least 1 hour to drain excess whey and compress paneer. For pakora batter: mix besan, ajwain, coriander powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, dry mango powder and salt. Slowly add water while whisking to make smooth semi-thin batter. Rest 10-15 minutes. Cut paneer block into cubes or desired shapes. Dip paneer pieces in batter to coat well. Deep fry in hot oil on medium-high heat until crispy and golden brown. Remove on absorbent paper. Serve hot and crispy with green mint chutney, ketchup or any dip of choice.

name: Vegetables in Paprika Sauce with Spinach Rice
instructions: For spinach rice: blanch spinach for seconds and transfer to ice water. Grind spinach with mint, coriander, green chillies and ice cubes into fine puree. Heat butter and oil, add garlic and red chilli flakes for 1-2 minutes. Add spinach puree and cook 4-5 minutes. Add cooked rice, salt, pepper and lemon juice. Stir and cook 2-3 minutes. For paprika sauce: sauté vegetables in oil, garlic and red chilli flakes. Prepare sauce by cooking flour and butter on low heat for 3-4 minutes. Add milk in batches while whisking to avoid lumps. Add paprika powder, salt, pepper and nutmeg. Cook 1-2 minutes. Add sautéed vegetables and paneer. Serve hot vegetables in paprika sauce with spinach rice.

name: Egg Galawati Kebab
ingredients: special galawati kebab spice mix 1 tbsp
instructions: Prepare galawati spice mix: roast all spices on medium-low heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add stone flower and rose petals, sauté briefly. Cool and grind to fine powder. For kebab: grind diced eggs until smooth. Mix with fried onion paste, cashew paste, ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder, salt, spice mix, rose water, kewra water and ghee. Add besan and mix. Place burning charcoal in centre, pour ghee over it and smoke for 3-4 minutes. Dip hand in cold water, shape spoonfuls into delicate tikki. Set pan on medium heat with ghee, slide shaped kebabs into pan and shallow fry on both sides until golden brown. Serve hot with onion rings, mint, green chutney and yogurt dip.

name: Vada Pav Tacos
instructions: For vada mixture: heat pan on medium, add oil, mustard and cumin seeds and let crackle. Add asafoetida, curry leaves, green chillies, ginger garlic paste and sauté for a minute. Add turmeric powder and garam masala, sauté for half a minute. Add boiled mashed potatoes, salt to taste and cook for 2-3 minutes. Finish with coriander leaves and lemon juice. Cool and keep aside. Prepare tamarind mayo by mixing tamarind chutney with mayonnaise. For tacos: cut bread slices into circles using cookie cutter or lid. Flatten with rolling pin. Heat pan with butter and toast bread on both sides until golden. Fold in half while hot to create taco shell. Keep aside to harden. Assembly: fill taco shells with vada mixture, coat with red sukha chutney and drizzle with tamarind mayonnaise. Serve immediately.

name: Masala Pasta
instructions: Set pan on high heat with oil, butter and jeera. Let jeera crackle then add onions, ginger garlic paste and green chillies. Cook until onions turn translucent. Add tomatoes and salt, cook on high flame for 4-5 minutes. Mash everything with potato masher. Lower flame and add ketchup, red chilli sauce and all powdered spices. Add water to avoid burning spices, cook for 2-3 minutes. Add raw pasta, carrots and sweet corn. Mix well and add enough water to cover pasta 1 cm above surface. Stir once. Cover and cook on medium-low flame until pasta is cooked, stirring occasionally. Open lid, check doneness and adjust seasoning. Add capsicum and cook for 2-3 minutes on high flame. Lower flame and grate processed cheese as per preference. Finish with coriander. For bread: mix soft butter, cheese, garlic, coriander, green chillies, oregano, red chilli flakes and black pepper. Apply mixture on bread slice and toast in buttered pan until cheese melts and bread turns crispy. Serve hot pasta with cheese chilli garlic bread.

name: Lasooni Palak Khichdi
instructions: Wash rice and moong dal separately and soak for at least 30 minutes. Strain water and transfer to pressure cooker. Add salt, turmeric powder and water to 2 inches above dal surface. Pressure cook for 1 whistle on medium heat. Once whistled, switch off and allow to depressurize naturally. Open lid and lightly stir with fork. Blanch cleaned spinach in boiling salted water for 15-30 seconds, immediately dip in ice cold water. Transfer blanched spinach to blender with mint leaves, coriander, green chillies and garlic. Blend into fine puree. For tadka: heat ghee and jeera on medium-high heat. Let jeera crackle, add hing, ginger, garlic and broken red chillies. Cook for a minute. Add onions and cook until translucent. Lower heat to medium and add tomatoes with salt and powdered spices. Stir and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add water to avoid burning. Cook until tomatoes are mushy. Add spinach puree and cook for 4-5 minutes. Add cooked moong dal and rice with boiling water. Stir gently and cook. Taste and adjust salt. Add lemon juice. For 2nd tadka: heat ghee, add garlic until light golden brown. Add hing, whole red chillies and pinch of red chilli powder. Pour over khichdi and serve hot with cucumber mint raita. For raita: peel and grate cucumber, sprinkle salt and squeeze excess moisture. Mix curd with powdered sugar, mint paste and black salt. Pass through sieve. Add grated cucumber, jeera powder and black pepper. Chill and serve.

name: Homemade Chicken Nuggets
instructions: Wash and clean boneless chicken well and cut into small pieces. Transfer to food processor or grinding jar and mince chicken with salt, pepper powder and garlic powder. Mix everything well and combine thoroughly. Transfer chicken mixture onto butter paper. Dip spatula in cold water and shape mixture into 1 cm thick rectangle slab. Cut and shape into 1.5 x 2 inch rectangles or preferred size and shape. Prepare three bowls with refined flour, whisked eggs mixed with pinch of salt, and bread crumbs mixed with salt and black pepper. Start coating chicken nuggets by first dipping in refined flour, then dipping and coating in whisked eggs, finally coating with bread crumbs. Coat all nuggets and keep aside. Option to store in zip lock bag in deep freezer. To fry: heat oil in wok to medium temperature and deep fry coated chicken nuggets until crisp and golden brown and chicken is cooked through. Serve hot and crispy with tomato ketchup or dip of choice.

name: Mini Cheese Burst Pizza
instructions: For cheese sauce: mix processed cheese, milk and butter in microwave-safe bowl, microwave at high for 30 seconds, whisk for 30 seconds, microwave again for 30 seconds and whisk until smooth and silky.
