Transfer to squeezy bottle. For pizza: cut sandwich bread into equal circles with cookie cutter, flatten one disc with rolling pin. Add cheese sauce dollop on unflattened disc and spread evenly, top with flattened bread and seal edges with thumb and index finger using water on edges. Spread pizza sauce, add mozzarella cheese and toppings of choice. Place in microwave with grill mode at 180°C for 6-7 minutes. For snowman variant: use two sized discs to form body and head, seal with water, add sauce, cheese and decorate with olives for eyes/buttons and bell pepper for muffler. Serve immediately while cheese oozes.

name: Masala Vada Pav
instructions: Prepare chutneys first. For coconut chutney: grind fresh coconut, green chillies, roasted chana dal, cumin powder and salt into fine paste. Make tadka with oil, urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, mustard seeds and curry leaves, add to chutney. For red garlic chutney: grind soaked red chillies, garlic, cumin powder, black salt and lemon juice into fine paste. Make batter by mixing besan with salt and water to smooth consistency, whisk for 4-5 minutes. Let rest 15-20 minutes. Make kharda by grinding green chillies, garlic and ginger into paste. Prepare aloo mixture by heating oil, adding mustard seeds and cumin until they crackle, adding asafoetida and curry leaves, then kharda, turmeric powder and garam masala. Add boiled mashed potatoes, lemon juice and coriander, cook 3-4 minutes while mashing. Cool to room temperature and shape into medium balls. Heat oil for deep frying, coat vadas with batter and deep fry on medium-high heat until golden brown. Fry green chillies briefly and coat with salt. Serve hot vadas with chutneys.

name: Chicken Bhuna
ingredients: boneless chicken 1 kg breast and thigh
instructions: Prepare chutneys: For green chutney, grind mint, coriander, ginger, green chillies, garlic, anardana powder, black salt with ice cubes and water until runny consistency. For red chutney, grind soaked red chillies, garlic, tamarind pulp, jaggery, cumin powder, black salt and black pepper into fine paste. Marinate chicken: wash and cut into small cubes, mix with salt, black pepper, red chilli powder, ginger garlic paste, green chilli paste and vinegar. Heat tawa with oil and ghee, add cumin and let splutter. Add finely chopped onions with salt and cook on medium flame until golden brown. Add turmeric powder and ginger garlic paste, cook until raw smell is gone. Lower heat, add red chilli paste and powdered spices with hot water to avoid burning. Add tomato puree, salt, black pepper, coriander stems and fresh coriander, cook on medium-high until tomatoes are cooked and ghee releases. Cook without water for proper bhuno. Add cashew paste and yogurt, stir to avoid curdling. Increase heat to medium and cook 10-15 minutes, stirring frequently until ghee releases. Add marinated chicken, cook on high flame until it takes shape, then lower heat and cook on medium until tender. Add hot water to adjust consistency and cook for few more minutes. Finish with garam masala, kasuri methi, green chillies, fresh coriander and lemon juice. Serve hot.

name: Chicken Lollipop
ingredients: salt and pepper powder to taste
instructions: Shape lollipops: divide each wing into drumette with one bone and wingette with two bones. Trim drumette, scrape meat upwards, collect and shape like lollipop. For wingette, run knife at bottom to separate bone joint, scrape meat upwards while separating thinner bone and discarding it. Marinate: place shaped lollipops in mixing bowl, add ginger garlic paste, crushed green chillies, salt, pepper, soy sauce, vinegar, schezwan sauce and red chilli sauce, mix well. Add egg, refined flour and cornflour, coat well and marinate for 15-20 minutes or refrigerate. Fry: heat oil in wok, slide lollipops in hot oil just before frying to hold shape. Deep fry on medium-low heat until chicken is cooked and crispy golden brown. Optional double-fry method: fry on medium-low for 6-7 minutes until cooked, then refry in hot oil on high flame for 1-2 minutes for extra crispiness. Serve hot with schezwan chutney or dipping sauce.

name: Cheese and Corn Bread Samosa
instructions: Prepare spinach filling: clean and wash spinach thoroughly. Blanch in boiling water for 15-20 seconds, immediately dip in ice cold water to retain colour. Lightly squeeze to remove excess water, transfer to blender and blend into coarse paste with little water. Prepare base filling: mix grated paneer, cheese, sweet corn kernels, green chillies, salt and black pepper. Divide into two equal batches. For spinach variant: add spinach paste to one batch, add lemon juice and mix well, taste and adjust salt. Keep both fillings aside. Assemble samosa: flatten bread slices thin with rolling pin, trim sides and corners, cut diagonally into two equal halves. Apply water on cut edge, bring corners together to form cone, press edges to seal. Pinch top to close cone completely. Fill with choice of filling, press lightly without overfilling. Apply water on opening side and seal to make samosa. Fry: heat oil and deep fry samosas in hot oil on medium-high flame until crisp and golden brown. Remove on kitchen towel. Serve hot and crispy with ketchup, mayo or dipping sauce.

name: Veg Pot Rice
instructions: Cook rice: wash basmati rice thoroughly and soak for 15-20 minutes. Boil water in stock pot, strain rice and add to boiling water with sliced red chillies, star anise, salt and oil. Cook on medium flame for 8-10 minutes until almost done, strain and keep aside. Prepare gravy: heat wok on medium, add oil, garlic, ginger, fresh red chillies and star anise, stir and cook for 3-4 minutes. Add vegetable stock and bring to boil on high flame. Add soy sauces, oyster sauce, vinegar, green chilli paste, aromat powder, salt and white pepper powder, stir well. Add harder vegetables (baby corn, carrot, french beans, zucchini, bell peppers, onion petals, mushrooms) and cook for 3-4 minutes on high flame. Add softer green vegetables (blanched broccoli, bok choy, spring onion greens) and honey, cook for 2 minutes on high flame. Make cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch and water in small bowl, add to sauce while stirring. Cook until sauce thickens. Assemble: use earthen pot or pan, add cooked rice and pour gravy with vegetables, garnish with fresh spring onion greens. Cover with lid and cook on low flame for 5-10 minutes (similar to biryani assembly). Serve immediately with favourite condiments.

name: Crispy Vegetable Cutlet
instructions: Mix boiled and grated potatoes with all vegetables, spices, and soaked poha. Add cornstarch and mix until the mixture holds shape. Grease palms with oil, take a spoonful, roll into a ball then shape into a cylinder. Coat the shaped cutlet in dry refined flour, dip in refined flour slurry, and coat with crushed vermicelli. Deep freeze for 5-10 minutes to set. Deep fry in hot oil on medium-high heat until crisp and golden brown. Serve hot with ketchup or dip of choice.

name: Vegetable Manchurian
instructions: Mix chopped vegetables with ginger, garlic, sauces, seasoning and butter. Add refined flour and cornflour, mix well and squeeze lightly. Rest 5 minutes. Dip hands in water, shape mixture into balls. Deep fry at 150-160°C on medium flame until crisp and golden. In a separate wok, sauté onions, ginger, chillies, garlic; add vegetable stock, sauces, and seasonings. Bring to boil. Make cornstarch slurry and add to thicken sauce. Add fried manchurian balls and cook 1-2 minutes. Serve immediately with fried rice.

name: Tari Poha
instructions: Soak chana overnight and pressure cook for 2-3 whistles. Reserve chana water. Make kala masala by roasting spices and grinding into fine powder. Wash poha and soak for 10 minutes. Heat oil, fry peanuts until roasted. Sauté mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves; add onions until translucent. Add turmeric, sugar, salt, potatoes; add poha and mix gently for 3-4 minutes. For tari: heat oil with dry coconut until brown. Add onions, ginger, garlic; roast whole spices for 2 minutes; cool and grind into paste. Heat oil, add jeera, rai, bay leaves; add paste and cook until golden. Add powdered spices and cook until oil separates. Add cooked chana, coriander, reserved water and 1-1.5 litres water. Boil for 20-25 minutes. Add amchur powder, tomatoes, and cook 5-7 minutes. Serve hot poha topped with kaccha chiwda and tari.

name: Stuffed Mango Kulfi
instructions: Set heavy bottom vessel on medium heat, add milk and bring to boil. Once boiling, add khoya and crushed elaichi, stir continuously until khoya dissolves. Wash mangoes, cut sides to scoop flesh, and squeeze seed for pulp. Grind mango flesh into fine puree (make 400 gm). Continue cooking milk, scraping sides, until reduced to half. Add sugar and cook 10-15 minutes until milk reduces to 1/3. Divide half for malai kulfi and keep half in wok for mango kulfi. Add fresh mango puree and cook 5 minutes on low flame. Cool both bases to room temperature. Trim mango heads, carefully remove seed without damaging mango, fill cavity with cooled kulfi mixture. Freeze for 6-8 hours. After freezing, peel mango skin and cut into disks. Serve immediately garnished with nuts.

name: Vegetable Kolhapuri
instructions: Dry roast whole spices on low heat for 1-2 minutes. Add coconut and roast 3-4 minutes until light brown. Cool and grind into paste. Grind tomatoes and boiled cashews together into fine puree. Half-fry vegetables separately on high flame 1-2 minutes each and set aside. Heat oil with jeera, bay leaves, dried red chillies. Add onions until light golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies, cook 1-2 minutes. Add turmeric and red chilli powder briefly on low flame. Add kolhapuri base gravy with 150-200 ml water. Cook 4-5 minutes until oil separates. Add tomato-cashew puree and salt, cook 4-5 minutes. Add kashmiri red chilli paste and cook 5-6 minutes. Add stir-fried vegetables carefully. Add water to adjust gravy consistency. Add paneer, garam masala, kasuri methi, coriander, lemon juice. Cook 1-2 minutes. Serve hot with roti or naan.

name: Amritsari Kulcha
instructions: Dough: Mix warm water, milk, curd, sugar, ghee. Sift dry ingredients and add to liquid. Knead well for 12-15 minutes until smooth, soft, stretchy. Apply ghee, cover with cling wrap. Rest 1 hour in warm place. Knead again, divide into equal balls, apply oil, rest 30 minutes covered. Filling: Dry roast jeera and coriander seeds, cool and crush coarsely. Grate boiled potatoes, mix with all ingredients and roasted spices. Add onions just before use. Chutney: Strain soaked tamarind pulp, mix with water and all remaining ingredients. Assemble: Roll dough ball, fill with potato mixture, seal edges, flatten slightly. Cook on tava/griddle or tandoor until golden. Chutney: Adjust consistency with water as preferred. Serve hot kulcha with tamarind-onion chutney.

name: Paneer Crust Pizza
instructions: Herbed paneer: Heat milk to medium, stir, bring to boil. Add oregano, red chilli flakes, chopped basil, salt. Cook 3-4 minutes. Mix vinegar and water, add slowly to boiling milk. Strain through sieve when curds separate, wash with fresh water. Divide in two halves, wrap in muslin cloth in square shape, stack in sieve with heavy weight for 1-2 hours. Coating: Make smooth refined flour slurry without lumps, add salt and pepper. Add salt and pepper to breadcrumbs. Dip herbed paneer slab in flour slurry, coat with breadcrumbs, deep fry in hot oil on medium-high heat until crisp and golden. Pizza assembly: Apply pizza sauce on fried paneer crust, top with mozzarella cheese and veggies. Bake in oven for 5 minutes at 200°C or cook on pan covered until cheese melts. Cut into desired slices and serve hot.

name: Mixed Vegetables
instructions: Blanch cauliflower: Boil water with salt and turmeric, submerge cauliflower for half a minute to remove impurities, remove and keep aside. Ginger-garlic paste: Add green chillies, ginger, garlic, salt to mortar pestle and crush coarsely. Heat wok with oil and ghee, add jeera to splutter. Add crushed ginger-garlic paste and sauté 3-4 minutes on medium flame. Add roughly chopped onions, cook until light golden brown. Add turmeric powder and cook 30 seconds. Add chopped tomatoes with salt, cook until mushy. Add coriander and red chilli powder, mix well, cook 2-3 minutes on low flame. Add water to prevent masalas burning, cook until ghee separates. Add blanched cauliflower and other raw vegetables, mix well, cook on medium-high flame for 5 minutes. Cover and cook 15-20 minutes on medium-low flame, stirring occasionally. Check vegetable doneness. Add kasuri methi, garam masala, lemon juice, fresh coriander. Mix gently and serve hot with roti or paratha.

name: Homemade Mango Squash
instructions: Remove pulp from ripe mangoes and blend into fine puree (need ~1 kg pulp). In a wok on medium heat, dissolve sugar in water. Add citric acid and remove impurities that float to the surface. Cook until one-string consistency (test by dipping spatula, pinching between fingers to see a string form). Switch off flame and add mango puree and salt, whisk well. Pass through sieve to remove pulp fibers. Transfer to sterilized glass bottles and submerge in hot water to sterilize and increase shelf life. Cool to room temperature and refrigerate. Use as concentrate for drinks (dilute with water, ice), milkshakes, or popsicles.

name: Tandoori Paneer Bread Samosa
instructions: For filling: Add paneer, coriander, mint leaves, powdered spices, ginger-garlic paste, and green chillies to food processor and grind coarsely. Smoke the mixture by placing live charcoal in centre, pouring ghee over it, covering and letting it smoke for 3-4 minutes. For samosa: Flatten bread slices thin with rolling pin, trim corners. Divide each slice diagonally into two triangles. Apply water on cut edge and bring corners together to form cone, press edges to seal. Fill cone with tandoori paneer filling (don't overfill). Apply water on edges and seal to form complete samosa. Rest for 5 minutes. Heat oil and deep fry samosas in hot oil until crisp and golden brown. Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or dip of choice.

name: Veg Manchow Momo Soup
instructions: For momos - dough: Mix maida, salt, water to make semi-stiff dough. Knead until smooth and rest 15-30 minutes. Knead again and divide into small balls. Flatten and coat with dry flour, roll into thin chapati. Cut 3-inch circles with cutter. For filling: Mix cabbage, carrots, onions, garlic, ginger, chilli paste, soy sauce, spring onion greens and salt. Place spoonful of filling in centre of each wrapper. Shape momos by pinching from one side, making pleats, pinching at each pleat in semicircular motion until sealed. Boil salted water, slide in momos and cook for 5-7 minutes until they float. For soup: Heat wok on high flame, add oil, garlic, ginger, green chillies and coriander stems, sauté 1 minute. Add vegetable stock and bring to boil. Add all veggies, both soy sauces, vinegar, white pepper, sugar, cook on high flame. Mix cornstarch with water to make slurry, add to soup and cook until thickened. Finish with fresh coriander and spring onion greens. Serve momos in hot manchow soup.

name: Garlic Bread Omelette Sandwich
instructions: For garlic butter: Mix soft butter with chopped garlic, fresh coriander, oregano, red chilli flakes, black pepper and green chillies in a bowl. Store in fridge. For egg-mayo filling: Grate boiled eggs and mix with mayonnaise, chopped green chillies, spring onion greens, salt and black pepper. For cheesy garlic bread omelette sandwich: Apply garlic butter on one side of bread slice and toast until golden brown, flip and toast other side until crisp. Whisk 2 eggs with salt, black pepper and fresh coriander. Heat ghee/oil in pan, pour whisked eggs to make omelette, cook until almost done. Place toasted garlic bread on egg facing garlic butter side up, press gently and flip, lower flame and fold egg sides inward. Place cheese slice, flip one bread side to make sandwich, cut and serve hot with dip. Alternative: fold omelette in square shape, place on toasted garlic bread, add cheese slice and egg-mayo mixture, drizzle ketchup and red chilli sauce, close sandwich, cut and serve.

name: Healthy Peri Peri Paneer Wrap
ingredients: thick curd 1 cup for creamy sauce
instructions: For spinach chapati: Mix wheat flour, spinach puree and salt. Add water in batches and knead well for 4-5 minutes to soft dough. Cover with damp cloth and rest 30 minutes. Divide into equal balls and roll into thin chapati. Cook on hot tawa from both sides until brown spots appear. For hot sauce: Char tomatoes on open flame, cool and remove skin. Grind charred tomatoes with soaked red chillies, green chilli, garlic, black salt, jeera powder, vinegar, black pepper, gud and water to smooth paste. Refrigerate. For creamy garlic sauce: Mix thick curd with garlic juice, lemon juice, fresh coriander, salt and black pepper. Refrigerate. For peri peri spice mix: Mix red chilli powder, black salt, cinnamon powder, garlic powder, ginger powder, oregano and salt. For paneer filling: Heat olive oil in pan, add garlic and green chillies, cook briefly. Add onions and cook 1-2 minutes. Add bell peppers and corn, cook 1-2 minutes. Add peri peri spice mix, salt and lemon juice, mix well. Add paneer cubes and stir gently. Finish with fresh coriander. Assembly: On spinach chapati, layer lettuce, peri peri paneer filling, drizzle garlic dip and hot sauce, add tomatoes, onions, fresh coriander and pomegranate seeds. Roll and serve.

name: Masala Idli
ingredients: butter 1 tbsp and oil 1 tsp for masala
instructions: For rava idlis: Mix rava, curd and salt in bowl and rest 30 minutes. Add water and mix to achieve batter consistency (not too thick or thin). Just before steaming, add baking soda to batter. Grease idli mold with oil and pour batter up to 3/4 full. Steam for 8-10 minutes until toothpick comes clean. Cool 1-2 minutes and demold. Set pan on medium heat with butter and shallow fry idlis on both sides until light golden brown. Cut idlis into quarters or half as preferred and keep aside. For masala idli: Heat pan on medium flame, add butter and oil. Add cumin seeds and sauté until they crackle. Add chopped green chillies and capsicum, sauté 1-2 minutes. Add onions and cook until translucent. Add red chilli paste, garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chilli powder and pav bhaji masala, mix and cook 1 minute. Add water to prevent masalas from burning, mix and cook until oil separates. Add chopped tomatoes and salt to taste, cook until tomatoes become mushy. Add shallow fried idli pieces and mix gently to coat with masala (don't overcook). Squeeze fresh lemon juice and finish with freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve immediately.

name: Cheesy Tava Paneer Hot Dog
instructions: For paneer filling: Heat oil in wok, add jeera and let it crackle. Add ginger garlic paste and chopped green chillies, sauté for 1 minute. Add chopped onions and cook until translucent. Add capsicum and sauté for 1-2 minutes. Lower flame and add powdered spices (turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder), mix well and cook for 1 minute. Increase flame and add chopped tomatoes, salt, ketchup, red chilli sauce, and garam masala. Cook until tomatoes are mushy. Add paneer pieces and cook for 3-4 minutes on medium-high heat. Finish with fresh coriander. For caramelized onions: Set pan on high flame, add butter and oil. Add thickly sliced onions with salt and sugar. Cook on medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until onions get a deep brown color. For cheese sauce: Set up a double boiler with water boiling in the base and a bowl on top. Add processed cheese, butter, and milk. Whisk continuously while adding milk gradually until cheese melts to desired consistency. For assembly: Make a slit in hot dog bun like vadapav. Toast bun on both sides with butter until light golden. Spread cheese sauce on toasted bun, add paneer filling, top with caramelized onions and more cheese sauce. Close and serve hot.

name: Eggless Chocolate Brownie
instructions: Choose your baking vessel: if using an oven, preheat to 180°C. If using a cooker or kadhai, add 1 kg of salt to the vessel and place a stand for keeping the baking tray (salt can be reused for future baking). Line an 8x8-inch baking tray with butter paper. Sift together refined flour, cocoa powder, salt, and baking powder. Set up a double boiler and add chocolate and butter to the bowl over the simmering water. Melt completely or use microwave for 30 seconds. To the melted chocolate, add yogurt, vanilla extract, and sugar. Whisk well until sugar dissolves completely. Combine the melted chocolate mixture with the sifted dry ingredients and mix until combined. Transfer the mixture to the butter-paper-lined tray and tap gently to remove air bubbles. If baking in an oven, bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes. If using a vessel, bake for 45-50 minutes. To check doneness, insert a toothpick - it should come out clean. Rest the brownies for at least 30 minutes before cutting into preferred shapes. Serve plain or topped with ice cream and chocolate sauce.

name: Creamy Veggie Pizza Toast
instructions: For pizza sauce: Wash tomatoes and make a cross slit. Immerse in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then immediately in cold water. Peel and grind into semi-fine puree. Heat oil in saucepan, add garlic and onions, cook on medium flame until translucent. Lower flame, add Kashmiri red chilli powder, cook for 15-20 seconds. Add tomato puree, salt, sugar, oregano, and red chilli flakes. Increase to medium heat and stir well. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes. Switch off and add basil leaves, tearing them roughly. For stir-fried veggies: Heat oil in wok, add garlic, cook for 1-2 minutes on high flame. Add carrot, french beans, sweet corn, and red bell pepper. Cook for 3-4 minutes. Add blanched broccoli, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1-2 minutes. For white sauce: Heat pan on medium-low, add butter and melt. Add flour and cook for 2-3 minutes without browning. Add milk in 3 batches, whisking well to avoid lumps. Cook for 3-4 minutes until thick and creamy. Add stir-fried veggies, oregano, and chilli flakes. Mix and cook for 1-2 minutes. For assembly: Apply butter on bread slice. Spread pizza sauce generously. Top with veggies in white sauce. Finish with mozzarella cheese. Bake in preheated oven at 200°C for 8-10 minutes until cheese melts, or use a pan with lid on medium-low flame until cheese melts and toast is crisp. Cut into squares or triangles and serve hot.

name: High Protein Multigrain Dosa
instructions: For dosa batter: Wash all grains, dals, and millets together 3-4 times until water is clear. Soak for 4-5 hours. After soaking, drain and rinse with fresh water. Transfer to mixer grinder, add green chillies and ginger. Add very little water and grind to make a fine thick paste (do not add excess water - keep consistency like regular dosa batter). Transfer ground batter to large vessel and ferment overnight in a warm place. After fermentation, lightly mix the batter and add salt to taste. For coconut chutney: Add fresh coconut, roasted chana dal, green chillies, jeera powder, salt, and black pepper powder to grinding jar. Grind to make a fine thick chutney, adding little water to adjust consistency. For tadka: Set pan on medium heat, add oil. Add urad dal and chana dal, cook for a few seconds. Add mustard seeds, dry red chillies, and curry leaves. Cook for a few seconds until fragrant. Pour tadka over chutney and mix well. For making dosa: Set dosa pan on medium heat. Spray some water to control temperature and wipe with cloth. Add a spoonful of fermented dosa batter and spread evenly without hurrying. Let batter dry slightly, add ghee and desired toppings. Cook on medium-high heat until bottom is golden brown and dosa releases from pan easily. Roll or fold as desired using a spatula-friendly utensil. Serve hot with coconut chutney. For variations: For Peri Peri Paneer Dosa, grate paneer and sprinkle peri peri spice mix while cooking. For Vegetable Uttapam, keep batter slightly thicker, add chopped vegetables, podi masala, and ghee. Lightly press toppings with spatula, flip and cook until vegetables are done and bottom is golden brown.

name: chicken shawarma rice
instructions: For rice: Wash and soak basmati rice 15 minutes. Heat ghee, add onions and garlic paste, cook until translucent. Add whole spices, turmeric powder and sauté. Add boiling water, saffron, soaked rice and salt. Cover and cook 7-8 minutes on medium low heat until water is absorbed. Fluff with fork. For garlic sauce: Mix curd, mayonnaise, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic juice, sugar, salt, pepper and fresh coriander. Keep in fridge. For hot sauce: Grind soaked red chillies, garlic, jeera powder, black pepper, black salt, sugar, vinegar, lemon juice and olive oil with water to smooth paste consistency. For chicken: Marinate boneless chicken with salt, chilli powder, jeera powder, coriander powder, turmeric, black pepper, curd, garlic paste, olive oil, vinegar and lemon juice for 1-2 hours or overnight. Cook marinated chicken on medium high heat 4-5 minutes each side until cooked and tender. Shred into smaller pieces. Assembly: Place rice in serving bowl, add vegetables, grilled shredded chicken, drizzle white garlic sauce and hot sauce. Serve with warm pita bread.

name: lasooni anda malai masala
instructions: For cashew paste: Boil water with onions and cashew nuts 10-12 minutes on high flame. Strain and rinse well. Grind with 100 ml fresh water to fine smooth paste. For eggs: Heat tawa or wide pan with oil and butter. Shallow fry boiled eggs from all sides until light golden brown. Remove and keep aside. In same pan on low heat, add more oil or butter if needed. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon and black cardamom. Stir once and add garlic and green chillies. Cook on low flame until garlic is well cooked. Add fresh coriander, cumin powder, white pepper powder, garam masala and black pepper powder. Add prepared cashew paste and stir well on medium low heat. Add salt and sugar. Cook 5-7 minutes stirring continuously. Adjust consistency with hot water if needed. Cook further 1-2 minutes. Add fried eggs, julienned ginger, green chillies, fresh cream and grated boiled eggs. Stir lightly and cook 2-3 minutes. Serve hot with tandoori roti or naan.

name: mutton shami kebab
instructions: Set wok on medium heat, add ghee and whole spices. Cook 1 minute. Add onions, garlic and ginger, cook until onions are translucent. Add mutton mince and soaked chana dal with salt. Stir and cook on medium high flame. Once mutton releases water, cover and cook on medium low flame. Stir regularly. After 30 minutes, add hot water and continue cooking. After 1 hour, mutton and dal should be cooked completely. Add powdered spices and fresh coriander. Stir and cook 1 minute until no excess water remains. Transfer to bowl to cool. Once cooled, grind mixture in food processor to fine paste, discarding cinnamon stick. Add chopped coriander, mint leaves and lemon juice. Mix well. Take spoonfuls of mixture and shape into tikkis. Heat pan with ghee on medium heat. Dip kebabs in beaten eggs and shallow fry on both sides until golden brown. Serve with chutneys, onion rings and fresh mint leaves.

name: paneer shashlik rice
instructions: For rice: Wash and soak basmati rice 15 minutes. Heat ghee, add onions and garlic paste, cook until translucent. Add whole spices, turmeric powder and sauté. Add boiling water, saffron, soaked rice and salt. Cover and cook 7-8 minutes on medium low heat until water absorbed. Fluff with fork. For garlic sauce: Mix curd, mayonnaise, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic juice, sugar, salt, pepper and fresh coriander. Keep in fridge. For hot sauce: Grind soaked red chillies, garlic, jeera powder, black pepper, black salt, sugar, vinegar, lemon juice and olive oil with water to smooth paste. For paneer shashlik: In bowl mix marinade ingredients with olive oil, garlic paste, chilli powder, oregano, jeera powder, black pepper, lemon juice, salt and fresh coriander. Cut paneer, vegetables into equal-sized squares. Add to marinade and mix gently. Marinate 15 minutes. Use bamboo skewers and prick vegetables and paneer cubes alternately. Set grill pan and grill shashlik from all sides until golden brown. Assembly: Serve rice on plate, place grilled paneer shashlik on top. Drizzle creamy garlic sauce and hot sauce. Serve immediately.

name: crispy butter garlic salt and pepper prawns
instructions: Clean prawns by deshelling while keeping tail on. Take sharp knife and cut prawn 90% from back to butterfly shape, keeping intact. Remove black vein and wash nicely. Transfer cleaned prawns to bowl and add salt, black pepper powder, ginger garlic paste, soy sauce, chinese cooking wine, egg white and cornflour. Mix and coat well. Mix cornstarch, refined flour, salt and black pepper. Coat prawns thoroughly with flour mixture. Use palm heel to flatten slightly. Dust off excess flour. Deep fry prawns in hot oil until crispy and light golden brown. For tossing: Set wok on medium heat, add butter and oil, garlic and green chillies. Cook 2-3 minutes. Add dry red chillies, red chilli flakes, ground black pepper, spring onion bulbs, almond slivers, light soy sauce, sugar and chinese cooking wine. Stir and cook 30 seconds. Add fried prawns and spring onion greens. Switch off flame and toss well. Serve immediately.

name: stir fried vegetable pasta
instructions: Set water for boiling and add salt and oil. When water boils, add pasta and cook 7-8 minutes until al dente. Strain pasta and immediately drizzle with oil. Season with salt and pepper powder, toss well to coat evenly. Keep aside and reserve some pasta water. Set wok on medium high heat, add olive oil, garlic, ginger and green chillies. Cook 1-2 minutes. Add carrots and mushroom, cook 1-2 minutes on high flame. Add yellow and green zucchini, cook 1-2 minutes on high flame. Add red, yellow and green bell peppers, broccoli and corn kernels. Cook 1-2 minutes on high flame. Add salt, black pepper powder, oregano, chilli flakes and soy sauce. Toss and cook 1-2 minutes. Add cooked pasta, spring onion greens, lemon juice and coriander leaves. Toss well and add 50 ml reserved pasta water. Toss and cook 1-2 minutes. Healthy stir fried pasta is ready. Serve hot and garnish with fried garlic and spring onion greens.

name: Cheese Stuffed Paneer Tikka
instructions: Cut paneer into square slices of 0.5 cm thickness. Slice cheese slightly thinner than paneer and sandwich between two paneer slices. Prepare marinade: roast besan in ghee until aromatic, cool and add to hung curd along with cashew paste, cream, mustard oil, ginger-garlic paste, green chilli paste, and all spices. Smoke marinade with live charcoal and ghee for 3-4 minutes. Ensure marinade is thick. Cut capsicum and tomatoes into squares matching paneer size, and quarter onions. Coat paneer sandwiches with marinade and skewer on wooden skewers alternating with vegetables, ensuring veggies are on ends. Cook on open flame over skewer holders, brush with melted butter, and cook again on flame until charred. Serve hot with dahi wali hari chutney and chaat masala.

name: Tandoori Laccha Paratha
instructions: Mix wheat flour and salt, add water gradually to knead semi-soft dough, add oil and knead for 7-8 minutes. Cover with damp cloth and rest for 30 minutes. For pudina powder: dry mint in microwave (3 minutes, mix, 1 minute more) or sun-dry, then crush by hand. Divide rested dough into equal balls. For pudina paratha: coat dough ball with dry flour, roll thin chapati, brush ghee, sprinkle pudina powder and salt, fold with pleats, roll into thick paratha, brush ghee and sprinkle more pudina powder. For mirchi paratha: roll thin, brush ghee, sprinkle red chilli powder and chopped green chillies, fold into cone, flatten to disc, brush ghee and add more chillies and coriander. Cook on hot iron tawa or cooker wall over direct flame, flipping until crisp and golden. Serve hot with butter and chaat masala.

name: Besan Papdi
instructions: Grind roasted urad dal into powder. Mix chickpea flour with urad dal powder, oil, carom seeds, black pepper, red chilli, asafoetida, baking soda, and salt. Add water gradually to make a thick, crumbly dough. Roll dough thin between plastic sheets. Cut into thin strips. Heat oil to medium-high temperature and fry papdi strips until golden and crisp, turning occasionally. Drain on paper towels. Store in airtight container.

name: Oats Idli with Coconut Chana Chutney
instructions: Mix oats, gram flour, and curd. Add water gradually and mix well. Let rest for 10 minutes to puff. Add chopped carrot, capsicum, green chilli, ginger, and salt to batter. Mix well. Boil water in steamer vessel and grease idli plates. Add eno fruit salt to batter and mix well. Divide batter into greased plates and place in steamer. Steam for 12 minutes on medium flame. For chutney: blend coconut, roasted chickpea, salt, green chillies, lemon juice, and water until smooth. Prepare tadka: heat oil, add mustard seeds, red chillies, and curry leaves. Pour tadka over chutney and mix. Serve hot idlis with coconut chana chutney and tadka.

name: Apple Coconut Burfi
instructions: Peel and grate 3 medium apples finely, discarding cores. Heat ghee in pan and add grated apples. Saute on medium flame for about 5 minutes until fragrant and mashy. Add 300 grams sugar to apples and cook on low-medium flame until sugar dissolves completely. Grind more than 1/2 cup peanuts to fine powder. Once sugar dissolves, add peanut powder and 100 grams desiccated coconut to pan and mix well. Cook on low-medium flame until mixture attains curdling consistency. Add 2 tbsp almond flakes and 1 tsp coarsely crushed cardamom, mix well. Pour mixture into greased tray and spread evenly. Garnish with almond flakes. Leave for 2 hours to set. Cut into desired pieces and serve.

name: Green Moong Dal Pakoda
instructions: Soak split green gram for 2-3 hours. Blend soaked moong dal with 1-inch ginger and 4 green chillies into fine paste. Transfer to bowl. Add 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 3/4 tsp red chilli powder, 1 pinch asafoetida, and 1/2 cup finely chopped methi to paste. Whisk mixture for 4-5 minutes. Cut cauliflower into florets and potato into slices. Dip potato slices and cauliflower florets in batter and fry in medium-hot oil until golden brown on all sides. For chutney: blend 1 cup coriander leaves, 1/2 lemon juice, 1/2 inch ginger, 4 green chillies, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp salt, and 2-3 tbsp water until fine. Serve hot pakoras with coriander chutney and tomato sauce.

name: Coconut Pak (Nariyal Paag)
instructions: For Mawa Coconut Pak: Grate or gound dry coconut and poppy seeds. Grind to fine powder. Heat ghee and add coconut-poppy seed powder to it. Roast lightly. Add 1 cup mawa and mix well. Add 1 cup sugar powder, 1/2 tsp nutmeg, and 1/2 tsp cardamom powder. Mix thoroughly and cook on low flame until mixture comes together, stirring constantly. Pour into greased tray and spread evenly. Let set for 2-3 hours. Cut into pieces. For Sugar Coconut Pak: Grind dry coconut and poppy seeds to fine powder. Heat ghee and roast coconut-poppy powder lightly. Add 1.5 cups sugar, 1 tsp white pepper, 1/2 tsp nutmeg, and 1/2 tsp cardamom powder. Mix well and cook on low flame until mixture thickens and comes together, stirring frequently. Pour into greased tray and let set 2-3 hours. Cut into pieces.

name: Paneer Khurma
instructions: Crumble paneer finely. Dissolve sugar in water to make a light syrup. Add crumbled paneer to the syrup and cook on medium heat, stirring frequently until the mixture thickens and reaches desired consistency. The paneer absorbs the sugar syrup and becomes soft and sweet. Serve warm or chilled.

name: Singhare ki Lapsi
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan. Add water chestnut flour and roast for 2-3 minutes on medium heat, stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Add sugar and roasted cardamom powder, mix well. Add water gradually to achieve desired pudding consistency. Cook for 5-7 minutes till well combined. Serve warm.

name: Ring Murukku
instructions: Mix rice flour, urad flour, salt, and all spices in a bowl. Add water gradually to form a soft dough. Transfer to a piping bag with a round nozzle. Heat oil in a deep pan. Pipe dough into rings directly into hot oil and fry until golden and crispy. Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Store in airtight container.

name: Katlambe
instructions: Mix refined flour, salt, and oil. Add water gradually to form soft dough. Knead for 3-4 minutes, cover and rest 20 minutes. Knead again and divide into 14 portions. Roll thin sheets, apply oil and dust with rice flour and carom seeds. Layer 6-7 sheets together. Roll into big sheet, cut into strips, roll strips into spirals and flatten into peda shape. Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides. Serve hot with chole or chutney.

name: Matar Masala Bati
instructions: Combine wheat flour with crushed green peas, cumin, carom seeds, chopped green coriander, green chilli, and ginger. Add salt and baking soda. Mix in ghee and knead into a firm dough using water if needed. Form into round balls. Steam in a steamer or pressure cooker until cooked through. Serve hot with dal or curry.

name: Custard Apple Basundi
instructions: Boil 1 liter full cream milk. Extract pulp from 2 custard apples by sieving and discarding seeds. Simmer milk over medium heat, stirring at intervals, until reduced to half. Add coarsely crushed cardamom pods and sugar to thickened milk. Turn off flame and cool. After 10 minutes, fold in custard apple pulp and mix well. Transfer to bowl, garnish with pistachio flakes, and refrigerate for 1 hour before serving.

name: Palak Mangodi Ki Sabji
instructions: Soak mangodi in water for 15 minutes. Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds. When seeds crackle, add asafetida and tomato pieces. Add ginger and green chilli, then the soaked mangodi. Stir in turmeric, coriander, and red chilli powder. Cook until tomatoes break down. Add fenugreek powder and chopped spinach. Simmer until spinach wilts. Stir in milk cream and garam masala. Cook for 2-3 minutes more and serve hot.

name: Crispy Namkeen Chips
instructions: Mix refined flour with oil, carom seeds, chaat masala, and salt. Knead into a firm dough using water. Roll out thin on a flat surface. Cut into chip-sized strips or desired shapes. Heat oil in a deep pan and fry chips in batches until golden and crispy, stirring occasionally to ensure even cooking. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Store in an airtight container.

name: Ginger Barfi
instructions: Peel and finely chop fresh ginger. Grind to a smooth paste. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and add ginger paste. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently for 10-12 minutes until ginger browns and moisture evaporates. Add jaggery and cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly. Spread mixture on a greased plate or tray. Once set, cut into pieces and store in an airtight container.

name: Champakali Nimki
instructions: Mix refined flour with cumin seeds, carom seeds, red chilli powder, black pepper, and salt. Add oil and knead into a firm dough using minimal water. Roll thin between plastic sheets. Cut into decorative champakali or strip shapes using a knife or cutter. Heat oil in a deep pan and fry in batches until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and store in airtight container.

name: Poha Modak
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and lightly roast almonds, cashews, and pistachios until fragrant. Remove and set aside. In the same pan, add poha and roast for 1-2 minutes. Pour in milk slowly and stir well to prevent lumps. Add sugar and crushed cardamom. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently for 8-10 minutes until poha softens and mixture thickens. Fold in roasted nuts. Pour onto a greased plate, cool slightly, and shape into modak dumplings using your hands or a mold.

name: Dry Fruits Laddu
instructions: Dry roast sesame seeds, watermelon seeds, poppy seeds, dry coconut, fox nuts, almonds, and peanuts separately on a tawa until fragrant. Coarsely grind sesame and watermelon seeds together, then poppy seeds and coconut together, fox nuts separately, and almonds with peanuts. Mix all ground ingredients together. Melt jaggery in a heavy pan with water over medium heat until it reaches a syrup consistency. Add dry ginger powder, white pepper, nutmeg, and cardamom to the jaggery. Pour the melted jaggery into the dry fruit mixture and mix well. Cool until warm enough to handle. Apply ghee to hands and bind the mixture into round laddus.

name: Moong Dal Cheese Pizza
instructions: Soak moong dal and rice for 4-5 hours. Grind to a smooth paste with green chilli, ginger, and salt. Add eno and mix quickly to create fermentation. Spread mixture as a thin crust on a greased pan and cook over medium heat for 2-3 minutes. Spread pizza sauce on top, then layer mozzarella cheese, capsicum pieces, tomato pieces, and paneer cubes. Sprinkle oregano, black pepper, and chilli flakes. Cover and cook until cheese melts and crust is crispy at edges, about 5-7 minutes.

name: oats and vegetable cheela
instructions: Grind or blend oats into fine powder. Mix oats powder with curd and chickpea flour to make a batter. Add grated ginger, chopped green chilli, capsicum, carrot and tomato to the batter. Season with salt, turmeric powder, black pepper and fresh coriander leaves. Mix well. Heat a non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat, lightly oil it. Pour batter and spread thin like a cheela. Cook for 2-3 minutes until bottom is cooked, then flip and cook the other side. Serve hot with any chutney or yogurt.

name: achari chana pulao
instructions: Soak rice and chickpeas for 30 minutes. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed vessel, add tejpat, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and black pepper. Temper and add chopped red and green chillies, ginger paste. Add soaked rice and chickpeas, stir gently to coat with ghee. Add all ground spices (mustard powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder). Mix in yogurt and pickle masala. Add water (approximately 1 cup per rice portion), bring to boil. Reduce heat, cover and cook until rice and chickpeas are tender and liquid is absorbed. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve.

name: raw mango stuffed chilli pickle
instructions: Clean green chilies and make a small slit carefully. Dice raw mango into small pieces and stuff inside the chillies. Mix fennel powder, black mustard powder, fenugreek powder, turmeric powder, salt and asafetida in a bowl. Heat mustard oil until it smokes, allow to cool completely. Coat stuffed chillies with the spice powder. Layer chillies in a glass jar, pour cooled mustard oil over them. Ensure all chillies are submerged in oil. Cover and let mature for 3-4 days before serving. Keep refrigerated.

name: paneer jalebi
instructions: Crumble paneer into fine particles. Mix maida/corn flour, baking soda, food colouring and milk to make a smooth batter. Add crumbled paneer and mix well. Prepare sugar syrup by dissolving 2 cups sugar in 1 cup water with crushed cardamom, bring to boil and let simmer. Heat oil in a deep pan. Fill a piping bag with the paneer batter. Carefully pipe spiral shapes of batter into hot oil and fry until golden brown. Immediately dip the fried jalebi into hot sugar syrup. Remove and place on a rack to cool and drain. Serve once completely cooled.

name: veg zingy parcel
instructions: Prepare yeast dough by mixing flour, yeast, sugar, salt, oil and water. Knead well and let it rise for 1-2 hours until doubled in size. For filling, sauté ginger in butter, add tomato and capsicums, cook until soft. Add oregano, schezwan sauce and tomato sauce, mix in paneer cubes. Divide risen dough into portions, roll out thin and fill with paneer mixture. Fold edges to create parcel shape, seal properly. Place parcels in a pressure cooker on a stand or tray, cook for 3-4 whistles on medium heat. Cool and serve.

name: mixed vegetable navrang pickle
instructions: Cut all vegetables into small uniform pieces. Blanch vegetables by boiling in water for 3 minutes, drain and dry thoroughly on cloth under fan for 1.5 hours. Dry roast yellow mustard seeds for 1 minute. Dry roast fennel, fenugreek and cumin seeds for 1-1.5 minutes separately. Grind roasted spices coarsely. Heat mustard oil until smoking, turn off heat and cool. Add carom seeds, asafetida, black pepper to cooled oil. Add dried vegetables, raw turmeric, ginger and green chillies. Add black cumin, salt, black salt and red chilli powder. Mix in ground spice paste. Finally add vinegar and mix thoroughly. Store in glass jars for 3-4 days before serving.

name: Rasaj ki Kadhi
instructions: Prepare rasaj (besan fritters) by mixing besan with salt, cumin seeds, and turmeric powder, then deep fry until golden. Prepare kadhi by whisking besan and curd together, heat oil with cumin seeds and fenugreek seeds, add asafoetida and spices, add ginger paste and chillies, then add the besan-curd mixture and cook until thickened. Add the fried rasaj fritters to the kadhi and simmer.

name: Mixed Veg Tehri
instructions: Heat oil in cooker, add cumin seeds and whole spices like bay leaf and cinnamon. Sauté onions until golden. Add ginger and garlic paste, then finely chopped or diced mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, potato). Add rice and water in 1:2 ratio. Stir well and cover. Cook under pressure for one whistle.

name: Rice Papdi
instructions: Mix rice flour and refined flour with salt, cumin seeds, dry fenugreek leaves, and chilli flakes. Knead with oil to form a stiff dough. Roll out very thin sheets and cut into diamond or rectangular shapes. Deep fry in hot oil until crispy and golden brown. Drain and sprinkle chaat masala while still hot.

name: Aloo Ke Chapli Kabab
instructions: Boil and mash potatoes. Mix with crushed cumin seeds and coriander seeds, pomegranate powder, chaat masala, red chilli powder, salt, grated ginger, and finely chopped green chilli. Add diced or crushed tomato and refined flour to bind the mixture. Form into flat round patties. Shallow fry or deep fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides.

name: Mooli Besan Stuffed Paratha
instructions: Prepare dough with wheat flour, salt, and water. For stuffing, finely shred radish and mix with chickpea flour, grated ginger, finely chopped green chilli, coriander powder, red chilli powder, cumin seeds, carom seeds, turmeric powder, chopped coriander leaves, dry mango powder, and salt. Roll dough into circle, stuff with radish-besan mixture, fold edges, gently flatten, and pan-fry on griddle with oil until golden and cooked through.

name: Patti Samosa
instructions: Prepare dough with refined flour, oil, salt, and water. Roll into thin sheets and cut into long strips. For filling, mix boiled mashed potatoes with finely chopped cabbage, finely chopped green coriander, finely chopped green chilli, finely chopped ginger, cumin powder, and salt. Place filling on dough strip and fold into triangular samosa shape. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy.

name: Banana Chocolate Chip Cake
instructions: Mash ripe bananas in a bowl. Mix olive oil with mashed banana and curd. Add sugar and mix well. In separate bowl, sift refined flour, baking powder, and baking soda together. Fold dry ingredients into banana mixture. Add vanilla essence and chocolate chips. Pour into greased baking vessel. Cook in pressure cooker using water bath method for 25-30 minutes. Cool before serving.

name: chandrakala gujiya
instructions: Make filling by roasting mawa with ghee, sugar powder, semolina, coconut, and dry fruits. Add cardamom and nutmeg. Prepare dough with flour, ghee, and sugar syrup. Knead well and let rest. Roll thin, fill with mawa mixture, fold into half-moon shape, seal edges. Deep fry until golden brown and crispy.

name: veg rice fara
instructions: Heat oil, crackle mustard and cumin seeds, add curry leaves. Mix rice flour, baking soda, and salt. Add sautéed vegetables and spices. Add ginger paste, green chilli, and coriander. Knead with minimal water into stiff dough. Divide into balls, flatten on wet cloth, and roast on hot griddle or pan until golden and crispy. Serve hot.

name: makki ka dhokla
instructions: Mix cornmeal with salt and spices. Add curd and vegetables. Add ginger-chilli paste, fenugreek leaves, and fresh coriander. Mix well. Add baking soda and mix gently. Pour into greased pan. Steam for 20-25 minutes until cooked through. Cool and cut into pieces. Pan-fry with ghee until golden if desired.

name: green peas idli
instructions: Crush green peas coarsely. Roast mustard seeds and urad dal in oil. Combine semolina, curd, peas, spices, curry leaves, ginger, and chilli. Mix well. Add eno fruit salt gently just before steaming. Pour into idli molds and steam for 10-12 minutes. For peanut dip: grind peanuts with green chilli, lemon, and salt into coarse paste.

name: apple jam
instructions: Peel, core, and chop apples into small pieces. Add sugar and let sit overnight. Cook on high heat stirring frequently. Add lemon juice halfway through. Add cardamom and cinnamon for flavor. Continue cooking until jam reaches setting point (wrinkle test or 104-105C). Cool completely. Store in sterilized jars.

name: atta cake
instructions: Mix wheat flour, semolina, baking powder, baking soda, and cinnamon. In separate bowl combine apple puree, sugar, oil, and milk. Mix wet into dry ingredients gently. Pour into greased cake pan. Place pan in cooker with water (without whistle). Cook on medium-high heat for 20-25 minutes. Test with toothpick for doneness. Cool in pan for 5 minutes before turning out.

name: sweet koki
instructions: Dissolve sugar in water and boil until syrup cools. Mix wheat flour with half the ghee. Gradually add cooled syrup and knead into stiff dough. Cover and rest 10 minutes. Knead again with ghee and water until soft. Divide into 4 parts. Roll each into 3-3.5 inch thick round and mark cuts with knife. Roast on low heat, then fry in oil on both sides until golden brown. Repeat for each koki. Serve hot with mango pickle.

name: paneer nuggets
instructions: Crumble paneer finely. Mix with refined flour, corn flour, baking powder, black pepper, salt, red pepper powder, and chaat masala. Knead into firm mixture. Form into nugget shapes. Roll in breadcrumbs coating evenly. Heat oil and deep fry nuggets until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towel. Serve hot with tomato ketchup or mayo.

name: peanut sundal
instructions: Boil peanuts until tender. In a separate tempering vessel, heat oil and add mustard seeds until they crackle. Add urad dal and let it turn golden. Add curry leaves and dry red chilli. Pour this tempering over the boiled peanuts. Add fresh coconut, asafoetida, and salt. Mix well and serve.

name: aloo parwal curry
instructions: Cut parwal and potatoes into medium pieces. Heat oil and add cumin seeds. Add ginger and green chilli. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and red chilli powder. Add parwal and potato pieces. Cook on medium heat until vegetables are tender. Add chickpea flour mixed with water to thicken. Season with salt and garam masala. Garnish with fresh coriander.

name: kalmi vada
instructions: Soak chana dal for 1-2 hours and grind to coarse paste without water. Add cumin seeds, asafoetida, coriander powder, turmeric, red chilli powder, and garam masala. Finely chop ginger, green chilli, and fresh coriander and mix into the paste. Add salt and mix well. Shape into long cylindrical vadas. Deep fry until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: modak samosa
instructions: Make dough with refined flour, salt, carom seeds, ghee, and water. Let it rest. For filling, boil and mash potatoes. Heat oil and add ginger and green chilli. Add mashed potato and mix in spices (cumin, coriander, red chilli, dry mango, garam masala). Add fresh coriander. Roll dough thin, cut into circles, fill with potato mixture, and shape into modak (teardrop shape). Deep fry until golden. Serve hot.

name: turmeric burfi
instructions: Grate fresh turmeric and cook with ghee until soft. Add powdered jaggery and mix thoroughly until well combined. Add wheat flour and cook over low heat, stirring constantly. Add desiccated coconut and almond powder. Roast muskmelon seeds and cashews separately and add. Season with nutmeg and white pepper. Pour onto a greased plate and let cool. Cut into squares and serve.

name: panpathi roti
instructions: Mix wheat flour and salt. Add ghee and rub into the flour. Add water gradually to form a soft dough. Knead well for 5-10 minutes. Divide into portions and roll out thin circles. Layer multiple thin circles and pan-fry on a griddle until cooked through and lightly golden, flipping to cook both sides evenly.

name: rice pakoda
instructions: Soak rice and urad dal separately for 1-2 hours. Grind to a coarse paste. Add carom seeds and mix well. Add finely chopped green chilli and ginger. Add salt and baking soda just before frying. Heat oil and drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil. Deep fry until golden and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: Khatta Dhokla
instructions: Mix rice flour, semolina, chickpea flour with curd. Add oil, ginger chilli paste, turmeric, and red chilli powder. Season with salt. Add Eno fruit salt and lemon juice just before steaming. Steam in a greased container for 15-20 minutes until cooked through and springy.

name: Sooji Malai Laddu
instructions: Dry roast semolina in ghee until golden and fragrant. Add desiccated coconut and roast briefly. Remove from heat and cool. Mix in malai, sugar powder, and cardamom powder. Chop nuts finely and add along with raisins. Add milk gradually to bind. Shape into balls while warm. Set for 2 hours.

name: Chocolate Rava Cake
instructions: Mix semolina, sugar powder, and cocoa powder. Add oil, curd, and milk. Stir well to combine. Add vanilla essence, baking powder, and baking soda. Mix gently. Pour into greased container. Steam in cooker or kadai with water for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool and demold.

name: Homemade Peanut Butter
ingredients: olive oil or peanut oil 1 tbsp
instructions: Blend roasted peanuts in a food processor or mixer grinder until smooth and creamy, pausing occasionally to scrape down sides. Add oil gradually while blending to reach desired consistency. Season with salt and blend once more. Store in an airtight jar.

name: Ladi Pav
instructions: Activate yeast with warm milk and sugar. Mix refined flour with salt. Add yeast mixture and oil to flour gradually, kneading until soft dough forms. Cover and let rise for 1-2 hours until doubled. Divide into portions, shape as pav. Place in greased container or wrapped foil. Cover and steam in kadai with water for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.

name: Amla Launji
instructions: Boil 2 cups water and add gooseberries. Cook until firm (test with knife). Cool and break into pieces. Heat mustard oil in kadai, add fenugreek and fennel seeds. Add ginger and roast briefly. Add amla pieces, turmeric, fennel powder, jeera powder, red chilli, garam masala, salt, and black salt. Add jaggery and cook on low heat, stirring frequently, until mixture thickens and jaggery dissolves. Cool and store. Let it rest for 2 days before serving.

name: Rice Namakpare
instructions: Mix rice flour with cumin seeds, turmeric, salt, and oil. Add chopped green chilli, chilli flakes, and coriander leaves. Gradually add water to form stiff dough. Knead well. Roll thin between plastic sheets. Cut into desired shapes. Heat oil and fry until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Cool and store in airtight container.

name: Matar Paneer Patties
instructions: For filling: Heat 2 tbsp oil, add cumin seeds, ginger, green chilli. Add coarsely ground peas and cook with spices (salt, coriander powder, red chilli, amchur, garam masala). Mix in grated paneer and coriander leaves. Cool. For dough: Grate boiled potatoes, add salt, pepper, sattu flour, cornflour, and coriander. Mix well. Shape dough into balls, fill with pea-paneer mixture, flatten into patties. Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides. Serve with sauce.

name: Aligarh Kachori
instructions: For dough: mix wheat flour, semolina, salt, carom seeds and oil. Add water gradually and knead stiff dough. Cover for 20 minutes. Divide into lumps and roll into thin pooris. Fry lightly, then roll again and fry until crispy and golden brown over low heat. For sabzi: heat oil, add cumin seeds, green chilli, ginger and dry red chilli. Add bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and black pepper. Roast briefly. Add chopped potatoes, coriander powder, fennel powder and red chilli powder. Saute 1-2 minutes. Add water and salt, cover and cook 5 minutes over low-medium heat. Remove bay leaf and cinnamon, mash potatoes. Add amchur and coriander leaves. For sannata: whisk sour curd, add water. Season with black salt, cumin powder, mint powder, red chilli powder, coriander leaves and boondi.

name: Rose Cookies
instructions: Mix refined flour, rice flour and powdered sugar in a bowl. Add oil and blend well. Gradually add milk to form smooth batter. Heat oil for frying. Using a rose cookie maker or achappam mold, dip into batter and carefully place into hot oil. Fry until golden on both sides. Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towel. Sprinkle sesame seeds if desired.

name: Immunity Soup
instructions: Heat oil in a pot. Add onion and saute until translucent. Add garlic, ginger and turmeric powder, cook for 1 minute. Add chopped vegetables and saute for 2-3 minutes. Add water and bring to boil. Simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are soft. Add salt and pepper to taste. Strain if desired or serve as is with vegetables.

name: Aloo ke Barule
instructions: Boil potatoes with skin until cooked. Mix chickpea flour, corn flour, garam masala, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder and salt in a bowl. Chop boiled potatoes into medium-sized pieces without removing skin. Coat potato pieces in the flour mixture evenly. Heat oil for deep frying. Carefully place coated potato pieces into hot oil and fry until golden brown on all sides. Drain on absorbent paper and serve hot.

name: Surti Ghari
instructions: For dough: mix refined flour with 1 tbsp ghee and knead with water into soft dough. Cover for 20 minutes. For stuffing: combine mawa, besan, 1 tbsp ghee, almond powder, pistachio powder, saffron threads, cardamom powder and less than 1 cup sugar powder. Divide dough into 6 portions. Roll each portion into disc, place stuffing in center, seal edges carefully. Fry in oil or bake until golden brown. While warm, coat generously with mixture of 4 tbsp ghee and 1/2 cup sugar powder.

name: Crispy Poha with Curd Chutney
ingredients: oil - 2 tbsp for mixing + oil for frying
instructions: 1. Soak poha in water for 10 minutes, then mash and knead. 2. Add gram flour, green chilli, ginger, carom seeds, fenugreek leaves, red chilli, turmeric, coriander, salt and spinach. 3. Heat oil and add to mixture, mix well and knead smooth. 4. Form small balls, flatten into disc shapes. 5. Heat medium-hot oil and fry until golden brown. 6. For chutney: grind coriander, green chilli, ginger, cumin seeds, salt, curd and water into fine paste. Serve together.

name: Spicy Tomato Green Chilli Sabzi
instructions: 1. Cut green chilli into bite-sized pieces, discard stalk. 2. Chop tomatoes into large pieces. 3. Heat mustard oil in kadai. 4. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, asafoetida, and grated ginger, saute 1-2 minutes. 5. Add turmeric powder and chopped tomatoes. 6. Add coriander powder, fennel powder, red chilli powder and salt, mix well. 7. Cover and cook for 2 minutes on medium heat. 8. Tomatoes and chillies should be lightly cooked, not mushy. 9. Check and cook 2 more minutes if needed. Serve hot.

name: Suran Curry
instructions: 1. Peel and chop jimikand into pieces. 2. Boil with water, salt and turmeric powder, add lemon juice. 3. Pressure cook at high flame for one whistle, release pressure and drain. 4. Heat oil and shallow fry the boiled pieces until golden brown on all sides, set aside. 5. In same pan add oil, cumin seeds, asafoetida, turmeric and coriander powder, saute briefly. 6. Add tomato-green chilli-ginger paste and red chilli powder, mix well. 7. Add cinnamon, black cardamom, black pepper, cloves and dry fenugreek, roast on low flame until oil separates, stir occasionally. 8. Add curd, mix well and cook until oil separates again, stirring continuously. 9. Add water as needed, salt, fried jimikand pieces and coriander leaves. Cover and cook on low flame for 4-5 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Sesame Brittle
instructions: 1. Dry roast sesame seeds in a pan until fragrant, set aside to cool. 2. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. 3. Add jaggery/sugar and heat until it reaches hard-crack stage (149-150°C), stirring occasionally. 4. Add roasted sesame seeds and quickly mix until well combined. 5. Pour onto a greased surface and press down with oiled hands or spatula to form a thin sheet. 6. Once set, break into pieces. Cool completely before storing in an airtight container.

name: Mangodi Curry
instructions: 1. Soak mangodi briefly if hard, or use directly. 2. Heat oil in pan. 3. Add cumin seeds and let them crackle. 4. Add asafoetida and turmeric powder. 5. Add chopped tomatoes and chilli-ginger paste, saute well. 6. Add mangodi pieces. 7. Mix in coriander powder, red chilli powder, garam masala and salt. 8. Add water as needed and cook covered until mangodi is cooked and curry reaches desired consistency. 9. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

name: Eggless Semolina Cake
instructions: 1. Mix semolina, powdered sugar, ghee, curd and milk in a bowl. 2. Add baking soda and mix gently. 3. Crush green cardamom and add to the mixture. 4. Add chopped almonds and raisins, mix well. 5. Add tutti frutti and fold in gently. 6. Grease a cake tin or pressure cooker vessel. 7. Pour mixture into the greased vessel. 8. Place a steel stand or trivet at the bottom of pressure cooker if using one. 9. Place the vessel on the stand. 10. Cook covered on medium heat for 25-30 minutes (without whistle if using cooker method). 11. Test with a toothpick for doneness. 12. Cool, invert and serve.

name: Almond Brittle
instructions: 1. Dry roast sliced almonds in a pan until lightly golden and fragrant, spread on a plate to cool. 2. In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat ghee over medium heat. 3. Add sugar and stir continuously until it melts and turns golden-amber color (around 149-150°C hard-crack stage). 4. Be careful not to let it burn. 5. Add roasted almonds and mix quickly and thoroughly. 6. Pour the mixture onto a parchment-lined surface or greased marble slab. 7. Quickly press and flatten with oiled hands or a spatula into a thin sheet before it sets. 8. Once partially set, mark into pieces with a knife or break into desired sizes when completely cooled. 9. Store in an airtight container.

name: Chakki Ki Sabzi
instructions: Heat oil and add cumin seeds, tejpatta, cinnamon, black pepper, clove, and green cardamom. Add asafetida. Stir in tomato, green chilli, and ginger baton. Add turmeric, coriander, and red chilli powder. Toast the wheat flour separately, then add to the spice mixture. Stir continuously. Mix in yogurt and cream. Add dried fenugreek leaves and garam masala. Cook until combined, garnish with green coriander.

name: Khile Khile Chawal
instructions: Use the traditional filtering method (pasa vidhi) to cook rice. Rinse rice thoroughly. Boil water with salt. Add rice and cook until perfectly fluffy and each grain is separate. The key is using proper water ratio and the traditional straining technique for light, fluffy rice.

name: Cornmeal Cookies
instructions: Mix cornmeal, wheat flour, and sugar powder. Crush cardamom and add to mixture. Add oil and gradually mix in milk to form a crumbly dough. Knead until combined. Shape into small rounds and flatten slightly. Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until golden brown and crispy.

name: Karela Achar
instructions: Chop bitter gourd into pieces and salt lightly (1 tsp salt). Let sit for 30 minutes to remove bitterness, then squeeze dry. Chop raw mango into pieces. Dry roast fennel, fenugreek, cumin, carom, and mustard seeds. Heat mustard oil and add the roasted seeds. Add bitter gourd and raw mango pieces. Add turmeric, asafetida, red chilli powder, black salt, and vinegar. Mix well and store in sterilized jars for shelf-stable pickle that lasts months.

name: Kormolas
instructions: Mix maida, ground cardamom, sugar powder, baking powder, and ghee. Gradually add lukewarm milk to form dough. Knead with oil until soft. Cover and rest 20 minutes. Divide into 3 parts. Roll thin sheets and cut circles with cutter. Roll circles thinner. Fold into half-moon, press bottom edges together, then twist top and bottom joints for pointed shape. Heat oil to medium temperature. Fry kormolas 1-2 minutes until golden brown on medium-low heat. Fry about 10 minutes per batch.

name: Bread Samosa
instructions: Prepare filling: heat 2 tsp oil, add green chilli and ginger, sauté. Add mashed boiled potato and fresh peas. Add red chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, dry mango powder, green coriander, and salt. Mix well. Prepare slurry: mix refined flour, salt, and black pepper with water to make paste. Cut bread into shape for cone, roll thin. Place filling inside, fold and seal edges using slurry. Heat oil in kadhai to medium temperature. Fry samosas for 10-15 seconds per side until golden. Drain on paper towel.

name: Pav Bhaji Cone Chat
instructions: For cone: mix refined flour, 1.5 tbsp oil, carom seeds, and salt. Add water gradually to form soft dough. Rest 20 minutes. Divide into balls, roll thin, and drape over cone mold. Fry in medium-hot oil until golden and crispy. For bhaji: heat oil in large pan, add cumin seeds, ginger, and green chilli. Sauté. Add chopped tomato, potato, capsicum, cauliflower, and green peas. Cook until vegetables soften. Mash slightly. Add pav bhaji masala, butter, and salt. Cook until well combined and bhaji is thick. Finish with green coriander. Fill fried cones with bhaji and serve hot.

name: sprouted moth chaat
instructions: Soak moth beans for 10-12 hours. Drain and wrap in wet towel to sprout for 20 hours. Boil sprouted beans with salt and turmeric for 5 minutes. Mix in black salt, chaat masala, green chilli, cumin, tomato, boiled potato, chutneys, lemon juice and coriander. Serve chilled.

name: green mango jam
instructions: Wash, peel and chop raw mangoes, remove seeds. Cook mango pieces in pressure cooker with water until whistles, reduce heat for 3 minutes. Release pressure and mash pieces. Filter to remove fibre. Add sugar to pulp and cook until it thickens, stirring occasionally. Add cinnamon while cooking. Add cardamom powder when jam appears thick. Check consistency on a plate - if it doesn't flow, jam is ready. Cool and store.

name: wheat jaggery biscuits
instructions: Combine wheat flour, jaggery, semolina, coconut, baking powder, and cardamom. Add ghee and milk to form dough. Knead well. Shape dough into small balls or rounds. Flatten slightly and place on a pan. Fry or bake in a pressure cooker/kadhai until golden and crispy. Sprinkle almond flakes on top before cooking.

name: rice vegetable cheela
instructions: Grind rice with green chilli and ginger. Add boiled mashed potatoes and mixed vegetables, salt, red chilli powder, cumin and baking soda to form smooth batter. Heat oil on griddle. Pour batter and make thin pancakes. Cook until golden on both sides. For chutney: grind peanuts, coconut, salt, green chilli and lemon. Heat oil with mustard seeds, red chilli and curry leaves, add to peanut mixture. Serve cheela with chutney.

name: chooda matar
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add asafoetida. Add flattened rice and stir for 1-2 minutes. Add green peas and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add ginger, green chilli, and cashews. Season with salt, garam masala, black pepper and sugar. Mix well. Finish with lemon juice and chopped coriander.

name: green moong laddu
instructions: Roast green moong dal on medium heat until color lightens. Cool completely. Melt jaggery with 2 tbsp water. Grind roasted dal into fine flour. Heat ghee in pan and roast the flour for 2 minutes. Add 2 more tbsp ghee and roast for another 2 minutes. Add chopped cashews and almond flakes, roast briefly. Add crushed cardamom and mix. Combine moong flour mixture with jaggery syrup. Apply ghee on hands and shape into small round balls (laddus). Store when cooled.

name: sweet sev
instructions: Mix chickpea flour, semolina, butter and cardamom powder. Prepare sugar syrup by dissolving sugar in water. Deep fry the batter using a sev maker or piping bag into hot oil until light golden. Remove and drain excess oil on paper towel. Immediately toss the fried sev in the warm sugar syrup. Allow to cool and set completely. Store in an airtight container.

name: bitter gourd pickle
instructions: Wash bitter gourd, cut ends and slice into 1/2 cm pieces. Mix with 1 tsp salt and let sit 1 hour. Drain excess water and dry on cloth under sun for 1-2 hours. Roast fennel, fenugreek, cumin, carom, mustard seeds, asafoetida and black pepper separately. Cool and coarsely crush. Heat mustard oil until smoke appears, cool slightly. Mix dried gourd pieces with crushed spice masala, turmeric, chilli powder, salt and black salt. Add lemon juice and vinegar. Mix well and transfer to glass jar. Keep in sun for 3 days (or inside for 3 days). Add 1/4 cup oil if needed. Store in sterile jar and consume within a year.

name: Matar Chaat
instructions: Boil white pulses until cooked. Boil potatoes and tomatoes separately. Cut potatoes into small pieces. Mix boiled pulses and potatoes. Add green chutney and red chutney. Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt to taste. Top with chopped green coriander and green chilli. Squeeze lemon juice and serve immediately.

name: Bajra Bhat
instructions: Roast pearl millet in dry pan. Heat oil and add pearl millet. Cook with water until grains are fluffy. Season with salt and spices. Serve hot as a winter special dish.

name: Veg Makhani Angara
instructions: Blanch paneer and vegetables. Heat oil and add whole spices (black pepper, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon). Add ginger and green chilli. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add turmeric, coriander powder and kashmeeri red chilli. Add cooked vegetables and paneer. Mix yogurt and cream, add to gravy. Add garam masala and kasuri methi. Top with butter. Simmer for 3-4 minutes and serve.

name: Instant Crispy Rava Wheat Dosa
instructions: Mix semolina, wheat flour, curd and salt. Add water to achieve dosa batter consistency. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, add water if batter is thick. Add baking soda and mix well. Heat tawa and grease with ghee. Drizzle water on tawa and wipe clean. Pour batter and spread in circular motion. Cook on high heat, drizzle oil around edges. Cook until golden brown on bottom. Roll dosa and serve hot with chutney.

name: Spongy Rasgulla
instructions: Boil milk and add lemon juice to curdle. Strain through muslin cloth to get chhena (paneer). Knead chhena until smooth and add baking soda. Make small spongy balls. Boil water with sugar to make syrup. Cook rasgulla balls in syrup. Use cornflour mixed with water to give spongy texture. Keep syrup warm. Cook for 15-20 minutes, remove carefully and serve in syrup while warm.

name: Besan Gatta Curry
ingredients: oil - 3 tbsp (1 tsp for dough + 2 tbsp for gravy)
instructions: Make gatta dough: Mix 1/2 cup besan, salt, red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, baking soda and 1 tsp oil. Add water to form a stiff dough. Knead well and shape into cylindrical logs. Boil water and cook gattas until they float and become spongy, about 10-15 minutes. Cut into pieces. Make gravy: Heat 2 tbsp oil, add cumin seeds. Add ginger and green chilli. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add turmeric and mix. Add curd mixed with 1 tsp besan. Add cooked gatta pieces. Add garam masala, salt and asafoetida. Simmer for 2-3 minutes and serve hot.

name: Wheat Kheer
instructions: Roast soaked wheat in ghee until light brown. Add milk and bring to boil. Simmer on low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally. Wheat should be soft and milk should reduce to half. Add sugar and jaggery, mix well. Add cardamom powder and nutmeg powder. Add roasted cashews and almonds. Garnish with grated coconut. Stir well and serve warm. Can be served as kheer with condensed consistency.

name: Baked Veg Pizza Pocket
instructions: Make dough: Mix maida, baking powder and salt. Add oil and knead with water to make smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes. Make filling: Heat 1 tbsp oil, add ginger. Add sweet corn, peas and carrot. Add green capsicum and tomato. Add salt. Mix in oregano, schezwan sauce and tomato sauce. Remove from heat and add cheese, mix well. Roll dough into thin rectangles. Place filling in center, fold and seal edges. Place on baking tray. Bake at 180C for 15-20 minutes until golden brown. Serve hot with ketchup or mayo.

name: Palak Saag Paneer
instructions: Blanch spinach, bathua, and methi for 7-8 minutes. Heat ghee in pan, add cumin and red chilli, roast briefly. Add chopped tomatoes and salt, cook until mushy then mash. Grind blanched greens coarsely and add to tomato mixture. Mix corn flour with water, add to saag and cook 10-12 minutes on low-medium heat. Add cubed paneer, cook 3-4 more minutes. Finish with Maggi Masala and serve with butter.

name: Bajra Masala Poori
instructions: Boil and grate 3 potatoes. Mix grated potato with bajra flour. Add salt, cumin, carom seeds, turmeric, sesame seeds, green chilli, chilli flakes, ginger, and coriander leaves. Add water gradually to form soft dough, cover and rest 15 minutes. Apply oil to hands, break dough into lumps and roll into thick poori. Fry in medium-high hot oil on medium flame until golden brown on both sides.

name: Crispy Veggie Rice Balls
instructions: Mix grated cauliflower and potato with rice flour. Add all spices, green chilli, ginger, coriander leaves, and salt. Add oil and mix well to form mixture. Roll into balls. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy on all sides.

name: Noodles Pakora Balls
instructions: Boil noodles and potatoes, then cool. Peel and mash boiled potatoes. Mix mashed potato with cooked noodles. Add refined flour, chopped capsicum, coriander leaves, noodles masala, green chilli, ginger, black pepper, and salt. Form into balls and deep fry in hot oil until golden brown on all sides.

name: Ginger Masala Mathri
instructions: Mix refined flour with urad dal. Add minced ginger, black pepper, cumin seeds, carom seeds, turmeric powder, and salt. Rub in ghee until mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Gradually add water to form a stiff dough. Knead well and rest for 15 minutes. Roll into thin sheets and cut into square or diamond shapes. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on both sides.

name: Garadu Chaat
instructions: Peel tapioca and slice into 1/2 inch pieces. Pressure cook with water and salt for one whistle. Cool completely and cut into smaller pieces. Dry roast cumin, coriander, fennel, black pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and black cardamom. Add asafoetida, turmeric, salt, black salt, sugar, red chilli powder, and ginger powder to roasted spices and grind to fine powder. Deep fry cooled tapioca pieces until golden brown. Toss fried tapioca with prepared masala powder and lemon juice. Serve hot.

name: Sabudana Halwa
ingredients: saffron strands 25-30 soaked in 1 tsp milk
instructions: Soak sago pearls in water for 30 minutes, then drain. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add drained sago and roast on low heat, stirring frequently for 8-10 minutes until slightly golden. Add sugar and mix well. Continue cooking on low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent burning. Add roasted nuts, cardamom powder, and saffron with milk. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes. Transfer to serving bowl.

name: rice fafda
instructions: Mix urad dal, rice flour, chickpea flour, red chilli powder, asafoetida and salt. Add water gradually to make a stiff dough. Mix well and add butter. Knead thoroughly. Let rest briefly. Using a ribbon maker or piping tool, press dough into hot oil in thin ribbons. Fry until golden and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels. Serve hot.

name: dhaniya wale aloo
instructions: Roughly chop green coriander. Chop green chilli and ginger. Heat oil in a pot. Add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add dry fenugreek. Add chopped coriander, green chilli and ginger. Add black pepper, cardamom and cloves. Sauté until fragrant. Add boiled potato pieces. Add salt and squeeze of lemon. Cover and cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes in dum (steam-cooking). Stir occasionally. Add more lemon juice if needed. Serve hot with roti or rice.

name: bread cheese bites
instructions: Remove crusts from bread slices. Apply pizza sauce on one slice. Place cheese pieces (1/2 tsp each) in 4 corners. Top with another bread slice, press gently. Cut into 4 equal pieces. Make slurry by mixing cornflour, refined flour, salt, black pepper and water to pouring consistency. Dip cheese bites in slurry. Roll in bread crumbs, coating all sides. Heat oil to medium-high temperature. Fry bites until golden brown on all sides. Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with any dip.

name: caramelized sabudana
instructions: Heat oil in a deep pan or wok. Test oil temperature with a single sago pearl - it should float and puff up within seconds. Carefully add sago pearls in small batches to hot oil. Fry until crispy and light golden, stirring occasionally. Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. In a separate pan, add sugar with minimal water and cook on high heat until it turns amber color (caramel stage). Add ghee to caramel. Add fried sago pearls to hot caramel and quickly toss to coat evenly. Spread on parchment paper to cool and harden. Store in airtight container.

name: green papaya curry
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds, let them crackle. Add turmeric powder and coriander powder. Roast spices briefly. Add ginger baton and whole green chillies. Add chopped tomatoes. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tomatoes soften. Add cut raw papaya pieces. Add salt and kashmiri red chilli powder. Mix well. Cover and cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until papaya is tender. Add garam masala. Adjust salt and spices to taste. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with roti or rice.

name: crushed peanut chikki
instructions: Grind roasted peanuts coarsely. Heat jaggery with ghee in a pan until melted. Test syrup consistency by dropping into water - if rubbery cook longer until thick, if breakable proceed. Add ground peanuts to syrup and mix well. Grease a board with ghee and spread mixture on it. Roll to 1/4 cm thickness with greased rolling pin. Make cut marks before completely cool. Let set for 30 minutes. Break into pieces and serve.

name: eggless custard cake
instructions: Mix refined flour, custard powder, baking powder and salt in a bowl. In another bowl, beat sugar with olive oil until light. Add milk to oil-sugar mixture.
