Combine wet and dry ingredients gently until smooth. Pour into greased baking vessel. Bake in cooker or oven at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until a skewer inserted comes out clean. Cool before serving.

name: steamed suji idli bomb
instructions: For batter: Mix semolina, curd, chopped spinach, green chillies, ginger and salt. For filling: Heat 2 tsp oil, add mustard seeds, cumin, turmeric, green chilli and ginger. Add mashed potato, red chilli powder, coriander powder, amchoor and peas. Mix well. To assemble: Grease idli moulds, fill halfway with batter, add spoonful of filling, top with more batter. Steam for 10-12 minutes until cooked. For tadka: Heat 2 tsp oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric and red chilli powder. Pour over steamed idlis before serving.

name: rice flour nankhatai
instructions: Mix rice flour, chickpea flour, sugar powder and baking powder together in a bowl. Add oil and milk, mix until a soft dough forms. Knead lightly. Shape into small balls, flatten gently with your palm to 1/4 inch thickness. Place on baking sheet. Bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes until edges turn golden. Cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer to rack. These are delicate - handle carefully. Store in airtight container.

name: moong namkeen
ingredients: sabut moong (whole green mung beans) 1 cup (200g)
instructions: Wash sabut moong thoroughly and soak in water for 4-5 hours. Drain completely on a clean cloth until completely dry. Heat oil for deep frying to medium-high temperature. Fry moong in small batches, about 1/4 cup at a time, for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy, stirring occasionally. Remove with slotted spoon onto paper towels. While still warm, sprinkle dry mango powder, red chilli powder and salt. Toss well to coat evenly. Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

name: samak rice halwa
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan, add samak rice and roast for 2-3 minutes until light golden and fragrant. Add 2 cups water (or milk for creamier texture) and bring to boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is completely soft and liquid is absorbed. Meanwhile, heat ghee in another pan and lightly fry chopped cashews and almond flakes until golden. Add crushed cardamom and mix. When rice is cooked, add sugar and cook for 2 more minutes until sugar dissolves completely. Mix in roasted dry fruits. Serve hot, garnished with extra almonds if desired.

name: Sev Paratha
instructions: Mix refined flour with salt, oil and water to form dough. Let rest 30 minutes. Boil and mash potatoes with spices. Roll dough into thin circle, fill with potato mixture and crushed sev. Pan fry on griddle with oil until golden brown on both sides.

name: Moong Dal Palak Tikka Curry
instructions: Boil moong dal until soft. In separate pan, blanch spinach and blend. Prepare tomato puree. Fry cumin seeds in oil, add ginger-green chilli paste. Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates. Add spice powders. Fold in moong dal, spinach puree and cooked spinach tikkas. Garnish with fenugreek.

name: Steamed Pav
instructions: Mix yeast with warm water and sugar. Let proof 5 minutes. Mix flour and salt. Add yeast liquid and oil. Knead into soft dough. Cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled. Divide into portions. Shape into buns. Place on parchment paper in steam cooker. Steam for 12-15 minutes until light and fluffy.

name: Rice Flour Jalebi
instructions: Mix rice flour, refined flour, black lentil and baking soda. Add water and food colour to form pourable batter. Boil sugar with water to make syrup. Heat oil for deep frying. Pipe batter into hot oil in spiral shape. Fry until golden. Immediately soak in warm sugar syrup.

name: Barley Veg Pulao
instructions: Dry roast barley on medium flame for 4 minutes until fragrant. Heat ghee in cooker, add cumin seeds. Add all vegetables and ginger-chilli. Saute briefly. Add roasted barley and toast 30 seconds. Add chopped tomato. Pour water and salt. Pressure cook for one whistle. Let rest 10 minutes before opening.

name: Kabuli Chana Namkeen
instructions: Boil chickpeas until tender but not mushy. Dry roast in pan over medium heat until completely dry and slightly crispy. Mix all spice powders, salt and black salt. Toss roasted chickpeas with spice mixture. Heat oil in wok or deep pan. Fry spiced chickpeas in batches until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towel and cool. Store in airtight container.

name: Corn Pulao
instructions: Wash rice and soak 15 minutes. Heat oil, add bay leaves and cinnamon stick. Add cumin seeds, cloves, cardamom and black pepper. Add ginger. Add all vegetables and saute 2 minutes. Add soaked rice and toast 1 minute. Pour water and salt. Bring to boil. Cover and simmer until rice is cooked and water absorbed. Serve with lemon juice.

name: Yam Fry
instructions: Peel and thinly slice yam. Toss with curd and chickpea flour to coat. Mix turmeric, coriander powder, chilli powder, garam masala and salt. Coat yam slices with spice mixture. Heat oil on griddle or tawa (cast iron pan). Fry yam slices on medium-high heat until crispy and golden on both sides. Serve hot with lemon juice.

name: Green Peas Uttapam
instructions: Mix semolina with curd. Add finely chopped ginger, green chilli, tomato, coriander leaves and green peas. Add cumin seeds, baking soda and salt. Make a batter. Pour on hot oiled griddle and cook on both sides until golden brown.

name: Raw Banana Cutlets
instructions: Boil and peel raw bananas. Mash and mix with singhara flour, roasted peanuts powder, ginger, green chilli, coriander and spices. Shape into cutlets. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Surti Khaman
instructions: Soak chana dal, grind with curd, ginger, green chilli, turmeric, asafoetida and salt. Add eno fruit salt and mix gently. Pour into oiled baking pan and steam for 20 minutes. Prepare tadka with oil, mustard and sesame seeds, green chilli. Pour over steamed khaman, add lemon juice, sugar, garnish with pomegranate and coriander.

name: Fasting Kadhi with Pakora and Sama Rice
instructions: Make pakora batter with singhara flour, curd, ginger, green chilli, coriander and rock salt. Slice potato and coat in batter. Deep fry until golden. Make kadhi by mixing curd and singhara flour with water. Temper with cumin seeds, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves. Add pakora to kadhi and simmer. Separately, cook sama rice with ghee, cumin seeds and rock salt. Serve kadhi with rice.

name: Atta Moong Dal Mathri
instructions: Mix wheat flour with soaked moong dal, oil, finely chopped coriander and green chilli, carom seeds, asafoetida and salt. Make a stiff dough. Roll thin and cut into diamond or square shapes. Deep fry in hot oil on medium-high flame until golden and crispy.

name: Handi Paneer Masala
instructions: Heat oil in handi, add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Add ginger and green chilli, saute briefly. Add tomato and cook until soft. Add turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, garam masala and salt. Add paneer pieces and cover with handi lid. Cook on low flame for 10-12 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

name: Instant Moong Dal Idli
instructions: Soak and grind moong dal with curd to a smooth batter. Mix with finely chopped vegetables, add ginger-chilli paste, salt, and eno fruit salt. Heat oil, temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves, pour into batter and mix well. Pour into idli molds and steam for 8-10 minutes until done.

name: Custard Halwa
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add vanilla custard powder and toast for 1-2 minutes, stirring continuously. Add sugar and mix well until the mixture comes together into a halwa-like consistency. Add roasted cashews and cardamom powder, mix thoroughly until well combined. The halwa should pull away from the sides of the pan.

name: Pumpkin Sweet Poori
instructions: Mix wheat flour with grated pumpkin. Add jaggery and grated nutmeg to the flour mixture. Add ghee and knead into a soft dough. Roll dough into small disc shapes, about 1/4 inch thick. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown and puffed on both sides.

name: Bajra Til Tikki
instructions: Mix millet flour with sesame seeds. Add jaggery (grated or powdered) to the flour mixture. Add little water if needed to bind the mixture into a dough. Shape dough into flat round tikkis or pua shapes. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy on all sides.

name: Urad Dal Khichdi
instructions: Heat ghee in a pot. Add cumin seeds and cinnamon stick, let them crackle. Add finely chopped ginger and green chilli, sauté for 30 seconds. Add rice and urad dal, toast for 1-2 minutes. Add peas, chopped tomato, and all spices including turmeric and red chilli powder. Add water (about 2 cups) and bring to boil. Reduce heat and cook covered until rice and dal are completely tender and creamy.

name: Mango Custard Halwa
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add vanilla custard powder and roast for 1 minute, stirring continuously. Add mango pulp and mix well. Add sugar gradually while stirring to avoid lumps. Keep stirring until the halwa thickens and leaves the sides of the pan. Add roasted cashews and melon seeds, mix thoroughly. Sprinkle cardamom powder and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Crispy Chana Namkeen
instructions: Soak dried chickpeas overnight, then dry them completely using a cloth or paper towel. Heat oil in a deep pan and fry chickpeas in batches until they are golden brown and completely crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Once cooled, crush the cloves and mix with dry mango powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, cumin seeds, black pepper, and salt. Toss the fried chickpeas in this spice mixture until well coated. Store in an airtight container.

name: Dharwad Peda
instructions: Combine paneer, mawa, and sugar together. Mix in cardamom powder. Add milk gradually to combine. Shape mixture into round peda balls. Roll or coat with powdered sugar (bura) on all sides. Store in airtight container.

name: Semiya Burfi
instructions: Heat ghee and toast vermicelli until lightly browned. Boil milk and reduce to half. Add roasted vermicelli and desiccated coconut to reduced milk. Mix sugar and cook until thickens to a fudgy consistency. Add cardamom powder. Add chopped nuts. Pour onto greased plate. Cool and cut into squares.

name: Chocolate Gulab Jamun
instructions: Mix mawa with cocoa powder and cardamom. Shape into balls. Heat oil or ghee and deep fry balls until golden brown. Prepare sugar syrup by dissolving sugar in water with rose water. Immerse fried balls immediately in hot sugar syrup. Cool before serving.

name: Stuffed Bafla Bati
instructions: Make dough with wheat flour, curd, baking soda, carom seeds, sugar, and salt. Let it rest. Prepare potato stuffing by mashing potatoes and mixing with fried cumin seeds, ginger paste, green chilli, and spices. Also prepare green peas stuffing similarly. Divide dough into balls, flatten, add stuffing, seal, and shallow fry in ghee until golden brown on both sides.

name: Til Peanut Ladoo
instructions: Dry roast sesame seeds until fragrant. Dry roast peanuts separately. Chop almonds finely. Mix roasted sesame, peanuts, almonds with powdered sugar and cardamom powder. Gradually add melted ghee while mixing. Form into balls of desired size.

name: Veggies Rice Dhokla
instructions: Mix rice flour and chickpea flour. Add curd and mix well. Add chopped vegetables, green chilli, turmeric, green coriander, and salt. Mix gently. Just before steaming, add Eno powder. Pour into greased idli mold or dhokla pan. Steam for 12-15 minutes until cooked through. Cool slightly. Heat oil with mustard seeds and curry leaves, then pour over dhokla. Serve warm.

name: High Protein Peanut Cheela
instructions: Roast peanuts and grind coarsely. Mix with chickpea flour, chopped vegetables, green chilli, ginger, black pepper, salt, and green coriander. Add water to make thick pancake batter. Heat oil in non-stick pan. Pour batter and spread into circular cheela. Cook until edges are golden, flip and cook other side. Prepare chutney by grinding green coriander, ginger, green chilli, cumin seeds with salt and lemon juice. Serve cheela with chutney.

name: Rava Pizza
instructions: Mix semolina, curd, eno fruit salt, and salt to form a batter. Add pizza sauce and mix well. Heat tawa on high flame. Spread cheese on tawa, then pour batter over it. Add pizza topping of capsicum, red bell pepper, and sweet corn. Sprinkle chilli flakes and oregano. Cook on medium heat until golden brown on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Atta Gujiya with Gur and Ginger
instructions: Make a dough with wheat flour and ghee. Let it rest for 15 minutes. Roll out the dough. Prepare filling with gur, ginger powder, and dry fruits. Stuff the filling into the dough, seal, and shape into semi-circle. Deep fry in ghee until golden brown. Serve warm.

name: Paneer Masala Bati
instructions: Mix wheat flour, semolina, ghee, carom seeds, black pepper, and salt. Prepare paneer filling with crushed paneer, capsicum, green coriander, green chilli, and salt. Knead with water into soft dough and let rest 15 minutes. Shape dough around paneer filling into oval balls. Boil water with salt, then slowly drop batis and cook until they float (about 4-5 minutes). Serve with chutney or gravy.

name: Gobhi Kofta Curry
instructions: Boil and mash cauliflower and potatoes. Mix with chickpea flour, green coriander, salt, and spices to form kofta mixture. Shape into balls and deep fry until golden. In a separate pan, make tomato gravy with ginger, green chilli, and spices. Add fried koftas to the gravy and simmer until well coated.

name: Sooji Peetha
instructions: Make sugar syrup with milk and sugar. Dry roast semolina in ghee until golden. Add roasted semolina to the sugar syrup slowly while stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Mix in mawa, crushed cardamom, and saffron. Pour into molds and steam for 2-3 minutes. Unmold while warm. Garnish with almond flakes and pista. Serve warm.

name: Aloo Mangodi in Peas Gravy
instructions: Dice potatoes and deep fry until golden. Soak mangodi in water for 5 minutes. Heat oil, add cumin seeds, ginger, and green chilli. Add chopped tomatoes and simmer until soft. Add turmeric, red chilli, coriander powder, and garam masala. Add fried potatoes, peas, and mangodi. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until well cooked. Garnish with green coriander and serve hot.

name: Chandrakanti Peetha
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal and rice together to a smooth paste. Heat ghee in a pan, add the ground paste and sugar. Stir continuously on medium heat until the mixture becomes thick and turns golden brown (about 8-10 minutes). Add ground cardamom and mix well. Transfer to a greased plate and spread evenly. Cool slightly, then cut into desired shapes. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Khasta Gulgula
instructions: Mix wheat flour, semolina, baking soda, fennel seeds, and sugar powder in a bowl. Add oil and mix well. Add water gradually to form a soft dough. Let rest covered for 20 minutes. Heat oil in a kadai until hot. Take small portions of dough, gently flatten and shape into balls. Deep fry in hot oil on medium-high heat until golden brown on all sides. Remove and cool on a paper towel. Serve with green chutney or pickles.

name: Indarhar
instructions: Soak mixed dals for 15-20 minutes, then drain. Heat oil and add cumin seeds, dals, ginger, and green chilli; fry for 2-3 minutes. Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, asafetida, and salt; fry until cooked. Shape into patties and fry until golden. For curry: heat oil, add whole spices (tejpatta, cinnamon, black pepper, cloves, badi ilayachi), then tomato and green chilli. Add turmeric, coriander powder, kashmiri chilli powder, curd, salt, and garam masala. Simmer and add fried dal mixture. Garnish with green coriander.

name: Masala Chakli
instructions: Mix refined flour with sesame seeds, cumin seeds, carom seeds, crushed black pepper, and salt. Prepare a smooth dough with water. Transfer to a chakli maker or piping bag. Heat oil for frying. Pipe dough directly into hot oil to form spiral shapes. Fry on medium heat until golden and crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels.

name: Broccoli Paratha
instructions: Make a dough with wheat flour, water, and salt; rest for 15-20 minutes. Prepare filling with chopped broccoli, ginger, green chilli, and salt. Divide dough into balls. Roll each into a thin circle, place filling in center, fold and seal. Roll into thin paratha. Cook on hot griddle with oil until golden spots appear on both sides.

name: Aloo Matar Stuffed Semolina Nuggets
instructions: Mash boiled potatoes and mix with green peas. Add chopped green chilli and coriander. Season with turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, dry mango powder, garam masala, and salt. Coat semolina-covered potato-pea mixture and shape into oval nuggets. Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on all sides.

name: Veg Roll Tikki
ingredients: oil 2 tbsp plus 4 tbsp for cooking
instructions: Make dough with whole wheat flour, mashed potato, oil, salt, and baking soda; rest 15-20 minutes. Prepare filling: mix grated cauliflower, carrot, chopped capsicum, green chilli, and green coriander; season with salt. Divide dough into balls, roll into thin circle, spread filling on one half, fold and seal. Roll out to thin sheet. Cook on hot griddle with oil until golden on both sides.

name: Semiya Dosa
instructions: Break roasted vermicelli into small pieces and mix with semolina. Pour hot water and let absorb for 2-3 minutes. Add curd and mix well. Season with salt, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves, and coriander. Just before cooking, add eno fruit salt. Heat non-stick griddle and pour batter in center; spread gently to form thin dosa. Cook on medium-high heat until bottom is light golden, flip and cook other side.

name: Kakara Pitha
ingredients: deshi ghee 1/2 tsp plus oil for frying
sugar 2 tsp for covering plus 1/4 cup
instructions: Roast semolina in ghee for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Spread on plate to cool. Mix grated coconut with sugar, chopped cashews, almonds, raisins, cardamom powder, and black pepper. Take cooled semolina, mix with salt and ghee. Take small ball of semolina, flatten, place coconut filling in center, fold and shape. Roll in sugar-fennel seed mixture. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy. Cool on paper towels.

name: annakoot
instructions: 1. Heat oil in pressure cooker. 2. Add cumin and mustard seeds. 3. Add mixed vegetables (traditionally includes potato, pumpkin, carrot, beans, etc.). 4. Add turmeric powder and salt. 5. Add water. 6. Pressure cook for 2 whistles. 7. Let pressure release naturally. 8. Serve hot.

name: methi khakhra
instructions: 1. Mix wheat flour and chickpea flour. 2. Add dry fenugreek, turmeric, red chilli powder, cumin seeds and salt. 3. Make a stiff dough with oil and water. 4. Knead well. 5. Roll thin circles. 6. Cut into desired shapes. 7. Sun-dry or oven-dry until crisp. 8. Store in airtight container.

name: bottle gourd sabudana kheer
instructions: 1. Soak sago pearls for 15 minutes. 2. Peel and grate bottle gourd. 3. Fry cashews in ghee until golden. 4. Heat milk. 5. Add bottle gourd and sago pearls to milk. 6. Cook until soft. 7. Add sugar and crushed cardamom. 8. Simmer for 5 minutes. 9. Garnish with pista and almond flakes. 10. Serve chilled or warm.

name: creamy green spinach pasta
instructions: 1. Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. 2. Blanch spinach in boiling water. 3. Blend spinach with green chilli to make puree. 4. Heat butter. 5. Add chopped ginger and fry lightly. 6. Add capsicum and mix herbs. 7. Add spinach puree and cook. 8. Add fresh cream. 9. Mix cooked pasta into sauce. 10. Season with salt, sugar and black pepper. 11. Toss well. 12. Garnish with fresh coriander. 13. Serve hot.

name: rice flour papad
instructions: 1. Mix rice flour with cumin seeds, salt and papad khar. 2. Add oil and mix well. 3. Add water gradually to form a firm dough. 4. Knead for 5 minutes. 5. Roll dough between plastic sheets into thin circles. 6. Sun-dry on a mat or cloth until completely dry and crisp. 7. Store in airtight container. 8. Deep fry or roast over flame when serving.

name: makuti
instructions: 1. Soak moong dal and rice for 30 minutes. 2. Grind to a fine paste. 3. Heat milk. 4. Add moong dal and rice paste to milk. 5. Cook stirring continuously for 10 minutes. 6. Add mawa and cook until thick. 7. Add sugar and crushed cardamom. 8. Fry dry fruits in ghee until golden. 9. Add fried dry fruits to kheer. 10. Add saffron strands. 11. Mix well and serve warm or chilled.

name: sama rice vada
instructions: 1. Rinse and drain sama rice 3 times. 2. Blend sama rice with curd to make fine paste. 3. Pour mixture into pan and add 3/4 cup water. 4. Add rock salt, green chilli, ginger, black pepper and cumin. 5. Cook stirring continuously until thickened like dough. 6. Add fresh coriander and cooled grated carrot. 7. Turn off flame and cool. 8. Oil your hands and knead the dough. 9. Roll into balls and flatten slightly. 10. Make a hole at center to form vada shape. 11. Heat oil and deep fry until golden brown. 12. Serve hot with chutney.

name: Semolina Veg Rolls
instructions: Mix semolina, curd, salt and baking soda for dough. Prepare filling with grated vegetables, ginger, green chilli, black pepper and green coriander. Steam the rolls over water until cooked through. Temper with oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves.

name: Noodle Momos
instructions: Knead maida dough with water. Cook and drain instant noodles. Stir-fry chopped vegetables with soy sauce, vinegar and ginger paste. Mix cooled noodles with vegetables. Roll dough thin, place noodle filling in center, seal edges and steam until cooked.

name: Til Gur Besan Laddu
instructions: Dry roast sesame seeds until puffed. Melt ghee and roast gram flour over low heat for 12 minutes. Heat jaggery with water to make syrup, testing for thread consistency. Mix jaggery with roasted gram flour until combined. Add roasted sesame seeds and cardamom powder. Cool mixture, grind to powder, mix with crushed cardamom and shape into laddus.

name: Besan Malai Burfi
instructions: Roast chickpea flour in ghee over medium heat. In separate pan, dissolve sugar with water to make syrup. Add roasted flour to syrup with malai and mix well. Cook until thickened like halwa. Pour into greased tray, cool and cut into pieces. Garnish with almond flakes.

name: Masala Vada
instructions: Soak chana dal for 3-4 hours, drain well. Grind green chilli, ginger and soaked dal into coarse paste. Add grated cabbage, spices, coriander and chickpea flour. Mix well. Shape into round vadas and deep fry in hot oil until golden brown.

name: Sooji Gujiya
instructions: Knead maida with ghee and rest 20 minutes. Roast semolina in ghee until golden. Make sugar syrup and mix with roasted semolina. Add coconut, cashew, buchania, raisin and cardamom to filling. Cool filling completely. Roll dough thin, fill and shape using mold or by hand. Fry until puffed and golden in ghee. Dip in kesar-infused sugar syrup.

name: sattu barfi
instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat ghee and add mawa. Fry for 2-3 minutes on low heat. Add sattu powder and mix well. Add sugar and roasted cardamom powder. Mix everything thoroughly on low heat for 5-7 minutes until combined. Spread the mixture onto a greased surface, press down, let cool, and cut into pieces. Garnish with almond flakes.

name: kurkure
ingredients: ararot or corn flour - 1/4 cup (30 grams)
instructions: Knead poha with chickpea flour, ararot, salt, chaat masala, and red chili powder into a stiff dough for 5-6 minutes. Make sure there are no cracks or air pockets. Heat oil on low flame. Using a piping bag or hand, extrude the dough into the hot oil. Fry on low-medium heat until golden and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels and store in an airtight container.

name: vegetable seekh kabab
instructions: Boil and mash potatoes. Finely chop all vegetables. Soak urad dal and grind into paste. Mix dal paste with boiled potatoes, finely chopped vegetables, green coriander, ginger, green chili, all spices, and bread crumbs. Form into cylindrical shape on skewers or roll into logs. Refrigerate for 1 hour. Deep fry on medium heat until golden brown on all sides. Drain and serve hot.

name: mango panna
instructions: Boil green mangoes until soft. Peel and remove the seed. In a blender, blend the mango pulp with sugar, roasted cumin, black pepper, black salt, green cardamom, ginger, and mint leaves into a smooth paste. Transfer to a jar. To serve, mix 3-4 tablespoons of concentrate with 1 cup of cold water or chilled water and stir well. Serve chilled.

name: apple kheer
instructions: Heat milk in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add baking soda and stir well. Grate or chop apples finely. When milk starts to reduce, add apples and sugar. Keep stirring occasionally. When milk reduces to about half, add crushed cardamom powder. Fry almond flakes and cashews in ghee and add to the kheer. Cook for 2-3 more minutes and serve warm or chilled.

name: whole wheat bhatura
ingredients: oil - 2 tbsp plus oil for frying
instructions: Mix whole wheat flour, salt, and baking soda in a bowl. Add yogurt and oil. Mix and knead into a soft dough with water. Cover and let rest for 1-2 hours until slightly risen. Divide into balls and let rest for 10 minutes. Heat oil in a deep kadhai. Gently stretch the dough ball into an oval shape and fry on medium heat. Press with the back of the ladle until it puffs up. Fry until golden on both sides. Drain on paper towels.

name: stuffed dal dhokli
instructions: For dough: Mix wheat flour, chickpea flour, carom seeds, turmeric, salt, and oil with water to form a soft dough. Roll thin and cut into strips. For stuffing: Mash boiled potatoes with green peas, green chili, coriander, garam masala, and mango powder. For dal: Soak arhar dal. Temper ghee with mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, asafoetida, red chilies, and curry leaves. Add green chili, ginger, and tomatoes. Add dal and cook until soft. Add coriander powder, red chili powder, tamarind pulp, and jaggery. Boil water with salt, add dough strips and stuffed portions, cook until dal and dough are cooked through.

name: green moong masala dosa
instructions: Soak moong dal and rice separately for 4-5 hours. Grind soaked moong dal and rice with green chili and ginger into a fine paste. Add salt and let ferment for 10 minutes. For stuffing: Heat oil, add chana dal and urad dal, roast until golden. Add mustard seeds, ginger, green chili, curry leaves, and chopped tomato. Add spices and mashed potatoes. Cook for 2-3 minutes. For chutney: Blend roasted peanuts, desiccated coconut, green chili, lemon juice, and salt into coarse paste. Prepare tadka with mustard seeds and red chilies in oil, add to chutney. Heat non-stick pan with oil. Spread batter thin to make crepe. Add stuffing and fold. Fry until golden brown. Serve with chutney.

name: Baked Noodle Spring Rolls
instructions: Make dough by mixing refined flour, salt, oil and water. For filling, heat oil and add ginger and green chillies. Add all capsicums and carrots, season with soya sauce, vinegar, tomato sauce, red chilli powder and black pepper. Add boiled noodles and mix well. Roll dough thin, fill with vegetable noodle mixture, fold into spring roll shape and bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.

name: Dal Moradabadi (Moong Dal Chaat)
instructions: Soak moong dal for 2-3 hours and boil with salt and asafoetida until soft but not mushy. Heat butter in a pan and add boiled dal. Add cumin powder, garam masala, chaat masala and black salt. Mix well and heat through. Crush dry red chillies and add to dal. Top with fresh chopped green coriander and ginger. Serve hot garnished with papadi and squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

name: Falafel (Air Fryer)
instructions: Transfer soaked chickpeas to food processor. Add salt, black pepper powder, cumin powder, paprika powder, lemon juice, onion, garlic, coriander and parsley. Process into coarse mixture. Transfer to bowl, add sesame seeds and mix. Cover and refrigerate 30-40 minutes. Divide into portions and roll into balls, flatten slightly. Preheat air fryer at 200°C for 2-3 minutes. Spray oil on basket, arrange falafels in single layer, spray oil on top and air fry for 25 minutes. Serve with hummus or dip.

name: Moong Vada (Whole Moong)
ingredients: soaked whole green gram (sabut moong) 1.5 cups
instructions: Transfer soaked moong to food processor and blend to coarse mixture. Transfer to bowl. Add fennel powder, cumin powder, green chillies, ginger, onion, curry leaves and salt. Mix well. Add rice flour and crushed black peppercorns and mix thoroughly. Divide into equal portions and roll into balls, flatten slightly. Heat oil in kadai or deep pan. Deep fry vadas until golden brown and crisp, turning for even cooking. Drain on absorbent paper and serve hot with coconut chutney.

name: Crispy Spinach Parcels
instructions: Make dough by mixing flour with baking soda, salt, 2 tbsp melted butter and water. Knead into soft dough. Blanch spinach in boiling water 1 minute, drain and squeeze, then chop finely. Chop onion. Heat 1 tbsp butter in non-stick pan, add onion and cook until soft. Add chopped spinach, salt and pine nuts, cook until dry. Transfer to bowl and cool. Heat oil in deep pan. Divide dough into 4 portions and roll each thin, dusting with flour. Use cookie cutter to cut roundels. Dampen edges, place spinach mixture in centre, fold into crescent shape and seal well. Slide into hot oil and deep fry until golden and crisp. Drain on absorbent paper and serve hot.

name: Mathri Tart
ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato boiled peeled chopped
instructions: Mix pearl millet flour, salt, carom seeds, ghee and whole wheat flour. Add warm water and knead soft dough, cover for 10-15 minutes. Preheat oven to 180C. Roll dough thin between silicone sheets, cut into roundels with cookie cutter. Grease tart tins and line roundels, dock with fork. Bake 10-12 minutes, cool and demould. Meanwhile, peel and chop avocado, mix with boiled sweet potato, tomato, green chillies, salt, pepper, lemon juice and coriander. Fill tart shells with avocado mixture, drizzle date-tamarind chutney, garnish with microgreens and serve.

name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
instructions: Heat mustard oil in kadai. Prick potatoes with wooden stick. Once oil smokes, add potatoes and deep fry until golden and crisp, drain on paper. Heat 2 tbsps mustard oil in pan, add bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and crushed black cardamom, sauté until fragrant. Lower heat, add red chilli powder, asafoetida, fennel powder, ginger powder and turmeric, mix well. Add yogurt and cook until oil separates. Add fried potatoes and salt, mix. Add 3/4 cup water and cook 2-3 minutes. Add garam masala powder, cook 1 minute more. Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Saffron Baked Yogurt
instructions: Whisk yogurt smooth. Add saffron strands and let infuse for color and flavor. Pour into baking dish and bake until set and lightly browned at edges. Serve at room temperature or chilled. Garnish with roasted nuts and edible flowers as desired.

name: Moong Pattice
instructions: Pressure cook sprouted moong with turmeric and salt until soft, drain well. Mix boiled potatoes with ginger-chilli paste, salt and fresh breadcrumbs. Heat oil, add cumin seeds, cook until brown. Add green chillies and sauté 30 seconds. Add onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute. Add spices and salt, mix well. Add drained moong and coriander, cook 2-3 minutes. Cool the moong mixture completely. Grease palms, take potato mixture, roll into ball, create cavity in center, stuff with moong mixture, seal edges. Dip in cornflour slurry, roll in dried breadcrumbs. Shallow fry in oil until golden and crispy on both sides. Drain on paper and serve hot with tomato ketchup.

name: Gobi Keema
instructions: Chop ginger, garlic and green chillies in a chopper. Heat oil in nonstick pan, add cumin seeds and asafoetida, sauté until golden. Add ginger-garlic-green chilli mixture and sauté for 1-2 minutes. Add grated cauliflower and mix well. Add salt and cook for 1 minute. Add coriander powder and red chilli powder and mix. Cover and cook on medium heat for 1 minute. Add yogurt and mix. Cover and cook on medium heat for 5-7 minutes until cauliflower is tender and flavors are well blended. Garnish with crushed cashewnuts and serve hot.

name: Moong Galouti
instructions: 1. Heat ghee in a shallow nonstick pan. Add caraway seeds, garlic, ginger and green chillies and sauté for 30 seconds. 2. Add cashew nuts, chironji, white pepper powder, green cardamom powder and garam masala powder and mix well. 3. Add fried onions, khoya and mix well. Cook for a minute. 4. Add cooked green gram, salt and mix well. Allow to cool slightly. 5. Transfer the cooked mixture in a food processor jar. Add lemon juice, mint, coriander and process to a smooth mixture. 6. Transfer the mixture in a bowl, add roasted gram flour and mix well. 7. Wet your palms with water, take a portion of the mixture and shape into a patty. Similarly make remaining galoutis. 8. Heat sufficient ghee in a shallow nonstick pan. Place the prepared galoutis and cook for 2-3 minutes on medium heat. 9. Flip and cook for 2 minutes more. Drain on absorbent paper. 10. Transfer on a serving plate and serve hot with green chutney and onion rings.

name: Chane Ke Chops
instructions: 1. Boil the kabuli chana with salt and tea leaves tied in a potli till completely soft. Drain and reserve the cooking stock. 2. Heat a non stick pan, add coriander seeds, fennel seeds and red chillies and roast till fragrant. 3. Roughly chop onion and add to the pan. Add ginger and roast for 2 minutes. Set aside to cool. 4. Mash the paneer in a bowl, add a little salt and shape into small balls. 5. Transfer the roasted spices into a mixer jar and grind with a little of the reserved cooking stock. Add the kabuli chana and grind, without adding any more water, till the chanas are well mashed. Transfer into a bowl. 6. Heat a little oil on a non stick tawa. Grease your palms, take a portion of the chana mixture and spread it. Place a paneer ball in the centre and enclose it completely. Flatten slightly and place on the tawa. Make other chops in a similar manner and place on the tawa. Turn once and cook till both sides are cooked evenly. 7. Serve hot.

name: Kaju Chicken Curry
ingredients: 500 grams boneless chicken leg, cut into 2 inch pieces
instructions: 1. Take chicken pieces in a large bowl, add green chilli paste, ginger-garlic paste and salt and mix well. Set aside for 15-20 minutes to marinate. 2. Heat 2.5 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan. Add black cardamoms, green cardamoms, cinnamon and cloves and sauté till fragrant. 3. Add boiled onion paste, saffron and cook on medium heat for 4-5 minutes. 4. Add cashew nut paste, salt, green cardamom powder, white pepper powder and mix well. Add 1 cup water and cook on medium heat for 6-8 minutes. 5. Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in another non-stick grill pan. Add marinated chicken and cook on high heat for 3-4 minutes. Flip and cook for 3-4 minutes more. 6. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Add 0.5 cup water, cover and cook for 3-4 minutes. 7. Add fresh cream and mix well. 8. Transfer in a serving bowl, drizzle some fresh cream, garnish with coriander sprig and serve hot with paranthas.

name: Moogacha Kadhan
instructions: 1. Heat pressure cooker, add sprouted green gram, salt and 2 cups water. Cover and cook on medium heat till pressure is released once. 2. Heat oil in pan, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, asafoetida and curry leaves, sauté for a few seconds. 3. Add chopped garlic, sauté till golden brown. 4. Lower heat, add turmeric powder and mix. 5. Add cooked green gram, salt and 1 cup water, cover and cook for 4-5 minutes. 6. Add coriander and mix well. 7. Transfer to serving bowl and serve hot.

name: Palak Ki Chutney
ingredients: split skinless black gram (dhuli urad dal) 1 tbsp
instructions: 1. Roughly chop onion and tomato. 2. Heat oil in pan, add chana dal and urad dal, sauté till light brown. Add asafoetida and red chillies. 3. Add onion and mix, then add tomato and mix again. 4. Tear spinach leaves and add, toss to mix. Add salt, green chillies, cook till spinach is soft. 5. Add coconut and mix well, then add tamarind pulp and mix. Cool. 6. Grind to a fine paste. 7. Serve as an accompaniment with idlis or dosas.

name: Aviyal
instructions: 1. Heat ghee or oil in a pan. 2. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves. 3. Add diced vegetables, turmeric and salt. Mix well. 4. Cook on medium heat for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender. 5. Add grated coconut and mix well. 6. Add green chillies. 7. Cook for 2-3 more minutes. 8. Add yoghurt and mix gently to combine. 9. Serve hot.

name: Saffron Rice Pudding
ingredients: short grain rice, soaked 2-3 hours, drained 0.75 cup
instructions: 1. Heat a shallow nonstick pan, add saffron and dry roast on low heat for 30 seconds. 2. Transfer to mortar and crush with pestle. Add 2-3 tbsp warm water and mix. 3. Heat a nonstick kadai, add 3 cups water and bring to boil. Add soaked rice and saffron water. 4. Cook on medium heat for 12-15 minutes till rice is completely cooked. 5. Add castor sugar and green cardamom powder, mix well. Cook till sugar melts. 6. Add butter and mix well. 7. Transfer to individual serving bowls. 8. Sprinkle cinnamon powder, garnish with pistachios and almonds. 9. Allow to cool to room temperature and serve.

name: Poha Biryani
ingredients: poha (flattened rice), washed and drained 2 cups
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds. 2. Add thinly sliced onions and fry until golden brown. 3. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies, sauté well. 4. Add bay leaf, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, turmeric powder and salt. Mix. 5. Add washed and drained poha, mix gently. 6. Cook on medium heat for 3-4 minutes. 7. Add fresh mint and coriander leaves. 8. Drizzle ghee and lemon juice. 9. Mix gently and serve hot.

name: Gahat Ka Parantha
ingredients: horse gram (gahat), soaked 8-10 hours, drained 0.75 cup
whole wheat flour (atta) 1.5 cups plus for dusting
instructions: 1. Heat pressure cooker, add horse gram, 0.5 tsp turmeric, 0.5 tsp red chilli, salt, 0.25 tsp amchur and 2 cups water. 2. Cover with lid and cook on medium heat till pressure is released 3-4 times. 3. Open lid once pressure settles. 4. Take whole wheat flour in a bowl. Add 2 tbsp oil, salt and 0.75 cup water, knead to soft dough. Cover and rest 10-15 minutes. 5. Drain water from horse gram and mash lightly. 6. Add coriander powder, remaining amchur, remaining turmeric, remaining red chilli, green chillies, ginger, garlic and coriander, mix well. 7. Divide dough and stuffing into equal portions. Roll dough into balls, make a dent, stuff mixture and gather edges. Seal properly. 8. Dust wheat flour and roll into thick disks. 9. Heat nonstick tawa. Place parantha and cook on medium heat for 2 minutes. Flip, drizzle ghee, cook 2 minutes. Flip again, drizzle ghee and cook on high heat for 1 minute on each side. 10. Serve hot with green chutney.

name: Shepu Moong Dal Bhaji
ingredients: 1/2 cup split skinless green gram (dhuli moong dal)
instructions: 1. Separate dill leaves and chop roughly. 2. Wash moong dal thoroughly and soak for 40-50 minutes. 3. Chop green chillies and garlic. 4. Heat oil in kadai, add asafoetida and cumin seeds, sauté until seeds change colour. 5. Add garlic and sauté until golden brown. 6. Add chillies and sauté for 1 minute. 7. Add soaked dal and turmeric powder, sauté for 3-4 minutes. 8. Add 3/4 cup water and salt, cover and cook for 5-6 minutes on low heat. 9. Add chopped dill leaves, mix well, cover and cook for 4-5 minutes on medium heat. 10. Serve hot with chapatis.

name: Til Pitha
instructions: 1. Wash rice thoroughly and soak for 3-4 hours. 2. Transfer sesame seeds to grinder jar, add fennel seeds and grind to coarse powder. 3. Mix ground sesame-fennel mixture with dried coconut and chopped jaggery in a bowl. 4. Drain soaked rice and pat dry with kitchen towel. 5. Grind rice to fine powder, transfer to bowl, sprinkle 1 tbsp water and mix until it forms stiff dough when pressed between fingers. 6. Heat tawa, sprinkle a portion of rice mixture and cook for 2-3 minutes. 7. Spread a portion of sesame-jaggery mixture on top and fold tightly. 8. Allow to cool and serve.

name: Onion Pakoda
instructions: 1. Slice onions thinly and transfer to bowl. 2. Add salt and mix, set aside for 10-15 minutes. 3. Add gram flour, crushed coriander seeds, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder and carom seeds, mix well. 4. Preheat air fryer at 200°C for 2-3 minutes. 5. Line air fryer basket with parchment paper and brush with oil. 6. Divide onion mixture into portions and place in single layer in basket. 7. Brush oil on top and air fry for 6 minutes. 8. Flip, apply more oil and air fry for 8 minutes. 9. Serve hot.

name: Dhaba Style Moong Tadka
ingredients: 1/4 tsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) powder
instructions: 1. Heat oil in nonstick kadai, add cumin seeds and once they change colour, add garlic and green chillies, sauté for 30 seconds. 2. Add onions and sauté until golden brown. Add tomato puree and salt, cover and cook until oil separates. 3. Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and cumin powder, mix well. 4. Add 1/2 cup water and cashew paste, mix well. 5. Add cooked green gram, garam masala powder, kasoori methi powder and fresh coriander leaves, mix well. 6. Add 1 cup water, cover and cook for 4-5 minutes. 7. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with coriander sprig and serve hot with paranthas.

name: oatmeal cookies
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with silicon sheet. Sift flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon powder into a bowl and mix well. In another bowl, beat butter and brown sugar with a hand blender for a couple of minutes. Add honey and vanilla essence and continue beating. Add eggs one at a time and beat. Add the flour mixture and mix well. Add oats and mix well. Add raisins and mix. Form walnut-sized balls of the cookie mixture and place on the tray with sufficient distance between each ball. Keep the tray in the preheated oven and bake for 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven and serve hot, or cool completely and store in an airtight container.

name: ice halwa
instructions: Crush roasted saffron coarsely and add 2 tbsps milk, mix well. Heat a nonstick kadai, add remaining milk and when warm, add ghee and refined flour and cook for 3-4 minutes until thick. Add castor sugar and cook till mixture starts to leave the sides of the pan. Add saffron milk and mix well. Test readiness by placing some on a plate; if it rolls easily without sticking when cooled, it's ready. Spread mixture between two pieces of butter paper and roll into a thin sheet with a rolling pin. Sprinkle almond flakes and pistachio powder and roll gently. Air dry for 2 days. Cut into squares and serve.

name: carrot and saffron risotto
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pan and add arborio rice with 2 tbsps butter and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Add onion and garlic and sauté till onion turns translucent. Add 1 cup vegetable stock and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add remaining vegetable stock and cook for 6-8 minutes. Add saffron and boiled carrot puree and mix well, cook for 1 minute. Add salt and black pepper powder. Separate leaves from thyme sprigs and add to the pan, cook for 1 minute. Grate parmesan cheese and add remaining butter and fresh cream, mix well. Transfer to serving plate, arrange blanched carrot slices on top, garnish with grated parmesan cheese and micro greens, and serve hot.

name: lauki moong dal sabzi
ingredients: 0.5 cup split skinless green gram (dhuli moong dal)
2 dried red chillies, stemmed and broken
instructions: Peel bottle gourd and cut into thin slices, then cut further into thin strips. Heat a shallow nonstick pan, add moong dal and sauté till golden brown. Transfer to water, wash well and drain. Heat mustard oil in a nonstick kadai. Add cumin seeds and when they start to change color, add ginger and sauté for 30 seconds. Add green chillies and dried red chillies and mix well. Add drained dal and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Add turmeric powder, cumin powder and salt and mix well. Add bottle gourd and mix well. Cover and cook on medium heat for 10-12 minutes. Add sugar and coriander and mix well. Transfer to a serving bowl and serve hot.

name: Soya Golmatol
instructions: 1. Heat sufficient oil in a kadai. Squeeze extra water from soaked soya nuggets and put in a bowl. Add green chilli sauce, soy sauce and 2 tsps cornstarch and mix. 2. Chop garlic coarsely and heat 2 tbsps oil in a non-stick wok. 3. Add soya nuggets to kadai oil and deep fry. 4. Add garlic to wok and sauté for 1-2 minutes. Add tomato ketchup, red chilli sauce and 0.5 cup water and mix well. Let it come to a boil. 5. Mix remaining cornstarch in 2 tbsps water and set aside. 6. Drain nuggets and add to sauce in wok and mix well. Cook for 2-3 minutes. 7. Add cornstarch mixture and mix well. Cook till sauce thickens, adjust water if needed. 8. Chop spring onion greens and transfer nuggets to serving bowl. Garnish with spring onion greens and sesame seeds. Serve hot.

name: Masala Aloo Fry
instructions: Cut boiled potatoes into cubes. Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds. Add minced garlic and ginger, sauté for 30 seconds. Add green chillies. Add potato cubes and mix gently. Sprinkle turmeric powder and salt. Fry on medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes get a golden-brown crust. Squeeze lemon juice and garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot.

name: Indian Style Macaroni
instructions: Boil water with salt, oil and macaroni for 6-7 minutes until al dente. Strain and coat with oil to prevent sticking. Heat oil in a wok, add jeera and let it splutter. Add ginger garlic paste and green chillies, saute for a minute. Add onions and cook until translucent. Add tomatoes and salt, cook until mushy. Add coriander powder, garam masala, amchur powder and tomato ketchup, cook 2-3 minutes. Add vegetables and cook 4-5 minutes. Add water and bring to boil. Add fresh cream and grated cheese, cook for a minute. Add boiled macaroni, mix well and cook 2 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

name: Dhuska with Aloo Curry
instructions: For Dhuska: Soak rice and both dals separately for 3-4 hours. Grind together with green chillies and ginger to a coarse paste. Add cumin seeds, coriander powder, chat masala, salt, and asafoetida. Mix well. Heat oil in a deep pan for frying. Make small oval shapes and deep fry until golden brown. For Aloo curry: Boil potatoes and cut into cubes. Heat oil, add onions and sauté. Add ginger-garlic paste and tomato. Add all spices (turmeric, red chilli, cumin, coriander, garam masala) and salt. Add potato cubes and simmer for 5-7 minutes. Serve dhuska hot with aloo curry on the side.

name: Rava Medu Vada
instructions: Mix semolina with yogurt, green chilli, ginger, onion, and coriander leaves. Add red chilli flakes, cumin seeds, and baking soda. Mix well to form a thick batter. Heat oil in a pan. Take spoonfuls of batter and drop into hot oil. Fry until golden brown on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Vegetable Dum Biryani
instructions: For marinate: In mixing bowl add winter carrots, cauliflower florets, french beans, fresh green peas and mix well. Add curd, ginger-garlic paste, ghee, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder, shahi jeera, saffron, javitri elaichi powder, mint leaves, salt, fried onion and mix well. Keep aside. For rice: In large saucepot add water for boiling, add bay leaf, big cardamom, javitri, clove, black peppercorns, salt and let water boil. Add soaked basmati rice and let it cook. Strain excess water and set aside. For biryani: In large saucepot add ghee, oil, onion and saute till translucent and brown. Keep aside. In same pot add remaining ghee, javitri, cloves, shahi jeera and let it splutter. Add marinated mixture and cook for 10 minutes. For jhol: In pan add saffron, green chilli, ghee and saute well. Add milk, onion flavored oil, kewra water, rose water and mix well. For layering: In saucepot arrange layer of rice at bottom, then half the cooked vegetables, then another layer of rice. Pour milk mixture around the rice with mint leaves and fried onion. Arrange remaining vegetables followed by remaining rice. Sprinkle remaining milk mixture, mint leaves and fried onion. Cover and seal with dough and cook for 20 minutes. Serve hot with raita. For burani raita: In bowl add curd, garlic, salt and mix well. Smoke with charcoal and clove.

name: Masala Paratha
instructions: Mix wheat flour with all spices: red chilli powder, garam masala, chat masala, cumin seeds, sambar masala, sesame seeds, and fenugreek leaves. Add coriander leaves. Knead with salt and water to form a soft dough. Let rest for 10 minutes. Divide into equal portions and roll out thin. Apply ghee, fold and roll again into a paratha. Cook on a hot griddle/tawa on medium-high heat until golden brown spots appear. Flip and cook the other side. Apply ghee on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Sooji Dahi Vada
instructions: Mix semolina with yogurt and let sit for 5 minutes. Add baking soda, green chilli, ginger, roasted cumin powder, coriander and mint leaves. Mix well. Heat oil in a pan. Using wet hands or a spoon, drop spoonfuls of mixture into hot oil. Fry until golden brown on all sides. Remove and soak in chilled yogurt for 30 minutes. Prepare sweet and spicy syrup with tamarind pulp and sugar. Pour syrup over vadas. Serve chilled.

name: Mysore Pak
instructions: Mix gram flour with ghee and sugar. Cook over medium heat while stirring continuously until mixture thickens and turns golden. Add cardamom powder. Pour onto a greased surface and cut into pieces once cool.

name: Eggless Waffle
instructions: Mix all purpose flour, powdered sugar, baking soda, and baking powder in a bowl. In another bowl, combine melted ghee and milk. Mix wet ingredients with dry ingredients until smooth batter forms. Pour batter into waffle maker and cook until golden brown.

name: Eggless Muffins
instructions: Mix all purpose flour, milk powder, baking powder, and baking soda. In separate bowl, combine melted butter, condensed milk, vanilla essence, and milk. Mix wet and dry ingredients until just combined. Fold in tutti frutti. Pour into muffin tins. Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until golden.

name: Maggi with Egg Omelette
instructions: Boil water and cook maggi noodles with tastemaker. Chop all vegetables finely. Add chopped vegetables to cooked maggi and mix well. In a separate pan, heat oil and make an omelette with beaten eggs, fold and serve alongside the maggi.

name: Red Chilli Pickle (Lal Mirch Ka Achar)
instructions: Roast and grind all spices (mustard seeds, fennel, cumin, coriander, methi, black pepper, dry red chilli, hing, ajwain, kalonji). Mix roasted spices with turmeric, red chilli powder, and dry mango powder. Slit red chillies lengthwise without cutting through completely. Stuff each chilli with the spice mix. Heat mustard oil, cool slightly, mix with stuffed chillies and salt. Pack in sterilized glass jars. Ferment for 3-7 days before serving.

name: Homemade Pepsi Cola Ice Lolly
instructions: Dissolve sugar in water over heat. Add cola essence and caramel coloring to get brown color. Add citric acid and lemon juice for tanginess. Cool the syrup completely. Pour into ice lolly molds and insert sticks. Freeze for 6-8 hours until solid.

name: Schezwan Noodles
instructions: Make noodle dough with refined flour, salt, vinegar, water, turmeric powder and knead with cornstarch. Rest for 20-30 minutes covered. Roll very thin, trim edges to rectangle, dust with cornstarch and fold repeatedly with dusting. Cut into strips and unroll gently. Boil water with salt and oil, cook noodles for 10 seconds until done. Strain and cool with oil. Heat oil in wok, add ginger, garlic, green chillies and saute. Add onions, carrot, cabbage, capsicum and saute for 2-3 minutes. Add szechuan chutney and char for a minute. Add cooked noodles, water and toss well. Garnish with coriander.

name: Rava Uttapam Pizza
instructions: Mix semolina with curd and water, add baking soda and let batter rest for 5 minutes. Heat greased non-stick pan, pour batter and spread thin, add chopped toppings (capsicum, onion, french beans, tomato) and cheese. Add tomato ketchup and schezwan sauce, sprinkle chilli flakes and oregano. Cook until golden from both sides and serve hot.

name: Sarso Ka Saag
instructions: Blanch mustard leaves, spinach and bahthua leaves, drain and grind to fine paste. Heat ghee, add chopped onion, add minced garlic and ginger, add tomato, cook well. Add greens paste, add corn meal for thickness and to absorb moisture. Add salt and red chilli powder if desired. Cook on low heat stirring occasionally for 8-10 minutes. Top with butter and serve hot.

name: Paneer Shimlamirch
instructions: Cut paneer into cubes and vegetables into pieces. Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds. Add diced onion and cook until translucent. Add diced tomato and cook until soft. Add turmeric, red chilli, coriander, cumin and garam masala powders. Add paneer and capsicum pieces, mix gently and cook for 3-4 minutes until coated with spices and heated through.

name: Anda Bhuna Masala
instructions: Boil and halve eggs. Roast cumin seeds, coriander seeds, fennel seeds, black pepper, nutmeg, cardamom, dry chilli, mace and cinnamon in a dry pan, let cool and grind to fine powder for bhuna masala. Heat oil, add sliced onion and fry until golden brown. Add ginger garlic paste, cook well. Add tomato and turmeric powder, cook until tomato is soft. Add red chilli powder, fenugreek leaves and bhuna masala powder. Add boiled eggs, mix gently and cook for 3-4 minutes until masala coats eggs well.

name: raw papaya kofta
instructions: Form raw papaya into koftas by mixing grated papaya with gram flour, ginger garlic paste, spices, and herbs. Deep fry until golden. Prepare curry by tempering oil with cumin seeds and bay leaves, add onions and tomato base, season with spice powders, then add fried koftas and simmer until tender.

name: baby potatoes and peas curry
instructions: Temper mustard oil with whole spices including cumin seeds, star anise, bay leaf, and cardamom. Add chopped onions and tomato paste, cook well. Add baby potatoes and peas, season with powder spices and salt. Pressure cook until potatoes are tender, then garnish with coriander leaves.

name: andhra mango pickle
instructions: Chop raw mangoes into pieces. Toast and grind mustard seeds partially. Mix all spices including turmeric, red chilli powder, and fenugreek seeds. Combine mango pieces with ground spices, garlic, and oil. Mix well and store in an airtight jar, avoiding direct sunlight for curing.

name: Veg Biryani
instructions: Make fried onions by deep frying sliced onions until golden. Marinate carrots, beans, cauliflower, paneer, fried onion, curd, mint, peas with salt, spices and ginger garlic paste. In cooker, heat ghee and temper with bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom. Add marinated vegetables and saute. Cover and cook 2-4 minutes. Add mint, soaked rice, hot water, fried onions, green chilli, garam masala, salt, kewra water and saffron strands. Cover and cook for 1 whistle on medium flame. Let cool naturally. Open and fluff with fork. Serve with raita made from potatoes, onion, tomato, curd, mint, coriander and spices.

name: Medu Vada
instructions: Grind soaked urad dal into smooth batter, adding little water while grinding. Transfer to bowl. Add chopped green chillies, coriander leaves, ginger, curry leaves, fresh coconut and crushed black peppercorns. Mix well with salt to taste. Apply water on both hands. Take some batter and make round shape. With thumb make hole in center or use banana leaves for shaping. Heat oil in kadai on medium flame. Slide vada into hot oil. Once slightly golden, turn to other side. Fry on medium flame so it cooks from inside. Remove on kitchen tissue. Fry again for even crispness and golden color. Drain on kitchen tissue to remove excess oil. Serve medu vada with hot sambar and coconut chutney.

name: veg roll
instructions: Make a thin dough with wheat flour, water, and oil. Cook on griddle to make thin wraps. Saute chopped vegetables lightly. Layer mayonnaise, vegetables, and sauces on wrap, roll tightly, and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Biscuit Kalakand
instructions: Crush biscuits finely. Mix butter with milk and prepare base. Blend paneer with condensed milk and sugar. Layer biscuit crumbs and paneer mixture. Sprinkle cardamom powder. Set in refrigerator and cut into pieces.

name: Veg Coconut Sandwich
instructions: Blend coriander, mint, coconut, green chilli, garlic and ginger to make chutney. Add spice powders and salt. Spread mayonnaise and chutney on bread. Layer grated vegetables and cheese. Butter and toast on pan until golden and crispy.

name: Ginger Mint Tea
instructions: Crush ginger and mint leaves. Boil water with crushed ginger and mint. Add tea leaves and boil for 2 minutes. Add milk and sugar. Simmer and strain. Serve hot.

name: Achari Mushroom
instructions: Heat oil and add ginger garlic paste. Stir-fry onions and tomatoes until soft. Add all spice powders and mix well. Add mushrooms and cook until tender. Add mixed pickle and finish with garam masala. Garnish with fresh herbs.

name: Boiled Egg Bhurji
instructions: Heat oil, add bay leaves, cinnamon and clove. Fry onions and add ginger garlic paste. Add tomatoes and all spice powders. Cook until oil separates. Add boiled eggs cut into pieces. Mix well and add garam masala. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Rava Dhokla
instructions: Mix semolina with all chopped vegetables, herbs and spices. Add water to make thick batter. Add eno salt just before steaming. Pour into greased container. Steam for 15-20 minutes until set. Temper with oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves. Serve warm.

name: chicken fried rice
instructions: Cook rice and chicken separately. Heat oil in a wok, add ginger and garlic. Stir-fry vegetables until cooked. Add cooked rice and chicken, mix well. Add soy sauce, chilli sauce, and vinegar. Scramble egg separately and fold in. Toss everything together with black pepper and salt.

name: wheat flour chocolate cake
instructions: Mix wheat flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and baking powder in a bowl. In another bowl, whisk condensed milk, ghee, vanilla essence, milk, and water. Combine wet and dry ingredients. Pour into greased cooker container. Place on medium heat for 40-45 minutes. Check with toothpick for doneness. Cool and slice.

name: Mysore Bonda
instructions: Mix refined flour and rice flour. Add curd and blend well. Add chopped coriander, green chili, ginger and cumin seeds. Add salt and baking soda. Heat oil and carefully drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil. Deep fry until golden brown on all sides. Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towel.

name: pizza sandwich
instructions: Chop all vegetables finely. Mix vegetables with oregano, chilli flakes, pizza mix, and salt. Spread butter on bread slices. Apply pizza mix seasoning. Layer vegetable mixture and grated cheese. Top with another bread slice. Toast on both sides on a tava or skillet until cheese melts and bread turns golden.

name: achari maggi
instructions: Boil water in a pan. Add maggi noodles and tastemakers. Cook until soft. Meanwhile, heat oil and sauté onions. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add peas and paneer pieces. Add mixed pickle and red chilli powder. Once noodles are cooked, drain and add to the pan. Toss everything together for 2-3 minutes.

name: masala macaroni pasta
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain and set aside. Chop all vegetables finely. Heat oil in a pan. Add green chilli and stir-fry vegetables until cooked. Add tomato ketchup, mixed herbs, pasta mix, and kashmiri chilli powder. Mix well. Add cooked pasta and toss everything together. Cook for 2-3 minutes on high heat. Top with cheese if desired.

name: No Onion Garlic Samosa
instructions: Make dough with maida and water. Prepare filling with boiled potatoes, ginger, green chilli, and spice blend. Encase filling in dough triangles and deep fry until golden.

name: Vegetable Bread Roll
instructions: Mix grated vegetables with boiled potatoes and cheese. Spread mixture on bread slices, roll tightly, and deep fry until golden brown. Serve hot.

name: Paneer Roll
instructions: Make dough with all purpose flour, wheat flour, salt, oil and water. Let it rest. For filling, saute garlic, onion and peppers. Add paneer, chilli flakes and schezwan chutney. Roll out dough, fill with paneer mixture, roll tightly. Cook on griddle until golden. Serve with tomato ketchup and mayonnaise.

name: Chilli Garlic Paratha
instructions: Make wheat dough with water and salt. Prepare garlic-herb butter with minced garlic, oregano, chilli flakes, and coriander. Roll dough, spread garlic butter, layer and roll again, flatten, and cook on hot tawa with oil until golden and crispy.

name: Vegetable Rice Manchurian
instructions: Shape leftover rice into balls and deep fry until crispy. Prepare gravy with garlic, onion, tomato, capsicum, cabbage, chilli flakes, ketchup, and chutney. Toss fried rice balls in gravy and serve hot.

name: Egg Roll
instructions: Mix wheat flour and all purpose flour. Make dough with 2 eggs and water. Finely chop onion and capsicum. Mix filling with mayo, ketchup, and chat masala. Roll the dough thin, add filling, roll into cylindrical shape. Beat remaining eggs and coat the rolls. Fry in hot oil until golden brown.

name: Mixed Pickle
instructions: Wash and cut carrots and radish into small pieces. Finely chop garlic and green chilli. In a large bowl, mix carrots, radish, garlic, and green chilli. Dry roast all the seeds separately in a pan until fragrant. Mix turmeric powder, red chilli powder, dry mango powder with the vegetables. Add the roasted seeds. Pour mustard oil over the mixture and mix thoroughly. Transfer to clean glass jar and let it sit for a few days before consuming.

name: Soya Biryani
instructions: Soak soya chunks in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze dry. Boil rice with whole spices until 70% cooked. Heat oil and ghee, deep fry sliced onions until golden brown and crispy. In a pot, layer rice, soya chunks, tomato, ginger-garlic paste, herbs, and fried onions. Sprinkle spice powders and saffron. Cover with foil and then place lid. Pressure cook on high flame for 1-2 whistles, then on low flame for 2-3 minutes.

name: Egg Drop Soup
instructions: Sauté ginger-garlic in butter, add chopped onion and cook till soft. Add chopped tomatoes and simmer. Mix corn flour with water and stir into the broth. Bring to boil, slowly pour beaten eggs while stirring. Add spring onion, coriander leaves, vinegar and black pepper. Simmer for 2-3 minutes and serve hot.

name: Tandoori Paneer Sandwich
instructions: Toast bread slices lightly. Spread tandoori mayonnaise on both slices. Layer cucumber, tomato, jalapeno, onion, lettuce and capsicum. Place grilled paneer on top. Add cheese if desired, sprinkle black pepper and salt. Close and serve immediately.

name: mixed vegetable pakora
instructions: Make batter: Mix gram flour, salt, carom seeds, baking soda and water. Add curd, mix in rice flour and oil, rest 9-10 minutes. For bhavnagri stuffing: Mix paneer, coriander leaves, salt, green chutney, nylon sev and crushed coriander seeds. Stuff into slit bhavnagri chillies. For bhajiya: Mix vegetables, seeds, salt, green chilli, turmeric and ginger-garlic paste. Remove excess water. Add gram flour and mix. Fry potatoes, onion, paneer and tomato slices in batter until half done. Dip stuffed bhavnagri in batter with nylon sev coating and deep fry. Add bhajiya mixture in small parts and deep fry until crisp. Fry battered green chilli. Deep fry half-done pakoras until crispy. Serve hot with chutney.

name: Sattu Paratha with Roasted Tomato Chutney
ingredients: mustard oil 2 tbsp plus for cooking
instructions: Knead wheat flour with water. Mix sattu with chopped green chilli, garlic, onion, ginger, coriander, lemon juice, ajwain and salt. Fill dough with sattu mixture, roll into paratha and cook on griddle with mustard oil until golden. For chutney: roast tomatoes on flame, then grind with green chilli, garlic, onion, coriander and salt. Serve hot paratha with roasted tomato chutney.

name: Chana Dal Sabzi
instructions: Heat oil and temper with cumin seeds. When seeds crackle, add onions and sauté till golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, then tomato paste. Cook till oil separates. Add turmeric and red chilli powder. Stir in cooked chana dal, add bay leaves, cinnamon, black cardamom. Simmer for 5-7 minutes. Add remaining spices, garnish with coriander and serve.

name: Egg Drop Curry
instructions: Boil and halve eggs. Heat oil and add cumin seeds. When they crackle, add onions and sauté till golden. Add ginger-garlic, then tomato paste. Cook till oil separates. Add turmeric and red chilli powder. Pour in water (about 1 cup), add bay leaf and green cardamom. Bring to boil, then add halved eggs and simmer. Add remaining spices, adjust salt and garnish with coriander.

name: desi paneer taco
instructions: Mix wheat flour with yogurt or water to form dough with baking powder. Prepare filling by mixing paneer, chopped onion, tomato, cumin seeds, chilli flakes, mixed herbs and tomato ketchup. Roll dough, stuff with paneer filling, seal edges. Cook on hot griddle with oil until golden brown and cooked through.

name: strawberry barfi sandwich
instructions: Soak jim jam biscuits briefly. Mix paneer with sugar and milk powder into thick paste. Add saffron to flavor. Layer biscuits with strawberry syrup and paneer mixture. Top with pistachio garnish. Set in refrigerator until firm.

name: Aloo Pakora
instructions: Mix chickpea flour and semolina. Add water to make a pouring consistency batter. Season with salt, coriander powder, chili powder, green chilis, and green coriander. Add baking soda and let sit for 10-15 minutes to puff up. Slice boiled potatoes into thin 1/2 cm rounds. Coat potato slices with batter. Heat a tawa with 2 tbsp oil and spread evenly. Place battered potato slices on the tawa at low flame. Roast until golden brown underneath, then flip and roast the other side until crispy. Remove and serve hot with tomato sauce or chutney.

name: desi veg chowmein
instructions: Boil noodles until cooked and drain. Chop all vegetables finely. Heat oil in wok or large pan. Stir-fry garlic and green chilli. Add all vegetables and stir-fry until partially cooked. Add cooked noodles and toss well. Season with chilli powder, black pepper, fennel powder, coriander powder and salt. Toss until combined.

name: Paneer Mayo Roll
instructions: Make dough with all purpose flour, salt and cooking oil. Let rest. Crumble paneer and mix with chopped vegetables, spices, mayo and ketchup. Roll out dough into thin sheets. Place filling on dough, roll tightly and fry in oil until golden brown.

name: soya chilli
instructions: Soak soya chunks in hot water and cook until soft. Drain and dry. Coat with corn flour and all purpose flour mixed with salt and pepper. Deep fry until golden. Make sauce by mixing soy sauce, ketchup, chutney, chilli sauce and vinegar. Chop onions, capsicum, spring onion. Stir-fry vegetables with garlic and green chilli. Add fried soya and sauce. Toss well.

name: Cabbage Egg Fry
instructions: Heat oil and temper with cumin seeds. Add chopped cabbage and cook until tender. Add tomato, green chilli and spices. Push vegetables to side and scramble eggs in the center. Mix everything together and garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Paneer Pulao
instructions: Sauté onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and spices. Add rice and paneer cubes. Add water and pressure cook until rice is done. Fluff with a fork and serve.

name: Bread Omelette
instructions: Beat eggs with salt and pepper. Heat oil in pan and add chopped onion, tomato, capsicum and green chilli. Pour beaten eggs over and scramble. Place on bread slices to form omelette and serve hot.

name: Oreo Black Forest Cake
instructions: Crush oreo cookies and mix with baking powder and soda. Add milk and melted ghee to form batter. Bake until cooked. Prepare sugar syrup with sugar and water. Pour syrup on cooled cake. Whip cream and layer on cake with chocolate compound. Garnish with cherry.

name: Mooli Kofta Curry
instructions: Make kofta dough by mixing grated radish, besan, carom seeds, ginger, green chilli, garam masala, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, salt. Shape into balls and fry until golden. For curry base, grind garlic and ginger. Heat oil, add cumin seeds and bay leaves, add garlic-ginger paste, cook until fragrant. Add chopped onion and tomato, cook until soft. Add turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, black pepper. Add the fried koftas and simmer until curry thickens.

name: Chena Rasgulla
instructions: Heat milk in a pot. Add white vinegar slowly until milk curdles. Drain the whey using a cheesecloth and collect the chena (paneer). Knead the chena to make it smooth and soft. Divide into equal portions and shape into balls. Prepare sugar syrup by boiling sugar and water. Add the chena balls to the boiling sugar syrup. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the rasgullas float and become spongy. Serve warm or chilled.

name: Crispy Rice Flour Vegetable Fritters
instructions: Mix rice flour with all vegetables and seasonings. Add water gradually to make a thick batter. Heat oil in a deep pan. Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil. Fry until golden brown on both sides. Drain on paper towels. Serve hot.

name: Poha
instructions: Rinse poha briefly and drain, mix with salt and sugar, heat oil and temper with mustard seeds, add green chili and curry leaves, add poha and cook 2 minutes, squeeze lemon juice, top with peanuts and besan sev.

name: Indian Style Spaghetti Pasta
instructions: Boil spaghetti according to package directions, drain and set aside. Heat oil in a pan, add curry leaves and green chilli. Add diced onion and cook until translucent. Add carrot, capsicum, french beans and broccoli. Stir-fry vegetables until tender-crisp. Add cooked spaghetti and toss well. Season with salt and black pepper. Serve hot.

name: Biscuit Cake
instructions: Crush bourbon biscuits into coarse crumbs. Heat oil/ghee/butter and add crushed biscuits. Mix in milk gradually to form a cake-like mixture. Layer the mixture in a baking pan. Top with chopped cashews. Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Cut into pieces and serve cold.

name: Corn Fried Rice
instructions: Cook rice and spread on a plate to cool completely. Mince garlic and green chilli. Heat oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Add garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add diced onion, carrot, french beans and corn. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp. Add rice and break up any clumps. Toss in chilli flakes and black pepper. Season with salt and lemon juice. Serve hot.

name: Red Lentil Carrot Soup
instructions: Boil red lentils and carrots with water. In a separate pan, temper cumin seeds and bay leaf in ghee. Add onion, garlic, and cook until golden. Add turmeric, salt, and green chilli. Combine with lentil mixture. Simmer for 5-10 minutes. Finish with fresh lemon juice and coriander leaves. Serve hot.

name: Maggi Manchurian
instructions: Boil maggi noodles and drain. Heat oil in a wok, add sliced garlic and green chilli. Add sliced onion and cook until golden. Add capsicum pieces and spring onion. Add cooked noodles. Mix in maggi tastemakers, soy sauce, vinegar, chilli sauces, and schezwan chutney. Toss continuously for 2-3 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Banarasi Tomato Chaat
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add finely chopped tomatoes, ginger, and green chilli. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, salt, and chaat masala. Prepare sweet and sour water by mixing water, sugar, roasted cumin powder, black salt, chaat masala powder, and amchur powder. Pour this mixture over cooked tomatoes. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve immediately.

name: Butter Garlic Noodles
instructions: Boil noodles and drain well. In a wok over high heat, add butter and let it brown. Add minced garlic and cook until fragrant and lightly burnt. Add sliced onion and green chilli. Sauté for 1 minute. Add capsicum, cabbage, and spring onion. Toss well. Add cooked noodles. Season with vinegar, soy sauce, ketchup, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly for 2-3 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Egg Omelette Curry
instructions: Beat eggs with chopped green chilli, onion, and salt. Heat 2-3 tbsp oil in a pan and make omelette, cook until set. Cut into pieces. For curry: heat 3 tbsp oil, add minced ginger and garlic, cook for 1 minute. Add chopped onion and cook until golden. Add tomato and simmer until soft. Add turmeric, red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala. Simmer for 2 minutes. Add omelette pieces and cook for 3-5 minutes. Garnish with coriander leaves. Serve hot.

name: Mixed Veg Pickle
instructions: Cut all vegetables into small pieces. Dry roast mustard seeds, fennel, coriander, cumin, black pepper and fenugreek seeds until fragrant. Cool and crush coarsely. Heat mustard oil, add crushed spices and let it cool. Mix all vegetables with turmeric, red chilli powder, dry mango powder, carom seeds and salt. Combine with spiced oil and vinegar. Store in airtight jar for 2-3 days before consuming. Flavor improves with time.

name: Potato Cheese Donuts
instructions: Mash boiled potatoes. Mix with corn flour, all purpose flour, chilli flakes, oregano and salt. Knead into dough. Shape into donuts/rings using donut mold or hands. Roll in bread crumbs. Heat oil in deep pan. Fry donuts until golden brown and crispy on both sides. Drain on paper towel. Serve hot as a snack.

name: Masaledar Aloo Baingan
instructions: Cut brinjal and potatoes into medium pieces. Chop onions, tomatoes, ginger and garlic. Heat oil, add cumin seeds, cardamom, bay leaves and cinnamon, let them crackle. Add ginger-garlic paste, sauté until fragrant. Add onions and cook until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add potatoes and brinjal, mix well. Add turmeric, red chilli and coriander powders. Cover and cook on low heat until vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally. Add garam masala and salt at the end. Cook for 2 more minutes.

name: Pitla Bhakri Thecha
instructions: For pitla: Mix besan with water smoothly. Heat oil, add mustard and cumin seeds, let crackle. Add curry leaves, green chilli-garlic paste and turmeric. Pour besan mixture slowly, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Cook until thickened. Add coriander leaves, lemon juice and salt. For bhakri: Knead jowar flour with water and salt, roll thin and cook on hot griddle. For thecha: Dry roast peanuts, crush coarsely. Pound garlic, green chilli, curry leaves with peanuts and salt to form coarse paste. Serve pitla, bhakri and thecha together.

name: Cajun Spiced Potatoes
instructions: Boil baby potatoes until tender. Drain and let dry. Mix mayonnaise with red chilli sauce, chilli flakes, oregano, black peppers, ginger-garlic powder and salt. Toss potatoes in corn flour and maida. Deep fry until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towel. Toss fried potatoes in the mayonnaise mixture. Garnish with spring onion and serve hot.

name: Sabudana Kheer
instructions: Boil full cream milk. Cut dry fruits and soak saffron strands in a little milk. Crush green cardamom seeds to make coarse powder. When milk boils, add soaked sago pearls and cook on high flame until it boils again. Add raisins, dry fruits and saffron milk. Stir at intervals and cook on medium flame until dense. Add sugar and cardamom powder, mix well and cook for 1-2 minutes. Turn off flame and let cool. Serve in bowls and garnish with dry fruits.

name: Ramen Noodles with Egg
instructions: Boil water in a pot. Add instant noodles and cook until tender. Drain well. In a wok or large skillet, heat oil over high heat. Add vegetables (broccoli, french beans, carrot) and paneer, stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Add cooked noodles, tastemaker, soy sauce, chilli flakes, red chilli powder and butter. Toss well. Top with sliced boiled egg, fried egg, spring onion and sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

name: Kadhi Pakoda
instructions: For pakoda: Mix besan with carom seeds, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, baking soda and salt. Add water to make thick batter. Heat oil in a deep pan for frying. Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil and deep fry until golden. Drain on paper towels. For kadhi: Mix besan with curd and water to make smooth paste. Heat oil in a pot, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. When they crackle, add green chilli and garlic. Add besan-curd mixture stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Add hing, curry leaves and turmeric powder. Cook until it comes to boil. Add salt. Gently add fried pakora into the kadhi. Simmer for 5-10 minutes.

name: Veg Mayo Parcel
instructions: For dough: Mix all purpose flour with baking soda, curd and salt. Add water gradually and knead into soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes. For stuffing: Mix cabbage, onion, capsicum and coriander leaves. Add mayonnaise, schezwan chutney, chilli flakes, oregano and salt. Mix well. Divide dough into equal portions. Roll out thin between plastic sheets. Place filling in center and fold into a parcel, sealing edges. Heat oil in a deep pan. Deep fry parcels until golden brown on all sides. Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with tomato sauce or green chutney.

name: corn mushroom sabzi
instructions: Heat oil and add cumin seeds, black cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaves. Once fragrant, add chopped onion and cook until golden. Add ginger garlic paste and cook. Add mushrooms and corn, stir well. Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chilli, and spice powders. Cook until mushrooms are tender. Add roasted gram flour if needed for consistency. Finish with garam masala.

name: shahi paneer masala
instructions: Heat oil and add cumin seeds, black cardamom, cloves, black peppers, bay leaves. Once fragrant, add tomato and cook until soft. Grind tomato, cashew paste, poppy seeds, and coconut together. Add this paste back to the pan. Add paneer pieces and cook gently. Add turmeric, red chilli, cumin, coriander powders. Finish with garam masala and dry fenugreek leaves. Top with butter.

name: manchurian fried rice
instructions: Prepare manchurian: chop vegetables finely, mix with corn flour, spices and sauces, form small balls and deep fry until golden. For fried rice: heat oil, add garlic, green chilli, spring onion. Add vegetables and boiled rice. Stir fry continuously, add schezwan chutney, soya sauce, black pepper. Finally toss in fried manchurian balls and serve hot.

name: papdi chaat
instructions: Make papdi dough with flour, semolina, salt, sugar, ghee and water. Roll thin and cut into squares. Deep fry until crisp. Make green chutney by grinding coriander, mint, ginger, green chilli with salt. Make tamarind chutney with tamarind pulp, salt, sugar, red chilli powder and water. Roast and crush cumin seeds.
