Strain jaggery syrup into the flour mixture, add ghee, mix well. Grease hands with ghee and shape the mixture into laddus. Cool and store in airtight container.

name: chocolate nankhatai
instructions: Mix wheat flour, chickpea flour, semolina, baking powder, and cocoa powder. Dissolve lumps with a strainer. Add powdered sugar, ghee, and mix well. Add milk and almond flakes and mix thoroughly. Preheat 300-400g of salt in cooker on high flame for 7-8 minutes. Grease a plate with ghee, shape dough into nankhatai. Place stand in preheated cooker and put plate on it. Close lid without whistle, turn to medium-high flame. Bake for 12 minutes. Remove plate and allow to cool.

name: cashew almond butter cookies
instructions: Cream butter and powdered sugar. Add almond powder and mix well. Fold in refined flour mixed with baking powder using a strainer to remove lumps. Add crushed green cardamom and milk gradually to form dough. Shape into cookies and place on greased baking surface. Top each with a cashew or almond. Bake in oven or cooker-based baking method until golden. Cool and store in airtight container.

name: raw banana bharta
instructions: Peel and dice raw bananas into small pieces. Heat oil in a pan, add chopped onions and cook until soft. Add ginger and green chili, fry for a minute. Add diced banana pieces and turmeric powder. Mash the banana pieces with the back of a spoon as they cook. Continue cooking until bananas are soft and well mixed with onions. Add salt to taste. Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot.

name: watermelon rind halwa
instructions: Peel the outer green skin of watermelon and shred the white rind. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add shredded watermelon rind and cook on medium flame, stirring continuously. Cook until the rind softens and moisture evaporates. Add milk and milk powder, continue cooking and stirring. Add sugar gradually and mix well. Cook until the mixture becomes thick and halwa consistency is achieved. Add cardamom powder and mix. Garnish with chopped almonds and cashews. Transfer to a plate and allow to cool slightly before serving.

name: ambarella pickle
instructions: Cut ambarella fruit into small pieces. Mix with salt and let sit for 2-3 hours to draw out juices. Heat oil in a clean glass jar. Add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and nigella seeds, let them crackle. Add red chili powder and turmeric powder, mix well. Add salted ambarella pieces and stir thoroughly. Close the jar tightly and store in sunlight for 3-4 days, shaking occasionally. The pickle will develop flavor as it ferments. Can be consumed after a week and will keep for several months.

name: Kidney Bean Tacos, Burger and Sandwich
instructions: Cook kidney beans until soft. Prepare filling with beans, mayo, and seasonings. For tacos: use tortillas; for burgers: toast bread buns and layer; for sandwich: use bread slices. Assemble with lettuce, tomato and bean mixture.

name: Paneer Stuffed Palak Paratha
instructions: Blanch and chop spinach. Make dough with wheat flour and spinach. For filling: crumble paneer and mix with chopped green chilies, ginger, garlic and salt. Roll dough into thin circle, place paneer mixture in center, fold and flatten. Cook on griddle with ghee until brown spots appear on both sides.

name: Steamed Masala Bun
instructions: Prepare dough with flour, yeast, salt, sugar and oil. Let rise for 1-2 hours. Prepare masala filling with boiled mashed potatoes mixed with sauteed onion, green chilies, ginger-garlic paste and spices. Stuff dough portions with filling. Steam in steamer basket for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.

name: Capsicum Pickle
instructions: Wash and chop capsicum into pieces. Salt and let sit for 1 hour. Mix mustard oil, vinegar and spices. Combine capsicum with spiced oil mixture. Transfer to clean jar and seal. Let pickle for 2-3 days before serving.

name: Potato Eggplant with Radish Leaves Sabzi
instructions: Cut potato and eggplant into small pieces. Clean and chop radish leaves finely. Heat oil and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds for tempering. Add onion and cook until soft. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Add potato and eggplant, cook covered until tender. Add radish leaves and cook for 2-3 minutes. Season with salt and spice powders.

name: Stuffed Brinjal
instructions: Cut brinjals lengthwise and scoop out centers. Finely chop scooped flesh. Heat oil, sauté onions until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and green chili. Add brinjal flesh, turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder and salt. Cook until dry. Stuff mixture into brinjal halves. Arrange in microwave dish with little water, cover and microwave on high for 8-10 minutes until tender.

name: Cabbage Stuffed Paratha
instructions: For dough: mix wheat flour with salt and 2 tsp oil, knead with water into soft dough, rest 15-20 minutes. For stuffing: clean and separate cabbage leaves, dip in salt water for 10 minutes, drain and dry. Chop finely. Heat 2 tsp oil, roast cumin seeds, add ginger paste and green chillies, sauté. Add cabbage, coriander powder, chilli powder, salt and cook 2 minutes. Add green coriander, cook 1-2 minutes more. Roll dough ball, spread oil, add stuffing, fold into square, seal. Roll flat, cook on griddle with oil until golden, pressing gently.

name: Rakhiya Vadi
instructions: Soak urad dal 2-3 hours, drain and grind to paste. Mix with asafoetida, grated ginger and 1 tbsp water. Peel kumhra, grate and squeeze dry in cloth with weight. Whisk dal, add baking soda, whisk again. Drop dal in water - if floats, it's ready. Add grated kumhra and mix well. Cover overnight. Next morning, mix in roasted spices (cumin, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon, coriander), add salt and green chili. Grease thalis and hands with oil. Pinch dal portions onto thalis leaving space between. Dry in sunlight for 2-3 days until completely dry. Store in airtight container.

name: Green Peas Halwa
instructions: Boil green peas and blend into smooth paste. Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan on medium heat. Add pea paste and roast for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly. Add milk and sugar, mix well. Continue cooking, stirring frequently for about 8-10 minutes until halwa leaves the sides of pan and attains a putty-like consistency. Add crushed cardamom and dry fruits. Pour into greased plate, let cool slightly and cut into desired shapes. Serve warm.

name: Besan Mawa Barfi
ingredients: dry fruits (almonds, cashews, raisins) 1/4 cup chopped
instructions: Heat 4 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan on medium heat. Add besan and roast for 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until light golden and fragrant. Add mawa/khoya and remaining ghee, mix well. Continue roasting for 2-3 minutes. Add sugar and cardamom, mix thoroughly. Cook for 2-3 minutes more, stirring constantly until mixture comes together and leaves the pan sides. Add chopped dry fruits and mix. Pour into greased 8x8 inch pan, press with back of spatula. Let cool slightly and cut into barfi pieces. Cool completely and store in airtight container.

name: Non-fried Gulab Jamun
ingredients: sugar syrup: sugar 1 cup, water 1 cup, cardamom 4-5 pods
instructions: Crumble khoya and mix with milk powder, ghee, crushed cardamom and chopped dry fruits. Shape into small balls (gulab jamun size). Prepare sugar syrup by boiling sugar and water with cardamom for 5 minutes. Add saffron and rose water to syrup. Gently place gulab jamun balls in hot sugar syrup (do not boil). Let simmer for 5-7 minutes on low heat. The jamuns will absorb syrup and become soft. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Butter Murukku
instructions: Mix chickpea flour and rice flour. Heat water with butter, asafoetida, cumin seeds and salt. Add this warm water to flour mixture to make a dough. Knead until smooth. Preheat oil for frying. Shape dough portions and fry on medium heat until golden brown on both sides. Drain and cool completely before storing in airtight container.

name: Lemon Peel Pickle
instructions: Cut squeezed lemon peels into small thin pieces. Mix with turmeric powder and salt. Boil peels in water for 30 minutes on low-medium flame until softened. Heat oil, add asafoetida, carom seeds and nigella seeds, then add lemon peels with spices. Mix in garam masala, roasted cumin powder, red chili powder and black salt. Add lemon juice. Divide into two portions: add powdered sugar and fennel powder to one portion. Store in containers and consume after one week.

name: Bajra Atta Ladoo
instructions: Crush jaggery coarsely. Heat ghee and deep fry edible gum until golden brown. Remove and set aside. Roast millet flour in same ghee for 15 minutes until aromatic and color changes. Melt jaggery in same wok. Mix roasted flour with chopped almonds, cashews, grated coconut, fried gum, cardamom powder and melted jaggery. Bind into small to medium sized balls. Cool completely and store in airtight container.

name: Atta Besan Ladoo
instructions: Roast chickpea flour and wheat flour separately. Fry edible gum in ghee until puffed. Mix roasted flours with crushed gum, melon seeds, cashew nuts, almonds and crushed green cardamom. Add melted jaggery and mix well. Spread mixture on greased plate. Set for 10 minutes, mark cutting areas and cut into desired size pieces. Store in container.

name: Semolina Papad
instructions: Add cumin seeds, salt and oil to water and bring to boil. Gradually add semolina while stirring continuously. Cook on high heat for 5 minutes until boiling, then cook for 2 more minutes while stirring. Grease thalis with ghee. Pour batter into thalis and spread into round shape. Dry in sun for 3 days. Heat oil in kadai and fry papads on high heat until brown on both sides. Sprinkle chaat masala while hot. Serve as crispy snack.

name: sweet mango appe
instructions: Peel mango and extract pulp by grinding in mixer. Mix semolina with mango pulp, sugar, and milk until smooth consistency achieved. Add grated dry coconut and cardamom powder. Let rest 10 minutes to allow semolina to absorb moisture. Adjust consistency with milk if needed. Add Eno fruit salt and stir well. Preheat Appe maker on low flame and grease molds with ghee. Fill molds with batter. Cover and cook 4-5 minutes on low flame. Add ghee around sides and cover. Cook 2-3 minutes more. Flip and cook until golden brown on all sides. Remove and serve.

name: aloo samosa
instructions: Pressure cook potatoes until soft. Peel and mash finely. Make stiff dough with refined flour, ghee and salt, add lukewarm water gradually. Rest dough 20 minutes. Heat oil and add ginger and green chillies, cook briefly. Add green peas and cook 2 minutes covered. Mix with mashed potatoes, salt, green chillies, coriander, garam masala, mango powder, raisins and cashews. Pinch small dough portions and shape into round balls. Roll each to 8-10 inch diameter thin circle. Divide circle into two halves, fold one half into cone shape. Apply water on edges, stuff with potato filling, fold top and seal edges. Deep fry samosas in hot oil on low-medium flame until golden and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper towel. Serve hot with chutney.

name: sweet corn potato curry
instructions: Heat oil in pan. Roast cumin seeds and asafoetida on low flame. Add finely chopped green chilli and ginger paste. Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, and coriander powder. Cook while mashing tomatoes until they break down. Add frozen sweet corn and boiled potatoes. Cover and cook on low flame for 2-3 minutes. Increase flame and add MAGGI masala. Add chopped green coriander and squeeze lemon juice. Mix well and serve hot with roti or rice.

name: aloo tuk
instructions: Cut peeled potatoes into halves then into 4 pieces each. Wipe potato pieces dry with cloth. Heat oil for frying and add potatoes. Cook on medium flame for 5-6 minutes until thoroughly cooked. Remove and let cool for 5-6 minutes. Place each cooled piece on wooden board and press to flatten. Heat oil again until very hot. Fry flattened potatoes until brown, flip and fry until crispy on all sides. Remove from oil. Mix chaat masala, red chilli powder, roasted cumin powder, and salt in a bowl. Sprinkle spice mixture over hot Aloo Tuk and serve immediately.

name: Aloo Papdi Mathri
instructions: Take 1 cup refined flour in a bowl and add 1/2 cup boiled and grated potatoes. Add 1/2 tsp salt and crushed 1/2 tsp carom seeds. Add 2 tbsp oil and mix all ingredients together. Knead to stiff dough, add 1 tsp water and knead stiffer. Cover and let set for 15-20 minutes. Mash dough slightly, divide into lumps, coat with dry flour and roll into round balls. Flatten balls to 2.5-3 inches diameter, expand from edges and prick both sides with fork. Preheat oil for frying. Fry in medium-hot oil on medium flame, flipping to ensure golden brown on both sides. Take out and serve.

name: Suji Shakarpara
instructions: Take fine semolina, add ghee and mix well. Add lukewarm milk in small portions and knead soft dough. Add sesame seeds and mix. Cover and let set for 20 minutes. Knead and smoothen dough, divide into 2 parts. Grease rolling board and pin with oil. Make balls from dough, press with hands and roll out thick. Cut in desired shape. Heat oil in wok to fry shakarpare. Check if oil is medium hot. Put as many shakarpare to fry as they fit, stir and fry until golden brown. Take out and keep on plate. Make sugar syrup by adding sugar and water to pan, stir and cook until sugar dissolves to 2-3 thread consistency. Cook for 3-4 minutes more, then turn off flame and cool. Put shakarpare in hot syrup, mix well to coat all with sugar, spread on plate to cool while separating.

name: Wheat Halwa
instructions: Soak cleaned wheat in water for 12 hours. When soaked, put in mixer jar with some water and grind to fine paste. Strain the paste well. Put leftover wheat back in jar, add water, grind and strain again. Add ghee to pan and add chopped cashews, slightly roast and stir regularly on medium flame until aromatic and puffy, then take out. Heat wok, add ghee and sugar, stir and cook on high flame until sugar completely melts and caramelizes to golden color. Turn off flame, slightly cover wok and add water to sugar, stir well and cook until sugar dissolves. Turn on flame, add wheat milk, reduce flame and stir continuously on medium flame until dense. Add ghee and cook until it absorbs, then add chopped cashews and green cardamom powder. Mix well and take out.

name: Puffy Moong Dal Spinach Cheela
instructions: Take 200 gms spinach, wash, drain water and remove stalk. Finely dice the spinach leaves. Take 1 cup soaked moong dal, put in jar and remove extra water. Add curd, 4 big green chilies cut into pieces and 1/2 x 1 inch ginger piece. Grind to fine paste. Pour dal in bowl, add 2 cup spinach and 1 tsp salt. Mix all ingredients well. Add 3/4 tsp eno fruit salt and mix again. If batter seems dense, add 2 tbsp water. Consistency should be like pakora batter. Heat pan, add little oil and spread evenly, reduce flame and wipe off extra oil. Pour 2 scoops of batter and spread. Keep flame medium and spread oil on sides of cheela. Cook on medium flame for 3-4 minutes, check if roasted from beneath with brown spots. Flip and roast until brown spots appear on other side as well.

name: Aaloo Bhujia Kachori
ingredients: mustard oil - for frying and kneading
instructions: Rinse potatoes thoroughly and dry. Chop potatoes to small chunks without peeling. In big mixing bowl, add wheat flour, semolina, carom seeds, kalonji, salt and 4 tsp oil. Mix well. Knead stiff and tight dough with lukewarm water, cover and rest for 20 minutes. Heat oil in wok or pan. Add 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and asafoetida, let seeds crackle. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, chopped potatoes, salt, red chilly powder and finely chopped green chilly. Stir and saute for 2-3 minutes. Add 2-3 tbsp water, cover and cook for 5 minutes on low flame until chunks are soft and tender. Add more water if required. Take rest of cumin seeds, black pepper, ginger and 1-2 tsp water in mixture jar and grind to paste. Add spices paste, mango powder and green coriander to sabzi and mix well. Cook for 2-3 minutes on high flame and turn off. Grease hands with oil and knead dough until smooth. Pinch 18-20 equal lumps from dough. Take one ball at a time, roll round shape and roll to 3-3.5 inch diameter. Heat oil in wok for deep frying. Gently slide 2-3 pooris in medium hot oil and fry until puffy and golden brown. Drain over kitchen paper towel. Serve steaming hot kachoris with aloo bhujiya sabzi and chutney or pickle.

name: Coconut Milk Dosa
ingredients: rice flour or coconut flour - 1 cup
instructions: Prepare batter from coconut milk and flour with salt. Heat a pan or dosa griddle with oil. Pour batter and spread thinly to make a dosa crepe. Cook until golden brown on one side, flip and cook the other side. Serve hot.

name: Amla Laccha Pickle
instructions: Boil 1-1.5 cups water in vessel and place strainer over boiling water. Place gooseberries on strainer and steam covered for 6-7 minutes. Coarsely grind 2 tsp fennel seeds, 1 tsp fenugreek seeds, 1 tsp black mustard seeds and 1/2 tsp cumin seeds. After 6 minutes, keep gooseberries aside to cool. Grate cooked gooseberries and 2-inch ginger baton. Preheat pan with 3/4 cup mustard oil, switch off flame and decrease temperature slightly. Add 2 pinch asafoetida and 1/2 tsp nigella seeds. Add grated ginger and roast while stirring for 2 minutes. Add coarsely ground spices and roast. Add grated gooseberries along with 1.5 tsp turmeric powder, 2 tsp red chilli powder and 2 tsp salt. Mix properly and stir and cook for 2 minutes. Wait until temperature decreases. Add 1/4 cup sugarcane vinegar and mix. Instant gooseberry pickle is ready or wait for 3 days to ferment, stirring once daily.

name: steamed brown bread
instructions: Mix flour and salt. Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water, add to flour with oil. Knead soft dough, let rise 1 hour. Steam in a vessel for 45 minutes until cooked through. Cool before slicing.

name: flaxseed pancakes
instructions: Soak flaxseeds, grind to paste. Mix with gram flour, yogurt, ginger paste and chopped green chili. Cook spoonfuls on hot oiled griddle until golden on both sides.

name: dry fruit paag with mawa
instructions: Roast muskmelon seeds on low flame 2 minutes. Roast grated coconut 15 minutes until fragrant. Fry edible gum in ghee until expanded. Roast almonds and lotus seeds in ghee until golden. Crush all dry fruits finely. Roast mawa 3 minutes, add powdered sugar, mix well. Add crushed dry fruits, cook 4-5 minutes until thick. Pour onto greased plate, let set 40 minutes, cut into pieces.

name: Instant Rava Dosa
instructions: Mix semolina, rice flour, and maida with water to make thin batter. Add chopped green chilly, ginger paste, green coriander, salt, asafoetida, and ground black pepper. Mix well. Rest batter for 15 minutes. Heat non-stick tawa and apply oil. Pour 2-3 tsp batter and spread thinly and evenly. Roast on high-medium flame until golden brown underneath. Transfer to plate. Repeat for remaining batter. Serve hot with chutney.

name: coconut fried rice
instructions: Heat peanut oil. Add mustard seeds to crackle. Add cumin seeds, chana dal, urad dal, curry leaves, and both chilies. Roast until dal browns. Add grated coconut and roast briefly. Add peanuts and salt, roast. Add cooked rice and stir well. Cook 2-3 minutes. Garnish with green coriander.

name: gulab jamun with mawa
instructions: Knead mawa and paneer together until smooth. Mix in refined flour. Shape into balls, stuffing each with a cashew or almond. Coat lightly with flour. Deep fry in ghee until golden brown. Prepare sugar syrup with green cardamom. Immediately dip fried jamuns into warm sugar syrup. Let soak for 30 minutes before serving.

name: Samvat Rice Khichdi
instructions: Soak samak rice for 30 minutes. Peel and cut potatoes into small pieces. Heat ghee in a vessel, add cumin seeds and roast. Add green chili and black pepper, roast for 1-2 minutes. Add soaked rice and 2 cups water, add salt, cover and cook for 3-4 minutes. In a separate pan, heat more ghee and fry potatoes until done, then fry peanuts until brown. When rice is puffy, add fried potatoes and peanuts with water if needed, mix well. Add green coriander and mix. Serve hot with ghee garnish.

name: Kashmiri Lauki Yakhni
instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add whole garam masala (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper) and cumin seeds, let them bloom. Add ginger powder, fennel powder, asafoetida, turmeric, coriander powder and red chilly powder. Add chopped green chilly. Add diced bottle gourd, salt and cook until tender. Add fresh curd and stir well, simmer until cooked through. Garnish with green coriander.

name: Cheese Corn Momos
instructions: Mix refined flour with salt and water in portions to knead soft dough. Cover and rest for 15-20 minutes. For filling: boil sweet corn kernels for 5 minutes, cool completely, then mix with grated cheese, salt and coarsely ground black pepper. After dough rests, grease hands with oil, smoothen dough and make small balls, coat with flour. Roll into thin 3-4 inch circles. Place 2 tsp filling in center, lift edges and make pleats, seal well. Grease a colander with oil, arrange momos and steam over boiling water for 10 minutes on medium-high heat. Serve hot with chutneys.

name: Bharwan Karela
instructions: Prepare stuffing by mixing fennel powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, asafoetida, chopped raw mango, green coriander and salt. Slit bitter gourds lengthwise and carefully remove seeds. Stuff the karelas with the spice mixture. Heat mustard oil in a pan, add stuffed karelas and fry until skin turns brown and tender, stirring occasionally. Cook until karelas are completely done. Serve hot.

name: Methi ki Launji
instructions: Toast fenugreek seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, set aside. Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add asafoetida, red chili powder and turmeric powder. Add toasted fenugreek seeds and mix well. Add sugar and salt, stir until sugar dissolves. Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until mixture thickens and turns golden. Cool and store in an airtight jar. Serve as a condiment with meals.

name: Palak Dosa
instructions: Soak rice and urad dal with fenugreek seeds for 6 hours. Grind soaked rice and dal into a smooth paste with water. Blanch spinach, cool and puree finely. Mix spinach puree into the ground dal-rice batter. Add salt and let batter ferment for 6-8 hours. Heat a dosa griddle or tawa, lightly oil it. Pour batter in circular motion to form a thin circular dosa. Cook until golden and crispy on one side, then flip and cook the other side. Serve hot with sambar and chutney.

name: Achari Lachha Paratha
instructions: Mix wheat flour with salt. Add pickle masala and oil. Knead into soft dough using water. Rest for 15 minutes. Divide into 8 balls. Roll into thin disc, apply ghee, fold into layers. Cook on hot tawa until golden and crispy on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Jeera and Atta Biscuits
instructions: Cut butter into pieces. Mix maida and wheat flour. Add butter and crumble. Add cumin seeds, sugar, salt, and baking powder. Mix well. Add cold milk in portions to form stiff dough. Roll out to 1/4 cm thickness. Cut shapes using cookie cutter. Place on greased tray. Bake at 180°C for 15-25 minutes until golden brown on both sides. Cool before storing.

name: Party Style Aloo Gobhi
instructions: Cut potatoes into cubes and soak in water. Wash cauliflower florets. Heat oil in pan, add cumin seeds and roast. Add potatoes and cauliflower, stir well. Add salt and turmeric, roast for 2 minutes. Cover and cook on low flame for 5 minutes. In separate pan, heat 2 tbsp oil, add cumin seeds, asafoetida, bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, and black pepper. Toast spices. Prepare paste of tomatoes, green chili, and ginger. Add paste to spiced oil. Add red chilly powder and coriander powder. Roast until oil separates. Stir the vegetable, cook covered for few minutes. Check after 20 minutes. Add masala to vegetables, add water. Add ginger juliennes, garam masala, and fresh coriander. Cook 4-5 minutes more. Serve hot.

name: chorafali
instructions: Make a dough with refined flour, ghee, salt, and carom seeds. Knead well and let it rest. Roll out thin sheets, cut into strips, and fry in hot oil until golden and crispy.

name: gobi paneer paratha
instructions: Prepare dough from wheat flour and water. For filling, sauté cauliflower with paneer, coriander, chilly, ginger paste, powders and salt. Roll dough, place filling in center, seal, and roll flat. Cook on griddle with oil until golden brown on both sides.

name: achari karela
instructions: Wash and cut bitter gourds into 1-1.5 inch pieces. Salt and rest for 15-20 minutes. Wash and steam for 5 minutes. In a pan, heat mustard oil and add all seeds and spices. Add steamed karela pieces, salt, chilli powder, mango powder and roast well. Cover and cook on low flame for 6-8 minutes, stirring regularly.

name: methi nimki
instructions: Clean and chop fenugreek leaves finely. Mix refined flour, salt, carom seeds, and fenugreek leaves. Add ghee and mix well. Knead a stiff dough with water and rest 20 minutes. Roll out thin sheets, fold and overlap edges, cut into desired shapes. Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides.

name: arbi paratha
instructions: Peel and boil taro roots until soft. Mash and mix with chopped green chilly, salt, turmeric and asafoetida. Prepare dough from wheat flour and water. Divide dough, flatten, fill with taro mixture, seal and roll flat. Cook on griddle with oil until golden brown on both sides.

name: bajra methi dhebra
instructions: Mix millet flour, wheat flour, curd, fenugreek leaves, sesame seeds, cumin seeds, green chilli, red chilli powder, turmeric powder and salt. Add lukewarm water to knead soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes. Apply ghee on palms and flatten dough portions. Roll out to 4-5 inch discs. Cook on heated griddle with ghee, flipping and cooking until brown spots appear on both sides.

name: aloo palak sabzi
instructions: Heat mustard oil. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Add diced potatoes and stir. Add chopped spinach and salt. Cook on high heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and spinach wilts. Serve hot.

name: nariyal migi mewa paag
instructions: Dry roast muskmelon seeds while stirring. Cover if seeds pop. Cool. Roast grated dry coconut for a minute. Cool. Heat sugar with water until it dissolves. Cook to long thread consistency. Grease tray with ghee. Lower flame and add coconut, muskmelon seeds, cardamom powder and nutmeg powder. Stir and roast for a minute. Continuously stir while cooling. Pour on greased tray and spread evenly. Set for 5 minutes. Mark cutting areas. Let set for half an hour. Cut into pieces.

name: makki ki roti sarson ka saag
instructions: For roti: Mix maize flour with salt and water to make a stiff dough. Rest for 10 minutes. Knead and roll into thick rounds. Cook on hot griddle until golden. For saag: Heat mustard oil, add cumin seeds. Add ginger, green chilly, tomato and all greens. Cook until soft. Add spices and cook until well combined. Serve roti with hot saag.

name: patta gobhi matar ki sabji
instructions: Heat mustard oil. Add cumin seeds and saute on low flame. Add grated ginger and green chilly. Add peas and saute for 2 minutes. Add turmeric powder and coriander powder. Add chopped cabbage with salt. Roast while stirring. Cook covered for 3 minutes on low flame. Add MAGGI masala and mix well. Cook for a minute. Serve hot.

name: mushroom manchurian
instructions: Clean and quarter mushrooms. Toss with cornstarch and salt. Deep fry until golden and crispy. For sauce: heat oil, add ginger-garlic paste and green chilly. Add tomato sauce, soy sauce and vinegar. Simmer. Add fried mushrooms and toss well. Serve hot as appetizer or with fried rice.

name: wheat flour mathri
instructions: Sieve wheat flour. Mix flour, semolina, carom seeds, cumin seeds, black pepper, salt and oil. Add water in small portions to knead stiff dough. Cover for 15-20 minutes. Knead again until smooth. Pinch small lumps and flatten slightly. Roll into 2-inch thick rounds. Prick with fork. Heat oil in wok. Deep fry in medium-hot oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Cool completely before storing in airtight container.

name: Samo Rice Poori
instructions: Rinse and soak samo rice for 2 hours. Drain and grind finely. Roast the rice paste in a heated pan for a minute until dense and cooked through. Cool slightly. Add oil, sendha salt, and black pepper, knead until smooth. Heat oil in a wok for frying. Divide dough into lumps. Using a greased polythene sheet, roll out thick pooris. Slide gently into hot oil and press with a ladle to puff up. Fry until golden brown. Drain on absorbent paper. Serve hot with aloo sabzi or other accompaniments.

name: Sweet Corn Masala Idli
instructions: Mix corn, rice flour, lentil flour with water and salt to form batter. Add spices including cumin seeds, turmeric, and black pepper. Pour into greased idli molds and steam until cooked through. Serve hot with sambar or chutney.

name: Palak Namak Pare
instructions: Blanch and puree spinach. Mix with flour, salt, pepper, and carom seeds. Knead into stiff dough with oil and spinach puree. Roll out thin and cut into diamond or rectangular shapes. Heat oil and deep fry crackers until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Store in airtight container.

name: Cold Coffee with Ice Cream
instructions: Prepare strong coffee and let it cool. In a tall glass, add ice cream. Pour cold coffee over the ice cream. Add milk and sugar. Stir well. Top with whipped cream if desired. Add ice cubes. Serve immediately.

name: Carrot and Mooli Pickle
instructions: Peel and chop radish and carrot into thin strips. Peel and chop ginger and green chilies. Mix all vegetables in a bowl. Add salt and let sit for 30 minutes. Add mustard oil, red chili powder, turmeric powder, ground black pepper, carom seeds, mustard powder, asafoetida, and vinegar. Mix thoroughly. Transfer to a clean glass jar. Let sit for 1-2 hours before serving. Store in airtight container for up to 2 months.

name: Spicy Matar Namkeen
instructions: Wash and soak dry peas with salt for 6-7 hours. Boil soaked peas in pressure cooker with water until first whistle, then turn off heat and release pressure. Drain thoroughly. Spread on cloth under a fan to dry for about 1 hour. Heat oil to high temperature. Fry peas in batches using a strainer until golden brown and crunchy. Drain on paper towels. Grind together mango powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, salt, black salt, and black pepper. Mix this masala powder with the fried peas. Cool completely. Store in airtight container for 1.5-2 months.

name: Dahi Paneer Bread Roll
instructions: Make hung curd: take 1 cup fresh curd, hang in cotton cloth for 2 hours. Crumble paneer and mix with hung curd. Finely chop capsicum, carrot, baby corn, green coriander, green chilies, and ginger. Add to the curd-paneer mixture along with black pepper and salt. Mix well. Trim dark edges from bread slices. Heat oil in wok. Dip a bread slice in water, press gently to remove excess water. Place some filling on the bread and fold into a roll. Fry rolls in hot oil, flipping occasionally, until golden brown on all sides. Drain on tissue paper. Serve with green coriander dip or tomato sauce.

name: Aloo Bhakarwadi
instructions: Pressure cook potatoes and peel. Make flour batter with 2 tbsp flour and water. Knead flour with salt, carom seeds and oil into stiff dough, rest 15-20 minutes. Mash boiled potatoes and mix with coriander powder, red chilly powder, mango powder, salt, ginger paste, green chilly paste and green coriander. Divide dough in 2 parts, roll out thin sheet, spread filling, fold into roll and seal edges. Cut into chunks and dip in flour batter. Deep fry on medium flame until golden brown. Drain on absorbent paper.

name: Fried Modak
instructions: Prepare filling by mixing jaggery with grated coconut, almonds, cashews and green cardamom. Make dough with wheat flour, refined flour, ghee and salt. Knead and shape dough portions into balls. Flatten each ball, add filling in center, seal and shape into traditional modak form. Deep fry in ghee until crispy and golden brown. Remove and drain on paper towels.

name: Arbi Jhol
instructions: Peel and cut arbi into cubes. Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook. Add turmeric, red chilly and coriander powders. Add arbi cubes and lotus seeds. Cook on high heat until tender. Adjust salt and consistency. Simmer until arbi is fully cooked and soft.

name: Kokum Kadhi
instructions: Soak kokum fruits in warm water for few minutes to release flavor and color. Prepare coconut milk. Mix kokum liquid with coconut milk, add turmeric powder, roasted cumin seeds and salt. Add ginger for extra flavor. Strain if needed and serve chilled.

name: Kadu Puri
instructions: Peel pumpkin, remove seeds and grate finely. Mix wheat flour with salt, red chilly powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, green chilli, green coriander, semolina and oil. Add grated pumpkin and knead stiff dough with water. Rest for 20-25 minutes. Divide dough into lumps and roll into 3-4 inch discs. Heat oil in wok and fry poori on medium flame until it floats. Press to puff, flip and fry until golden brown on both sides. Drain on absorbent paper.

name: besan churma ladoo
instructions: Dry roast chickpea flour in ghee on low-medium heat. Add sugar and mix well. Add roasted dry fruits. Cool and shape into ladoos. Serve fresh or store in airtight container.

name: two layer chocolate burfi
instructions: Make mawa fudge base layer with sugar and ghee. Cool. Prepare chocolate layer with chocolate powder and mawa. Layer on top of base layer. Cool and cut into pieces. Serve chilled.

name: besan chutney
instructions: Heat oil in pan. Add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add minced ginger and green chilies. Add besan flour and roast until golden. Add water to make smooth paste. Cook until thick. Serve with snacks.

name: lauki gatta curry
instructions: Make gatta dough with besan, curd, ginger, chilies and spices. Roll into thin logs and boil in salted water. Cut into pieces. Prepare tomato-based curry with spices. Add boiled gatta pieces and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes. Serve hot with rice or bread.

name: bedmi paratha
instructions: Grind soaked urad dal coarsely with ginger and green chilies. Mix with wheat flour, spices and oil. Knead soft dough and rest 15-20 minutes. Roll small portions and shape into half-moon folded paranthas. Roast on greased tawa with oil until golden brown spots appear. Serve hot with curd and pickles.

name: pickle masala
ingredients: red chilli flakes 4 tbsp (20 gms) coarsely ground
instructions: Dry roast fennel seeds, fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds and black pepper together for 3-4 minutes on medium flame while stirring continuously. Remove to a plate to cool. Add to grinder and grind coarsely. Transfer to bowl and mix with salt, turmeric powder, red chilli flakes, degi mirch and asafoetida. Mix well. Store in airtight container for 6-7 months. Use 4 tablespoons of this masala with oil and vinegar to make pickles.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
instructions: Prepare cooked rice. Heat oil in wok, add aromatics and vegetables. Add rice and stir-fry on high heat until combined. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Aloo Baingan Mangodi
instructions: Chop vegetables. Heat oil, add aromatics and tomato base. Add potatoes and brinjal, cook until soft. Add mangodi and spices. Simmer until flavors combine.

name: Potato Sev Namkeen
instructions: Boil water with salt and oil. Add semolina, puff for 5 minutes. Peel and grate boiled potatoes. Mix semolina dough with grated potatoes. Fill sev press with fine die. Fry in hot oil until golden brown. Cool and store in airtight container.

name: Rice Papadi
instructions: Mix rice flour with salt, carom seeds, black pepper and 1 tsp oil. Add water and knead soft dough. Microwave dough on high for 1 minute. Knead until smooth. Roll thin papadis. Fry in hot oil on low flame until golden and crispy. Drain and cool.

name: Corn Flakes Chivda
instructions: Heat oil, fry peanuts until brown, set aside. Roast cashews on low flame, set aside. Reduce flame, add curry leaves to 2 tsp oil and roast crisp. Mix spices and salt. Add corn flakes and mix. Add raisins, cashews and peanuts. Heat on low, stir once. Add boondi. Cool completely before storing in airtight container.

name: Sweet Potato Curry
instructions: Cut sweet potatoes into chunks. Heat oil, add onion and aromatics. Add tomato and cook base. Add sweet potatoes and spices. Cook until tender. Garnish with cilantro.

name: Mishti Doi
instructions: Boil milk in a vessel and simmer until reduced to half, stirring occasionally. Add 50g sugar and crushed cardamom seeds to the reduced milk. Caramelize remaining 50g sugar in a separate vessel and add to milk. Mix well and pour into kulhads or bowls. Cool slightly, then add 2 tsp curd to each container and mix. Keep at a warm place for 10-12 hours until set.

name: Roasted Salted Almonds
instructions: Add water to salt and mix until it dissolves. Pour salty water over almonds and coat well. Heat 2 cups salt in a heavy-based wok for 5 minutes, stirring every minute. Once hot, add almonds and roast for 3 minutes while stirring regularly on medium flame. Once almonds puff up and turn roasted, turn off flame and sieve to remove salt. Drain excess oil and let cool. Mix roasted almonds with additional salt and pepper to taste.

name: Steamed Atta Modak
instructions: Mix wheat flour, grated coconut, crumbled jaggery, ghee, finely chopped nuts, cardamom seeds, and salt. Form mixture into modak shape using hands or modak mold. Steam for 15-20 minutes until cooked through. Serve warm as a sweet delicacy.

name: Aloo Lachha Namkeen
instructions: Peel potatoes and grate using coarse grater. Rinse grated potatoes thoroughly in water twice to remove starch. Drain well and wipe with cloth to remove excess water. Heat oil in a wok to medium-high temperature. Fry potato lachhas in batches, stirring until crispy and lightly golden, about 5-6 minutes. Drain on sieve. Fry peanuts separately until lightly colored. Mix fried lachhas and peanuts together. Season with rock salt and black pepper powder. Cool completely before storing in airtight container.

name: Methi Ke Gatte
instructions: Mix besan with finely chopped fenugreek leaves, onion, green chili, ginger, and garlic. Add garam masala, turmeric, salt and oil. Knead into a stiff dough. Boil water in a pot. Roll dough into cylindrical shapes (gattas) and drop into boiling water. Boil until gattas float and cook for 2-3 minutes more. Drain well. Prepare gravy with yogurt and spices. Add cooked gattas to the gravy and simmer until flavors combine.

name: Karonda Launji
instructions: Clean and wash karonda berries. In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat ghee and add cleaned berries. Cook on medium flame until soft, stirring occasionally. Add sugar gradually and continue cooking. Stir frequently to prevent sticking and burning. Cook until mixture becomes thick and glossy, about 30-40 minutes. Add cardamom and nutmeg powder. Mix well and let cool. Transfer to clean jars for storage.

name: Lapsi
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add broken wheat and roast for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until lightly golden and fragrant. Add crushed cardamom and chopped nuts, roast for 1 more minute. Add water carefully and bring to boil. Reduce flame to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until wheat is completely tender and water is absorbed, about 15-20 minutes. Add crumbled jaggery and salt. Mix well and cook for 2-3 more minutes until jaggery dissolves completely.

name: Stuffed Mooli Paranthas
instructions: Peel and grate radishes, squeeze out juice. Mix wheat flour with salt and oil, add water gradually to form soft dough, rest 20-25 minutes. Prepare stuffing by combining grated radish with salt, ginger, green chilly, coriander powder, mango powder, red chilly powder, and green coriander. Roll dough portions into thin chapatis, place 2-3 tsp stuffing between two chapatis, seal edges, and roll again. Cook on hot tawa with oil until brown spots appear on both sides. Serve hot with chutneys or curries.

name: Turmeric Latte
instructions: Heat milk in a pan. Add turmeric and cardamom powder, cinnamon powder, and nutmeg. Simmer gently. Pour into cups and sweeten with honey to taste. Serve warm as a nutritious winter drink.

name: Methi Coconut Laddus
instructions: Soak fenugreek seeds in milk for 3-4 hours. Roast in ghee on medium flame until color changes (7-8 minutes). In separate batches, roast wheat flour in ghee until golden brown (12 minutes), roast edible gum in ghee, lightly roast almonds in ghee (2 minutes), and roast dry coconut in ghee (2 minutes). Melt jaggery in ghee on low flame, stirring constantly. Grind almonds, combine with flour, and mix cardamom, pepper, peepar, and ginger powder. Mix all ingredients including roasted fenugreek while slightly warm. Bind together and shape into laddus.

name: Vegetable Rava Handvo
instructions: Mix semolina, chickpea flour, and whisked curd in a bowl. Add water to form dense dough. Mix in turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, ginger paste, green chili, and salt. Add grated carrot, chopped cauliflower, chopped capsicum, and roasted peanuts. Let batter rest 10 minutes. Heat pan with 2-3 tbsp oil. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and sesame seeds. Add eno fruit salt to batter, mix well. Pour into pan, spread evenly, cover and cook on low-medium flame for 10 minutes. Flip and repeat on other side with remaining oil and seeds for 12 minutes until handvo is roasted well.

name: Eggless Mayonnaise
ingredients: cream 1 cup (200g) or full cream milk 1/4 cup (60ml)
instructions: Take cream or milk base in a bowl. Add oil gradually while mixing. Add vinegar, ground black pepper, mustard powder, salt, and powdered sugar. Mix well until mayonnaise reaches desired consistency. Store in an airtight container. Use as a dip for salads, breads, sandwiches, or burgers.

name: Dahi Sandwich
instructions: Mix hung curd with finely chopped cabbage, finely chopped capsicum, grated carrot, finely chopped green coriander, ground black pepper, grated ginger, and salt. Spread ghee on bread slices. Apply curd-vegetable mixture generously on one slice. Top with another slice. Cut into halves or triangles. Serve immediately as a quick sandwich for kids' tiffin or breakfast.

name: Aloo Patta Gobhi Matar Sabzi
instructions: Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds. Add ginger paste and green chilli paste. Add tomato paste and cook until oil separates. Cut cabbage finely and potatoes into small cubes. Add vegetables to the pan. Season with red chilli powder, asafoetida, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix well and cook on medium heat until vegetables are tender. Garnish with finely chopped green coriander. Serve hot as a side dish with rice or bread.

name: Govind Gatte ki Sabzi
instructions: 1. Prepare dough with chickpea flour, salt, and water. 2. Stuff mawa into dough portions and boil until they float. 3. Prepare tempering: heat oil, add cumin seeds, onions, ginger-garlic paste. 4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. 5. Add boiled gatta dumplings to the curry. 6. Season with turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala. 7. Simmer until gatta absorbs flavors. 8. Serve hot as a Rajasthani main course.

name: Banana Pancakes
instructions: 1. Mash 2 ripe bananas until smooth. 2. Mix wheat flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. 3. Combine mashed banana with milk and sugar. 4. Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients; mix until just combined into a thick batter. 5. Heat butter on a griddle or pan over medium heat. 6. Pour 0.25 cup batter onto hot surface. 7. Cook until bubbles form on surface, then flip. 8. Cook until golden brown on both sides. 9. Serve warm with desired toppings.

name: Vattayappam
instructions: 1. Soak rice for 1 hour, grind to smooth paste. 2. Grate jaggery and mix with rice paste. 3. Add grated coconut, cardamom powder, salt, and melted ghee to rice-jaggery mixture. 4. Mix well until combined. 5. Pour batter into banana leaf cups. 6. Steam in a steamer for 20-25 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. 7. Cool slightly before removing from banana leaves. 8. Serve warm.

name: Amla Pickle Andhra Style
instructions: 1. Wash and prick fresh amla fruits with a knife. 2. Mix amla with salt in a bowl; let sit overnight. 3. Drain excess water next day. 4. Heat oil and add mustard seeds, let them crackle. 5. Add fenugreek seeds, dry red chilies, and garlic cloves. 6. Add turmeric powder and roast spices briefly. 7. Add salted amla to the oil and spices mixture. 8. Mix well ensuring all amla is coated. 9. Transfer to sterilized glass jars. 10. Keep in sunlight for 3-4 days, stirring daily, until fully fermented. 11. Store in cool, dark place.

name: Fried Bati
instructions: 1. Mix all-purpose flour, salt, and turmeric powder in a bowl. 2. Add ghee and mix with fingertips until mixture resembles breadcrumbs. 3. Add water gradually while mixing to form a firm dough. 4. Knead well for 5 minutes. 5. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes. 6. Divide into 6 equal portions and roll into balls. 7. Flatten slightly into disc shape. 8. Heat oil to 175°C. 9. Carefully place bati in hot oil one at a time. 10. Fry on medium heat for 4-5 minutes until golden and puffed, turning occasionally. 11. Drain on paper towels. 12. Serve warm.

name: Roomali Roti
instructions: Mix wheat flour, refined flour, salt, baking powder and oil. Add water in small portions and knead soft dough. Knead for 6-7 minutes, cover and rest for 20 minutes. Grease hands, squash dough for 2-3 minutes. Roll dough into balls, coat with dry flour and roll thin. Flip to remove excess flour. Place on upside-down heated wok, flip when bubbles form, roast until brown spots appear. Fold like a handkerchief.

name: Stuffed Potato Curry
instructions: Prepare stuffing with spices and ingredients. Hollow out potatoes and fill with prepared mixture. Cook curry with tomatoes, onions, ginger and spices. Add stuffed potatoes and simmer until cooked through and tender.

name: Mawa ki Gujiya
instructions: Prepare dough with flour, ghee and eggs. Make filling with khoya, sugar and dry fruits. Roll dough thin, place filling on half, fold in half, seal edges. Microwave in ghee or fry until golden. Serve warm.

name: Spicy Nutri Kulcha
instructions: Soak soya nuggets in tea water for 10 minutes and boil until soft, drain. Heat oil, add cumin seeds. Make tomato-chilli-ginger paste and add to oil. Roast with spices until oil separates. Add soaked soya nuggets with salt and tea water, cook until thick. Add butter and coriander. Serve with grilled kulcha on the side.

name: Khoya Matar Curry
instructions: Heat oil, add onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-chilli paste, tomatoes and fry. Add spices and cook until oil separates. Crumble khoya into the curry, add peas and salt. Cook on low heat until peas are tender and curry is well-mixed.

name: Gur Ka Paratha
instructions: Knead wheat flour with salt and ghee into smooth dough. Roll out thin. Crumble jaggery on one half, fold into half, seal edges. Roll gently into paratha shape. Cook on hot griddle (tawa) with ghee until golden brown on both sides. Serve warm.

name: Soya Chunks Stuffed Paratha
instructions: Soak soya chunks and cook. Mix cooked soya with spiced onion masala. Roll paratha dough, stuff with soya mixture, seal edges, and fry on griddle until golden brown. Serve hot.

name: Soft Chewy Caramel Candies
instructions: Combine condensed milk, butter and sugar in a heavy-bottomed pan. Heat and stir continuously until mixture reaches soft-ball stage (240°F). Pour into buttered pan. Cool completely. Cut into squares. Wrap in butter paper.

name: Pav (Indian Dinner Rolls)
instructions: Mix flour with yeast, sugar and salt. Make well, add warm milk and butter. Knead soft dough. Let rise 1-2 hours. Divide into portions, shape into round buns. Place on tray. Let rise again 30 minutes. Brush with egg wash. Bake at 375°F for 15-20 minutes until golden.

name: Banana Chips
instructions: Peel raw bananas and slice using chips cutter into long strips. Heat oil to medium-high temperature. Test with small dough ball. Fry banana strips one by one until golden brown. Drain on plate. Sprinkle chaat masala and serve.

name: Plum Chutney
instructions: Soak dried plums. Heat oil and add cumin seeds. Add finely chopped onion and garlic, sauté until golden. Add ginger, green chili and cook. Add soaked plums and cook until soft. Add salt and sugar to taste. Simmer until thick. Cool and store.

name: Moth Dal
ingredients: soaked whole moth beans 1/2 cup (100 grams)
instructions: Soak whole moth beans for 7-8 hours or overnight. Add dal to cooker with water, salt, turmeric and baking soda. Boil until one whistle. Heat ghee, add cumin seeds. Add asafoetida, turmeric, coriander, green chili and ginger paste. Roast spices. Add tomato puree and red chili powder. Roast until ghee separates. Add boiled dal and garam masala. Cook 2 minutes. Garnish with green coriander and ghee. Serve with roti or rice.

name: Mung Dal Paratha
instructions: Make soft dough with flour, salt and oil. Soak and grind moong dal. Saute dal with cumin, asafoetida, green chilli, ginger, spices and coriander leaves. Cool filling. Knead dough, roll balls, hollow with fingers, fill stuffing, seal and flatten. Cook on griddle with ghee until golden spots appear on both sides.

name: Besan Dhokla
instructions: Mix besan with yogurt, oil, ginger, green chilli, asafoetida, cumin seeds and spices. Add baking soda and salt just before steaming. Pour into greased pan. Steam for 15-20 minutes until set. Cut into pieces.

name: Rice Flour Poori
instructions: Mix rice flour with spices, salt and oil. Add warm water gradually to form soft dough. Rest for 20-25 minutes. Heat oil for deep frying. Roll small dough balls into thin rounds. Deep fry until puffy and golden brown on both sides. Drain on paper towels.

name: Soup Sticks
instructions: Mix flour, salt and oil. Add water gradually to form soft dough. Knead well. Divide into long thin strips. Place on baking sheet. Bake at 190C for 20-25 minutes until golden and crispy, or deep fry until golden brown.

name: Instant Bhature
instructions: Mix maida with semolina. Mash boiled potatoes and add to flour. Add yogurt and oil, mix well. Just before frying, add baking soda and salt. Knead lightly. Divide into balls. Heat oil for deep frying. Flatten each ball gently and deep fry until puffy and golden brown on both sides.

name: Rava Barfi
instructions: Heat a pan, pour ghee and add semolina. Stir and roast semolina until golden brown. Make sugar syrup by dissolving sugar in water. Grease a plate with ghee. Add roasted semolina to sugar syrup, reduce flame and cook until setting consistency. Add chopped cashews and cardamom powder, stir well. Check consistency by pouring mix into bowl to form a ball. Turn off flame and cool. Grease spoon and spread mix evenly on plate. Add almond shavings on top and press with spoon. After 5 minutes, mark desired shapes. Once set, pick out barfi pieces. Store in airtight container.

name: Punjabi Masala Mathri
instructions: Coarsely grind coriander seeds, fennel seeds, black pepper and clove. In a mixing bowl, combine refined flour, wheat flour, gram flour, semolina, salt, cumin seeds, carom seeds, asafoetida, dry fenugreek leaves and ground spices. Mix well. Add oil and mix. Gradually add water and knead into a stiff, tight dough. Cover and rest for 15-20 minutes. Knead again until smooth. Make small lumps from dough. Roll each lump into a thin circle, flatten on palms. Heat oil in a wok and fry mathris on medium-low flame until golden brown and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper. Cool completely and store in airtight container for up to 2 months. Serve with pickle.

name: Lotus Root Chips
instructions: Peel lotus root and slice thinly into chips. Soak in water for 15 minutes to prevent discoloration. Pat dry with kitchen towels. Heat oil in a deep pan or wok. Once hot, carefully slide lotus root chips into oil and fry on medium heat until golden brown and crispy. Drain fried chips on kitchen paper towels to remove excess oil. While still warm, sprinkle salt, chili powder and cumin powder. Mix well. Cool completely and store in airtight container for 2-3 weeks.

name: Rabri Kheer
instructions: Grind soaked rice into a coarse paste. Finely chop cashews and almonds. Boil milk in a vessel. As milk simmers, add rice paste and mix well. Stir every 1-2 minutes. Once rice is cooked through, add cashews, almonds and raisins. Stir to mix well. When kheer becomes thick, turn off flame. Mix in sugar and crushed green cardamom. Cover vessel for 2-3 minutes for sugar to dissolve completely. Add rabri and mix well. Transfer to serving bowl. Garnish with almonds and cashews. Serve chilled or warm.

name: Whole Wheat Brown Bread
instructions: Mix whole wheat flour with salt. In a small bowl, dissolve sugar and yeast in lukewarm water. Let sit for 5 minutes until frothy. Make a well in flour and add yeast mixture. Add oil. Mix and knead into a smooth dough, adding water as needed. Cover and let rise for 1-2 hours until doubled in size. Punch down dough and transfer to greased baking pan or loaf tin. Cover and let rise for 30 minutes. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped. Cool on wire rack before slicing.

name: bhakarwadi sandwich
instructions: Make stiff dough with refined flour, salt, carom seeds, oil and water. Rest 15-20 minutes. Grind sesame seeds, poppy seeds, coriander powder, fennel powder, cumin seeds, red chilli powder, garam masala, ginger powder, turmeric powder, asafoetida, and salt together. Divide dough into 4 parts, flatten each into thin rounds. Spread tamarind chutney and ground spice mixture on one round, cover with another round. Flatten together and cut into small squares. Poke with fork and separate pieces. Let rest 1 hour. Fry in preheated oil on medium-low flame until golden brown (5-6 minutes). Store in airtight container.

name: arhar ki khatti daal
instructions: Wash and soak arhar dal. Cook with water until soft. Season with salt and spices to taste to create tangy dal curry.

name: guava halwa
instructions: Boil milk in a pan. Pressure cook guavas with beetroot until soft. Reduce milk to thick consistency. Grind cooled guavas into paste and strain to remove seeds. Heat ghee and roast chopped almonds and cashews. Add guava paste and roast until thick. Mix in cooked milk and continue roasting. Add sugar and cook until dissolved. Garnish with dry fruits and serve.

name: caramel custard
instructions: Heat sugar in pan on high flame, stirring continuously until light brown caramel forms. Pour caramel into bowl and set aside. Mix milk and custard powder until smooth. Add whisked curd, condensed milk and vanilla essence to milk mixture. Pour mixture over caramel in bowl. Place bowl in water bath and steam cook for 25 minutes on low-medium flame. Remove from water bath, separate custard from sides with knife. Invert onto plate. Refrigerate for 1 hour and serve chilled.

name: stuffed red chilli pickle
instructions: Wash red chillies and sun dry for 2-3 hours. Heat pan and roast fennel seeds, fenugreek seeds, cumin seeds, carom seeds, black pepper for up to 2 minutes. Set aside to cool. Heat mustard oil until it smokes, then cool. Grind roasted spices coarsely with plain salt. Add ground black mustard seeds separately. Mix roasted spices with black salt, turmeric powder, asafoetida and lemon juice. Add 2 tbsp of cooled oil. Remove chilli stalk, slit vertically from center, remove seeds and pulp. Mix removed seeds with spice mixture. Fill each chilli with spice mixture. Dip each stuffed chilli in oil. Fill sterilized container with stuffed chillies, add leftover spices, pour remaining oil, close lid. Keep in sunlight or cupboard for 3 or more days to soften.

name: khajur burfi
instructions: Chop cashews, almonds, walnuts and dates. Slice pistachios thinly. Grind green cardamom seeds and nutmeg to fine powder. Dry roast cashews, almonds and walnuts for 2-3 minutes on medium flame. Transfer to bowl. Add ghee to hot wok, fry poppy seeds for 2 minutes on low flame while stirring. Add nutmeg-cardamom powder, dates, roasted dry fruits, coconut and chironji. Mix on low flame. Turn off flame and transfer to plate to cool. Pinch mixture with greased hand and roll into long logs. Coat barfi with pistachios. Wrap logs in aluminum foil and refrigerate for 2 hours. Unwrap and cut into 1/2 cm thick chunks. Serve cold.

name: Kaddu Kofta Curry
instructions: Cut pumpkin into pieces, boil until soft. Mash and mix with chickpea flour, ginger, green chili, onion, salt and make patties. Deep fry until golden. In separate pan, make masala base with onion, garlic, tomato and spices. Add fried koftas and simmer until gravy thickens.

name: Microwave Idli
instructions: Mix rice flour and urad dal flour in 3:1 ratio. Add salt and water to make batter. Ferment if possible or use immediately. Fill greased microwave idli molds and microwave on high for 3-4 minutes.

name: Instant Sweet Chutney
instructions: Roast dry mango powder lightly. Mix with finely chopped ginger, green chili, sugar and salt. Add little water to adjust consistency. Mix well and serve with chaat or snacks.

name: Sweet Corn Paneer Balls
instructions: Mix boiled corn with grated paneer, green chili, salt and cornflour. Make balls and coat with breadcrumbs. Deep fry until golden brown. Serve hot.

name: Dahi Ka Paratha
instructions: Knead wheat flour with ghee and salt, let rest 20 mins. Make filling with hung curd, grated paneer, ground besan sev, salt, green chili, spices and coriander. Layer dough sheets with ghee, add stuffing, seal and roll. Roast on greased skillet on medium flame with ghee until golden.

name: Eggless Mango Cake
instructions: Mix flour, sugar and baking powder. Add mango puree and oil. Mix well. Pour into greased pan. Bake at 350F until golden brown.

name: Sweet Corn Vada
instructions: Grind sweetcorn coarsely. Mix with chickpea flour, vegetables, spices and salt. Heat oil and fry shaped vadas until golden brown on both sides. Takes about 5 minutes per vada.

name: Aloo Bread Pakora
instructions: Boil and mash potatoes with spices. Stuff potato mixture between bread slices. Cut into shapes. Make chickpea flour batter. Dip bread pieces in batter. Deep fry until golden brown on both sides.

name: Methi Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch and chop methi and palak. Cube paneer. Sauté onion, garlic and ginger. Add tomato and spices. Add methi and palak. Cook until leaves are tender. Add paneer cubes and cook for 2-3 minutes.

name: Nimbu Pudina Sharbat
instructions: Crush mint leaves. Mix with lemon juice, water, salt and cumin powder. Add sugar or honey to taste. Serve chilled.

name: beetroot fry sabzi
instructions: Peel and cut beetroot into small pieces. Heat oil, add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add asafoetida, then ginger-garlic, chillies and turmeric. Add beetroot pieces and salt. Cover and cook on low flame for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally until beetroot is cooked through. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: tiranga sandwich dhokla
instructions: Mix besan, semolina, yogurt, ginger-green chilli paste, turmeric, and salt. Divide batter into three parts and color with food coloring. Add baking soda just before steaming. Pour layers into a greased dhokla pan, alternating colors. Steam for 12-15 minutes. Cool and cut into pieces. Prepare tadka by heating oil, adding mustard seeds and curry leaves, then pour over dhokla.

name: mawa barfi
instructions: Microwave mawa in a microwave-safe bowl for 3 minutes, stirring after each minute. Add powdered sugar and green cardamom powder to warm mawa and mix thoroughly. Transfer to a greased plate and spread evenly. Sprinkle pistachios on top and press gently with spoon. Refrigerate for 1 hour to set. Heat plate from bottom to separate barfi easily. Cut into desired size pieces and serve.

name: murmure namkeen
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Splutter mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and cumin seeds. Add dried chillies and asafoetida. Add puffed rice, salt, and turmeric powder. Toss well until evenly coated. Add coriander leaves and serve immediately while warm.

name: tomato chutney
instructions: Wash and chop tomatoes and ginger. Heat oil and splutter fenugreek seeds and cumin seeds. Add mustard seeds and stir. Add asafoetida and coriander powder and roast. Add chopped tomatoes, ginger, salt, whole red chillies and black peppercorns. Mix well and cover. Cook for 5 minutes, then remove cover and stir continuously for 5 more minutes. Cook on high flame for 1-2 minutes more. Cool completely, then blend into a fine paste. Transfer to bowl. Heat some oil, splutter mustard seeds, add red chilly powder, and pour this tempering over the chutney.

name: dal ke papad
instructions: Mix urad dal flour, moong dal flour, oil, papad khar, black pepper, salt, and asafoetida. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough. Divide into portions and roll thin between plastic sheets. Sun-dry for 1-2 days until completely crispy. Once dried, papads are ready to store. Fry briefly in hot oil before serving or roast over flame until they puff up.

name: Masala Boondi
instructions: 1. Mix chickpea flour with oil, curry leaves, salt and red chilli powder. 2. Prepare a thick batter consistency. 3. Heat oil in a deep pan or wok. 4. Drop the batter through a boondi maker into the hot oil. 5. Fry until golden and crispy. 6. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. 7. Serve as a snack or with raita.

name: Cornmeal Muffins
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). 2. Grease muffin tins. 3. Mix cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in a dry bowl. 4. In another bowl, combine buttermilk, beaten eggs, melted butter and sugar. 5. Fold the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined. 6. Pour batter into muffin tins, filling each cup about 2/3 full. 7. Bake for 15-20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. 8. Cool in pan for 5 minutes before turning out.

name: Besan Stuffed Paratha
instructions: 1. Knead whole wheat flour with salt and water to make dough. 2. Prepare filling with roasted chickpea flour mixed with spices, ginger and green chilli. 3. Roll dough into thin circles. 4. Place filling in center and seal edges. 5. Roll gently to even thickness. 6. Heat griddle and cook paratha on both sides with oil until golden brown and crispy. 7. Flip and cook other side. 8. Serve hot with pickle or yogurt.

name: Ragda Patties
instructions: 1. Soak white peas overnight. 2. Boil peas with water, salt, turmeric and baking soda until tender (about 1-2 whistles). 3. Cook for additional 5 minutes on low heat. 4. Peel and grate boiled potatoes. 5. Mix mashed peas with ginger paste, green chilli, coriander and salt. 6. Mix in grated potatoes and form round patties. 7. Heat oil on medium-high. 8. Fry patties until golden brown on both sides. 9. Drain excess oil. 10. Arrange patties on plate, top with ragda curry. 11. Sprinkle tamarind dip, coriander dip, chaat masala, red chilli powder, black salt, cumin powder and sev. 12. Serve immediately.

name: Turai Moong Dal
instructions: 1. Wash and peel turai, cut into small pieces. 2. Soak moong dal and rinse well. 3. Heat oil in a pan. 4. Sauté onions until translucent. 5. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilli. 6. Add turmeric and salt. 7. Add turai pieces and cook for 3-4 minutes. 8. Add moong dal and required water. 9. Cook on medium heat until dal and turai are tender (about 10-15 minutes). 10. Stir occasionally. 11. Finish with fresh coriander. 12. Serve hot with rice or bread.

name: Dry Mini Kachori
instructions: 1. Soak urad dal for 2 hours and drain. 2. Mix refined flour with salt, baking soda and oil. 3. Knead soft dough with chilled water. 4. Let dough rest 15-20 minutes covered. 5. Coarsely grind soaked urad dal without water. 6. Heat oil in pan, add cumin seeds. 7. Add asafoetida and coriander powder. 8. Add ground urad dal and roast while stirring until dry (about 12 minutes). 9. Add salt, ginger powder, garam masala, fennel powder, dry mango powder. 10. Mix well and cool. 11. Add red chilli powder. 12. Divide dough into 2 parts and make small dough balls. 13. Stuff each ball with 0.5 tsp filling and seal edges. 14. Shape into round kachori. 15. Heat oil for frying on low heat. 16. Fry kachori until golden brown. 17. Remove and drain excess oil. 18. Cool completely before storing.

name: Virgin Lemon Mint Mojito
instructions: 1. Take sugar in a vessel and add water. 2. Heat on flame until sugar dissolves and syrup reaches one-thread consistency. 3. Cut lemons and extract juice in a bowl. 4. Wash and clean fresh mint leaves. 5. Check syrup has reached proper consistency (3-thread). 6. Add 1 tbsp lemon juice to cooled syrup. 7. Put mint leaves and lemon juice in mixer and grind finely. 8. Pour ground mixture into bowl and add remaining lemon juice. 9. Mix ground mint and lemon juice into cooled syrup. 10. Strain through fine sieve to separate pulp. 11. Fill syrup in bottle. 12. To serve: put ice in glass, add 3 tbsp mojito syrup, add soda water, lemon slice and fresh mint leaves. 13. Stir and serve immediately.

name: Dana Methi Ki Sabji
instructions: Heat oil in pan. Add onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste. Add fenugreek seeds and cook for few minutes. Add turmeric and salt. Cook until seeds are tender and flavors blend well.

name: Aloo Paneer Kachori
ingredients: singhare ka atta (water chestnut flour) - 1 cup
instructions: Make stiff dough with singhare flour and water. Mash potatoes and mix with crumbled paneer, salt, pepper and chopped green chili. Form balls of dough, fill with paneer-potato mixture, flatten and fry in ghee until golden brown.

name: Dhania Burfi
instructions: Roast coriander seeds and grind coarsely. Heat ghee and add ground coriander. Add milk powder. Add sugar and cook until mixture thickens and leaves the sides of pan. Pour on greased plate and cut into pieces when cooled.

name: Samak Katli
instructions: Roast samak in dry pan until fragrant. Heat ghee and add roasted samak. Cook for few minutes. Add jaggery and water, stirring continuously. Cook until mixture thickens and becomes solid. Pour on greased plate, add peanuts on top and press. Cut into pieces when cooled.

name: Sandwich Dhokla
instructions: Mix besan with yogurt to make smooth batter. Add sugar, oil and salt. Keep aside 10-15 minutes. Divide batter. Add eno to one portion and pour on greased plate. Steam for 5 minutes. Spread chutney on layer. Divide remaining batter, add eno, spread over chutney. Steam for 12-14 minutes until cooked. Prepare tempering: heat oil, add mustard seeds and let crackle, add water and sugar. Cool dhokla, cut into pieces and serve with tempering.

name: Veg Tawa Fry
instructions: Prep vegetables including bitter gourds (salt and set aside 20 min), arbi, potatoes, brinjals, and ladyfingers. Fry all vegetables individually in hot oil until crispy. Prepare masala mixture with roasted spices and tomato-ginger-chilli paste, cook until oil separates. Combine fried vegetables with masala on a griddle, add butter, and serve hot.

name: Palak Dhokla
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with spinach puree, peanuts, and spices. Prepare batter with salt and turmeric. Steam in a greased tin until cooked through. Cool and cut into pieces. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Besan Mathri
instructions: Mix refined flour and chickpea flour with oil and spices. Knead into dough with water and salt. Let rest. Roll out thin and shape into spirals or coils. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.

name: Rajma Palak Curry
instructions: Soak and cook rajma until tender. Prepare base with onions, garlic, and ginger. Add tomatoes and cook masala. Add spinach puree and cooked rajma. Season with spices and salt. Simmer until well combined.

name: Annkoot
instructions: Wash and chop all vegetables. Fry vegetables in oil with cumin, asafoetida, turmeric, green chilli, coriander powder and ginger paste. Add salt and water, cover and cook. Prepare separate tomato masala with roasted spices. Mix tomato masala into vegetables and cook until well combined. Add garam masala and green coriander. Serve hot with bread.

name: Rajgira Ladoo
instructions: Roast rajgira seeds in batches in hot pan until puffed, sieve and collect. Heat ghee and melt jaggery, add water and cook. Strain jaggery syrup into puffed rajgira. Add cashews and raisins, mix well. Shape into ladoos with wet hands while still warm. Cool and serve.

name: Kair Sangri Sabzi
instructions: Rinse beans thoroughly multiple times. Soak overnight then rinse again. Pressure cook beans with water until tender, drain. Heat oil and splutter cumin seeds, add asafoetida, turmeric, coriander powder and red chilli. Add beans, red chilli powder, mango powder, garam masala, salt and raisins. Cook for 3-4 minutes. Garnish with green coriander.

name: Til Gud Bati
instructions: Dry roast sesame seeds. Finely chop almonds. Mix mawa and jaggery together. Combine sesame seeds, jaggery-mawa mixture, and chopped almonds. Mix in green cardamom powder. Divide into portions and shape into balls or bati. Serve at room temperature.

name: Malai Puri
instructions: Dissolve sugar in 1.5 cups water and bring to boil. Add saffron and cardamom powder. Mix gulab jamun ready-mix with 3/4 cup water to pouring consistency. Heat ghee in a pan. Pour batter into hot ghee using a serving spoon and fry until golden brown on both sides. Dip fried puris in sugar syrup for 4 minutes. Place on plate and garnish with chopped pistachios.

name: Warqi Paratha
instructions: Mix refined flour, wheat flour, salt, and carom seeds. Add 2 tsp ghee and knead into soft dough with water. Cover and rest 20-25 minutes. Grease hands with ghee and squash dough into round shape. Coat with flour and roll to 10-12 inch diameter. Spread ghee over surface and fold into thirds. Spread ghee again and fold into thirds again. Roll thin and cook on heated tawa with ghee on both sides over medium flame until brown spots appear, flipping as needed.

name: Muchi Bara
instructions: Mix chickpea flour and urad dal. Prepare batter with cumin seeds, fennel seeds, green coriander, green chilli, ginger, asafoetida, coriander powder, turmeric powder, mango powder, salt, and water to achieve thick consistency. Heat oil and fry sev (thin noodles) and vada (spheres) from the batter. Prepare curry gravy using onions, tomatoes, and spices. Add fried sev and vada pieces to the gravy and simmer until flavors combine.

name: Amboli (Maharastrian Pancake)
instructions: Wash and soak 1 cup rice for 3-4 hours, grind finely. Wash and soak 1 cup urad dal for 3-4 hours, drain and grind with 1-2 tbsp water. Mix both pastes, add 1/4 tsp baking soda. Ferment for 10-12 hours. Add salt and adjust consistency with water. Heat griddle with oil, spread 1 tbsp batter in circular motion, add oil around edges, cover and cook 3-4 minutes on medium until dark brown. Flip and cook other side until brown. Repeat for all batter.

name: Curd Rice Tadka
instructions: Soak 1 cup rice for 20 minutes, drain and add to pressure cooker with 2.5 cups water. Close lid and cook until first whistle, lower flame to low for 2 minutes, then turn off. After pressure releases, remove rice and cool. Mix cooled rice with 2 cups fresh curd and 1 tsp salt. For tempering: heat 2 tbsp oil, add 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp split chickpeas, 1 tsp urad dal, sauté until brown. Add 2-3 chopped green chillies and 3 dry red chillies, roast together. Add 10-12 curry leaves and sauté. Pour tempering over curd rice and mix gently.

name: Choliya Puri (Green Chickpeas Poori)
instructions: Prepare dough using wheat flour and green chickpea flour. Knead with water and salt to soft consistency. Let rest for 15-20 minutes. Roll small portions into thin circles. Heat oil in pan and deep fry each puri until golden and puffed on both sides. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: Lemon Pickle with Jaggery
instructions: Wash and cut lemons into pieces. Mix with jaggery and salt. Let sit for 2-3 days in a glass jar in sunlight. Stir occasionally. The lemons will release juice and pickle naturally.

name: Mango Custard
instructions: Grind sugar to fine powder, add chopped mangoes and grind to paste. Add 2 tbsp custard powder and grind together. Grease a pan with ghee. Add mango mixture and water, mix well. Cook on medium flame, stirring continuously until thickens. Add ghee gradually while stirring. When ghee is absorbed, add chopped cashews and cardamom powder, mix well. Turn off flame. Transfer to greased tray, garnish with melon seeds, press lightly. Let set for 30 minutes. Cut into pieces and serve.

name: Kasuri Methi Paratha
instructions: Mix kasuri methi into flour dough with salt and minimal water. Knead until soft. Roll into flat rounds and cook on a griddle with oil until golden and slightly crispy on both sides.

name: Methi Kadhi
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Temper with cumin and mustard seeds. Add ginger and green chilli paste. Whisk yogurt with gram flour and turmeric. Add to the pan slowly. Stir well to avoid lumps. Add chopped methi leaves and chilli powder. Simmer for 5-7 minutes on low heat. Season with salt.

name: Club Kachori
instructions: Soak urad dal for 1 hour. Grind with green chilli and ginger coarsely. Mix with refined flour, semolina, curd, salt and oil. Knead into stiff dough and rest 15-20 minutes. Divide into lumps and flatten into 2.5-3 inch rounds. Fry on medium heat until golden on both sides. For curry: temper panch phoran spices, add tomato-ginger-chilli paste, roast masalas, add diced potato and pumpkin, add water and pressure cook until tender. Garnish with green coriander.

name: Chana Jor Garam
instructions: Soak dry chickpeas overnight and drain well. Heat oil and deep fry chickpeas until crispy and golden. Drain on paper towels. Once cooled, toss with salt, black salt, roasted cumin seeds, red chilli powder, garam masala and mango powder. Mix well and store in an airtight container.

name: Amchur Pickle
instructions: Sun-dry mango slices (khatai) for 2-3 weeks until completely dry. Heat oil and temper with mustard and fenugreek seeds. Add dried mango slices and roast. Add salt, chilli powder, turmeric and asafoetida. Stir well. Add a little water if needed. Cool completely and store in glass jars in a cool place.

name: Raw Mango Kadhi
instructions: Peel and grate raw mango. Whisk yogurt with gram flour and turmeric to avoid lumps. Heat oil and temper with cumin seeds, mustard seeds and curry leaves. Add ginger and green chilli. Pour yogurt mixture slowly into hot oil, stirring constantly. Add grated raw mango, chilli powder and salt. Simmer on low heat for 5-6 minutes until thickened.

name: Luchi Poori
instructions: Mix refined flour and salt together. Add oil and rub well into the flour. Add warm water gradually to form a soft dough. Knead for 3-4 minutes until smooth. Cover and let rest for 15-20 minutes. Divide into small balls. Roll each ball into a thin round disc. Heat oil for frying on medium-high heat. Carefully place disc in hot oil and it will puff up. Fry until golden on both sides.

name: Sem Ka Achar
instructions: Clean and prepare broad beans. Sun dry or cure with salt. Temper mustard and fenugreek seeds in oil. Mix with dried beans and spices. Store in airtight container for 2-3 days before consumption.

name: Gur Ke Sev
instructions: Heat oil and add chickpea flour. Gradually add water to form soft dough. Rest for 15-20 minutes. Heat oil for deep frying. Using sev maker with largest holes, extrude dough into hot oil. Fry until golden brown. Drain on paper towels. Melt jaggery with ghee on low flame. Break sev into pieces and coat with melted jaggery. Cool and store in airtight container.

name: Masale Bhat
instructions: Dry roast poppy seeds, sesame seeds, coriander seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon, star anise, cardamom, cloves and black pepper. Set aside. Toast coconut and cashews separately. Heat oil with mustard and cumin seeds. Saute potatoes for 2 min. Add cauliflower and capsicum, roast until crunchy. Add green chilli, ginger and tomato. Add soaked rice with turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Roast rice for 2-3 minutes. Add water and roasted spices. Cook covered on low flame for 10 minutes. Garnish with cashews and coriander.

name: Lavang Latika
instructions: Make a dough with flour and water. Roll thin, cut into strips, fry in ghee until golden. Prepare sugar syrup, coat fried pieces with it, garnish with dry fruits.

name: Boondi Laddu
instructions: Make a smooth batter with chickpea flour and water like pakora batter. Heat ghee and fry boondis using a slotted spoon until crisp. Prepare sugar syrup. Mix boondis with hot syrup, add cardamom and muskmelon seeds. Cool and bind into laddu balls. Garnish with grated pistachios.

name: Watermelon Lemonade
instructions: Cut and deseed watermelon, blend with water to get juice. Strain to remove pulp. Add lemon juice and sugar to taste. Mix well. Serve chilled with ice cubes. Can add black salt for flavor.

name: Gulab Jamun Curry
instructions: Mix mawa and paneer, add ararot, form smooth dough and make balls. Deep fry in oil until golden brown. For gravy, heat oil with cumin seeds and spices. Add cashew-tomato-chili paste, roast. Add curd, water, salt and garam masala. Simmer, add fried gulab jamuns, cook 1 minute. Garnish with coriander.

name: Fried Vegetable Momos
ingredients: salt 3/4 tsp plus 1/4 tsp for dough
instructions: Prepare momo dough with flour, water and salt. Let rest. Heat oil, sauté ginger and green chili, add cabbage and carrot, cook until tender, season with salt and coriander. Cool filling. Roll dough thin, cut circles, fill with vegetable mixture, fold into momo shape. Pan fry or deep fry until golden brown and crispy on both sides.

name: Firki Matri
instructions: Mix refined flour with salt, crushed carom seeds, crushed dry fenugreek leaves, and oil. Add lukewarm water gradually to knead stiff dough. Cover for 15-20 minutes. Oil palms and mash dough. Divide into lumps and flatten into 3-6 inch rounds. Cut partially from corners without cutting centre. Fold corners from end to centre creating windmill shape. Preheat oil to medium heat. Fry at low-medium flame for 5-6 minutes until golden. Drain and cool. Store in airtight container.

name: Farali Neer Dosa
instructions: Grind soaked samo rice with grated fresh coconut and water until fine. Transfer to bowl. Add 1.5 cups water to batter to thin consistency. Add sendha salt and mix. Heat non-stick tawa and apply ghee evenly. Stir batter and pour small portions thinly on tawa. Spread evenly and cook slightly. Pour ghee on sides and roast well from beneath. Cover to steam for 2 minutes. Reduce flame and roast 1-2 minutes more. Flip and cook other side on medium flame. Total time per dosa is 5-6 minutes.

name: Puff Chana Chikki
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add jaggery and melt on low heat, stirring occasionally until it reaches hard-ball stage. Quickly add roasted puffed chana dal and salt.
