Mix rapidly on high heat coating all pieces. Pour on greased surface immediately. Once cooled slightly, break into pieces. Store in airtight container.

name: Cheese Tomato Sandwich
instructions: Slice tomatoes. Spread pasta sauce on one bread slice. Place cheese slice over sauce, then tomato slices. Sprinkle salt and pepper. Add another cheese slice. Top with second bread slice and spread butter. Repeat for second sandwich. Heat pan on medium flame. Place sandwich butter-side down and cook. Cover and cook 2-3 minutes. When brown underneath, spread butter on top and flip. Cook other side on low flame until cheese melts and bread browns. Cut diagonally and serve hot.

name: Kathal Masala Bharta
instructions: Peel and chop jackfruit into small pieces. Boil in cooker with 1/2 cup water until first whistle, then simmer 4-5 minutes on low. Chop tomatoes finely. Heat mustard oil, add cumin seeds on low flame. Add asafoetida and roast until brown. Add green coriander and saute. Add turmeric, dry fenugreek, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Roast well. Add salt. Add boiled jackfruit to masala mixture. Stir in garam masala and mango powder. Cover and cook on low flame 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.

name: Methi Achar
instructions: Dry roast fenugreek seeds lightly and crush coarsely. Heat mustard oil and let it cool. Add turmeric, red chili powder, asafoetida. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds. Mix in salt and crushed roasted fenugreek. Combine well. Store in glass jar. Let ferment for 3-4 days before using. Stir occasionally. Store in cool, dark place.

name: Singhare ke Aate Ladoo
instructions: Mix chestnut flour and roasted peanuts. Heat ghee and add the flour-peanut mixture. Roast until fragrant. Add desiccated coconut and roast further. Cool the mixture. Add powdered sugar and cardamom powder. Mix well. Roll into balls and serve.

name: Cheesy Vegetable Pasta
instructions: Cook pasta until al dente. Make a white sauce by melting butter, adding refined flour, and gradually adding milk. Season with salt, pepper, and oregano. Chop green capsicum finely. Add capsicum to sauce. Grate mozzarella cheese and mix into sauce. Combine cooked pasta with sauce and serve hot.

name: Corn Meal Upma
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add urad dal and fry until golden. Add onion, green chili, ginger, and curry leaves. Saute until fragrant. Add cornmeal and roast for 2-3 minutes while stirring continuously. Slowly add water while stirring to avoid lumps. Cook until the mixture is thick and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and serve hot.

name: Vegetable Noodle Soup
instructions: Boil water with salt. Add noodles and cook until tender, then drain. Heat oil in a pot. Add garlic and ginger, saute. Add finely chopped carrot and cabbage. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes. Add water or stock and bring to boil. Add cooked noodles and soy sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Crispy Fried Soya Chaap
instructions: Make marks on soya chaaps with a knife. Powder soya chunks coarsely. Make a thin slurry of refined flour with water. Mix spices: curd, ginger paste, garam masala, coriander powder, red chili powder, turmeric, and salt. Marinate soya chaaps in spice mixture for 20 minutes. Mix refined flour slurry with spices: chili flakes, black pepper, oregano, and salt. Coat marinated chaaps with soya chunk powder. Heat oil in wok. Fry chaaps until golden brown and crispy, about 4-5 minutes. Serve with chutney.

name: Kamrakh Lonji
instructions: Wash and chop star fruits. Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds, let them crackle. Add chopped star fruits and cook until soft. Add salt, red chili powder, and turmeric powder. Gradually add sugar and stir well. Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens to jam consistency. Cool and store in clean jars.

name: Semolina Jalebi
instructions: Mix semolina, refined flour, and baking powder. Add whisked curd and orange food color. Mix to form a thick batter. Let rest for 30 minutes. Heat ghee in a wok. Fill batter into a squeeze bottle or jalebi maker. Squeeze hot batter into hot ghee in spiral coils. Fry until golden and crispy. Meanwhile, make sugar syrup: dissolve sugar in water, add lemon juice and crushed cardamom. Dip hot jalebis in warm sugar syrup. Serve at room temperature.

name: Spongy Chenna Rasgulla
instructions: Make fresh homemade chenna from milk. Shape chenna into small balls. Boil in sugar syrup on high flame. The rasgullas will absorb the syrup and become spongy.

name: Kathal Kabab
instructions: Prepare raw jackfruit and chop finely. Mix with spices, onion, garlic, and ginger. Shape into kebabs. Fry or bake until golden and crispy.

name: Hari Mirch Fry
instructions: Slit green chilies lengthwise. Season with spices and salt. Shallow fry in oil until skin blisters and cooks through.

name: Besan Toast
instructions: Mix besan with curd and water to thin batter. Add spices, chopped vegetables. Heat pan with oil. Spread batter on bread, place in pan batter-side down. Cook 3 minutes on low-medium flame. Oil top, flip, cook another 3 minutes.

name: Karela Tomato
instructions: Slice bitter gourd, remove seeds, soak in salt water. Cut tomatoes. Heat oil, add spices and onion-garlic paste. Add bitter gourd, cook until tender. Add tomatoes and cook until well combined. Serve hot.

name: Rava Appam
instructions: Mix semolina with whisked curd. Add chopped vegetables, green chili, ginger paste, and salt. Rest for 10-15 minutes. Prepare tempering with mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil. Add tempering to batter and mix. Add baking soda gently. Heat appam maker with oil in molds. Fill molds with batter. Cover and cook on low-medium flame for 3 minutes. Flip and cook until golden brown on both sides, about 2 more minutes. Serve hot with chutneys.

name: Makka ki Maheri
instructions: Roast cornmeal in ghee until golden and fragrant. Add hot milk gradually while stirring to avoid lumps. Cook on medium flame until thickened. Add sugar and cardamom powder. Stir well and cook for few more minutes. Garnish with chopped dry fruits. Serve warm.

name: Crispy Fried Corn
instructions: Boil 2 cups water and add 1 cup sweet corn. Boil for 5-6 minutes. Drain using sieve. Add corn flour, red chili powder, and salt. Mix until corn is coated. If powdery, add 1/2-1 tsp water. Heat oil in wok. Add coated corn and spread with laddle. Keep flame low-medium and roast for 3 minutes. Increase flame gradually. Cover wok and continue cooking, checking frequently. Remove corn after 5 minutes total using sieve. For topping, mix finely chopped green chili, green coriander, black pepper, dry mango powder, and lemon juice. Serve crispy corn hot with topping as appetizer or snack.

name: Achari Kaddu
instructions: Peel and chop pumpkin into medium pieces. Heat oil and add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and nigella seeds for tempering. Add chopped onions and cook until golden. Add turmeric and red chili powder. Add pumpkin pieces and mix well. Add salt and chopped tomatoes. Cook covered on medium flame until pumpkin is tender, stirring occasionally. Serve hot as accompaniment to rice or bread.

name: Anjeer Kofta Curry
instructions: Soak dry figs and chop finely. Mix with mashed potato, bread crumbs, ginger-garlic paste, green chili, and salt. Form into kofta balls. Heat oil and lightly fry koftas until light brown. For curry, heat oil, temper with cumin seeds, add sliced onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened. Add yogurt and salt. Gently add koftas to curry. Simmer on low flame until koftas are coated with curry. Garnish with cream and cilantro. Serve with rice or bread.

name: Pizza Without Yeast
instructions: Mix all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Add oil and water gradually while mixing to form soft dough. Knead well. Cover and let rest for 15-20 minutes. Divide dough into portions. Roll out each portion to pizza base thickness. Place on pizza pan or baking sheet. Spread pizza sauce on base. Add finely chopped vegetables as topping. Sprinkle cheese and oregano. Bake in preheated oven at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until cheese melts and base turns golden brown. Slice and serve hot.

name: Paneer Bread Balls
instructions: Break bread slices and grind finely into crumbs. Grind 2 more slices separately for coating. Mix crumbled paneer with salt, coriander powder, mango powder, red chilli powder, green chilli, black peppercorns, and ginger paste. Combine bread crumbs with milk and knead into dough. Add paneer mixture, green coriander, and ground cashews. Mix refined flour with water to make a thin batter. Shape mixture into balls, dip in batter, coat with bread crumbs, and deep fry in medium-hot oil until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels and serve with chutney.

name: Plain Paratha
instructions: Mix wheat flour and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes. Divide into 4 equal portions and roll into balls. On a floured surface, roll each ball into a thin circle. Brush with ghee and fold into quarters, then roll again into a thin paratha. Heat a skillet or tawa and cook paratha on both sides until golden spots appear and it puffs up slightly. Brush with ghee while cooking. Serve hot.

name: Soya Matar Bhurji
instructions: Boil 2-2.5 cups water with salt. Add soya chunks and cover. Turn off flame and let rest 20 minutes until soya becomes soft. Heat oil in a pan and add tomato, green chilli, and ginger paste. Saute on medium flame and add cumin powder and coriander powder. Add red chilli powder and roast. Add green peas and mix well. Cover and cook on low flame for 4 minutes. Add curd on low flame and mix. Add the softened soya chunks, Maggi Masala, and butter. Mix well and cook on low flame for 2-3 minutes. Garnish with green coriander and serve hot.

name: Sattu Ladoo
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan and add cashews and peanuts. Roast until light golden. Add sattu powder and roast for 2-3 minutes. Grind jaggery to a fine powder. Add jaggery powder to the sattu mixture along with cardamom powder. Mix well until everything is combined. Cool slightly and shape into small balls (ladoos). Place on a plate to set. Store in an airtight container.

name: Kamal Kakdi Achaar
instructions: Clean and cut lotus stems into small pieces. Dry them in sun for 1-2 days or use a dehydrator until they lose most moisture. Heat oil in a glass jar or ceramic container. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds and let them crackle. Add asafoetida, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder. Add the dried lotus stem pieces and salt. Mix well. Cover and let it sit for 2-3 days, stirring occasionally. Transfer to clean glass bottles and store in a cool dark place. Serve as a side with meals.

name: Mango Cardamom Iced Tea
instructions: Boil water and add tea leaves along with crushed cardamom pods. Steep for 3-4 minutes and strain. Cool the tea completely. In a glass, add mango pulp and tea. Add honey or sugar and stir well. Add lemon juice. Fill the glass with ice cubes and stir. Garnish with mint leaves and serve chilled. Can also be prepared by blending mango pulp with chilled tea and then chilling further.

name: Chocolate Peanut Bars
instructions: Line a square baking pan with parchment paper. Melt 100g dark chocolate and butter together. Chop or crush roasted peanuts coarsely. In a bowl, mix peanut butter with powdered sugar and vanilla extract. Add crushed peanuts and salt. Press this mixture into the prepared pan evenly. Spread melted chocolate over the peanut layer. Melt milk chocolate and spread a thin layer on top or drizzle. Chill in refrigerator for 2-3 hours until firm. Cut into bars or squares. Store in an airtight container in cool place.

name: Til Dry Fruits Burfi
instructions: 1. Roast sesame seeds lightly in a pan. 2. Mix roasted sesame seeds with dry fruits. 3. Prepare sugar syrup at soft-ball stage. 4. Mix sesame seeds and dry fruits into syrup. 5. Spread on greased pan and cut into pieces once cooled.

name: Cheesy Veg Kulcha Pizza Sandwich
instructions: 1. Heat pan and add butter, sauté carrot, capsicum, corn until crunchy (1.5-2 min). 2. Add salt and cook for 1 minute. 3. Add tomato and sauté. 4. Add black pepper and tomato sauce. 5. Cool the filling. 6. Cook kulcha on pan with butter until golden. 7. Spread pizza sauce on kulcha. 8. Add filling and grated cheese. 9. Cover with another cooked kulcha. 10. Cook on low-medium flame, flip, spread butter. 11. Remove and cut into desired shape.

name: Mirchi Methi Dana
instructions: 1. Wash and pat dry green chilies, remove stalk and chop. 2. Soak fenugreek seeds for 4 hours, then drain. 3. Heat oil in pan. 4. Add cumin seeds, asafoetida, turmeric, coriander and fennel powder. 5. Add chopped green chilies and salt. 6. Stir well, cover and cook for 2 minutes. 7. Stir again, add mango powder. 8. Turn off flame and serve as a side dish.

name: Hare Matar ki Dal
instructions: 1. Heat cooker with oil. Make paste of tomato and green chili. 2. Add cumin seeds when oil is hot. 3. Add asafoetida, turmeric, coriander powder and roast. 4. Add tomato-chili paste and ginger paste. 5. Roast masala until oil floats. 6. Add coarsely ground green peas. 7. Roast for 1 minute with spices. 8. Add water and salt. 9. Close cooker, cook until single whistle. 10. Add garam masala and green coriander. 11. For tempering: heat ghee, add cumin seeds and sliced green chili, roast and pour over dal.

name: Farali Potato Fingers and Balls
ingredients: sendha salt (1.5 tsp or to taste)
instructions: 1. Soak samo rice for 1 hour, remove extra water. 2. Cook soaked rice in cooker with 2 cups water for single whistle. 3. Peel and grate boiled potatoes. 4. Coarsely grind black pepper. 5. Mix cooled samo rice with grated potatoes, salt, cumin seeds, green chili, pepper and green coriander. 6. Grease hands with oil and shape into potato fingers and balls. 7. Heat oil until very hot. 8. Fry fingers and balls one by one until golden brown on high flame. 9. Serve with vrat chutney or coconut chutney.

name: Alsi ki Roti
instructions: 1. Mix wheat flour, ground flaxseeds and salt in a bowl. 2. Add oil and mix well. 3. Add water gradually and knead into soft dough. 4. Divide into 4 portions and roll out thin chapati. 5. Heat griddle/tawa until very hot. 6. Place roti on hot tawa and cook until puffed. 7. Flip and cook the other side until light brown spots appear. 8. Apply ghee and serve hot.

name: aloo khasta kachori
ingredients: red chilly powder less than 1/4 tsp
instructions: Mix refined flour with oil, salt, carom seeds, and water to form soft dough. Rest 10 minutes. For filling: heat oil, add ginger and green chilly, add green peas and cook 2 minutes. Add mashed boiled potatoes and spice powders, cook 2 minutes. Cool filling. Divide dough into balls, stuff with filling, and seal. Heat appam maker on low flame with oil. Place kachoris in moulds, add oil drops on top. Cover and cook 3 minutes, flip, and cook until golden brown on both sides.

name: til peanut gajak
instructions: Heat wok and roast sesame seeds on medium flame by stirring until puffy and color changes. Set aside. Heat ghee in wok, add crumbled jaggery and cook on low flame, stirring occasionally. Once jaggery melts, increase flame and cook until it foams up. Check readiness by dropping in water - should be strechy when undercooked. When jaggery breaks as it cools, it is ready. Add roasted peanuts and ground sesame seeds to jaggery syrup and mix well on flame. Pour mixture onto ghee-greased board, sprinkle sesame seeds on top and press with greased hands and rolling pin. Cut into desired pieces and cool. Store in airtight container.

name: aloo chana subzi
instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add ginger and green chillies and stir briefly. Add cubed potatoes and green chickpeas. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt. Cover and cook on medium flame until potatoes are tender. Mash slightly if desired. Finish with garam masala and serve hot.

name: macaroni pulao
instructions: Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds. Add finely chopped onion and cook until golden. Add ginger and garlic paste, stir briefly. Add finely chopped carrots and green peas, cook for 2 minutes. Add boiled macaroni and cooked rice. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt. Toss well on high flame. Finish with garam masala and chopped green coriander. Serve hot.

name: methi besan thepla
instructions: Mix gram flour and wheat flour with chopped fenugreek leaves. Add salt, turmeric powder, and red chilly powder. Add oil and mix well. Gradually add water to form a soft dough. Knead well and rest for 10 minutes. Divide dough into balls and roll out into thin round flatbread. Heat a griddle or tawa on medium-high flame. Place thepla on griddle and cook until light brown spots appear. Flip and cook other side until golden brown. Apply oil or ghee. Serve hot with pickle or yogurt.

name: sweet guna
instructions: Roast wheat flour in ghee until golden. Add roasted sesame seeds. Mix in jaggery powder and salt. Knead mixture with warm ghee to form a halwa-like consistency. Shape into balls or logs. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: bread kulcha
instructions: Cut bread into thick slices. Boil and mash potatoes. Mix with finely chopped onion, green chili, ginger paste, coriander powder, cumin seeds and salt. Spread filling on bread slices. Top with curd mixture. Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until golden. Serve hot.

name: dal bati
instructions: For bati: Blend semolina with curd. Grate boiled potatoes. Mix wheat flour with salt and crushed carom seeds. Add baking soda, grated potatoes and fermented semolina. Knead stiff dough with minimal water. Divide into lumps, flatten and hollow center. Bake at 250°C for 15-20 minutes, coat with ghee. For dal: Heat ghee, add cumin and asafoetida. Roast spices and curry leaves. Add tomato-green chili-ginger paste. Roast until oil separates. Add soaked dal and chickpeas. Roast 1-2 minutes. Add water and salt. Pressure cook until soft. Stir in green coriander. Serve dal and bati together.

name: aloo paneer kofta
instructions: Grate boiled potatoes and paneer. Mix with corn flour, salt, crushed spices, chopped green chili and green coriander. Add chopped cashew and raisins. Form balls, flatten and make hollow. Stuff with cashew and raisins, seal into round shape. Deep fry until golden brown. For gravy: Heat oil, add cumin seeds and roast spices. Add ginger paste and tomato-green chili paste. Roast until oil separates. Add poppy seed paste, spices and water. Cook for 7-8 minutes. Add fried koftas, simmer 2 minutes. Garnish with green coriander. Serve with bread or rice.

name: masala baati
instructions: Knead wheat flour with salt, carom seeds and water to form soft dough. Let rest 20 minutes. Heat ghee, add cumin seeds. Fry finely chopped onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste, green chili, coriander powder, turmeric and red chili powder. Cook until aromatic. Divide dough into 8 parts. Roll each into circle, place spice filling in center, gather edges and seal. Roll gently without breaking. Deep fry in hot ghee until golden on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Besan Arbi
instructions: Peel and cut arbi into desired shape. Mix gram flour with turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Coat arbi pieces with the flour mixture. Heat oil in a pan and deep fry arbi until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

name: Bharwa Kundru
instructions: Cut kundru lengthwise and remove seeds carefully. Mix gram flour with spices. Stuff the kundru halves with the spiced flour mixture. Heat oil in a pan and shallow fry stuffed kundru until golden and tender. Serve hot as a side dish.

name: Soybean Pancake
instructions: Mix soybean flour and rice flour. Add salt, turmeric, finely chopped green chilli and ginger. Mix with water to form smooth batter. Heat oil on a griddle. Pour batter and spread thin. Cook until golden on both sides. Serve hot with chutney or dhal.

name: Tomato Bhindi Sabzi
instructions: Cut okra into pieces and tomato into chunks. Heat oil, add cumin seeds. Add onion and sauté until translucent. Add okra and cook on high heat initially to reduce moisture. Add tomato pieces and spices. Cover and simmer until okra is tender. Serve hot as a side dish.

name: Dry Fruits Namkeen
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan. Fry lotus seeds until golden brown and transfer to a plate. Fry cashews separately until light brown, then fry almonds similarly. In a large bowl, combine fried lotus seeds, cashews, almonds, raisins, sendha salt and black pepper powder. Mix well. Cool completely and store in an airtight container for up to 2 months.

name: Kaju Korma
instructions: Grind tomatoes, green chilli, ginger and cashews into a fine paste. Heat oil and fry cashews until color changes slightly, then add cumin seeds. After seeds splutter, add asafoetida and whole garam masala. Sauté spices briefly. Add tomato-cashew paste and cook until fat separates. Add red chilli powder, turmeric and coriander powder. Add cream and 1/2 cup water. Simmer until gravy thickens. Add roasted cashews, salt and green coriander. Simmer covered for 3-4 minutes. Serve with chapatti or rice.

name: Jal Jeera
instructions: Dry roast cumin seeds until fragrant. Soak overnight or use powder. Mix with water, add lime juice, mint leaves, and rock salt to taste. Strain and serve chilled.

name: Spring Roll Wrappers
instructions: Knead flour, corn flour, salt and oil with water to make soft dough. Rest 15-20 minutes. Make small balls and roll thin. Stack two rolled pieces with oil and flour between them, press and roll thin. Cook on greased griddle on low heat until slightly roasted on both sides. Separate the two layers to get transparent wrappers.

name: Bajra Thepla
instructions: Mix bajra flour with grated lauki, fenugreek leaves, minced ginger, chopped green chili, salt, and oil. Add water gradually to form soft dough. Knead well. Let rest 10-15 minutes. Take small portions, flatten slightly, and roll thin on oiled surface. Cook on hot griddle with oil until golden brown spots appear on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Rabri
instructions: Boil milk in a heavy-bottomed pan. Keep stirring and let it reduce to about 1/3 of original volume, scraping the cream layer that forms on the surface and mixing it back. This takes about 1.5-2 hours. Add sugar and cardamom powder. Heat ghee, fry cashews and raisins, and add to rabri. Cook for 2-3 more minutes. Garnish with sliced pistachios and serve chilled.

name: Kaju Paneer Barfi
instructions: Soak cashews in milk for 2 hours. Grind cashews with sugar and paneer into fine paste. Heat ghee in nonstick pan, add cashew-sugar-paneer paste and roast, stirring constantly until thick and ghee separates. Add cardamom powder and mix. Spread on greased plate evenly, top with sliced pistachios, and let set for 2-3 hours. Cut into desired sized pieces.

name: Aloo Lachha Tokri Chaat
instructions: Peel and grate potatoes from larger pores. Wash twice to remove starch. Press to remove excess water. Mix with refined flour. Heat oil in deep pan. Grease two steel strainers and layer potato mixture in larger one to form tokri shape. Place smaller strainer on top to close. Dip in hot oil for 2-3 minutes on each side until golden brown. Remove and drain excess oil. Arrange on plate and top with chickpeas, sweet curd, chutneys, boondi, sev, pomegranate, chili powder, black salt, and roasted cumin powder.

name: Parwal Pickle
instructions: 1. Wash and cut parwal pieces. 2. Apply salt and turmeric and let sit for 30 minutes. 3. Heat oil in a pan and temper with mustard and fenugreek seeds. 4. Add chilli powder and turmeric. 5. Add parwal pieces and mix well. 6. Cook until tender. 7. Cool and store in glass jars.

name: Flax-seed Paratha
instructions: 1. Mix wheat flour with crushed flax seeds and salt. 2. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough. 3. Let dough rest for 20 minutes. 4. Divide dough into equal portions and roll into circles. 5. Apply ghee between layers if desired. 6. Cook on a griddle over medium heat until golden spots appear on both sides. 7. Serve hot with butter or pickle.

name: Alsi Dry Chutney Powder
instructions: 1. Dry roast flax seeds in a pan on medium heat until aromatic, stirring constantly. 2. Dry roast red chillies separately. 3. Cool both ingredients completely. 4. Grind flax seeds to a coarse powder. 5. Grind red chillies to a fine powder. 6. Mix flax seed powder with chilli powder, salt and asafoetida. 7. Store in an airtight container.

name: Ghugni Choora
instructions: 1. Soak chickpeas overnight and boil until soft. 2. Heat oil and add chopped onions, cook until golden. 3. Add ginger and sauté. 4. Add boiled chickpeas and cook for 5 minutes. 5. Add turmeric and chilli powder. 6. Mix in flattened rice gently. 7. Cook for 2-3 minutes and garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Gajar Beans Sabzi
instructions: 1. Cut green beans into 2-inch pieces and carrots into similar size pieces. 2. Heat oil in a pan and add sliced onions, cook until golden. 3. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies, sauté for 1 minute. 4. Add turmeric and coriander powder. 5. Add green beans and carrots, stir well. 6. Cover and cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally. 7. Add salt, cumin powder, red chilli powder and garam masala. 8. Cook uncovered for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are tender. 9. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Bread Pizza Katori
instructions: Brush bread slices with pizza sauce. Top with grated mozzarella cheese and chopped vegetables (capsicum, sweet corn, baby corn). Sprinkle oregano, chili flakes, and black pepper. Place in preheated pan or kadhai and cook on medium heat until cheese melts and bread becomes crispy at the edges.

name: Meethi Seviyan
instructions: Preheat pan and add 2 tbsp ghee. Add vermicelli and roast on medium flame until golden brown while stirring continuously. Add chopped almonds and cashews and roast on low flame. In another pan, heat 2.25 cups water and dissolve 1/2 cup sugar to make syrup. Add roasted vermicelli to sugar syrup and cover. Cook on low to medium flame for 5 minutes. Stir and add cardamom seeds. Cook 5 minutes more with lid partially open, then 2 minutes uncovered. Cover and let rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Sooji Golgappa
instructions: Mix semolina with salt and water to form a thick dough. Cover and rest the dough. Take small portions and shape into thin hollow balls. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels. The hollow golgappa shells are ready to fill with filling and pani.

name: Dhania Panjiri Prasad
instructions: Dry roast coriander seeds until fragrant. Grind or pound into powder. Heat ghee and mix with ground coriander and jaggery powder. Mix well and form into balls or make as a granular mixture. Serve as a sacred offering or sweet prasad.

name: Hare Chane ki Burfi
instructions: Cook green chickpeas until soft. Drain and grind into fine powder. Heat ghee and cook the chickpea powder on medium heat, stirring continuously. Add sugar and mix well. Continue cooking until mixture starts leaving the sides of the pan. Pour into a greased tray and let cool. Cut into pieces and serve.

name: Punjabi Mango Pickle
instructions: Cut raw mangoes into small pieces. Dry roast mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and nigella seeds. Mix with turmeric powder and red chili powder. Heat mustard oil and let it cool. Combine mango pieces with spice mixture and oil. Mix well in a jar. Cover tightly and let it sit in sunlight for 3-4 days, stirring daily. The pickle will be ready to use after setting.

name: mixed vegetable water pickle
instructions: Boil 600ml water in a vessel. Cut peeled turnips, carrots and radish into 1 inch pieces. Add to boiling water, cover for exactly 3 minutes. Turn off flame and keep covered for 5 minutes. Cool the vessel. Remove vegetables into a bowl. Add salt, black mustard seeds, fennel powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, mustard oil and vinegar. Mix thoroughly. Store in sterilized container.

name: raw banana halwa
instructions: Rinse and chop bananas. Pressure cook with 1 cup water until one whistle, let steam escape naturally. Cool and peel bananas, chop into rough chunks and mash finely. Heat 4-5 tbsp ghee in a wok, add mashed bananas and stir on low flame until color changes and ghee leaves the sides. Add milk and sugar, stir well. Simmer until thick, add chopped dry fruits and raisins, continue cooking until dense. Mix in cardamom powder. Transfer to serving bowl and garnish with dry fruits and ghee.

name: stuffed fenugreek leaves paratha
instructions: Knead wheat flour with water and salt. Prepare filling by mixing chopped fenugreek leaves with onion, green chili, turmeric and salt. Divide dough into portions. Roll a portion thin, add filling in center, fold and seal edges. Roll gently into a paratha. Cook on hot griddle with ghee until golden brown spots appear on both sides.

name: mango dry fruit laddu
instructions: Heat pan, add ghee and roast muskmelon seeds until they puff up and change color. Remove to plate. Add ghee again, roast ground cashew and almonds, remove to plate. Roast grated coconut on medium flame for 1 minute, remove to plate. Put mango pulp in pan, add sugar and stir, cook until dense on medium-high flame. Add roasted dry fruits, reduce flame, add cardamom powder and cook for 1-2 minutes. Cool slightly. Grease hands, take small portions and shape into round laddus. Coat with cashew or coconut powder.

name: chenna murki
instructions: Cut paneer into small pieces. Peel and coarsely grind cardamom. In a non-stick pan add sugar and 0.5 cup water, stir well and heat. Cook for 2 minutes. Check syrup consistency by dropping a few drops in cool water - when it forms a single thread, syrup is ready. Add paneer pieces and cardamom powder to syrup. Cook on low flame, stirring regularly until sugar syrup becomes transparent and reaches setting consistency with even coating on paneer. Turn off flame, place pan on a stand and add rose water, stir constantly while cooling. Once sugar is set, pick out paneer pieces.

name: spinach stuffed paratha
instructions: Knead wheat flour with water and salt to make soft dough. Prepare filling by mixing chopped spinach with onion, green chili, turmeric powder, red chili powder and salt. Divide dough into equal portions. Roll a portion thin, place filling in center, fold edges to seal, then roll gently into a paratha shape. Cook on preheated griddle with ghee until light brown spots appear on both sides, flip and cook other side until golden brown.

name: mango mastani
instructions: Blend ripe mangoes with milk and sugar until smooth. Add finely chopped cashew nuts and almonds. Pour into tall glasses, top with scoops of ice cream, garnish with chopped pistachios and chocolate syrup. Serve immediately.

name: atte ka halwa
instructions: Roast wheat flour in ghee over medium heat, stirring frequently until golden brown and fragrant. Add sugar and continue mixing until it dissolves completely. Cook until the mixture reaches a thick, crumbly halwa consistency. Serve warm.

name: khatta mitha kaddu
instructions: Peel and cut pumpkin into small chunks. Heat oil, temper with cumin seeds. Sauté chopped onions until translucent. Add ginger-chili paste, then tomato. Add pumpkin chunks and all dry spices. Cover and cook on medium heat until pumpkin is tender. The sweet-sour balance comes from the cooked pumpkin, tomato tanginess, and spices.

name: aloo bhujiya
instructions: Boil potatoes and mash them. Mix with besan and all spices thoroughly. The mixture is then extruded through a bhujiya maker (or similar device) directly into hot oil to create thin noodle-like strands. Fry until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels and store in an airtight container.

name: tomato pulao
instructions: Heat oil and temper cumin seeds and bay leaf. Sauté sliced onions until golden. Add tomato puree, turmeric, and red chili powder. Cook until oil separates from the tomato mixture. Add washed rice and stir to coat with the tomato-oil mixture. Add water and salt, bring to boil, then simmer covered until rice is tender and water is absorbed.

name: Makhana Kaju Curry
instructions: Prepare cashew nuts and makhana. Sauté aromatics with spices. Add cashew nuts and makhana to the gravy and simmer until cooked through. Serve hot.

name: Arbi Leaves Kofta Curry
instructions: Mix gram flour, spices, and finely chopped green coriander into arbi leaves. Form into balls and fry until golden. Make curry base with tomato paste and spices. Add fried koftas to gravy and simmer.

name: Moong Gobhi Kofta Curry
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal coarsely with ginger and green chilli. Mix with grated cauliflower and spices. Form into balls and fry until light brown. Prepare curry base with whole spices and tomato paste. Add fried koftas to gravy and simmer for 2 minutes.

name: Cheese Namakpara
instructions: Make a well in flour, add ghee, salt, carom seeds and grated cheese. Knead with lukewarm milk to make stiff dough. Rest for 20 minutes and knead again. Roll thin and cut into 1/2 to 3/4 inch squares. Deep fry on medium flame until golden brown. Store in airtight container.

name: Noodle Spring Rolls
instructions: Boil noodles and stir-fry with chopped vegetables and aromatics. Season with soy sauce and sesame oil. Wrap filling in spring roll wrapper. Fold and seal edges. Deep fry until golden brown and crispy. Serve hot.

name: Aloo Gobi Masala Paratha
instructions: Knead wheat flour with oil and salt into a soft dough and rest for 20 minutes. Prepare filling by sautéing carom seeds and green chillies, adding ginger, then cauliflower and potatoes with spices. Cool filling. Flatten dough portions, add filling, seal edges, and flatten again. Cook on tawa with oil on both sides until light brown spots appear and paratha puffs up.

name: Tomato Kadhi
instructions: Blend tomatoes and green chillies into fine paste. Temper cumin, fenugreek, and mustard seeds with asafoetida. Add spices and curry leaves. Add tomato paste and sauté until oil separates. Prepare gram flour slurry and add to masala with water. Simmer for 10-12 minutes stirring regularly. Prepare final tempering with cumin seeds, green chilli, and curry leaves. Pour over kadhi and serve hot with rice or Indian breads.

name: Khoba Roti
instructions: Mix flour with water and salt to form a stiff dough. Let it rest. Roll thick rotis and cook on griddle until puffed and golden, flipping frequently until cooked through.

name: Til Mawa Gajak
instructions: Toast sesame seeds lightly. Heat ghee and melt jaggery in it. Mix in mawa and sesame seeds. Spread on a greased tray, mark portions and cool completely before breaking into pieces.

name: Methi Pakora
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with salt, turmeric and chilli powder. Add chopped methi leaves and water to form thick batter. Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and deep fry until golden and crispy on both sides.

name: Singada Curry
instructions: Pressure cook water chestnuts with water for first whistle plus 2 minutes low flame, then cool and peel. Heat mustard oil, temper with cumin seeds and asafoetida. Sauté turmeric and coriander powders. Add tomato-ginger-chilli paste and red chilli powder, cook until oil separates. Temper chickpea flour in oil separately and add to masala. Add peeled water chestnuts, salt and garam masala. Cook covered for 5 minutes. Garnish with green coriander.

name: Sweet Mathri
instructions: Mix wheat flour with ghee until breadcrumb texture. Add powdered jaggery/sugar, salt and spices. Knead into stiff dough. Roll thin and cut into shapes. Deep fry in oil until golden and crispy. Cool completely before storing.

name: Potato Stuffed Bread Rolls
instructions: Mix boiled mashed potatoes with all spices, green peas, coriander, and ginger. Stuff bread slices with this mixture. Seal with flour paste. Fry in hot oil on medium flame until golden brown on all sides.

name: Atta Namakpare
instructions: Mix wheat flour with salt and cumin seeds. Add ghee and mix well. Knead with lukewarm water into stiff dough. Rest for 15-20 minutes. Flatten thin and cut into strips. Fry in preheated oil on medium flame for 3-4 minutes until floating, then fry until golden brown on low-medium flame. Drain and store in airtight container.

name: Pizza Buns
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, salt, sugar, and butter with warm water to form soft dough. Cover and let rise for 1-2 hours. Divide into 4 portions, flatten, fill with pizza sauce, cheese, vegetables, and spices. Shape into buns, let rise for 30 minutes. Bake at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until golden.

name: Stuffed Dum Aloo
instructions: Hollow potatoes and stuff with mixture of crumbled paneer, cashews, raisins, ginger, chilli, coriander, and salt. Seal with flour paste. Sear stuffed potatoes in oil. Make gravy with fried spices, tomato paste, ginger, and cashews. Add stuffed potatoes to gravy. Pressure cook until first whistle, then low flame for 5 minutes. Garnish with coriander.

name: Instant Rava Vada
instructions: Mix semolina with curd, salt, green chilli, ginger, coriander, and baking soda. Let it rest for 5 minutes. Drop spoonfuls of batter into preheated oil. Fry on medium flame until golden brown on all sides. Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

name: Gujarati Bottle Gourd Thepla
instructions: Peel, grate, and wash bottle gourd. Mix flour with grated gourd, curd, oil, salt, spices, green chilli, ginger paste, and coriander. Knead into soft dough. Cover and rest for 15-20 minutes. Divide into balls, roll into thin 6-7 inch rounds. Heat greased tawa. Roast thepla on tawa, grease with oil, flip and cook until golden brown spots appear on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Tendli Pickle
instructions: Wash and chop tindora. Heat oil and add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and cumin seeds. Add tindora pieces with turmeric powder, chili powder, asafoetida and salt. Dry roast over medium heat until pickle is ready to serve.

name: Aloo Kathal Kofta Curry
instructions: Boil and mash potatoes with jackfruit pieces to form koftas. Heat oil, sauté onions, add ginger-garlic paste. Add tomatoes and spices. Gently place koftas into the curry and simmer until cooked through. Garnish with fresh coriander.

name: Bakla Aloo Sabzi
instructions: Chop bakla beans and potatoes. Heat oil and splutter cumin seeds. Add asafoetida, turmeric, coriander powder, green chili, salt and ginger paste. Add potatoes and beans. Roast briefly, add water, cover and simmer on low heat for 3-4 minutes until tender. Add mango powder, green coriander and garam masala. Mix well and serve.

name: Aloo Matar Paratha
instructions: Knead wheat flour with salt and oil, let rest 20 minutes. For stuffing, heat oil and roast cumin seeds. Add spices, green peas paste and boiled potatoes. Add salt, garam masala, chili powder and mango powder. Mix well. Roll dough, place stuffing, seal and roll into thick paratha. Roast on hot tawa with oil until brown spots appear on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Moonglet Pizza
instructions: Soak moong dal for 2 hours. Grind soaked dal with green chili, ginger and salt. Add water and baking soda. Heat oil in pan and spread batter to 1/2 cm thickness. Place chopped vegetables over batter. Pour oil over vegetables and press lightly. Cover and cook on medium heat for 6-7 minutes until roasted from below. Flip and cook other side for 4 minutes. Slice and serve with chutney.

name: Roasted Potato Wedges
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into wedges. Toss with oil, salt, pepper and herbs. Spread on a baking sheet in single layer. Bake in oven at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until golden and crispy. Serve hot with ketchup or mayo.

name: kaju chikki
instructions: Roast cashew nuts lightly. Heat sugar with ghee on medium flame until it caramelizes to golden brown. Add roasted cashews and quickly spread on greased parchment paper. Cool completely and break into pieces. Store in airtight container.

name: fried rice
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or pan. Add minced garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add all vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add cooked rice, breaking any lumps, and mix well. Pour soy sauce and continue stir-frying for 3-4 minutes. Season with salt and white pepper. Toss until rice is heated through and well coated.

name: besan ki chakki
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add chickpea flour and roast on medium flame for 12-15 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and slightly darkened. Add sugar and cardamom powder, mix well. Add chopped nuts and continue stirring. Once mixture comes together, pour into greased pan and press evenly. Cool completely and cut into pieces.

name: candied watermelon rind
instructions: Peel watermelon, remove pink flesh, and cut white rind into small cubes. Soak rind in water for 30 minutes. In a heavy-bottomed pan, dissolve sugar in water and add ginger and cardamom. Add drained watermelon rind and lemon juice. Bring to boil and then simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rind becomes translucent and syrup thickens. Cool completely and store in sterilized jars.

name: dal stuffed lachha paratha
instructions: Make a soft dough with refined flour, oil, salt and water. Cook chana dal and mash it with spices. Divide dough into portions, roll out, layer with oil (lachha technique), fill with dal mixture, roll again and cook on griddle until golden brown on both sides.

name: sabudana mango kheer
instructions: Soak sago pearls in water for 1 hour. Boil milk in a vessel. Add drained sago pearls to boiling milk and cook until transparent (about 15 minutes), stirring occasionally. Add grated fresh coconut and sugar, cook for 5 minutes on low flame. Add mango pulp and cardamom powder, cook on high flame for a few minutes. Let cool, add chopped mangoes, chill for 30 minutes. Serve garnished with pistachios and mango pieces.

name: pizza mcpuff
instructions: Make a stiff dough with refined flour, salt, baking powder and oil. Cover and set for 30 minutes. Sauté ginger in 2 tsp oil, add chopped carrots, capsicum and corn. Cook for 2 minutes covered, then add tomato sauce, salt and oregano. Cook for 30 seconds more. Cool filling and mix in grated mozzarella cheese. Roll dough to thick sheets, cut into 9x4.5 inch rectangles. Place filling on one half, fold and seal edges with water, press with fork. Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Deep fry in medium-hot oil for 6-7 minutes until golden brown on all sides.

name: frozen mini cheese samosa
instructions: Mix refined flour, semolina, salt and carom seeds. Add 2 tbsp oil and knead into stiff dough with water. Cover and set for 20 minutes. Mix crumbled paneer, grated cheese, salt, black pepper and chopped green chili for filling. Roll dough pieces into oval shapes. Cut in half, grease edges with water, form cone, add 1 tsp filling, seal edges and press with fork. Arrange samosas with gaps on a plate and freeze for 5-6 hours until hard. Transfer to airtight container and freeze. Deep fry frozen samosas in medium-hot oil for 4-5 minutes until golden brown.

name: shikanji
instructions: Roast 2 tbsp cumin seeds on medium flame, cool. Grind roasted cumin with black salt, cinnamon, cardamom, fennel seeds and black pepper to fine powder. Sieve to remove fibers. For syrup: cook 1 kg sugar with 2 cups water until dissolved. Cool, add spice powder and mix well. Extract juice from 1/2 kg lemons and add to cooled syrup. Filter syrup. To serve: Add 1/2 tsp spice powder in a glass with 2 tbsp sugar and lemon juice, add chilled water and stir. Add mint leaves and ice cubes. Alternatively use 2 tbsp prepared syrup in a glass with chilled water, mint and ice.

name: karela fry
instructions: Wash bitter gourds and cut into thin rings or slice lengthwise then into pieces. Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add asafoetida pinch. Add bitter gourd pieces and sauté on high heat for a few minutes. Add coriander powder, fennel powder, turmeric and red chili powder. Mix well. Add salt and dry mango powder. Continue cooking on medium heat, stirring occasionally until bitter gourds become tender and edges turn crispy, about 10-15 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Tomato Cucumber Raita
instructions: 1. Finely chop tomatoes and cucumber, discarding excess water. 2. Whisk yogurt until smooth. 3. Add chopped tomatoes and cucumber to yogurt. 4. Season with salt and cumin powder. 5. Mix well and refrigerate. Garnish with coriander leaves before serving.

name: Bharwa Baingan
instructions: 1. Heat pan, roast cumin and sesame seeds until color changes. 2. Roast freshly grated coconut. 3. Coarsely grind roasted peanuts, coconut and seeds together. 4. Add coriander powder, fennel powder, ginger paste, turmeric, red chili powder, mango powder, chopped green chili and garam masala to ground mixture and mix well. 5. Cross-cut eggplants and fill with prepared masala. 6. Heat oil in cooker, add cumin seeds and asafoetida. 7. Roast remaining masala briefly. 8. Add stuffed eggplants and mix well with spices. 9. Add water to desired gravy consistency. 10. Close cooker and cook until single whistle, then turn off heat. 11. Garnish with green coriander before serving.

name: Agra Ka Petha
instructions: 1. Remove soft pulpy part of ripe petha fruit, peel green skin and cut into smaller pieces. Poke pieces with fork. 2. Prepare limestone water (2 litre water with limestone), add petha pieces and keep for 10-12 hours. 3. Drain limestone water and wash petha pieces thoroughly. 4. Boil petha pieces in 2 litre water for 20 minutes on high flame. 5. Drain and keep in strainer. 6. Prepare sugar syrup by dissolving sugar in water over high flame. 7. Add petha pieces to syrup and cook until dense. 8. Let pieces cool in syrup for 6-7 hours or overnight. 9. After 12 hours, cook again until dense with regular stirring. 10. Spread petha pieces on net and dry under fan for few hours. Store in container at room temperature for up to 2 months.

name: Wheat Nachos with Salsa and Cheese Sauce
instructions: 1. For nachos: Mix wheat flour, chickpea flour, 1 tbsp oil, 1/2 tsp turmeric, carom seeds and 1/3 tsp salt. Add water and knead into stiff dough. Rest 15 minutes. 2. Roll thin and cut into chip shapes. 3. Deep fry until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. 4. For tomato salsa: Finely chop tomatoes. Add coriander, ginger, green chilies, black pepper, roasted cumin seeds, olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt. Mix well. 5. For cheese sauce: Heat butter over medium heat. Add refined flour and turmeric, mix well. Add milk gradually while stirring to avoid lumps. Add cheese, salt and black pepper. Cook until thickened. 6. Serve nachos with salsa dip and cheese sauce on the side.

name: Soyabean Kofta Curry
instructions: 1. Soak soya chunks in boiling water for 10 minutes until expanded. 2. Boil and grate potatoes. 3. Mix expanded soya with grated potatoes, salt, coriander powder, red chili powder, green chili, turmeric, green coriander and chickpea flour. Knead into dough. 4. Form round balls from dough. Heat oil to medium-high temperature. 5. Fry cutlets until golden brown on all sides (6-7 minutes per batch). Drain on paper towel. 6. For gravy: Heat oil in pan, add cumin seeds, bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, black peppers on low flame. 7. Add turmeric, coriander powder, and paste of tomatoes, ginger and green chili. 8. Roast until oil separates from spices. Add fenugreek leaves. 9. Temper chickpea flour in butter and roast until brown, then add to gravy. 10. Add water and bring to boil, add garam masala and green coriander. 11. Add cream and salt, cook covered for 3-4 minutes on low flame. 12. Arrange fried kofta in plate and pour gravy over. Garnish with green coriander.

name: Mung Dal Ladoo
instructions: Dry roast mung dal until fragrant and grind to fine powder. Mix powder with sugar and ghee, stirring continuously over low heat. Add crushed dry fruits and mix well. Cool slightly, shape into balls using wet palms or hands, and garnish with nuts.

name: Chyawanprash
instructions: Combine amla fruit pulp with sesame oil and clarified butter. Heat gently and add powdered dry fruits, herbs and Ayurvedic ingredients. Cook over low heat for extended time until it achieves thick paste consistency. Add honey at the end when cooled slightly. Store in glass container.

name: Sev Barfi
instructions: Knead chickpea flour with water and ghee, rest for 10-15 minutes. Chop dry fruits and grind cardamom. Prepare sev using sev maker and fry until light brown. In another pan, dissolve sugar in water and milk, add mawa and yellow colour. Bring to boil, add crushed sev and cook while stirring continuously until thick. Add ghee and cardamom powder. Cool, spread on tray with butter paper, garnish with dry fruits, press gently, and let set before cutting.

name: Paneer Dahi Vada
instructions: Grate paneer and boil potatoes. Mix paneer with mashed potatoes, ararot (arrowroot powder), finely chopped green chilli, grated ginger, and salt. Make soft dough consistency. Shape into small vadas and deep fry until golden brown. Serve with chilled yogurt (dahi) as topping or sauce.

name: Khatta Meetha Karela
instructions: Wash bitter gourds, peel and salt them, rest 30 minutes. Wash thoroughly and soak. Slit vertically keeping joined at bottom. Make stuffing with gourd peels, spices and mango powder. Fill gourds with stuffing. Heat oil in pan, place gourds, cover and cook on low flame for 3-4 minutes per side until tender and slightly brown. Flip sides 3-4 times during cooking. Garnish with green coriander and serve hot with bread or rice.

name: Bharwan Tinda with Gravy
instructions: Preheat oil in pressure cooker, add cumin seeds and turmeric. Add coriander powder and roast. Make paste of tomato, green chilli and ginger, add to spices with red chilli powder and roast until oil separates. Prepare stuffing with spices and chickpea flour. Peel tindas, cut from top keeping joined at bottom, cut into four parts. Stuff with spice mixture. Add water to gravy, place stuffed tindas, close lid and cook until first whistle, then 2 minutes on low flame. Cool and open. Garnish with green coriander and serve hot with flatbreads or rice.

name: mixed veg besan cheela
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with finely chopped spinach, grated cabbage, tomato, coriander leaves, green chilies, and ginger. Season with salt and water to make batter consistency. Heat oil in a pan and pour batter, cook until golden brown on both sides.

name: ker sangri pickle
instructions: Clean ker and sangri vegetables. Dry them completely. Mix with salt and spices. Pack in oil for preservation. Allow to cure for several days before serving.

name: mini bhakarwadi
instructions: Mix all dry ingredients together. Add tamarind chutney and knead into stiff dough. Roll small portions into logs. Cut into 2-inch pieces. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.

name: Chirote
instructions: Layer maida dough with ghee, roll and fold to create thin layers. Cut into rectangular pieces. Deep fry until golden and crispy. Soak in sugar syrup with cardamom. Garnish with nuts.

name: Instant Green Chilli Pickle
instructions: Slit green chilies and keep aside. Heat mustard oil. Add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add fennel seeds, fenugreek seeds, and cumin seeds. Add asafetida. Add sliced green chilies and salt. Mix well. Add vinegar and turmeric powder. Stir and let cool. Store in an airtight container.

name: Molded Chocolate Candy
instructions: Melt chocolate over double boiler or in microwave. Temper the chocolate if desired for smooth finish. Pour into candy molds. Tap molds gently to remove air bubbles. Let set at room temperature or refrigerate. Unmold once completely set. Store in airtight container.

name: Aloo Bharwan Mirch
instructions: Boil and mash potatoes. Mix in spices - cumin powder, garam masala, turmeric, coriander powder, ginger paste, and dry mango powder. Slit green chilies lengthwise carefully. Stuff with potato mixture. Heat oil and temper with asafetida. Place stuffed chilies in a microwave-safe dish. Microwave on high for 3-4 minutes. Garnish with green coriander.

name: Raw Tomato Chutney
instructions: Wash green tomatoes and chop finely. Add salt and let rest briefly. Finely chop green chilies and ginger. Mix tomatoes with chilies, ginger, and fresh coriander leaves. Add lemon juice and salt to taste. Mix well. Transfer to serving bowl. Serve fresh as a raw chutney accompaniment.

name: Raw Banana Sabzi
instructions: Remove stalk from bananas and peel off thick green skin. Cut into pieces and place in water to prevent darkening. Boil water with salt and turmeric powder. Add banana pieces and cook until soft, checking regularly. Drain bananas. Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Reduce flame. Add curry leaves and asafetida. Add chopped green chili and ginger paste. Roast briefly. Add turmeric powder and coriander powder. Roast. Add boiled bananas and mix well. Add salt and red chili powder. Add mango powder and green coriander. Stir continuously and cook for 2-3 minutes. Serve hot.

name: amla methi pickle
instructions: Wash and dice amla. Heat pan with oil, roast fenugreek seeds until brown on low flame. Add carom seeds and turmeric powder. Add amla with red chilly powder, garam masala, salt, fennel powder and asafoetida. Cover and cook 3-4 minutes until tender on low flame. Remove lid, press gently to check doneness. Take off flame, add vinegar. Transfer to plate and allow to cool completely before storing in airtight container. For first 3 days, stir twice daily.

name: masala missi paratha
instructions: Mix besan and wheat flour with chopped onions, green chillis, salt and all spices. Add water gradually to form soft dough. Let rest 15 minutes. Divide into portions and roll into thin rounds. Cook on hot griddle with ghee until both sides are golden brown and crispy.

name: mini farsan samosa
instructions: Mix flour with ghee and salt. Add crushed carom seeds. Knead stiff dough with water. Rest 20-25 minutes. Prepare filling: grind aloo bhujiya with sesame seeds, fennel powder, coriander powder, red chili, sugar and salt. Add raisins, chopped cashews and tamarind pulp. Roll small dough portions, cut into half. Form cone shape with water on edges, fill with stuffing, seal edges. Keep open 15-20 minutes. Deep fry in low-medium heat oil until golden and floats. Fry until crispy.

name: unni appam
instructions: Grate jaggery. Mix rice flour with grated jaggery, ghee, powdered cardamom and salt. Mash ripe banana and add to mixture. Add chopped dry fruits and grated coconut. Mix well. Heat appam mould or small pan with ghee. Drop spoonful of mixture into each mould. Cook until golden on both sides. Remove and serve warm.

name: palak paneer biryani
instructions: Parboil basmati rice until 70% cooked. Blanch spinach and grind to smooth paste. Cut paneer into cubes. Heat ghee, add cumin seeds, cardamom, bay leaves and cinnamon. Add sliced onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic-chilli paste. Add yogurt and spinach paste. Cook 2 minutes. Layer rice with spinach-paneer mixture in heavy-bottomed pot. Sprinkle fried onions on top. Cover with foil and lid. Cook on high heat 1-2 minutes until steam forms. Reduce heat to low and cook 20-25 minutes. Switch off and let stand 5 minutes. Open lid and gently mix.

name: Gajar Gobhi Shalgam Achar
instructions: Wash and cut vegetables into desired size. Boil vegetables for 3 minutes to blanch, then drain thoroughly and dry in sunlight or under fan. Roast cumin seeds, black pepper, fenugreek seeds, and fennel seeds for 1 minute, then cool. Heat mustard oil and turn off flame. Grind mustard seeds coarsely. Once oil cools, add asafoetida, turmeric powder, ground spices, green chili, ginger, ground mustard, red chili powder, and salt. Mix oil and spices well and add vinegar. Store pickle in food-grade container; flavor develops after 3 days.

name: Cheese and Vegetable Stuffed Bread Pakora
instructions: Mix cheese, capsicum, tomatoes, green coriander chutney, and tomato sauce for filling. Prepare batter with chickpea flour, oregano, black pepper, salt, chili flakes, baking soda, and water to achieve dipping consistency. Spread filling on bread slices, stack and cut into desired shapes. Dip bread pieces in batter to coat completely. Heat oil and fry until golden brown and crispy. Serve immediately.

name: Chocolate Mousse
instructions: Chop dark chocolate finely and melt with butter over double boiler or microwave. Heat milk separately. Whisk melted chocolate with milk using mixer to incorporate air and create light, airy texture. Sweeten with sugar and add vanilla extract to taste. Divide into serving glasses and chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.

name: Chana Dal Burfi
instructions: Soak chana dal in lukewarm water for 2 hours, then drain and dry on cloth. Heat ghee in pan and roast soaked dal until crispy, approximately 12 minutes on high flame. Cool and grind roasted dal into fine flour. Heat pan with sugar and milk, stir until sugar dissolves completely. Add ground dal flour to milk and cook on medium flame, stirring continuously until mixture reaches thick barfi consistency. Pour remaining ghee into mixture and mix well. Add coarsely chopped cashews, almonds, pistachios, and crushed cardamom powder. Turn off flame, grease plate with ghee, pour mixture onto plate, press well, top with dry fruits, and press again. Cool completely, mark into pieces with heated knife, and serve.

name: Masala Chaas
instructions: Add chopped green coriander, mint leaves, coarsely ground black pepper, green chili, roasted cumin powder, and black salt to mixer jar. Add small portion of fresh curd and grind into paste. Add remaining curd, water, and ice cubes to jar and churn until well mixed and frothy. Pour into serving glass and sprinkle roasted cumin powder on top. Garnish with mint leaf and serve immediately.

name: Mango Rabdi
instructions: Heat milk in heavy-bottomed pan and reduce on medium-high flame, stirring occasionally, until reduced to half. Toast cashews and almonds in ghee until golden and set aside. Crush cardamom pods and add to reducing milk. Once milk is sufficiently thickened and reduced, add condensed milk and stir well. Add mango pulp and mix thoroughly. Add toasted nuts and raisins. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, then add saffron soaked in milk. Stir and cool to room temperature. Chill before serving.

name: Petha Ladoo
instructions: Grate petha on fine grater and keep aside. Slice pistachios and chop cashews into small pieces. Crush green cardamom seeds using mortar and pestle into fine powder. Roast mawa in hot pan over medium-high flame, stirring constantly until slight color change. Transfer warm mawa to bowl. Add grated petha, chopped cashews, sliced pistachios, and crushed cardamom powder to warm mawa. Mix all ingredients thoroughly. Roll mixture into ladoos of desired size using your hands. Dust prepared ladoos evenly with desiccated coconut. Arrange on serving plate. These can be served as dessert or during fasting.

name: Gajar Aaloo Matar Sabzi
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes, carrots into medium-sized pieces. Heat oil in pan and add cumin seeds to splutter. Add minced onion and cook until golden brown. Add ginger and garlic paste, cook for 1 minute. Add minced tomato and cook until softened. Add turmeric, coriander, red chili, and salt. Add cut potatoes and carrots, mix well. Add water to cover vegetables halfway, bring to boil. Cover and simmer on medium-low flame for 12-15 minutes. Add green peas and cook for another 3-4 minutes. Sprinkle garam masala, mix well, and serve hot.

name: khatta mitha chivda
instructions: Roast poha and nuts separately. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, then combine roasted ingredients. Mix in spices, sugar, and salt. Cool and store.

name: rava methi masala paratha
instructions: Boil water with salt and carom seeds. Add oil and semolina, stir well. Cool slightly. Add finely chopped fenugreek leaves. Knead smooth dough. Pinch portions, roll into round shapes, dust with flour, fold and roll into thick parathas. Heat tawa, cook paratha on both sides with oil until golden.

name: malai chop
instructions: Boil milk, cool slightly. Mix lemon juice to curdle milk. Strain through cloth to get chena. Wash and mash chena with flour. Make sugar syrup. Cook chena pieces in syrup for 15 minutes total. Cool for an hour. Mix mawa with saffron milk and boora. Stuff cooled chena pieces with mawa mixture. Garnish with pistachios.

name: soya malai chaap tikka
instructions: Mix curd, cream, and butter. Add all spices and chopped coriander. Coat soya chaaps thoroughly in marinade. Let sit for 30 minutes. Grill or bake at high temperature until cooked through and edges are browned.

name: raw jackfruit pulao
instructions: Heat oil, add cumin and bay leaves. Saute onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilli. Add diced raw jackfruit, cook until soften. Add washed rice, stir. Add water and salt. Cook covered on high until boiling, then low heat until rice is tender.

name: aloo malai cutlets
instructions: Boil potatoes until soft, peel and mash. Mix in flour, mayonnaise, chopped coriander, chilly, ginger-garlic, spices. Shape into round or oval cutlets. Coat with bread crumbs. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown on all sides.

name: urad dal pinni
instructions: Dry roast urad dal in a heavy pan until fragrant and lightly golden. Heat ghee in a pan, add roasted dal and cook on medium heat, stirring continuously. Add crushed cardamom. Continue cooking until mixture is golden and aromatic. Add powdered sugar and dry fruits. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes. Spread on a plate to cool and set.

name: Strawberry Kulfi
instructions: Reduce 1 litre of full cream milk by half by simmering on medium heat, stirring regularly. Wash and chop strawberries into fine and thick pieces. Add sugar and cardamom powder to reduced milk, stir well and turn off heat. Allow to cool on a jali stand. Once cool, add strawberry pieces, paste, and coarsely ground cashews, mix well. Pour mixture into moulds, close lids and freeze for 7-8 hours. Cut into pieces and serve.

name: Mango Malai Khandvi
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with 1/4 cup mango pulp. Grind with 1.25 cups water to dissolve lumps. Pour into pan and cook on medium flame while stirring continuously. Add 3 tsp sugar and cook with furious stirring. Continue cooking after boiling for more than 10 minutes. Spread batter thinly on plates using flat spatula. Cover remaining batter until thicker consistency is reached. Keep plates aside for 10 minutes to set. Chop into 1.5-2 inch pieces and separate with knife. Roll to fold. Mix 2-3 tbsp mango pulp with 2 tbsp condensed milk, sugar, and 2 tbsp milk. Spread this sauce over rolled khandvi and garnish with chopped pistachios. Serve immediately.

name: Vegetable Burgers
instructions: Mix boiled vegetables, mashed potatoes, bread crumbs, chopped onion, green chilies, ginger, coriander, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Form into patties. Heat oil in pan and fry patties until golden brown on both sides. Toast burger buns lightly. Assemble burger with patty, lettuce, tomato slices, and spread of mayonnaise or chutney. Serve hot.

name: Sweet Matthe
instructions: Roast refined flour in ghee on medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring continuously. Add milk gradually to the roasted flour while stirring to avoid lumps. Add sugar and cardamom powder. Cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes while stirring. Add chopped dry fruits and mix well. Serve warm.

name: Coconut Milk Shake
instructions: Add grated fresh coconut and milk to a blender. Blend until smooth. Add sugar and cardamom powder. Blend again for 1 minute. Strain if desired to remove coconut pulp, or serve as is for thicker consistency. Pour into a glass, add ice cubes. Serve immediately.

name: Green Mango Mint Chutney
instructions: Wash mint leaves thoroughly. Peel and chop raw mango into small pieces. Add mint leaves, chopped mango, green chilies, fennel seeds, cumin seeds, black salt, and salt to a blender. Blend until smooth paste forms. Transfer to serving bowl. Chutney is ready to serve with meals. Store in refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

name: Milk Mathri
instructions: Mix refined flour, powdered sugar, ghee, sesame seeds, salt, and grated nutmeg in a bowl. Add milk in small portions and knead to form stiff dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes. Heat ghee in wok to medium-hot temperature. Break dough into lumps and form balls. Flatten each ball slightly with palms. Fry mathris in hot ghee. When they float to top, flip them carefully. Fry until golden brown on both sides. Drain excess ghee using ladle held over wok. Place fried mathris on plate. Cool completely and store in airtight container. Will stay fresh for up to 2 months.

name: mixed fruit jam
instructions: Wash and prepare fruits. Grate apples. Heat pan, add sugar to grated apple. Grind grapes and strawberries, add to pan. Add pineapple. Cook on medium flame until dense, stirring regularly. Add cinnamon stick. Add cardamom powder. Continue cooking until jam is thick. Pour onto plate to test consistency. Cool and add lemon juice. Store in container.

name: chena kheer
instructions: Heat 1/2 liter milk. Add lemon juice in portions while stirring until milk coagulates. Strain chena through cloth and drain completely. Heat 1 liter milk, reduce flame and simmer until thick, stirring regularly. Add cardamom powder, saffron and powdered sugar. Knead cooled chena until smooth, taking 5-6 minutes. Roll into balls. In pressure cooker, dissolve sugar in water and bring to boil. Add chena balls, simmer 10-12 minutes. Close cooker with low flame. Release steam naturally. Cool chena balls. Drop into thickened milk and simmer 5-6 minutes on low flame. Garnish with pistachios. Refrigerate 1-2 hours. Serve chilled.

name: musk seeds namkeen
instructions: Clean melon seeds. Heat pan and dry roast melon seeds on medium flame, stirring constantly until slightly brown. Transfer to plate and cool. Pass through sieve to remove skin. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in wok and add almonds. Stir fry for 2 minutes until slightly brown. Add roasted melon seeds and stir. Turn off flame. Add salt, chaat masala and ground black pepper. Mix well and transfer to serving bowl.

name: samo rice chakli
instructions: Rinse samvat rice and soak in water for 2 hours. Drain water and coarsely grind rice in mixer without water. Heat 1 tsp oil in wok, add rice paste and saute for 1 minute on medium flame until dense and dough-like. Transfer to bowl and cool. Add cumin seeds, sesame seeds, sendha salt and peppercorns, knead until smooth and soft. Insert small ball of dough into chakli machine. Press onto polythene sheet in spiral motion to form round chaklis. Heat oil in wok and gently place chaklis into oil. Fry until golden brown on each side. Drain on kitchen paper towels. Cool and store in airtight container. Can be stored for up to 1 month.

name: Rava Cutlets
instructions: 1. Combine semolina, finely chopped capsicum, grated carrot, finely chopped cauliflower, plain flour, chopped green coriander, chopped green chilly, ginger paste, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. 2. Mix well to form a thick mixture. 3. Take bread slices, soak in water slightly, and crumble into the mixture. 4. Mix until a moldable consistency is achieved. 5. Shape mixture into oval or round cutlets. 6. Heat oil in a pan until medium-hot. 7. Carefully place cutlets in hot oil and fry until golden brown on one side. 8. Flip gently and fry the other side until golden brown. 9. Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. 10. Serve hot with green chutney or tomato sauce.

name: Sev Gur ke Laddu
instructions: 1. Coarsely crumble jaggery or prepare jaggery paste by melting. 2. Heat ghee in a pan. 3. Add crumbled sev to hot ghee and mix gently. 4. Add crumbled or liquid jaggery to the sev and stir constantly. 5. Add chopped nuts (almonds, cashews, peanuts) and mix thoroughly. 6. Continue stirring over low heat until mixture is well combined and warm. 7. Remove from heat and let cool slightly, about 2-3 minutes. 8. Wet hands lightly with ghee and shape mixture into round laddu balls, approximately 30-40g each. 9. Place on a plate to cool completely. 10. Store in an airtight container.

name: Chocolate Basundi
instructions: 1. Pour 1 can of condensed milk into a mixing bowl. 2. Add 1 can of evaporated milk to the condensed milk. 3. Add 2 tbsp chocolate powder to the milk mixture. 4. Add 1/4 tsp cardamom powder. 5. Stir well with a whisk or spoon until chocolate powder is fully dissolved and no lumps remain. 6. Divide the mixture into serving glasses. 7. Garnish with chopped mixed nuts. 8. Serve immediately, preferably chilled or at room temperature.

name: Chocolate Clusters
instructions: 1. Chop dark chocolate into small pieces. 2. Create a double boiler by placing a heat-safe bowl over a pot of simmering water (bottom bowl should not touch water). 3. Place chocolate pieces in the top bowl and melt, stirring occasionally until smooth. 4. Remove from heat and let cool for 1-2 minutes. 5. Add coconut shreds and chopped mixed nuts to the melted chocolate. 6. Stir well until nuts and coconut are evenly coated. 7. Line a tray with parchment paper. 8. Drop spoonfuls of the chocolate mixture onto the parchment paper, spacing them apart. 9. Let cool at room temperature for 30 minutes or refrigerate for 15 minutes until set. 10. Remove from parchment paper and store in an airtight container.

name: Gobi Ka Achaar
instructions: 1. Wash cauliflower and cut into small florets. 2. Toss florets with 2 tsp salt and let sit in a sieve for 2-3 hours to drain excess moisture. 3. After draining, use the florets and discard any liquid collected. 4. Heat 1/2 cup mustard oil in a pan over medium heat. 5. Add 2 tsp coarsely ground mustard powder and let it crackle in the oil. 6. Add 2 tsp coarsely ground fennel seeds and 1 pinch asafoetida to the hot oil. 7. Sauté for about 30 seconds. 8. Add 1 tsp turmeric powder, 1 tsp red chili powder, and 1 tsp coarsely ground fenugreek powder. 9. Stir well and cook for another 30 seconds. 10. Add the drained cauliflower florets and 2 tsp salt. 11. Mix everything thoroughly, coating all florets with spice and oil. 12. Add 2 tbsp white vinegar and stir well. 13. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally. 14. Transfer to a clean glass jar. 15. Cover and let it rest for 24 hours before consuming. 16. Store in a cool, dark place. Consume within 2-3 months.

name: Peanut Rava Halwa
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan. Add semolina and roasted peanuts, fry until golden brown. Add green cardamom. Add sugar and stir well to combine. Add dry fruits (cashews, almonds, raisins) and continue stirring. Cook until the halwa reaches proper consistency with a rich, golden color. Serve warm.

name: Moong Dal Gujiya
instructions: Soak moong dal and cook until soft, then dry and roast. Prepare filling by mixing roasted moong dal, ghee, sugar, and crushed green cardamom with dry fruits. Make a dough with flour, ghee, salt, and water. Divide dough into balls and roll into thin circles. Place filling in center, fold into semicircle, seal edges, and roll gently into gujiya shape. Either fry in hot ghee until golden brown or bake until crispy. Cool and serve.

name: Makhana Namkeen
instructions: Clean and rinse the lotus seeds. Heat ghee in a pan and fry lotus seeds on medium-hot flame, stirring occasionally, until they become crisp and turn slightly brown. Drain the fried seeds onto a plate. While still hot, sprinkle chaat masala, black pepper powder, and salt over the lotus seeds. Mix thoroughly. Serve crispy and fresh, either as a snack or with tea.

name: Aloo Masala Paratha
instructions: Make a soft dough with wheat flour, ghee/oil, salt, and water. Knead well and let rest for 20 minutes. Boil and mash potatoes, mix with cumin seeds, red chilly powder, garam masala, and salt to make filling. Divide dough into portions. Roll each into a small circle, place filling in center, fold and seal edges, then gently roll into a paratha. Heat a griddle or tawa, cook paratha with ghee or oil on both sides until golden brown and crispy. Serve hot with pickle or yogurt.

name: Fruits Shrikhand
instructions: Make hung curd by spreading cloth on strainer and draining 4 cups curd for 1-2 hours. Mix 2 cups hung curd with 0.5 cup powdered sugar. Add 1 tbsp saffron milk and cardamom powder, whisk 2-3 minutes until smooth. Add chopped grapes, apples, kiwi, pomegranate seeds and walnuts. Mix well and refrigerate for 1 hour. Serve chilled, garnished with fresh fruits.

name: Bhee Aloo Wadi Masala
instructions: Peel and cut lotus root and potatoes into pieces. Heat oil in pan, add cumin seeds, onion, ginger-garlic paste and green chili. Saute until golden. Add tomatoes and cook. Add lotus root and potato pieces. Add turmeric, red chili and coriander powders. Cover and cook on medium flame until vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and serve hot.

name: Cashew Nut and Almond Cookies
instructions: Roast cashews and almonds separately and cool. Grind nuts to coarse powder. Cream butter and sugar together. Add cardamom powder. Mix in ground nuts and flour. Shape dough into small balls, flatten slightly. Place on baking tray. Bake at 180C for 12-15 minutes until golden. Cool on wire rack before storing.

name: Karonda Chutney
instructions: Wash and dry karonda berries. Heat oil in pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add curry leaves and asafoetida. Add karonda berries and salt, cook on high flame. When berries soften, add red chili powder and jaggery. Stir well and cook until thick and chutney-like consistency. Cool and store in an airtight jar.

name: Instant Lemon Pickle
instructions: Cut lemons into small pieces, removing seeds. Boil lemons with salt for 5 minutes until softened. Heat oil in pan, add mustard seeds and let crackle. Add fenugreek seeds, asafoetida, garlic, and ginger. Cook until fragrant. Add boiled lemons and red chili and turmeric powders. Mix well and simmer for 2-3 minutes. Cool completely and store in an airtight jar for instant use or further maturation.

name: Semiya Upma
instructions: Boil water in vessel and add roasted vermicelli. Boil until soft and drain. Heat butter in pan, add ginger paste and green chili. Add carrots and baby corn, stir on high flame for 1 minute. Add cauliflower, green peas and capsicum. Cook for 3 minutes. Add tomatoes and roast slightly. When veggies are cooked, add pasta sauce, chaat masala and salt. Stir well. Add cooked vermicelli to veggies with green coriander. Mix until blended. Reduce flame and cook for 2 minutes. Serve hot.

name: jal jeera powder
instructions: Dry roast cumin seeds and dried mint separately until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes each. Cool completely. Grind roasted spices together with other dry ingredients until fine powder. Store in airtight container.

name: watermelon rind curry
instructions: Cut watermelon rinds into small cubes. Heat oil, add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add minced ginger and garlic, sauté until golden. Add chopped onions, cook until translucent. Add tomato paste and tomatoes, cook until soft. Add turmeric, red chili, and coriander powder. Add watermelon rind pieces and salt. Cook covered on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until rinds are tender. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve.

name: cornmeal vegetable upma
instructions: Toast cornmeal lightly. Heat oil, add mustard seeds and let crackle. Add curry leaves. Add toasted cornmeal and vegetables. Mix well with salt and water to desired consistency. Cook until done, stirring occasionally.

name: pineapple raita
instructions: Cook pineapple paste in a pan until softened. Add sugar and chopped pineapple, mix well and sauté until rawness disappears. Cool completely. Add cooled pineapple mixture to hung curd along with salt, green coriander and mix well. Garnish with roasted cumin powder and serve cold.

name: kesar pulao
instructions: Soak saffron in warm water for a few minutes. Wash and drain rice. In microwave-safe container, add ghee, rice, salt and measured water. Add saffron along with soaking water. Cover and microwave on high for 12-15 minutes until rice is cooked and water is absorbed. Fluff with fork and serve.

name: makhana raita
instructions: Roast makhana lightly until slightly crisp. Mix yogurt with salt and black salt. Add roasted makhana to yogurt. Top with roasted cumin powder and garnish with green coriander. Serve chilled.

name: crispy rava idli
instructions: Mix semolina with whisked curd, salt, ginger paste and finely chopped green chili. Add water to make batter consistency. Let rest 5-10 minutes. Heat tadka pan with oil, add mustard seeds to crackle. Add urad dal and roast until pink. Add curry leaves. Mix tadka into batter. Add eno fruit salt and mix. Heat wok on low flame, add oil, pour batter portion, even it out, oil the sides and top. Cover and cook 2-3 minutes. Flip carefully, cover and cook another 3 minutes until golden and crispy. Serve hot with chutneys.

name: narali bhat
instructions: Heat ghee in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add green chili, curry leaves and peanuts. Roast for a minute. Add grated coconut and roast for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Add cooked rice and jaggery, mix gently until jaggery melts and rice is well coated. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Add salt and mix well. Serve hot.

name: Mix Dal Tadka with Dahi
instructions: 1. Wash and soak 2 tbsp each of masoor dal, chana dal, moong dal, and urad dal; drain excess water. 2. Heat cooker with ghee, add cumin seeds, asafoetida, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves, and peppers; roast slightly. Add black cardamom seeds after removing peel. 3. Add grated ginger and finely chopped green chilies; roast slightly. Add turmeric powder, then add the drained dals and stir-roast for 2 minutes on medium flame. Add water and salt. 4. Close cooker lid and cook until single whistle, then reduce flame and cook on low until pressure releases completely. 5. Once cooked, open lid and add curd mixed with cumin powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder in small portions while stirring on high flame. 6. Add green coriander and mix well. 7. For tadka: Heat ghee in a tadka pan, add cumin seeds on reduced flame, add dry red chilies, turn off flame, add red chili powder. Pour tadka over dal and mix slightly.

name: Mango Besan Barfi
instructions: 1. Melt 1/3 cup clarified butter in a pan. 2. Roast 1 cup chickpea flour continuously on medium flame until brown in color. 3. Peel 2 mangoes, grind and extract pulp to get 1 cup. 4. Cook the mango pulp and 3/4 cup sugar together until mixture becomes thick in consistency. 5. Add the roasted chickpea flour, finely chopped cashews, and green cardamom powder to the mixture. 6. Stir and cook until thick in consistency. 7. Spread clarified butter on a plate. Pour and spread the mixture on it. Garnish with chopped cashews and pistachios, pressing them into the mixture. 8. Allow to set for 7-8 hours or overnight in a dry, cool place. 9. Heat the plate from bottom and cut into pieces.

name: Chana Saag with Urad Dal
