instructions: 1. Soak chickpeas and urad dal overnight. 2. Boil both until soft and cooked through. 3. Blanch spinach and chop finely. 4. Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and asafoetida. 5. Add ginger and green chilies, sauté briefly. 6. Add the boiled chickpeas and urad dal. 7. Add spinach and spices (turmeric, coriander powder, red chili powder, and salt). 8. Cook on medium flame for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally until well combined.

name: Til Atta Laddu
instructions: 1. Roast sesame seeds lightly on medium flame until fragrant, then set aside. 2. Roast wheat flour in ghee on medium flame for 5-7 minutes until golden brown. 3. Heat remaining ghee in a pan, add sugar and dissolve on low flame. 4. Add roasted wheat flour and sesame seeds to the ghee-sugar mixture. 5. Add crushed cardamom powder and mix well. 6. Add finely chopped cashews and pistachios. 7. Mix everything thoroughly until well combined. 8. Remove from heat and allow to cool slightly. 9. Roll into laddus of desired size.

name: Spicy Mixture Namkeen
ingredients: green peas 1/2 cup soaked and boiled
instructions: 1. Prepare boondi by making a thick paste with chickpea flour and baking soda. 2. Press through a boondi maker into hot oil to create small fried balls. Remove and drain on paper towel. 3. Fry flattened rice in hot oil separately until crispy. Drain and set aside. 4. Boil soaked chana dal and green peas until soft. 5. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large bowl and add cinnamon stick pieces, green cardamoms, and cumin seeds. 6. Add the fried boondi, fried rice, cooked chana dal, and green peas. 7. Season with black peppers, salt, and crushed green cardamom powder. 8. Mix thoroughly to combine all ingredients evenly.

name: Begun Bhaja
instructions: 1. Wash and cut eggplant into thin strips or rounds. 2. In a bowl, combine chickpea flour, all spice powders (cumin, coriander, turmeric, red chili, garam masala), ginger paste, green chili, asafoetida, and salt. 3. Coat the eggplant pieces evenly with this spice-flour mixture. 4. Heat mustard oil in a large pan or tawa on high flame. 5. Add the coated eggplant pieces and fry on high flame until golden brown on both sides, stirring occasionally. 6. Continue cooking until eggplant becomes soft and caramelized. 7. Sprinkle dry mango powder and finish with fresh green coriander. 8. Serve hot.

name: Raw Banana Masala Poori
instructions: 1. Boil 50 grams raw banana in cooker with water until first whistle. Cool and peel completely, removing black portions. 2. Grate the remaining raw bananas vertically until black inner portion appears. 3. In a bowl, mix wheat flour, grated bananas, finely chopped green coriander, chopped green chilies, red chili powder, turmeric powder, crushed carom seeds, and salt. Add water to knead a tight dough. 4. Cover and let rest for 20-25 minutes. 5. After resting, apply oil on palms and knead the dough again. 6. Divide dough into small portions and roll into balls. 7. Preheat oil for frying. 8. Flatten dough balls into rounds using a rolling pin, making them thin in the center and thick at edges. 9. Drop flattened dough into hot oil and fry on high flame, pressing with a spoon to expand. Flip and fry until golden brown. 10. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: Mango Frooti
instructions: Blend ripe and raw mangoes together. Mix with sugar to desired sweetness. Strain if needed. Chill and serve cold as a refreshing summer drink.

name: Besan Gatte Ki Sabzi
instructions: Prepare gram flour dumplings, boil them. In a pan, cook onions and tomatoes, add yogurt and spices. Add boiled dumplings and simmer until flavors blend.

name: Dry Masala Kachori
instructions: Prepare dough with flour, salt and oil. Make filling with dry masala, roasted spices, and fried onions. Stuff dough balls with filling and deep fry until golden and crispy.

name: Homemade Curd
instructions: Boil milk and let cool to lukewarm. Divide milk into three portions. In first portion add drenched green chilies, in second add red chilies, in third add lemon juice. Cover and keep in warm place for 10-12 hours. Check if curd has set. Use 2 tsp of this yogurt culture to set 1 liter milk for 6-7 hours for regular curd.

name: Mix Vegetable Pakora
instructions: Mix besan flour with salt and spices. Chop vegetables into small pieces. Mix vegetables into besan batter. Heat oil and drop spoonfuls of batter. Deep fry until golden and crispy on all sides. Drain on paper towels.

name: Zafrani Zarda Rice
instructions: Soak rice for 1 hour. Toast dry fruits, coconut and spices in ghee. Boil colored water and cook rice 80 percent. Roast cardamom and cloves in ghee with soaked rice. Add sugar and saffron-infused milk. Cover and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

name: Poha Chivda Namkeen
instructions: Roast the beaten rice in oil on medium heat with spices until crispy, then store. This microwave version requires heating components in microwave instead of stovetop frying.

name: Bhandara Style Aloo Sabzi
instructions: Cook potatoes until tender. Prepare a tempering with spices and onions. Mix cooked potatoes with the spiced base. Simmer until flavors combine. Serve hot.

name: Palak Vada
instructions: Soak urad dal and grind with spinach to form a paste. Mix with spices. Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and deep fry until golden brown on all sides. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: Sama Kachori
instructions: Grind soaked samak rice into fine paste. Pressure cook potatoes, peel and mash. Mix rice paste with salt and oil to form dough. Prepare filling with mashed potatoes, spices and coriander. Stuff dough balls with filling, flatten slightly. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown. Serve hot.

name: Mango Mint Smoothie
instructions: Peel and chop mango into pieces. Peel banana and cut into pieces. Remove seeds from dates. Add banana, mango, mint leaves and dates to a blender. Add chilled water. Blend until smooth and creamy. Pour into glasses and serve immediately.

name: Methi Laddu
instructions: Roast methi seeds until fragrant, grind coarsely, mix with ghee and powdered sugar, shape into balls.

name: Gur Ki Kheer
instructions: Cook rice in milk until soft, add jaggery and ghee, stir until jaggery dissolves, garnish with dry fruits.

name: Khasta Thekua
instructions: Mix semolina, flour, sugar, coconut, cardamom, fennel, raisins. Knead with ghee and milk. Shape using mould or roll and press. Fry in moderately heated oil until golden on both sides. Drain and cool. Store in airtight container.

name: Shahi Tukra
instructions: Fry bread pieces in ghee until golden, prepare milk rabri with condensed milk and sugar, soak fried bread in rabri, garnish with dry fruits and saffron.

name: Macaroni Cheese Samosa
instructions: Cook macaroni, mix with cheese and sauteed onions and chillies, stuff into samosa pastry, fry until golden.

name: Date Chutney
instructions: Soak dates, blend with amchoor powder, cumin, salt and green chillies to form smooth paste, adjust consistency and seasoning.

name: Honey and Lemon Green Tea
instructions: Brew green tea in hot water, cool or chill, add honey and fresh lemon juice, serve over ice.

name: Besan Kadhi with Pakora
instructions: 1. Prepare besan pakora by making small dumplings from besan batter and deep fry them. 2. In a bowl, mix yogurt with water and besan to create a smooth base. 3. Heat ghee or oil, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds for tempering. 4. Pour the yogurt-besan mixture, add fried pakoras, and cook on medium heat while stirring occasionally. 5. Add turmeric and salt to taste. 6. Cook in microwave or on stovetop until it reaches a smooth gravy consistency. 7. Serve hot with rice or bread.

name: Sabudana Kurure
instructions: 1. Put sago pearls in a jar and add black pepper and salt. Coarsely grind the ingredients. 2. Peel and grate the boiled potatoes. Add the ground sago mixture to it. 3. Add oil and mix well to form a dough. Cover and let it rest for 15-20 minutes. 4. After 20 minutes, take a sev machine with the thickest pore jali. Grease hands and make a log from the dough. Put it in the machine. 5. Preheat oil to medium-hot temperature. Press the sev machine and fry the kurkures in oil on low flame until golden brown. 6. Once fried, transfer to a plate and prepare the remaining kurkures. Store in an airtight container for up to a month.

name: Soybean Flour Dosa
instructions: 1. Mix soybean flour with rice flour in a bowl. 2. Add water gradually and mix to form a smooth, thin dosa batter consistency. 3. Add salt to taste and let the batter rest for 10 minutes. 4. Heat a non-stick griddle or dosa pan and lightly oil it. 5. Pour a ladle of batter in the center and spread it quickly with the back of the ladle to form a thin crepe. 6. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the bottom turns golden brown. 7. Apply oil around the edges and flip carefully. 8. Cook the other side for another minute until crispy. 9. Remove from pan and serve hot with sambar and chutney.

name: Patishapta Pitha
instructions: 1. Mix flour with a pinch of salt and make a thin batter using water and milk. Let it rest for 15 minutes. 2. Prepare the filling by mixing grated coconut with powdered jaggery and cardamom powder. 3. Heat ghee in a non-stick pan. 4. Pour a thin layer of batter and spread it evenly to form a crepe. 5. Cook on low heat for 30 seconds to 1 minute until it sets. 6. Spread the coconut-jaggery filling on one half of the crepe. 7. Fold the crepe in half and then roll it into a cylindrical shape. 8. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Aam ka Panna
instructions: 1. Wash and peel the mangoes. Remove the seed and cut off the pulp. 2. Boil 2 cups of water in a vessel and add mango pulp. Add black peppercorns and ginger. Cover and let it cook for 7-8 minutes. 3. Turn off the flame and let the pulp cool down. 4. Place the cooked pulp in a mixer jar along with sugar and soaked fennel seeds. Finely grind everything. 5. Strain the mixture through a sieve and discard the threads and fibers. 6. Add 5 cups of water to the strained mixture. 7. Take mint leaves and 1 cup of water in a mixer jar and churn them lightly. 8. Add this mint water to the mango mixture. 9. Add black salt, cardamom powder and roasted cumin powder. Mix everything really well. 10. Transfer to a jar and refrigerate. 11. To serve, pour mango panna into a glass, add 2-3 ice cubes, garnish with mint leaves and serve.

name: Sprouts Chilla
instructions: 1. Take moong sprouts and grind them in a mixer jar with some water to get a coarsely ground consistency. 2. Take chickpea flour in a bowl and add water to make a smooth batter. 3. Add the ground sprouts to the batter and blend together. 4. Add finely chopped spinach to the batter. 5. Crush carom seeds and add them along with asafoetida. 6. Add red chilli powder and finely chopped green chillies. 7. Add grated ginger, coriander powder and salt to taste. 8. If the batter appears too thick, add more water. 9. Preheat a non-stick pan with oil until hot. 10. Spread the batter on the pan using a spatula to your desired size (should be thicker than crepes). 11. Cover the pan and cook on medium flame for 2-3 minutes. 12. Spread oil around the edges of the chilla. 13. After 3 minutes, flip the chilla. 14. Cook the other side for another 2-3 minutes until cooked. 15. Serve hot with green coriander dip, tomato sauce or any preferred chutney.

name: Namkeen Gatta
ingredients: oil 2 tbsp plus oil for frying
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with cumin seeds, carom seeds, dry fenugreek leaves, coarsely ground coriander, turmeric powder, and red chili powder. Add finely chopped green chilies, black pepper-cloves powder, asafoetida, baking soda, salt, and oil. Knead with water into stiff dough. Rest 10 minutes. Divide into small parts and roll into logs on oiled board. Cut into gatta pieces. Heat oil to medium-hot temperature. Fry gattas for 5 minutes, then increase flame to high until golden brown. Cool completely and store in airtight container.

name: Roasted Peanuts
instructions: Mix 1/2 tsp salt with 1 tbsp water. Coat 1 cup peanuts with salty water. Heat 2 cups salt in heavy-based wok on flame, stirring every minute for 5 minutes. When salt is hot, add coated peanuts and roast for 4 minutes on medium flame with regular stirring. Turn off flame and sieve peanuts to remove salt. Cool on plate. Peel by rubbing between hands. Winnow to remove skin pieces.

name: Bhindi Masala Curry
instructions: Wash okra, remove head and tail, cut into 1-1.25 inch pieces. Heat oil and fry okra pieces until soft (6-7 minutes), then remove to plate. In same oil, roast cumin seeds, asafoetida, turmeric, coriander powder, and green chili with ginger. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until tender on medium flame, stirring regularly. Add chickpea flour and roast until oil separates. Add red chili powder and garam masala, roast, then add 1 cup water. Mix in green coriander, cover and cook on low flame 3-4 minutes. Add cream and stir until simmers. Increase flame to boil, add salt and fried okra. Cover and cook on low flame 8-10 minutes.

name: Bajra Aloo Parantha
instructions: Boil and mash potatoes. Mix millet flour with salt and knead into soft dough with water and oil. Make potato filling with mashed potatoes. Divide dough into 2-3 parts. Roll thin, add potato filling, fold and seal. Roll out gently into paratha shape. Cook on hot griddle with ghee until golden brown spots appear on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Sweet Corn Kachori
instructions: Knead flour with oil, salt, carom seeds, and water to make dough. Rest for 15 minutes. Prepare filling by mixing corn kernels with turmeric, red chili powder, and salt. Divide dough into 8 parts. Flatten each part, add corn filling in center, seal edges. Roll gently into round kachori. Heat oil to medium-high temperature. Fry kaçoris until golden brown and crispy on both sides. Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

name: Amla Candy Spicy
instructions: Boil water in vessel until steam appears. Place gooseberries in colander over boiling water, cover and cook for 8 minutes on high flame. Heat pan, add cumin seeds, carom seeds, black pepper, and asafoetida. Roast lightly for 30 seconds and cool. Grind roasted spices with black salt and ginger powder to fine powder. Cool boiled gooseberries completely. Remove seeds and cut into small pieces. Mix amla pieces with ground masala until well blended. Keep in bowl for 1 hour to absorb spices. Spread evenly on tray and dry in sunlight for 2 days or under fan. Store in airtight container for 6 months.

name: Carrot Halwa with Condensed Milk
instructions: Peel and grate 1 kg carrots. Heat 3-4 tbsp ghee in a wok and add grated carrot. Cook covered on medium-low flame, stirring every 5 minutes. Chop cashews, almonds, and crush cardamom seeds. After 10 minutes of cooking, add condensed milk and stir on medium flame. Add chopped nuts, raisins, and cardamom. Cook until fragrant. Serve warm or store in refrigerator for up to 7 days.

name: Sabudana Moong Nuggets
instructions: Soak sabudana and moong dal separately for 30 minutes. Mix soaked sabudana and moong dal with finely chopped green chilli and ginger. Season with salt. Form into nugget shapes. Deep fry in hot oil until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot.

name: Coconut Besan Barfi
instructions: Sieve gram flour. Chop cashews and slice pistachios. Peel cardamom and powder the seeds. Heat ghee and roast gram flour on medium flame, stirring constantly until dark and fragrant. Transfer to plate. Roast coconut for 1-2 minutes in same wok. Combine sugar and milk in vessel, simmer until syrup thickens to thread consistency. Mix roasted coconut, gram flour, cashews, pistachios, and cardamom powder into syrup. Pour onto greased plate and spread evenly. Sprinkle pistachios on top. Let cool and set. Cut into desired shapes and store in airtight container.

name: Amla Meethi Chutney
instructions: Wash amla and remove seeds. Cut into small pieces. Heat oil in a pan and add ginger and green chilli. Add amla pieces and cook until soft. Add jaggery and salt, stir well. Cook on low heat until it reaches desired consistency, stirring occasionally. The chutney will thicken as it cools. Store in airtight container and use as a condiment with meals.

name: Bread Pizza Pockets
instructions: Make a thin paste with refined flour and water, add salt. Heat 2 tsp oil, add ginger, then carrot, capsicum, corn. Cook for 2 minutes. Add chopped tomato, salt, oregano, tomato sauce. Cool stuffing. Cut corners of bread slices and roll flat. Mix mozzarella into cooled stuffing. Place 1-1.5 tsp stuffing on bread, seal edges with flour paste. Heat oil and coat packets with flour paste using a brush. Deep fry on medium-hot oil until golden and puffed, 3-4 minutes total. Drain oil and serve hot.

name: American Chop Suey Vegetarian
instructions: Boil water with salt and oil, add noodles and simmer 5-6 minutes until soft. Drain and cool. Mix 1-1.5 tsp corn flour into noodles. Heat oil and fry noodles in circular motion until crispy on both sides. Drain on paper towel. Leave 2 tsp oil in wok, add carrot, beans, capsicum, cabbage, and sprouted moong. Fry on high heat until crunchy. Add 1 cup water, soya sauce, chilly sauce, tomato sauce, salt and simmer. Mix corn flour with water to make batter, add to sauce. Add basil and vinegar, simmer 2-3 minutes. Serve sauce over fried noodles.

name: Macaroni Pasta Paratha
instructions: Mix cooked macaroni with finely chopped onion, ginger, and green chilli. Season with salt. Knead wheat flour with water and salt to make dough. Let rest 20 minutes. Divide into portions. Roll each into thin circle. Place macaroni mixture in center, fold and roll into paratha shape. Cook on griddle with ghee on both sides until light golden and crispy. Serve hot with pickle, yogurt, or any curry.

name: Rava Pua
instructions: Crush cardamom and make powder. Mix semolina with refined flour. Add water gradually to make dense batter. Add sugar and mix well. Rest for 20-25 minutes. Add more water if needed, whisk in cardamom powder and blend for 3-4 minutes. Heat ghee in wok on medium heat. Using a ladle, drop batter into hot ghee. Puas will puff up; flip them and fry until golden brown on both sides. This takes 4-5 minutes total. Remove with slotted ladle and let extra ghee drain back into wok.

name: Makki ki Mathri
instructions: Mix cornmeal, flour and spices including salt, carom seeds and red chilli powder. Add water to form a dough. Knead well. Roll out thin circles and cut into mathri shapes. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.

name: Idli Dhokla
instructions: Sieve chickpea flour in a bowl. Grease idli moulds with oil. Add semolina and curd to the flour along with 1/2 cup water. Whisk to form lump-free batter. Add salt, ginger paste, lemon juice, sugar and turmeric powder. Mix well and let sit for 10 minutes. Add eno fruit salt and mix gently. Pour batter into greased moulds. Place on idli stand over boiling water. Steam on medium flame for 15 minutes until a knife inserted comes out clean. Cool slightly. Prepare tempering by heating oil, spluttering mustard seeds, adding curry leaves and sauteing. Pour 1/2 cup water with salt and sugar. Remove idlis from moulds. Spread tempering over idlis. Garnish with chopped coriander and grated coconut.

name: Besan Stuffed Mathri
instructions: Mix refined flour and chickpea flour with spices including red chilli, turmeric, carom seeds, asafoetida, salt and fenugreek. Add mustard oil and refined oil. Add water gradually to form a stiff dough. Knead well. Roll out thin circles. Cut and stuff with spiced filling. Deep fry in hot oil until crispy and golden brown.

name: Peanut Coconut Chutney
instructions: Roast peanuts until golden. Grate fresh coconut. Grind peanuts, coconut and green chilli with salt to a fine paste using a food processor or grinding stone. Serve with idlis, dosas or other Indian breads.

name: Idli Upma
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Splutter mustard seeds. Add curry leaves. Add chopped onion and green chilli. Saute until soft. Break idlis into small pieces and add to the pan. Mix well. Add salt and turmeric powder. Toss and mix until the idli pieces are well coated and heated through. Serve warm.

name: Chashni Wali Gujiya
instructions: Mix refined flour with ghee and water to form a soft dough. Cover and rest. Prepare filling by mixing mawa with powdered sugar, chopped almonds, raisins, cardamom powder and pistachios. Roll out dough into thin circles. Place filling on one half, fold and seal edges into semicircle shape. Fry in hot ghee until golden and puffed. Make sugar syrup by dissolving 2 cups sugar in 1 cup water. Dip hot gujiya into the syrup for 1-2 seconds on each side. Place on a plate to cool and set.

name: Jimikand Achar
instructions: Peel and cut yams into small pieces. Dry roast spices. Mix yams with salt and spices. Sun-dry or store in oil in an airtight jar for 3-4 days.

name: Vegetable Appam
instructions: Chop tomatoes, capsicum, and ginger. Mince green chili. Mix idli batter with vegetables, salt, and coriander. Preheat appam maker and oil molds. Fill with batter. Cook 2 minutes on low flame until golden brown. Flip and cook until crispy. Serve hot with chutney.

name: Sabudana Sama Cheela
instructions: Soak samo rice and sago pearls separately for 3 hours. Grind sago pearls finely and soaked rice coarsely. Mix both pastes. Add rock salt, green chili, coriander, and cumin seeds. Heat tawa with oil. Spread 2-3 tbsp batter in circular motion. Cook on medium flame until golden brown. Flip and roast other side. Make 6-7 cheelas from this quantity.

name: Lal Masoor Dal Tadka
instructions: Heat ghee, add cumin seeds and roast. Add turmeric, coriander powder, green chili, ginger, and curry leaves. Add chopped tomato and cook until mashed. Add soaked lentils and water. Cook in pressure cooker until single whistle. Reduce flame and cook 2 minutes more. For tempering, heat ghee with cumin seeds, green chili, and curry leaves. Pour over dal and mix. Serve hot with bread or rice.

name: Sprouted Moong Cutlets
instructions: Boil sprouted moong and mash. Mix with finely chopped onion, green chili, ginger, salt, and pepper. Shape into cutlet forms. Dip in beaten egg and coat with bread crumbs. Deep fry or shallow fry until golden brown on both sides. Serve hot with green chutney.

name: Green Chickpeas Mushroom Curry
instructions: Heat oil and add cumin seeds. Sauté onion until golden. Add ginger, garlic, and green chili. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add cooked green chickpeas and sliced mushrooms. Season with turmeric, coriander powder, garam masala, and salt. Add water and simmer 10-15 minutes. Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve hot.

name: kasundi
instructions: Combine chopped raw mangoes with ginger and green chilies. Toast mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds separately. Temper mustard oil with toasted seeds and add asafoetida. Mix in mango mixture along with vinegar, spices (turmeric, red chilly, black pepper, coriander), sugar, and salt. Combine well and cook until mangoes soften.

name: idli batter sandwich toast
instructions: Preheat sandwich maker and grease the moulds with oil. Add salt to idli batter and stir well. Pour batter into moulds and spread evenly. Add cooked potato and spinach stuffing over the batter. Cover with more batter. Cook on low flame for 3-4 minutes covered. Spread oil over top and cook the other side for 3-4 minutes on low-medium flame until crispy and brown on both sides.

name: aloo vada
ingredients: green coriander 2 to 3 tbsp finely chopped
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with water to make pouring consistency batter. Add salt, red chili powder, turmeric, carom seeds. Add baking soda and let sit for 10 minutes. For stuffing, peel and crumble boiled potatoes. Heat oil, add cumin seeds, asafoetida, turmeric, coriander powder, green chili, ginger paste. Add potatoes, red chili powder, salt. Mash and roast for 2-3 minutes. Cool potato mixture. Make balls from cooled mixture. Coat with chickpea batter. Cook in appam maker on low flame for 4-5 minutes covered. Flip, add oil, cook another 3-4 minutes until brown.

name: dalia upma
ingredients: green coriander 1 to 2 tbsp finely chopped
turmeric powder less than 1/4 tsp optional
salt more than 1/2 tsp or to taste
instructions: Dry roast dalia in a pan for 2-3 minutes while stirring until fragrant and color changes. Heat oil in pressure cooker. Add black mustard seeds and roast until they crackle. Add urad dal and roast until brown. Lower flame and add curry leaves, green chili, ginger, mix well. Add chopped vegetables and roast for 1 minute. Add tomato and mix. Add roasted dalia, peanuts, turmeric, salt. Add 1.25 cup water and cook on high flame until 1 whistle. Turn off flame and let pressure release naturally. Open lid and stir gently. Cover partially and rest 5-10 minutes. Add green coriander and serve.

name: sweet tamarind chutney
instructions: Take tamarind pulp and add water. Add sugar and cook on high medium flame till sugar dissolves. Add spices: ginger powder, roasted cumin powder, red chili powder, black salt, plain salt, and garam masala. Mix well. Add finely chopped dates and raisins. Cook till dense, about 7 minutes. To check if cooked, pour drops from spatula and verify if thread forms. Cool on jali stand. Roast muskmelon seeds and add for nutty flavor. Mix and store in container for up to 6 months.

name: moong dal chilla with paneer stuffing
instructions: Soak moong dal for several hours. Grind soaked dal into smooth batter. Add finely chopped paneer, ginger, green chilies and salt to batter. Heat oil on tawa. Pour batter in circular motion and spread thin. Cook covered till bottom turns golden. Flip and cook other side till crispy. Serve hot with chutney or sauce.

name: fruit ice lollies
instructions: Grind green grapes finely, add 1 tsp honey and mix. Fill mould with mixture and insert stick. Grind black grapes finely, add 1 tsp honey and mix. Fill second mould with mixture and insert stick. Extract mango pulp, add water and 1/2 tsp honey, mix and fill mould with stick. Grind strawberries finely, add 1 tsp honey and mix. Fill mould and insert stick. Repeat process with orange juice. Place moulds in freezer for 7-8 hours to set. Dip mould in water and remove lolly from mould. Serve immediately.

name: masoor dal kebab
instructions: Soak whole masoor dal for 7-8 hours. Pressure cook dal with 1/4 cup water till first whistle, release pressure. Peel and grate boiled potatoes. Grate paneer. Grind roasted chickpeas into powder. Mix cooked dal with grated potato, paneer, mint, coriander, chilies, ginger, and all spices to form dough consistency. Shape into cutlets. Preheat oil in pan on low flame. Fry cutlets on medium-low flame till golden brown on bottom, about 5 minutes. Flip and fry other side till crispy, about 5 minutes. Serve with green coriander or tamarind chutney.

name: sooji cheela
instructions: Whisk paneer, curd and semolina in mixer till smooth. Add wheat flour and water, churn again. Transfer batter to bowl and mix in cabbage, cauliflower, capsicum, green chilly, salt, ginger and green coriander. Preheat non-stick pan or tawa. Pour oil and spread evenly with cloth. Sprinkle mustard seeds. Pour 1-2 tsp batter and spread into circular motion, keeping thick. Cover and cook on medium flame 2-3 minutes. When cheela turns brown underneath, flip and roast other side till golden brown spots appear. Stack on plate. Repeat with remaining batter. Serve hot with any Indian dip or chutney.

name: palak kadhi
instructions: Pluck spinach leaves, discard stalks, wash twice and drain completely. Dry the leaves and chop finely. Heat oil in pan, add cumin seeds and sauté. Add asafoetida, turmeric powder, ginger paste and green chilies. Sauté the masala. Add chopped spinach and 1 cup water, cover and simmer 1-2 minutes till tender. Prepare batter by whisking chickpea flour with curd till smooth. Add 3 more cups of water and mix well. Add prepared batter to spinach and stir constantly till kadhi starts simmering. Reduce flame and cook 10-12 minutes. Add red chilly powder and salt. Cook 10-12 minutes more on low flame, stirring regularly. For tempering: heat oil in small pan, add cumin seeds and red chilly powder. Turn off flame and pour over kadhi. Serve hot with chapatti, parantha, naan or rice.

name: Potato Rava Finger Fries
instructions: Boil water with oil, turn off heat and add semolina to puff it up. Mix puffed semolina with grated boiled potatoes, salt, and finely chopped green chili. Grease hands with oil, form dough into long logs. Heat oil and deep fry the logs until golden brown. Drain on paper towel.

name: Bread Paneer Pakora
instructions: Mash boiled potatoes and mix with crumbled paneer, chopped green chili, ginger-garlic paste, and spices. Stuff this mixture between two bread slices or onto bread pieces. Coat with besan batter and deep fry until golden brown.

name: Raw Banana Kofta Curry
instructions: Boil raw banana pieces in pressure cooker for 2 minutes. Peel and mash them. Mix mashed banana with chickpea flour, salt, spices and chopped green chili. Roll into balls and deep fry until golden. Make curry base by roasting spices, tomato and ginger paste. Add fried kofta balls to curry gravy and simmer for 2 minutes.

name: Kashmiri Pulao
instructions: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes. Heat ghee, add sliced onions until golden brown and remove. In same ghee, add ginger-garlic paste and spices. Add drained rice and stir well. Add water in 2:1 ratio and bring to boil. Cover and cook on low heat until rice is tender.

name: Strawberry Halwa
instructions: Roast semolina in ghee until fragrant. Add strawberry puree and stir well. Add sugar and milk gradually while stirring to avoid lumps. Cook on medium heat, stirring continuously until mixture thickens. Add cardamom powder. Spread on a plate to cool and set.

name: Spinach Cheela
instructions: Blanch and chop spinach finely. Mix chickpea flour with spinach, chopped onion, green chili, ginger, salt and turmeric. Add yogurt to make a batter. Heat oil in a griddle and pour batter to make thin pancakes. Cook until golden on both sides. Serve hot with mint chutney.

name: Soya Chunks Spinach Curry
instructions: Soak soya chunks in boiling water with salt for a while. Boil spinach with water and blend coarsely. Temper cumin seeds in oil, add onion paste and tomato paste with ginger and green chili. Add spices and fry until oil separates. Add chickpea flour paste and spinach puree. Add soaked soya chunks and cook until done. Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.

name: besan guthla curry
instructions: Take chickpea flour and add water in portions to make a dense batter. Add salt and red chili powder, mix well and let sit for 10 minutes. Heat mustard oil in a wok, add cumin seeds and reduce flame. Add asafoetida and chopped green chili. Make a paste from 2 tomatoes, 2 green chilies and ginger piece, and add to the hot oil. Add turmeric powder, coriander powder and red chili powder, then roast the spices on medium flame until oil separates. Add whisked yogurt and cook for 2-3 minutes on high flame, stirring constantly. Add 3 cups water and bring to boil. After 10-12 minutes when the batter has puffed up, slowly add it to the gravy with a spoon. Cook for 2 minutes, then add salt and garam masala. Cover and cook on low-medium flame for 2 minutes, then continue on low flame for 10-12 minutes. Add fresh green coriander and mix. Serve hot.

name: steamed sandesh
instructions: Boil 2 liters of cow's milk in a vessel. Extract juice from 4 lemons and make powder of green cardamom pods. After milk boils, switch off flame and add lemon juice in intervals, stirring well each time. Continue until milk solids separate from liquid. Spread a cotton cloth over a strainer, filter the mixture and separate solids. Wash the chena (milk solids) in water. Squeeze well to remove excess water. Add chena to a grinder jar with 1/4 cup milk and 6 tbsp powdered sugar, whisk into smooth paste. Add cardamom powder and mix well. Apply clarified butter to a container, spread the paste evenly, tap it down and place 15-20 saffron strands on top. Take a vessel, add 2-3 cups water, cover and boil until steam forms. Turn flame to low and place the container in the steaming vessel. Cover and steam for 30 minutes on low-medium flame. Remove and let cool. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to set. Remove from container by separating edges with a knife, heat the bottom for 10-12 seconds and flip onto a plate. Cut into desired pieces and serve.

name: peanut cookies
instructions: Roast peanuts and crush them into small pieces. Mix crushed peanuts with wheat flour, sugar, salt and baking powder. Add butter and mix well until a cookie dough forms. Scoop spoonfuls onto a baking tray, spacing them apart. Bake at 350°F until golden brown. Remove from oven and cool on the tray before storing.

name: moong dal with dill leaves
instructions: Soak moong dal for 30 minutes. Chop dill leaves finely. Heat ghee in a pot, add cumin seeds and let them crackle. Add a pinch of asafoetida, followed by ginger and green chili. Add turmeric powder. Add the soaked dal and 3-4 cups water. Cook on medium heat until the dal is completely soft, stirring occasionally. Add the chopped dill leaves and cook for a few more minutes. Add salt to taste and serve hot with rice or flatbread.

name: choliya halwa
instructions: Boil green chickpeas until soft. Dry roast them. Grind into fine powder. Heat ghee, add chickpea powder and roast continuously. Add sugar and milk gradually, stirring to avoid lumps. Cook until mixture thickens and leaves the pan. Spread on greased surface and set. Cut into pieces.

name: anarsa goli
instructions: Mix refined flour with ghee and salt. Add water and knead stiff dough. Prepare filling with jaggery, sesame seeds, poppy seeds, and spices. Roll dough thin, fill with mixture, shape into balls. Deep fry in ghee until golden and crispy on both sides.

name: vegetable makhani
instructions: Chop all vegetables into bite-sized pieces. Heat oil and butter in a pan, add cumin seeds and whole spices. Add green chillies and ginger, saute briefly. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add vegetables and saute. Add powder spices, salt and cook until vegetables are tender. Stir in cream and green coriander. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until well combined.

name: aliv ladoo
instructions: Roast aliv seeds until fragrant. Dry roast grated coconut. Mix with jaggery powder. Heat ghee, add aliv seeds and other ingredients. Stir continuously until well combined. Cool slightly. Shape into small ladoos (balls) with greased hands.

name: Lobia and Potato Masala
instructions: Soak black-eyed beans overnight. Heat oil and add cumin seeds. Sauté onions, garlic and ginger. Add tomatoes and cook until soft. Add soaked beans and potatoes. Season with turmeric, coriander, and salt. Cook until beans and potatoes are tender. Finish with cilantro.

name: Chikoo Kulfi
instructions: Puree ripe chikoo fruits. Mix with condensed milk, evaporated milk and cream. Add cardamom powder. Pour into kulfi molds. Freeze for 8-12 hours. Dip in warm water and push out to serve.

name: Cheese Naan
instructions: Mix flour with yogurt, sugar, baking soda and salt. Knead with ghee and oil. Let dough rest. Roll out portions into discs. Add shredded cheese and chopped coriander in center. Fold and seal. Cook on tawa over medium-high heat until golden spots appear on both sides. Serve hot with ghee.

name: Lauki Paratha
instructions: Grate bottle gourd and squeeze excess water. Mix with chopped onions, green chilies, ginger and spices. Knead whole wheat flour with water and salt. Roll out and spread gourd mixture. Roll up and coil. Flatten and cook on tawa with ghee until golden and crispy on both sides.

name: Til Besan Ki Barfi
instructions: Dry roast sesame seeds until color changes and cool. Grind into powder. Melt ghee and add chickpea flour. Roast on medium flame until golden and fragrant. Add crumbled mawa and cook for 10 minutes stirring constantly. Add powdered sugar and mix well. Add ground sesame seeds and cardamom powder on low heat. Stir and roast well. Grease tray with ghee and spread mixture evenly. Garnish with almond flakes. Set for 1 hour and cut into pieces.

name: Cholia Pulao
instructions: Heat ghee and add cumin seeds. Sauté minced onions until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste. Add soaked rice and green chickpeas. Roast briefly. Add water and spices (bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon, turmeric). Bring to boil and cover. Cook on low heat until rice is tender and water is absorbed. Garnish with cilantro.

name: Cornmeal Halwa
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add cornmeal and roast on medium heat, stirring continuously until golden and aromatic. Add sugar and water, stirring to combine. Continue cooking and stirring until halwa reaches desired consistency and leaves the sides of the pan. Serve warm.

name: Bhavnagari Ganthiya
instructions: Heat oil and turn off flame. Mix salt and baking soda in hot oil. Pour into besan in a bowl. Add carom seeds, asafoetida, and black pepper. Mix well. Add water gradually to knead soft dough. Heat oil for frying. Use gathiya mold in machine, press dough through mold into hot oil. Fry until golden. Drain on paper. Once cooled, store in airtight container.

name: Bread Mawa Roll
instructions: Prepare sugar syrup from sugar and water. Remove bread crusts and flatten slices. Make filling with mawa, sugar powder, coconut, nuts, and cardamom. Dip bread in milk, place filling inside, roll tightly. Fry in ghee until golden. Soak in warm sugar syrup. Garnish with nuts.

name: Crispy French Fries
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into fries. Soak in water. Boil salted water, add fries, simmer 5 minutes. Drain and pat dry. Freeze for 1 hour. Heat oil, fry fries until light brown, drain and cool 15-20 minutes. Fry again in hot oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper. Sprinkle chaat masala and serve with ketchup.

name: Spicy Amla Chutney
instructions: Cut amla and remove seeds. Chop coriander leaves coarsely. Place amla chunks and coriander in mixer. Add halved green chilies, salt, cumin seeds, asafoetida, peppercorns, and water. Grind to paste consistency. Serve with samosa, pakoras or kachoris. Store in refrigerator for 6-7 days.

name: Eggless Orange Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 350F. Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. In another bowl, combine oil, milk, orange juice, orange zest, and vanilla. Mix wet and dry ingredients until smooth. Pour into greased pan. Bake 30-35 minutes until golden. Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out to cool completely.

name: Moong Dal with Dalia
instructions: Heat ghee in pressure cooker, add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Add turmeric and coriander powder. Add green chilies and roast. Add chopped tomato and red chili powder, roast until mashed. Add moong dal and salt, stir and roast 1 minute. Add water, close lid, cook until 1 whistle. In another cooker, heat ghee, roast wheat porridge, add water, cook until 1 whistle. Mix cooked dal with water, add green coriander, boil. Serve with ghee and ginger julienne.

name: Rice Chakli
instructions: Boil water with oil and spices. Turn off flame. Add spice mixture to rice flour. Mix well and let sit 20 minutes. Knead into stiff, tight dough with hands. Pinch portions and roll. Load into chakli machine with mold attached. Press dough onto polythene sheet in circular motion to form chaklis. Heat oil and fry chaklis until golden brown. Drain on paper towels. Cool completely and store in airtight container for up to 2 months.

name: Fried Idli
instructions: Slice leftover idlis into finger-like pieces or leave whole. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on all sides, about 3-5 minutes. Drain on paper towels and serve hot with sambar or chutney.

name: Atta Namakpara
instructions: Mix wheat flour, chickpea flour, salt, carom seeds, and fenugreek leaves. Add ghee and knead into a stiff dough. Roll out thin and cut into diamond or rectangular pieces. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.

name: Veg Pitor Tikka
instructions: Make a smooth chickpea flour paste with water. Add salt, cumin seeds, red chili powder, coriander powder, ginger paste, green chilies, green coriander, capsicum, cauliflower, and tomato. Heat pan with oil and add the batter. Cook on high flame for 5 minutes, stirring continuously, then reduce to medium and cook for 5 more minutes until thick. Spread on a plate to set for 10 minutes. Cut into pieces, heat non-stick pan with oil, and pan fry pieces on medium flame until golden brown on both sides.

name: Gulab Nariyal Modak
instructions: Boil water with 2 tsp ghee and salt. Reduce flame and add rice flour, mix well, turn off flame and cover for 5 minutes. For filling: heat 1 tsp ghee, add crumbled jaggery, cook until melted, add grated coconut and cook on low flame. Add chopped nuts, cardamom powder, and raisins. When dough cools, knead with ghee for 6-7 minutes. Shape into lemon-sized lumps, create a bowl shape with thumb and fingers, stuff with filling, make pleats around edges and form a pointed top. Steam in a greased colander for 12 minutes on high flame. Cool and serve.

name: Besan Gujhiya
instructions: Make dough with wheat flour, ghee, salt, and water. Prepare filling with roasted besan, powdered jaggery or sugar, dry fruits, and cardamom powder. Roll dough into thin circles, place filling on one half, fold and seal edges with water, shape into semicircle. Deep fry in hot oil until golden. Serve warm.

name: Urad Dal Khasta Kachori
instructions: Mix wheat flour with oil and salt, knead into stiff dough with water. For filling: mix soaked urad dal with cumin seeds, asafoetida, ginger paste, green chili, coriander powder, fennel powder, red chili powder, garam masala, dry mango powder, carom seeds, and salt. Roll dough balls into thin circles, place filling in center, fold edges and seal completely, shape into oval. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy, about 5-6 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels.

name: Aloo Palak Paratha
instructions: Knead wheat flour with 2 tsp oil and salt into smooth dough with about 3/4 cup water. Rest for 20 minutes. Wash and chop spinach finely. Boil and peel potatoes. Dry roast chickpea flour until golden. Heat pan with 2 tsp oil, add cumin seeds, carom seeds, asafoetida, turmeric, ginger paste, and green chilies. Add chopped spinach and cook. Crumble and add boiled potatoes, add salt, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Mix in roasted chickpea flour. Heat tawa, roll dough balls into thin circles, place spinach-potato filling, cover edges, press lightly, roll out to 6-7 inches. Roast on tawa with oil until brown spots appear on both sides, pressing edges gently. Makes 6-8 parathas.

name: Dahi Gujia
instructions: Soak and blend moong dal to make a smooth batter. Mix with spices and baking soda. Drop spoonfuls into oil and fry until golden and puffed. Prepare yogurt sauce with spices. Dip fried dumplings in yogurt. Serve chilled or warm.

name: Sweet Corn Kheer
instructions: Add sweet corn to milk and bring to boil. Simmer for 10 minutes. Add condensed milk and sugar. Stir well and cook for 5 more minutes. Roast dry fruits in ghee and add to the kheer. Crush cardamom pods and sprinkle. Serve warm or chilled.

name: Basil Sorbet
instructions: Crush fresh basil leaves lightly. Add to water and bring to boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Strain and cool. Add fresh lemon juice and zest. Dissolve sugar in the liquid. Add salt. Chill and serve cold with ice.

name: Atta Kachori
instructions: For dough: Mix wheat flour and semolina. Add salt and ghee. Add water gradually and knead soft dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes. For stuffing: Grate boiled potatoes. Heat oil and add fennel seeds. Add potatoes and spices (turmeric, salt, coriander powder, mango powder, garam masala, chilis). Roast for 2-3 minutes. Add green coriander. For kachori: Apply ghee on palms and divide dough into lumps. Roll each lump, hollow with thumb and fingers. Fill with potato stuffing and seal. Fry in low-medium heated oil, first without stirring, then fold to cook evenly until golden brown.

name: Steamed Moong Dal Vadi
instructions: Soak moong dal for 2-3 hours. Drain and grind into a batter. Add salt and baking soda. Steam the batter in a greased pan for 15-20 minutes until cooked. Cool and cut into pieces. For sabzi: Heat oil and add ginger and green chili. Add mixed vegetables and cook until soft. Add turmeric and red chili powder. Add steamed moong dal pieces and mix. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Serve hot.

name: Sattu powder and sattu drink
instructions: Roast chana, barley, and wheat daliya separately. Grind all roasted ingredients to make powder. Mix with sugar powder and black salt. To make drink: dissolve sattu powder in water, add lemon juice, chopped green chilli, mint leaves, and salt to taste.

name: Besan stuffed karela
instructions: Clean bitter gourds and remove stalk. Peel and slit down the center keeping it joined at back. Remove seeds and pith. Salt gourds and rest for 30 minutes then wash. Prepare stuffing by roasting besan with cumin seeds and asafoetida, then add gourds scraps and all spices. Stuff the prepared gourds. Fry in preheated mustard oil at low flame with lid until brown on all sides, checking every 3-4 minutes.

name: Palak kachori
instructions: Knead refined flour with spinach puree, oil, and water to make smooth dough. Cover and rest 15 minutes. Prepare peas stuffing by grinding peas and mixing with cumin seeds, asafoetida, ginger paste, chopped green chilli, spices (red chilli powder, dry mango powder, coriander powder, garam masala), and salt. Fill kachori with peas mixture. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy from all sides.

name: Baked gujiya
instructions: Grease baking tray with ghee. Mix 2 tsp milk with condensed milk. Knead refined flour with melted ghee and warm milk portions to make stiff dough. Cover and rest 15-20 minutes. Microwave mawa for 1 minute to roast. Mix mawa with ground green cardamom powder, chopped cashews, raisins, chironji, and powdered sugar. Roll dough portions into 3.5-4 inch diameter pouris and place on gujiya mold. Fill with 2 tsp mawa mixture, close mold, and separate excess dough. Transfer to greased tray. Bake at 200°C in convection mode for 10 minutes. Apply milk and condensed milk mixture with brush on both sides. Bake again for 8 minutes at 200°C until golden brown. Cool before storing in airtight container.

name: Sweet milk dinner rolls
instructions: Mix refined flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in bowl. Heat milk and add butter to make warm. Add warm milk to flour mixture and knead into soft dough. Cover and let rise until doubled (1-2 hours). Punch down dough and shape into 8 equal rolls. Place on greased baking tray. Cover and let rise again until puffy. Bake at 190°C for 15-20 minutes until golden brown.

name: Lasoda Sabzi
instructions: Wash and remove stalks from lasoda. Boil lasoda in 2-2.5 cups water for 6-7 minutes until tender. Drain and cool. Remove cap and seeds, chop into 4-5 pieces. Heat oil in pan, splutter cumin and carom seeds. Add asafoetida, fennel, coriander and turmeric powders along with lasoda. Add salt, red chilly powder and mango powder. Mix well until each piece is coated with spices. Serve hot with pooris or paranthas.

name: Soya Sag Aloo
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into small cubes. Wash and chop dill leaves. Heat oil in pan, add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Add potatoes and cook till half done. Add dill leaves, turmeric, coriander and red chilli powder. Mix well and cook till potatoes are tender. Adjust salt to taste.

name: Gur Mewa Gujiya
instructions: Mix maida and salt, add ghee and make soft dough. Knead well and keep for 30 minutes. Crumble dry fruits and mix with powdered jaggery and khoya. Add cardamom powder to filling. Roll dough thin, place filling on half, fold and seal edges with fork to create semi-circle gujiya shape. Deep fry in oil till golden brown on both sides. Remove and cool on paper towel.

name: Ginger Candy
instructions: Peel and slice ginger thinly. Boil ginger in water in pressure cooker with lid for one whistle, then reduce to low flame and cook. Drain cooled ginger on sieve. In separate vessel, dissolve sugar in water over high flame. Add ginger slices to sugar syrup and cook on high flame until syrup becomes dense. Turn off flame, add cardamom powder and mix well. Spread on jali stand and let sit 10-12 hours or overnight. Next day, gently heat over flame until syrup melts, turn off and cool on jali stand. Take out candies one by one and place on net to dry for several hours. Store in airtight container.

name: Eggless Mango Muffins
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. In another bowl, combine mango puree, yogurt, sugar, oil and vanilla extract. Combine wet and dry ingredients. Pour batter into greased muffin tins. Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.

name: Traditional Thandai
instructions: Soak almonds, remove skin. Grind almonds, aniseeds, black pepper, khaskhas, muskmelon seeds and cardamom into fine paste. Make sugar syrup with water. Mix spice paste with syrup. Add rose water. Chill and serve with ice.

name: Whole Wheat Sweet Biscuits
instructions: Cream butter and sugar. Add milk gradually. Mix flour, baking powder, salt and crushed cardamom. Combine wet and dry ingredients. Knead into dough. Roll out and cut shapes. Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes.

name: Chana Sundal
instructions: Soak and boil chickpeas until soft. Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, cumin seeds, urad dal, green chili and asafoetida. Add curry leaves. Add boiled chickpeas and cook 1-2 minutes. Add grated coconut and mix well. Serve warm.

name: Singhara Achar
instructions: Cut water chestnuts into pieces. Heat mustard oil until smoking. Add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds for tempering. Add ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder and turmeric. Add water chestnuts and salt. Cook and cool. Store in glass jar for 3-4 days before consuming.

name: Steamed Maida Papad
instructions: Mix refined flour with water in small portions to form smooth batter without lumps. Add cumin seeds and salt. Keep batter aside for 10-15 minutes. Grease small plates with oil. Spread batter evenly on greased plates. Steam over boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Cool and remove from plate. Dry for 2-3 days. Fry in hot oil until puffed. Sprinkle chaat masala.

name: Cheese Paratha
instructions: Mix wheat flour with curd, oil, baking soda, sugar and salt. Knead into soft dough. Mix grated vegetables, cheese, green coriander and green chili. Divide dough into portions. Roll out, add vegetable-cheese mixture, fold and seal. Roll again gently. Cook on hot griddle with oil until golden on both sides.

name: Til Sweet Mathri
instructions: Dry roast sesame seeds lightly. Mix flour with baking powder and salt. Cream ghee and sugar. Add roasted sesame seeds and crushed cardamom. Combine with flour and milk to form dough. Knead well. Roll out thin. Cut into diamond shapes. Deep fry in ghee until golden. Drain on paper towel.

name: Crispy Jalebi
ingredients: red food color less than 1/2 pinch
ghee or refined oil for frying
instructions: Soak urad dal for 2 hours, drain and grind to fine paste. Mix refined flour with baking powder and red food color. Add water in portions and stir to dissolve lumps. Mix in ground dal to make smooth batter, consistency neither too thick nor thin. For syrup: dissolve sugar in 1.5 cup water, simmer 4-5 minutes until one thread consistency forms. Add lemon juice and ground cardamom powder to syrup. Heat ghee in wok until medium hot. Fill batter in cone or sauce bottle, make circular motions to pipe jalebis into oil. Fry until crispy and golden brown. Immediately dip into warm syrup for 1-2 minutes until well soaked. Remove and place on plate.

name: Dhaba Style Urad Dal Tadka
instructions: Rinse and soak urad dal for 30 minutes. Pressure cook with 3 cups water for 3 whistles until soft. Heat oil in tadka pan, splutter cumin seeds. Add dried red chillies and asafoetida. Add minced ginger and saute briefly. Pour this tadka over cooked dal. Add salt to taste and stir well. Garnish with chopped green coriander. Serve hot.

name: Steamed Idli Cake
instructions: Coarsely grind 6 green cardamom and make powder. Take 1 cup semolina in mixing bowl, add 1 cup milk and stir well until blended. Add 2 tbsp ghee and 1/2 cup sugar, mix well. Keep batter aside for 15-20 minutes. After 20 minutes stir batter well, add cardamom powder and 3/4 tsp baking powder and mix. Pour 2 cups water in vessel, cover and bring to boil. Grease idli molds, pour batter in small quantities and arrange diagonally on idli stand. Place stand in boiling water vessel on high flame. After 12 minutes, poke with knife to check doneness. Let cool slightly before removing from molds.

name: Rice Flour Laddu
instructions: Dry roast rice flour in ghee over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until light golden and fragrant. Remove from heat and let cool slightly. Add powdered sugar and cardamom powder, mix well. Once cooled enough to handle, roll into balls of equal size. Place on a plate and let set for 30 minutes.

name: Naan Khatai
ingredients: ghee or vegetable oil 1/2 cup (125 grams)
instructions: Grind green cardamom pods to make powder. Mix gram flour with powdered sugar and baking powder. Add ghee or oil gradually and mix until breadcrumb consistency forms. Knead lightly into dough. Roll small balls and flatten slightly on cooking surface. Top each with a pistachio piece. Heat a flat pan or griddle on low heat. Place naan khatai on pan and cook on low flame for 3-4 minutes per side until light golden and cooked through. Remove and cool on wire rack.

name: Sweet Corn Paratha
instructions: Mix wheat flour with boiled corn, salt and spices. Make soft dough. Roll into paratha and cook on griddle with ghee until golden brown on both sides.

name: Yellow Pumpkin Halwa
instructions: Boil milk until thick. Grate and roast pumpkin in ghee. Cook until soft. Add thickened milk and sugar. Stir continuously. Add cardamom powder and nuts. Serve warm.

name: Aloo Ka Bharta
instructions: Boil and peel potatoes. Mash them. Temper with oil, mustard seeds, onion and garlic. Mix in spices and green chili. Cook until well combined.

name: Cheese Kachori
instructions: Make dough with flour and salt. Prepare filling with grated cheese, spices and onion. Stuff dough balls with filling. Deep fry until golden brown and crispy.

name: Zucchini Stir Fry
instructions: Slice zucchini. Temper oil with cumin seeds. Add onion and garlic. Stir fry zucchini with spices until cooked and tender. Garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Peanut & Poha Pakoda
instructions: Soak and drain poha. Mix with besan, crushed peanuts and spices. Make batter consistency. Deep fry spoonfuls until golden brown and crispy.

name: Steamed Poha
instructions: Soak and drain poha. Mix with sugar, salt, turmeric and lemon juice. Steam in colander over boiling water for 10 minutes. Temper with oil, mustard seeds, curry leaves and chili. Mix and serve with peanuts and namkeen sev garnish.

name: Palak Soya Bhurji
ingredients: red chilly powder less than 1/4 tsp
instructions: Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds, asafoetida, and finely chopped green chili and ginger paste. Stir briefly. Add soy chunks and cook for 1 minute. Add chopped spinach and tomatoes. Season with turmeric powder, coriander powder, salt, garam masala and red chilly powder. Stir well and cook until spinach is tender. Add kasuri methi and mix. Cook for another 1-2 minutes and serve hot with roti or rice.

name: Til ki Chutney
instructions: Dry roast sesame seeds lightly on a hot pan until fragrant. Grind roasted sesame seeds with fresh green chili and salt to a smooth paste. Adjust seasoning to taste. Serve as accompaniment with bread, rice or rotli.

name: Hing Jeere ke Aloo
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into thin slices or small cubes. Heat oil in a pan on high heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add asafoetida. Add cut potatoes and mix well. Sprinkle turmeric and salt. Fry over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are golden brown and crispy at edges, about 15-20 minutes. Adjust seasoning. Serve hot as a side dish.

name: Honey Oat Cookies
instructions: Cream butter and honey together. In another bowl, mix flour, oats, baking soda and salt. Combine wet and dry ingredients to form a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls onto a greased baking tray. Flatten slightly. Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until edges turn light brown. Cool on baking tray for 2 minutes before transferring to wire rack. Store in an airtight container.

name: Cashew Pistachio Cookies
instructions: Chop cashews and pistachios finely. Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add vanilla extract. In a separate bowl, mix flour, baking soda and salt. Combine wet and dry ingredients. Fold in chopped nuts. Drop spoonfuls onto greased baking tray. Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until golden. Cool on tray for 2 minutes then transfer to wire rack.

name: Caramel Kheer
instructions: Boil 1 litre of milk in a heavy-bottomed vessel on high flame, stirring occasionally. Chop 10-12 cashews finely. Peel and powder 4 green cardamoms. Add soaked rice to boiling milk and stir well. Cook on high to medium heat until rice melts and mixture thickens, approximately 30 minutes, stirring frequently. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan, add chopped cashews and roast until color changes to light brown. Similarly roast 1-2 tbsp raisins in the same ghee. In a separate pan, add 1/2 cup sugar and cook on medium-high flame. Stir continuously until sugar dissolves completely. Continue cooking while stirring furiously until sugar turns brown and caramelizes. Add 2 tbsp water carefully (mixture will bubble). Switch on flame if heat is off. Add caramelized sugar to the cooked kheer and stir well. Add roasted dry fruits and cardamom powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes more. Transfer to serving bowl and garnish with chopped pistachios. Serve hot or chilled as desired.

name: Sooji Dry Fruits Gujhiya
instructions: Dry roast dry fruits. Mix with mawa. Prepare dough with sooji, ghee, and water. Fill with mawa mixture. Shape into gujhiya. Deep fry in ghee until golden brown. Dip in sugar syrup and let cool.

name: Fruit Falooda
instructions: Soak sabja seeds. Make arrowroot sev in chilled water. Prepare kulfi. In a glass, add fruit pulp, sabja seeds, cold milk, falooda sev, rose syrup, kulfi pieces and garnish with dry fruits.

name: Kundru Chutney
instructions: Wash and chop kundru. Dry roast cumin seeds. Sauté kundru with cumin and green chili. Grind to desired consistency. Serve as condiment.

name: Mixed Vegetable Raita
instructions: Grate or finely chop mixed vegetables. Mix with yogurt. Add roasted cumin powder, chili powder, salt and fresh coriander. Chill before serving.

name: Samo Rice Dosa
instructions: Grind soaked samo rice with water. Mix water chestnut flour with samo rice paste and water to make batter. Prepare coconut-curd chutney with tempering. Heat tawa, spread ghee, pour batter and spread in circular motion. Drizzle ghee on edges. Cook until golden brown on both sides.

name: Aloo Bonda
instructions: Boil and peel potatoes. Roast cumin seeds, add green chili and ginger. Mash potatoes with spices and coriander. Form into balls. Prepare water chestnut flour batter with salt and pepper. Coat potato balls in batter. Deep fry in oil until golden brown, or cook in appam maker with minimal oil on low flame.

name: soya stick namkeen
ingredients: salt less than 1 tsp or to taste
instructions: Mix soya bean flour and chickpea flour with red chili powder, black pepper, turmeric, carom seeds, cumin seeds, coriander powder, salt, baking soda and oil. Add water in small portions and make soft dough, cover for 15-20 minutes. Grease hands with oil, smooth dough and heat oil. Using sev machine with star jali, press dough to make straight sticks, cut into 2-3 inch pieces. Fry on medium flame until golden brown. Store in airtight container for 2-3 months.

name: palak mangodi
instructions: Cook mangodi in water until soft. In a pan, heat oil and add garlic, sauté briefly. Add chopped onion and ginger, cook until golden. Add spinach and mangodi, add turmeric powder, red chili powder and salt. Cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until spinach is tender and well-mixed.

name: instant dahi vada with rawa
instructions: Mix semolina and curd together. Add finely chopped ginger, green chili, salt and baking soda. Mix well. Heat oil in deep pan. Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil and fry until golden brown on both sides. Remove and place on paper towels to cool.

name: lemon rasam
instructions: Heat oil, add cumin seeds and peppercorns, let them crackle. Add curry leaves and asafoetida. Add chopped tomatoes and turmeric powder, cook until tomatoes soften. Add water and bring to boil. Simmer for 5-7 minutes. Add lemon juice and salt to taste. Strain if desired or serve as is. Serve hot as soup or with steamed rice.

name: Moong Burger
instructions: Heat butter and oil in a nonstick pan, add garlic, celery, green chilli and sauté. Add onions and sauté till translucent. Add salt, boiled moong and mix, mash with a masher. Add parsley, breadcrumbs, lemon juice, sugar and mix. Divide into 4 portions and shape into patties. Heat oil in shallow nonstick pan, shallow fry patties on both sides for 2 minutes on medium heat, drain on paper. Mix tomato ketchup with hung yogurt. Apply spread on burger buns, place lettuce, patty, cheese slice, onion and tomato slices, sprinkle salt and mustard sauce. Close with other half of bun. Serve with ketchup and chips.

name: Pecan and Red Quinoa Salad
instructions: Heat nonstick pan, add black grapes and brown sugar, mix and cook for 1 minute. Mash mixture, add salt and cook till pulpy and slightly reduced. Cool in a bowl. Mix cooked red quinoa, edamame, corn kernels, cherry tomatoes, pecans, and torn lollo rosso lettuce in a bowl. Add crushed peppercorns, malt vinegar and oil to the dressing and mix well. Place salad on serving platter, add feta cheese and drizzle dressing on top. Serve immediately.

name: Moong Masoor ki Dal
ingredients: split green gram with skin 1 cup soaked
split red lentils masoor dal 1 cup soaked
instructions: Put drained green gram and red lentils in deep nonstick pan, add 3.5-4 cups water, salt, turmeric powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder and dried mango powder, mix well. Cover and cook till lentils are done. In another nonstick pan, heat oil, add asafoetida and garlic, sauté till garlic is burnt. Add round red chillies and onion, sauté for half a minute. Add green chilli and remaining red chilli powder, mix well. Add tomato and mix. Add this mixture to cooked dal and mix well. Cook for a minute. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with coriander sprig and serve hot.

name: Moong Avocado Chaat
ingredients: medium sweet potato 1 boiled and peeled
instructions: Boil sufficient water in deep nonstick pan. Add turmeric powder and salt and mix well. Add sprouted green gram and blanch for 4-5 minutes. Drain water and allow to cool. Cut sweet potato into 1 cm pieces. Deseed avocado, scoop out pulp and cut into 1 cm pieces. Transfer blanched sprouted green gram in a bowl. Add avocado, sweet potato, onion, tomato, lemon juice, salt, roasted peanuts, chana jor garam and coriander leaves and mix well. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with coriander sprig and serve.

name: Paneer Payasam
instructions: Transfer reduced milk in deep nonstick pan. Add saffron and mix well. Grate fresh paneer. Once milk comes to gentle boil, add grated paneer and mix well. Add castor sugar and mix well. Cook for a minute more. Add green cardamom powder, cashew nuts and raisins and mix well. Transfer to serving bowls, garnish with saffron strands and serve.

name: Dahi Tikki
instructions: Mix hung curd with chopped green chilli, coriander leaves, salt and black pepper. Divide into equal portions and shape into round patties. Coat each patty with crushed cornflakes to create a crispy exterior. Deep fry in hot oil on medium heat until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Drain on absorbent paper and serve hot.

name: Muesli with Chia Seeds
ingredients: dried berries cranberries raspberries strawberries (3-4 tbsp)
instructions: Soak chia seeds in yogurt overnight. Soak oats in apple juice for 15 minutes. In a bowl, combine soaked chia seeds with yogurt and honey and mix well. Add soaked oats with apple juice and mix. Fold in dried berries. Divide mixture into shot glasses, layering with berries, walnuts, almonds and yogurt mixture. Garnish with pistachios and serve.

name: Vanilla Sponge Cake
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C. Grease a 6 inch round cake tin with butter and dust with flour. Cut butter into pieces and add castor sugar in a bowl. In another bowl, beat eggs with vanilla essence until light and fluffy ribbon consistency forms. Cream butter-sugar mixture until light and fluffy. Sift flour and baking powder into butter mixture, add half the egg mixture and fold gently. Add remaining eggs and fold gently. Add milk and mix until smooth batter forms. Transfer to greased tin, spread evenly, and bake 30-35 minutes until golden. Cool slightly, loosen sides with knife, de-mould and cool completely on cooling rack. Cut into wedges and serve.

name: Sesame Dal
ingredients: split bengal gram chana dal (1/4 cup) soaked
split skinless black gram dhuli urad dal (2 tbsp) soaked
split pigeon pea toor dal (1/4 cup) soaked
split skinless green gram dhuli moong dal (2 tbsp) soaked
split green gram with skin chilkewali moong dal (1/4 cup) soaked
instructions: Put all soaked lentils, salt, turmeric powder and 2.5 cups water in pressure cooker. Cook under pressure for 3 whistles, then reduce heat and cook for 15 minutes. Dice tomato. Heat oil in non-stick pan, add white and black sesame seeds and cumin seeds, sauté until they splutter. Add chopped onions and sauté until well browned. Add diced tomato and sauté for 1 minute. Add red chilli powder and mix well, sauté until tomato becomes pulpy. Add tempering to cooked dal and mix well. Transfer to serving bowl and serve hot with rice, roti or parantha sprinkled with sesame seeds.

name: Moong Toast
ingredients: whole green gram sabut moong soaked boiled (1 cup)
medium onion cut into thin roundels (1)
instructions: Chop onion finely and combine with boiled green gram in a bowl. Crush boiled potatoes and add to mixture. Add salt, chaat masala and pav bhaji masala, mix well mashing slightly. Apply coriander-mint chutney on all bread slices. Spread gram mixture generously on 4 slices and cover with remaining slices to make sandwiches. Apply butter on outer sides of sandwiches. Grease sandwich toaster with butter, place sandwich in it, close and cook on medium heat, turning sides until both sides are golden brown. Cut into 2 triangles, arrange on serving plate, garnish with onion rings and serve hot.

name: Black Rice Kheer
ingredients: black rice washed soaked overnight (2-3 tbsp)
instructions: Take soaked black rice in blender jar, add 3/4 cup water and crush lightly. Heat a non-stick pan, add crushed rice and almond milk and cook on medium heat for 20-25 minutes stirring at regular intervals until mixture thickens. Add green cardamom powder and mix well. Add Sugar Free Green sweetener and mix. Add raisins and mix well. Transfer prepared kheer to individual bowls, garnish with pistachio slivers and serve warm or chilled.

name: Green Moong Tikki
instructions: Heat water in steamer, place steamer basket and arrange raw bananas on it. Place another basket over it with green moong sprouts. Cover and steam for 20-25 minutes. Switch off heat. Peel steamed bananas and place on plate. Add steamed moong sprouts and mash well with masher. Add red chilli powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, dried mango powder, salt and coriander leaves, mix until well combined. Take small portion of mixture, shape into ball and flatten to thin disc. Mix bread crumbs with white sesame seeds, black sesame seeds, salt and crushed peppercorns. Dip each tikki into corn flour slurry, place on bread crumb mixture and coat well on both sides. Heat oil in kadai, gently slide in tikkis a few at a time and deep fry until golden brown and crisp. Drain on absorbent paper. Serve hot with green chutney, onion rings and mint sprigs.

name: pecan and pear salsa
instructions: Deseed and chop pear. Chop pecans. Transfer both to a bowl. Squeeze lemon juice. Add salt, crushed black peppercorns, green chillies, sugar, and coriander. Mix well and mash lightly. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with coriander sprig and pecans. Serve with baked nachos.

name: spinach gnocchi with tomatoes
instructions: Boil 2 cups water in a deep pan. Mash potatoes. Finely chop spinach and add to potatoes with peppercorns, salt, garlic, and flour. Knead into soft dough. Divide into 7-8 portions and shape into balls. Cook in boiling water until done, then drain. For sauce, heat olive oil, sauté garlic until browned, add tomato puree and seasonings, cook until thickened. In another pan, sauté gnocchi until lightly browned. Plate sauce, top with gnocchi, garnish with basil leaves.

name: konkani chicken and raw mango curry
ingredients: 750 gms chicken, cut into 2 inch pieces on bone
instructions: Marinate chicken with salt and turmeric powder. Heat coconut oil, sauté coconut, red chillies, rice, and half the onion with half the masala. Blend into fine paste. Sauté remaining onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste. Add remaining turmeric, chilli powder and mix. Cut raw mango into pieces. Add chicken to pan, mix and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Add remaining masala, then prepared paste and 1 cup water. Add raw mango pieces and tamarind pulp. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes. Add kokum petals. Garnish with coriander and serve with red rice.

name: phodshi chana dal bhaji
ingredients: 1/2 cup cooked split bengal gram (chana dal)
instructions: Discard white stem parts and chop phodshi leaves. Soak leaves in salted water for 10-15 minutes. Crush garlic and green chillies in mortar. Heat oil and sauté crushed garlic-chilli until garlic turns golden. Add onions and salt, sauté until golden. Add chana dal and mix. Add turmeric and red chilli powder. Add soaked phodshi, cover and add water. Cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes. Add scraped coconut and mix. Transfer to serving bowl, sprinkle more coconut on top, serve hot with bhakri.

name: fish head curry
ingredients: 4 tbsps mustard oil + for deep frying
1/2 cup short grain rice, soaked and drained
instructions: Place fish heads in bowl with salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric. Let sit 10-15 minutes. Heat mustard oil in kadai and deep fry fish heads until golden and crisp. Drain on absorbent paper. Heat 4 tbsps mustard oil in deep pan. Add green chillies, bay leaves, and onion. Sauté until onions turn light golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and mix. Add turmeric, red chilli and cumin powder. Add soaked rice and mix. Add fried fish heads and mix until combined. Add 3 cups water and garam masala powder. Cover and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes. Transfer to serving bowl and serve hot.

name: coconut chickpea rice
ingredients: 1.5 cups basmati rice, washed and soaked
instructions: Heat coconut oil in deep pan and gently sauté soaked rice for 2-3 minutes on low heat. Add coconut milk, salt and bring to boil. Cover and cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes. For chickpea mixture, heat coconut oil in another pan. Add garlic and sauté on high heat for 1 minute. Add onion and salt, cook until translucent. Add broccoli and sauté 1-2 minutes, add water and cover for 2 minutes. Add chickpeas and mix. Add garam masala, red chilli, turmeric and cumin powder. Mix until combined. Add coconut and coriander leaves. Transfer rice to serving bowl, top with chickpea mixture, garnish with coconut.

name: Protein Cheela
instructions: 1. Mix chickpea flour, carrot, sweet corn, paneer, coriander, green chillies, salt, black peppercorns, sesame seeds and yogurt in a bowl. Add 3/4 cup water gradually to form lump-free batter. 2. Heat non-stick pan on medium heat, drizzle oil, pour ladleful of batter and spread lightly. Cook 1-2 minutes, drizzle oil, cook 1-2 minutes more. 3. Flip and cook other side 2-3 minutes until golden brown.

name: Oat Milk Pancakes
instructions: 1. Mix powdered oats, rolled oats, baking soda and oat milk into a batter. 2. Add sugar free green and vanilla extract, mix well. 3. Squeeze lemon and mix. 4. Heat non-stick pan, add few drops oil, pour spoonful of batter, cook on low heat until underside golden. 5. Flip and cook other side until done. 6. Plate with strawberry puree, pancake, more puree, blueberries. Stack another pancake with puree. 7. Garnish with strawberry pieces, blueberries and mint. Serve immediately.

name: Apple Pie
instructions: 1. Slice green apples thinly. 2. Heat pan, add apple strips and castor sugar, mix well. Add cinnamon powder, cook 4-5 minutes until apples soften. 3. Turn off heat, add biscuit crumbs, mix, transfer to plate to cool. 4. Preheat oven to 200°C. 5. For dough, mix flour with butter using fingertips until breadcrumb texture. 6. Add sugar and mix, then add milk gradually until dough forms. 7. Roll half the dough into disc, place in pie mould, press sides and trim edges. 8. Add cooled apple mixture, spread evenly. 9. Roll remaining dough into disc, place over pie, seal edges with rolling pin, trim excess. 10. Roll extra dough thin and cut shapes with cookie cutters. 11. Brush pie with milk, arrange cut shapes on top, brush entire pie with milk, make holes, bake 20-25 minutes. 12. Cool slightly, de-mould, cut and serve warm.

name: Mutton Naga Phall
ingredients: 750 grams mutton, cut into 2 inch pieces on bone
instructions: 1. Heat ghee in pressure cooker, add panch phoran, sauté 30 seconds. 2. Add chopped onion, sauté until golden brown. Add ginger garlic paste and boiled onion paste, sauté 5-6 minutes. 3. Add mutton pieces, mix well. Add tomatoes and tomato puree, sauté 5-6 minutes. 4. Add curry powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, sauté until oil separates. Sprinkle dried naga chillies, mix well. 5. Add yogurt, mutton stock and salt, mix well. Lower flame, cover and cook 4-5 whistles until mutton cooked. 6. When pressure releases, remove lid, sprinkle garam masala powder, mix and cook 4-5 minutes. 7. Transfer to serving bowl, garnish with coriander sprig and serve hot.

name: Jackfruit Pepper Fry
ingredients: 400 grams raw jackfruit, peeled and cut into 1/2 inch pieces
instructions: 1. Boil water with salt, turmeric powder and jackfruit, cook 10-15 minutes. 2. Heat pan, add coriander seeds, fennel seeds, cinnamon, cloves and black peppercorns, dry roast until fragrant, cool completely. 3. Transfer roasted spices to grinder, grind to fine powder. 4. Drain jackfruit and set aside. 5. Heat oil in pan, add mustard seeds, once sputtering add curry leaves, onions, sauté until translucent. 6. Add green chillies and ginger-garlic paste, sauté 1 minute. 7. Add boiled jackfruit, mix well. Add 3 tbsps ground spice mix, salt and 1/2 cup water, mix and cook 2-3 minutes. 8. Add coconut slices, drizzle coconut oil, sprinkle curry leaves, mix well. 9. Transfer to serving plate, garnish with coconut slices and serve hot with dosas.

name: Sabut Moong with Onion Tomato Tadka
instructions: 1. Add ingredients to Wonderchef Chef Magic cooker. 2. Press start and let the smart kitchen assistant cook the dish automatically. 3. The cooker will handle the cooking process and produce a perfectly cooked dish with onion tomato tadka in minimal time.

name: Blueberry Oats Muffins
instructions: 1. Prepare muffin batter with oats and blueberries. 2. Fill muffin cups with batter. 3. Place in Wonderchef Air Fryer. 4. Cook with minimal oil until muffins are fluffy and cooked through. 5. Perfect for breakfast, brunch, snacking or kids' tiffin.

name: Pecan Kulfi
instructions: Heat milk on medium heat and reduce to half the original volume, scraping pan sides regularly. In a separate pan, dry roast pecans for 6-8 minutes. Grind half the pecans into a fine paste. Chop remaining pecans. Add pecan butter to reduced milk with condensed milk and cardamom powder. Mix in chopped pecans. Cool completely and transfer to kulfi moulds. Freeze for 6-8 hours. Demould, garnish with pecans, and serve chilled.

name: Cheesy Sprout Sev Puri
instructions: Layer crispy sev puris with boiled sprouts and drizzle generously with melted cheese. Serve immediately while warm.

name: Peri Peri Paneer Pakoda
instructions: Cut paneer into 1-inch pieces. Mix gram flour, peri peri spice, carom seeds, ginger-garlic paste, coriander, and salt in a bowl. Add 1½ cups water and whisk well to form a smooth batter. Spread cornstarch on a plate with salt and remaining peri peri spice. Heat oil in a kadai. Roll paneer pieces in cornflour mixture, dip in batter, and deep fry until golden brown and crisp. Drain on absorbent paper. Sprinkle peri peri spice mix and serve hot.

name: Tandoori Fish Kababs
instructions: Mix yogurt with tandoori spice, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and salt. Cut fish into cubes and marinate in the tandoori mixture for 30 minutes. Thread marinated fish onto skewers. Place on a tandoor or grill and cook until charred and cooked through, basting with oil occasionally. Serve hot with lemon wedges and fresh coriander.

name: Upma Stuffed Moong Dosa
instructions: Prepare upma: Heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves. Sauté onions and green chillies until golden. Add carrot and peas, cook until soft. Add semolina gradually and toast for 2-3 minutes. Pour hot water and cook until done. Cool the upma. Prepare moong dosa batter and heat a non-stick pan. Spread thin layer of dosa, place upma filling in the center, fold and cook until golden on both sides. Serve hot.

name: Moong Dal Idli with Cheese
ingredients: 1 cup split skinless green gram (dhuli moong dal), washed and soaked 3-4 hours
1 cup split skinless black gram (dhuli urad dal), washed and soaked 3-4 hours
instructions: Blend soaked moong dal and urad dal with ½ cup water to a fine paste. Transfer to a bowl, cover, and ferment for 6-8 hours at room temperature. Finely chop cheddar cheese. Add salt, ginger-green chilli paste, and asafoetida to the fermented batter and mix well. Heat water in a steamer and grease idli mould cavities with oil. Pour batter into cavities, sprinkle chopped cheese in the center, and cover with more batter. Steam for 15 minutes. Demould onto a plate and sprinkle gun powder, red chilli powder, and drizzle melted butter. Garnish with coriander and serve hot with coconut chutney.

name: Kadi Patta Fish Curry
instructions: Heat oil and add cumin seeds and curry leaves. Add sliced onions and cook until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute. Add turmeric and red chilli powder, mix well. Add fish pieces and sauté for 2-3 minutes. Pour coconut milk and add slit green chillies. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until fish is cooked through. Season with salt. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

name: Matcha Tiramisu
instructions: 1. Heat a non-stick pan, add matcha powder and 1 cup water, simmer for 2-3 minutes. Add sugar free natura diet sugar and mix till dissolved. Transfer to bowl and cool. 2.
